title: Changes in self-reported Long COVID in different variant-dominant phases of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic: the influence of vaccination on a diverse Israeli cohort study
abstract: PURPOSE OF RESEARCH: Long COVID (LC) risk varies across SARS-CoV-2 variants, but causal inference is complicated by rising vaccine coverage coinciding with viral evolution. We examined how pre-infection vaccination status modified LC risk across different pandemic periods dominated by different variants, to disentangle the contributions of viral evolution and vaccine-induced immunity. In this prospective cohort study of Israeli adults with SARS-CoV-2 infections from July 2021-March 2023, participants completed baseline and follow-up online surveys ≥60 days post-infection. LC was defined as ≥3 symptoms within validated symptom clusters. Infections were assigned to an infection period corresponding to the predominant circulating variant (Wild type, Alpha, Delta, Omicron) at onset time. Pre-infection vaccination was categorized as unvaccinated (0-1 doses), partially vaccinated (2 doses), or fully vaccinated (≥3 doses). Generalized estimating equations estimated multivariable risk ratios, adjusted for age, sex, and follow-up time. Among 1715 participants reporting 2018 infections, LC was reported following 30·4% of infections. In models adjusted for vaccination, LC risk did not differ between the Delta and Omicron-dominant periods (aRR 1·01, 95% CI 0·80-1·26). Among partially vaccinated individuals, infections during the Omicron-dominant period carried lower LC risk than during Delta (aRR 0·62, 95% CI 0·40-0·98). LC risk did not differ by variant-dominant periods among unvaccinated or fully vaccinated individuals. MAJOR CONCLUSIONS: Observed differences in LC risk at various periods of the pandemic dominated by different variants may be largely explained by concurrent increases in vaccine coverage rather than intrinsic changes in variant pathogenicity. Full pre-infection vaccination conferred consistent protection against LC regardless of the period of variant dominance.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study investigates how pre-infection vaccination status modifies the risk of Long COVID (LC) across different pandemic periods dominated by various SARS-CoV-2 variants, aiming to disentangle the effects of viral evolution and vaccine-induced immunity on LC risk.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This prospective cohort study of Israeli adults with SARS-CoV-2 infections from July 2021 to March 2023 used baseline and follow-up online surveys ≥60 days post-infection. Generalized estimating equations estimated multivariable risk ratios, adjusted for age, sex, and follow-up time. Pre-infection vaccination status was categorized as unvaccinated (0-1 doses), partially vaccinated (2 doses), or fully vaccinated (≥3 doses).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that LC risk did not differ between Delta and Omicron-dominant periods when adjusted for vaccination status. Among partially vaccinated individuals, infections during the Omicron-dominant period had lower LC risk than during Delta. Full pre-infection vaccination conferred consistent protection against LC regardless of the variant-dominant period. The major conclusion is that differences in LC risk across pandemic phases may be primarily due to increasing vaccine coverage rather than intrinsic changes in variant pathogenicity.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study acknowledges that LC risk differences across variant-dominant periods may be influenced by other factors not fully accounted for in the analysis. analysis.summary_en: This study examines the influence of pre-infection vaccination status on Long COVID (LC) risk across different SARS-CoV-2 variant-dominant phases of the pandemic in an Israeli cohort. It finds that LC risk did not differ between Delta and Omicron-dominant periods when adjusted for vaccination status, but partially vaccinated individuals had lower LC risk during Omicron-dominant periods. Full vaccination consistently protected against LC regardless of the variant. The study concludes that vaccine coverage, rather than variant pathogenicity, may explain observed LC risk variations. It highlights the need for further research on vaccination's role in preventing LC and underscores the importance of vaccination in public health strategies.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究探讨了感染前疫苗接种状态如何改变不同流行期中由各种严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株主导的长新冠(长新冠)风险,旨在区分病毒进化和疫苗诱导的免疫对长新冠风险的影响。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这项针对以色列成年人的前瞻性队列研究研究,涵盖了2021年7月至2023年3月期间的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染病例,使用了感染后≥60天的基线和随访在线调查。通过广义估计方程计算多变量风险比,并调整了年龄、性别和随访时间。感染前的疫苗接种状态被分为未接种疫苗(0-1剂)、部分接种疫苗(2剂)或完全接种疫苗(≥3剂)。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究发现,在调整了疫苗接种状态后,Delta和Omicron主导阶段的LC风险无差异。在部分接种疫苗的个体中,Omicron主导阶段的感染相较于Delta主导阶段具有较低的LC风险。无论在何种变异株主导阶段,感染前的完全接种疫苗接种均能提供一致的保护作用,以防止LC的发生。主要结论是,不同疫情阶段中LC风险的差异可能主要由疫苗覆盖率的增加而非变异株本身的致病性变化所导致。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究承认,不同变异株主导阶段中LC风险的差异可能受到未在分析中完全考虑的其他因素的影响。证据并未提供关于所观察到的关联背后机制或疫苗接种对LC风险的长期影响的详细信息。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果表明,在评估不同疫情阶段的LC风险时,应考虑感染前的疫苗接种状态。需要进一步研究以探讨疫苗接种如何影响LC风险的机制,并解决潜在的混杂因素。公共卫生策略应强调疫苗接种作为预防长新冠的保护措施,无论主导变异株是什么。

title: [Dynamics of behavioral factors and attitudes toward vaccination in moscow during the COVID-19 pandemic: from the acute phase to adaptation].
abstract: BACKGROUND: The transition of the COVID-19 pandemic from the acute phase to adaptation was accompanied by changes in preventive behavior, institutional trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination. OBJECTIVE: To analyze the dynamics of awareness, preventive behavior, trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination among Moscow residents in 2021 compared with 2020. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The survey tool was developed by the WHO Regional Office for Europe with support from the University of Erfurt and adapted to the Moscow context. CATI was conducted using a stratified dual-frame sample. The article analyzes the 4th and 5th survey waves: February 2021 (n = 1038) and July-August 2021 (n = 998). RESULTS: By the 5th wave, adherence to most preventive measures decreased, especially social distancing, limiting contacts and using hand sanitizers. The proportion not wearing gloves increased sharply after the requirement was lifted. The mean self-assessment of emotional state decreased to 3.47 points; institutional assessments declined and vaccination attitudes became more polarized. CONCLUSIONS: Public health strategies should combine consistent scientific communication, targeted work with vaccine-hesitant groups and horizontal trust.

analysis.summary_en: This review analyzes the dynamics of awareness, preventive behavior, trust, emotional state, and attitudes toward vaccination among Moscow residents during the transition of the COVID-19 pandemic from the acute phase to adaptation. It compares data from 2020 and 2021, highlighting a decline in adherence to preventive measures and a polarized stance on vaccination. The study, based on survey data collected via CATI using a stratified dual-frame sample, underscores the importance of consistent scientific communication and targeted efforts to address vaccine hesitancy. The findings suggest that public health strategies must adapt to evolving public perceptions and behaviors to effectively manage the pandemic.

analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 公共卫生策略应着重于持续的科学传播、针对疫苗犹豫群体的定向工作以及建立横向信任,以应对大流行期间对疫苗接种态度和行为的变化。

title: Introducing SARS-CoV-2 wastewater surveillance in Lebanon
abstract: UNLABELLED: Wastewater surveillance (WWS) gained global attention during the COVID-19 pandemic as an early warning system to continuously monitor SARS-CoV-2 and its evolving variants. The aim of this study is to detect and sequence SARS-CoV-2 in wastewater from an area in Lebanon that hosts vulnerable groups of Lebanese residents and refugees. A total of 188 wastewater samples were collected from 18 manholes between 20 February 2023 and 31 May 2023. Viral RNA extraction, RT-PCR, and genomic sequencing were performed. Eighteen percent of collected samples were SARS-CoV-2-positive. Omicron BA.2 was the only circulating variant in February. An overlap between Omicron BA.2 (33.33%) and B.1.1-like sublineages, including C.26 (16.67%), B.1.1.207 (16.67%), B.1.1.214 (16.67%), and C.2.1 (16.67%) was detected in March. In April, while Omicron circulation decreased to 12.5%, a BA.1 and BA.2 recombinant (XM) was detected. The lack of disaggregated data sets and case-specific SARS-CoV-2 reports from the study site residents limited our ability to perform correlation and comparative analyses between wastewater and national clinical data. However, wastewater samples showed higher positivity rates during most of the months prior to national surges of cases. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating WWS in public health interventions to complement clinical and epidemiologic surveillance. IMPORTANCE: Wastewater surveillance (WWS) is a valuable environmental surveillance tool that facilitates the real-time detection of circulating viruses and emerging variants. The COVID-19 pandemic has led to significant acceleration in the use of WWS as an early warning system for detecting SARS-CoV-2 and monitoring community transmission. This is the first study introducing SARS-CoV-2 community-based WWS in Lebanon. The findings of this study highlight the importance and feasibility of implementing WWS in a limited-resource setting to complement epidemiological surveillance in monitoring trends of SARS-CoV-2 at the population/community level.
authors: On behalf of CAEP Study Group

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,污水监测可以提供严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2传播趋势的早期信号。这些结果突出了在资源有限的环境中实施WWS的重要性与可行性,以补充流行病学的监测。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究为利用污水监测监测黎巴嫩严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2趋势提供了证据。它强调了WWS在资源有限地区对公共卫生干预措施的潜在价值,并补充临床数据以监测严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2在人群/社区层面的趋势。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于研究地点居民缺乏细分数据集和病例特定的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2报告,限制了我们对污水与国家临床数据之间进行相关性和比较分析的能力。由于数据可用性的限制以及研究的观察性质,证据强度中等。

title: COVID-19: An updated comprehensive review
abstract: More than six years after the emergence of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) remains a complex global health challenge shaped by continued viral evolution, heterogeneous population immunity, and unequal access to prevention and care. The transition from the acute pandemic phase has changed the relationship between infection, hospitalization, and mortality, while reduced testing and surveillance complicate assessment of the contemporary burden. Ongoing diversification of Omicron descendants, waning protection against infection, and recurrent exposure have introduced additional uncertainties regarding transmissibility, immune escape, and clinical risk. Beyond acute respiratory illness, COVID-19 encompasses multisystem complications and persistent postinfectious symptoms, requiring an integrated appraisal of virological, immunological, clinical, and public health evidence. The aim of this narrative review is to critically synthesize current knowledge of SARS-CoV-2 epidemiology, genomic evolution, transmission, pathogenesis, host immune responses, and the spectrum of clinical manifestations. It also examines advances and limitations in diagnostic testing, severity-stratified therapeutics, vaccination, nonpharmaceutical interventions, and the recognition and management of long COVID. Particular attention is given to evidence gaps surrounding reinfection, immune durability, variant-specific risk, postacute disease mechanisms, equitable access to countermeasures, and sustainable surveillance. By connecting these domains, the review seeks to provide an updated framework for interpreting COVID-19 evidence and identifying priorities for clinical practice, public health policy, and future research.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on SARS-CoV-2, specifically examining its epidemiology, genomic evolution, transmission, pathogenesis, host immune responses, and the spectrum of clinical manifestations. The central question is to critically synthesize current knowledge about the virus and its associated disease, COVID-19, and to identify priorities for clinical practice, public health policy, and future research.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of current knowledge, with no explicit mention of systematic search methods, databases, or meta-analysis. It includes a general overview of the evidence without detailing specific eligibility criteria or selection processes.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve, leading to uncertainties in transmissibility, immune escape, and clinical risk. It also emphasizes the need for an integrated appraisal of virological, immunological, clinical, and public health evidence to understand the broader implications of the disease.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There are unresolved issues regarding reinfection, immune durability, variant-specific risk, and the mechanisms of postacute disease. Additionally, the review notes that reduced testing and surveillance complicate the assessment of the current burden of the disease.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review identifies specific priorities for research, surveillance, diagnosis, treatment, vaccination, and nonpharmaceutical interventions. It also calls for improved understanding of long COVID and equitable access to countermeasures.

analysis.summary_en: This review provides an updated synthesis of SARS-CoV-2 and its associated disease, COVID-19, emphasizing the ongoing challenges posed by viral evolution, population immunity, and access to care. It outlines the complexities of the disease, including multisystem complications and persistent postinfectious symptoms, and highlights the need for integrated evidence appraisal. The review identifies key areas of uncertainty, such as reinfection and immune durability, and underscores the importance of addressing these through targeted research and public health strategies. It also calls for improved surveillance and equitable access to countermeasures, suggesting that these efforts are critical for managing the long-term impact of the virus.

The central question is to critically synthesize current knowledge about the virus and its associated disease, COVID-19, and to identify priorities for clinical practice, public health policy, and future research.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of current knowledge, with no explicit mention of systematic search methods, databases, or meta-analysis. It includes a general overview of the evidence without detailing specific eligibility criteria or selection processes.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve, leading to uncertainties in transmissibility, immune escape, and clinical risk. It also emphasizes the need for an integrated appraisal of virological, immunological, clinical, and public health evidence to understand the broader implications of the disease.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There are unresolved issues regarding reinfection, immune durability, variant-specific risk, and the mechanisms of postacute disease. analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review identifies specific priorities for research, surveillance, diagnosis, treatment, vaccination, and nonpharmaceutical interventions. It also calls for improved understanding of long COVID and equitable access to countermeasures.

title_zh: COVID-19: An updated comprehensive review
source_body_en: More than six years after the emergence of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) remains a complex global health challenge shaped by continued viral evolution, heterogeneous population immunity, and unequal access to prevention and care. The transition from the acute pandemic phase has changed the relationship between infection, hospitalization, and mortality, while reduced testing and surveillance complicate assessment of the contemporary burden. Ongoing diversification of Omicron descendants, waning protection against infection, and recurrent exposure have introduced additional uncertainties regarding transmissibility, immune escape, and clinical risk. Beyond acute respiratory illness, COVID-19 encompasses multisystem complications and persistent postinfectious symptoms, requiring an integrated appraisal of virological, immunological, clinical, and public health evidence. The aim of this narrative review is to critically synthesize current knowledge of SARS-CoV-2 epidemiology, genomic evolution, transmission, pathogenesis, host immune responses, and the spectrum of clinical manifestations. It also examines advances and limitations in diagnostic testing, severity-stratified therapeutics, vaccination, nonpharmaceutical interventions, and the recognition and management of long COVID. Particular attention is given to evidence gaps surrounding reinfection, immune durability, variant-specific risk, postacute disease mechanisms, equitable access to countermeasures, and sustainable surveillance. By connecting these domains, the review seeks to provide an updated framework for interpreting COVID-19 evidence and identifying priorities for clinical practice, public health policy, and future research.

title: Real-world safety outcomes of COVID-19 mRNA vaccine: A result from Korea post-marketing surveillance
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has caused a substantial global health burden, highlighting the need for post-authorization safety evaluation in real-world settings. BNT162b2 is a widely used mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, and, in addition to the original strain-based formulation, BA.1-, BA.4/5-, XBB.1.5-, and JN.1-adapted formulations were introduced sequentially. This study aimed to evaluate the real-world safety profile of the BNT162b2 product family using post-marketing surveillance data collected in Korea. Data collection was conducted from 50 sites. Solicited adverse events (AEs) were collected for 7 days, and unsolicited AEs for 28 days after vaccination. AEs occurring beyond Day 28 were also collected if reported during routine follow-up, without restriction on the collection period. Of 6,343 enrolled participants, 6,251 were included in the safety analysis set. Overall AEs were reported in 1,640 participants (26.2%) and adverse drug reactions (ADRs) in 1,610 participants (25.8%). Serious AEs occurred in 2 participants (<0.1%), and serious ADRs in 1 participant (<0.1%); no unexpected serious ADRs were identified. Solicited AEs were predominantly mild reactogenicity events, most commonly injection site pain, myalgia, fatigue, and headache. The overall safety profile of the BNT162b2 product family was generally manageable in this predominantly adult population, with very few serious ADRs and no unexpected serious ADRs identified. However, due to limited systematic capture of adverse events of special interest (AESIs) and underrepresentation of pediatric participants, AESI-related findings and pediatric safety conclusions should be interpreted with caution. These findings provide complementary real-world evidence regarding the safety of BNT162b2-adapted vaccines in Korea.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using post-marketing surveillance data collected in Korea from 50 sites, with 6,343 enrolled participants and 6,251 included in the safety analysis set.
analysis.methods: Solicited adverse events (AEs) were collected for 7 days, and unsolicited AEs for 28 days after vaccination. AEs occurring beyond Day 28 were also collected if reported during routine follow-up, without restriction on the collection period.
analysis.main_results: Overall AEs were reported in 1,640 participants (26.2%) and adverse drug reactions (ADRs) in 1,610 participants (25.8%). Serious AEs occurred in 2 participants (<0.1%), and serious ADRs in 1 participant (<0.1%); no unexpected serious ADRs were identified.

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study notes limited systematic capture of adverse events of special interest (AESIs) and underrepresentation of pediatric participants, which should be interpreted with caution. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the real-world safety profile of the BNT162b2 product family of mRNA vaccines in Korea using post-marketing surveillance data. It reports that overall adverse events (AEs) were observed in 26.2% of participants, with serious AEs occurring in less than 0.1% of cases. Solicited AEs were predominantly mild reactogenicity events, while unsolicited AEs were collected for 28 days. The findings suggest that the safety profile of these vaccines is generally manageable in adults, with no unexpected serious adverse drug reactions (ADRs) identified. However, the study acknowledges limitations in capturing adverse events of special interest and underrepresentation of pediatric participants, which may affect the generalizability of the results. These results contribute to the understanding of vaccine safety in a real-world setting and may inform public health strategies.

title_zh: Real-world safety outcomes of COVID-19 mRNA vaccine: A result from Korea post-marketing surveillance
source_body_en: The COVID-19 pandemic has caused a substantial global health burden, highlighting the need for post-authorization safety evaluation in real-world settings. BNT162b2 is a widely used mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, and, in addition to the original strain-based formulation, BA.1-, BA.4/5-, XBB.1.5-, and JN.1-adapted formulations were introduced sequentially. This study aimed to evaluate the real-world safety profile of the BNT162b2 product family using post-marketing surveillance data collected in Korea. Data collection was conducted from 50 sites. Solicited adverse events (AEs) were collected for 7 days, and unsolicited AEs for 28 days after vaccination. AEs occurring beyond Day 28 were also collected if reported during routine follow-up, without restriction on the collection period. Of 6,343 enrolled participants, 6,251 were included in the safety analysis set. Overall AEs were reported in 1,640 participants (26.2%) and adverse drug reactions (ADRs) in 1,610 participants (25.8%). Serious AEs occurred in 2 participants (<0.1%), and serious ADRs in 1 participant (<0.1%); no unexpected serious ADRs were identified. Solicited AEs were predominantly mild reactogenicity events, most commonly injection site pain, myalgia, fatigue, and headache. The overall safety profile of the BNT162b2 product family was generally manageable in this predominantly adult population, with very few serious ADRs and no unexpected serious ADRs identified. However, due to limited systematic capture of adverse events of special interest (AESIs) and underrepresentation of pediatric participants, AESI-related findings and pediatric safety conclusions should be interpreted with caution. These findings provide complementary real-world evidence regarding the safety of BNT162b2-adapted vaccines in Korea.

title: How Did the Clinical Presentation of COVID-19 in Children Change Across SARS-CoV-2 Variants? A Systematic Review
abstract: (1) Background: SARS-CoV-2 variants clinical presentation and severity may differ in children. This systematic review evaluated changes that occurred in pediatric COVID-19 across successive viral variants. (2) Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science were searched through 26 September 2026 for comparative studies of SARS-CoV-2 variants in patients aged 18 years or younger. We assessed their methodological quality with the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale (NOS) and their clinical manifestations and severity outcomes were synthesized narratively. (3) Results: Twenty-nine studies were included. Delta was generally associated with a greater symptomatic burden than Alpha, even though the differences in severe outcomes were inconsistent. Omicron was associated with a distinct clinical phenotype, more frequent croup and seizures, some of which were reported as febrile seizure, while gastrointestinal findings varied across studies. Population-based studies generally indicated lower risks of hospitalization or severe disease with Omicron than Delta, but findings among hospitalized children were less consistent. Studies of Omicron subvariants identified differences in individual symptoms without a consistent trend in disease severity. (4) Conclusions: The clinical phenotype of pediatric COVID-19 evolved across SARS-CoV-2 variants. Omicron was particularly associated with increased upper-airway, particularly croup, while several studies also reported increased seizure frequency, including febrile seizures. Population-based studies generally suggesting less severe disease than Delta infections. analysis.scope_and_question: The review investigates how the clinical presentation of COVID-19 in children changed across successive SARS-CoV-2 variants, focusing on symptoms, severity, and hospitalization risks.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science up to 26 September 2026 for comparative studies of SARS-CoV-2 variants in children aged 18 years or younger. The methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale (NOS), and clinical manifestations and severity outcomes were synthesized narratively.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The clinical phenotype of pediatric COVID-19 evolved across SARS-CoV-2 variants. Delta was generally associated with a greater symptomatic burden than Alpha, while Omicron was linked to a distinct clinical phenotype, including more frequent croup and seizures, with some studies reporting increased seizure frequency, including febrile seizures. Population-based studies generally indicated lower risks of hospitalization or severe disease with Omicron than Delta, though findings among hospitalized children were less consistent.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There was inconsistency in the differences in severe outcomes between Delta and Alpha, and findings among hospitalized children were less consistent. Differences in age, study setting, variant ascertainment, and outcome definitions should be considered when interpreting these findings. The review also notes that studies of Omicron subvariants identified differences in individual symptoms without a consistent trend in disease severity.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to clarify the differences in disease severity across SARS-CoV-2 variants in hospitalized children and to standardize outcome definitions and study methodologies. Surveillance and diagnostic efforts should account for variant-specific clinical phenotypes, particularly the increased frequency of upper-airway symptoms and seizures associated with Omicron.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines how the clinical presentation of pediatric COVID-19 evolved across successive SARS-CoV-2 variants. It highlights that Delta was associated with a greater symptomatic burden than Alpha, while Omicron presented a distinct clinical phenotype, including more frequent croup and seizures. Population-based studies suggested lower hospitalization risks with Omicron compared to Delta, but findings among hospitalized children were inconsistent. The review emphasizes the need for standardized methodologies and further research to clarify variant-specific disease severity and symptoms, particularly in subvariant analyses. The implications underscore the importance of surveillance and diagnostic efforts tailored to variant-specific clinical features.

title: Modeling the cost-effectiveness of NVX-CoV2705 and the public health impact of vaccination for the prevention of seasonal COVID-19 in the US
abstract: BACKGROUND: Older adults and those with comorbidities have increased risk of severe disease and mortality from COVID-19. This analysis estimated the cost-effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccination versus no vaccination in the US and potential impact of increased vaccine coverage. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A Markov-based model was updated using the latest epidemiology and vaccine reactogenicity data. Cases, costs, and outcomes for individuals aged 18-64 with ≥1 comorbidity and ≥65 years were estimated for NVX-CoV2705 (Nuvaxovid) versus no vaccination from a third-party payer perspective. Scenario analyses considered the societal perspective and analogous comparisons for BNT162b2 (Comirnaty), mRNA-1273 (Spikevax), and mRNA-1283 (mNEXSPIKE). Results were scaled for public health impact analyses. RESULTS: Base-case results associated NVX-CoV2705 with fewer cases (0.0447), hospitalizations (0.0037), and deaths (0.0004) per person on average. NVX-CoV2705 yielded an ICER of $9,840/QALY gained, reflecting fewer QALYs lost (0.0039) alongside increased direct costs ($38.09) per person. Differences for mRNA vaccines were driven by price and reactogenicity. Increasing vaccine coverage by 5-15 percentage points resulted in 114-341 hospitalizations and 11-33 deaths averted per 1,000,000 individuals. CONCLUSIONS: NVX-CoV2705 was predicted to be cost-effective over no vaccination. This analysis included a more granular approach to modeling reactogenicity events, an important consideration in vaccine cost-effectiveness analyses.

title: Therapeutic opportunities of marine-derived bioactive compounds against SARS-CoV-2 and other enveloped viruses
abstract: Abstract Marine ecosystems are a vast, underexplored reservoir of bioactive compounds with unique structural diversity and potent biological activities. Enveloped viruses, including severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the causative agent of COVID-19, continue to pose significant global health threats, exacerbated by emerging variants, limited therapeutic options beyond vaccines, and challenges such as drug resistance and immune dysregulation. Compounds derived from marine organisms, including lectins (e.g., griffithsin from red algae Griffithsia sp .), sulfated polysaccharides (e.g., iota-carrageenan from red algae Chondrus crispus ), polyphenols (e.g., dieckol from brown algae Ecklonia cava ), and depsipeptides (e.g., plitidepsin from tunicates), have shown promising antiviral effects in preclinical studies. These molecules primarily act by inhibiting viral entry (via the spike glycoprotein or glycan binding), replication (targeting proteases such as the main protease [Mpro] and the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase [RdRp]), or by modulating host immune responses (e.g., reducing cytokine storms or oxidative stress). In vitro, in vivo, and in silico evidence highlights their potential against SARS-CoV-2 and related enveloped viruses (e.g., HIV, HSV, influenza, HCMV), which share mechanistic similarities, including envelope-mediated fusion and RNA-based replication. This narrative review provides a cohesive overview of selected marine-derived bioactive compounds with reported activity against SARS-CoV-2 and other enveloped viruses. It examines their sources, structural features, mechanisms of action, key activity metrics (e.g., IC50/EC50 values), and translational prospects, and addresses challenges such as scalability, preclinical-to-clinical gaps, and sustainability aligned with the European Blue Economy. By integrating recent findings, this review aims to highlight promising leads and guide future research toward innovative, broad-spectrum antiviral therapies.

Compounds derived from marine organisms, including lectins (e.g., griffithsin from red algae Griffithsia sp .), sulfated polysaccharides (e.g., iota-carrageenan from red algae Chondrus crispus ), polyphenols (e.g., dieckol from brown algae Ecklonia cava ), and depsipeptides (e.g., plitidepsin from tunicates), have shown promising antiviral effects in preclinical studies. These molecules primarily act by inhibiting viral entry (via the spike glycoprotein or glycan binding), replication (targeting proteases such as the main protease [Mpro] and the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase [RdRp]), or by modulating host immune responses (e.g., reducing cytokine storms or oxidative stress). In vitro, in vivo, and in silico evidence highlights their potential against SARS-CoV-2 and related enveloped viruses (e.g., HIV, HSV, influenza, HCMV), which share mechanistic similarities, including envelope-mediated fusion and RNA-based replication. This narrative review provides a cohesive overview of selected marine-derived bioactive compounds with reported activity against SARS-CoV-2 and other enveloped viruses. It examines their sources, structural features, mechanisms of action, key activity metrics (e.g., IC50/EC50 values), and translational prospects, and addresses challenges such as scalability, preclinical-to-clinical gaps, and sustainability aligned with the European Blue Economy. By integrating recent findings, this review aims to highlight promising leads and guide future research toward innovative, broad-spectrum antiviral therapies.
title_original: Therapeutic opportunities of marine-derived bioactive compounds against SARS-CoV-2 and other enveloped viruses

analysis.scope_and_question: This review explores the therapeutic potential of marine-derived bioactive compounds against SARS-CoV-2 and other enveloped viruses, focusing on their antiviral mechanisms and translational prospects. The central question is whether these compounds can serve as effective antiviral agents for SARS-CoV-2 and related viruses, considering their structural diversity and biological activities.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of preclinical studies on marine-derived bioactive compounds, including in vitro, in vivo, and in silico evidence. It does not report specific databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods. The review includes compounds such as lectins, sulfated polysaccharides, polyphenols, and depsipeptides, with their sources, structural features, and mechanisms of action discussed.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Marine-derived bioactive compounds have demonstrated antiviral effects against SARS-CoV-2 and related enveloped viruses, primarily by inhibiting viral entry, replication, or modulating host immune responses. These findings are supported by in vitro, in vivo, and in silico studies, highlighting their potential as broad-spectrum antiviral therapies.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while these compounds show promise, there are challenges in scaling up production, bridging preclinical-to-clinical gaps, and ensuring sustainability. Additionally, the evidence is primarily preclinical, and there is a lack of large-scale clinical trials to confirm their efficacy in humans.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for further research to validate the antiviral potential of marine-derived compounds in clinical settings. It also highlights the importance of addressing scalability, sustainability, and translational challenges to develop effective therapies against SARS-CoV-2 and related enveloped viruses.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 海洋来源的活性化合物已显示出对抗严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2及相关包膜病毒的抗病毒效果,主要通过抑制病毒进入、复制或调节宿主 免疫应答实现。这些发现得到了体外、体内和计算机模拟研究的支持,突显了它们作为广谱抗病毒药物的潜力。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述指出,尽管这些化合物显示出前景,但在扩大生产规模、弥合临床前研究与临床应用之间的差距以及确保可持续性方面仍存在挑战。此外,目前的证据主要来自临床前研究,缺乏大规模临床试验来验证其在人体中的有效性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述强调需要进一步研究以验证海洋来源化合物在临床环境中的抗病毒潜力。同时,它也突出了应对生产规模、可持续性和转化挑战的重要性,以开发有效的治疗手段对抗严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2及相关包膜病毒。

title: Biosafety level‐3 cryo‐electron tomography of active severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 virions
abstract: Abstract Understanding the structural properties of pathogenic viruses in their native, infectious state is critical for rational vaccine and drug development. However, conducting cryo‐electron microscopy (cryo‐EM) under biosafety level 3 (BSL‐3) containment presents significant challenges. Here, we established and validated a high‐end cryo‐EM workflow within a BSL‐3 facility, comprehensively integrating facility design, containment measures, sample handling, cryo‐transfer systems, and decontamination protocols. To demonstrate the utility and reproducibility of this workflow, we applied cryo‐electron tomography to investigate severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 in its native, active state. Our observations confirm that unfixed viral particles display pleomorphic features comparable to those previously reported in fixed or inactivated preparations, validating that these structural characteristics represent native features rather than artifacts of chemical fixation. Furthermore, spatial redistribution of surface spikes was observed. title_zh: Biosafety level‐3 cryo‐electron tomography of active severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 virions
source_body_en: Abstract Understanding the structural properties of pathogenic viruses in their native, infectious state is critical for rational vaccine and drug development. However, conducting cryo‐electron microscopy (cryo‐EM) under biosafety level 3 (BSL‐3) containment presents significant challenges. Here, we established and validated a high‐end cryo‐EM workflow within a BSL‐3 facility, comprehensively integrating facility design, containment measures, sample handling, cryo‐transfer systems, and decontamination protocols. To demonstrate the utility and reproducibility of this workflow, we applied cryo‐electron tomography to investigate severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 in its native, active state. Our observations confirm that unfixed viral particles display pleomorphic features comparable to those previously reported in fixed or inactivated preparations, validating that these structural characteristics represent native features rather than artifacts of chemical fixation. Furthermore, spatial redistribution of surface spikes was observed. The establishment of this robust BSL‐3 cryo‐EM workflow provides a practical blueprint for the structural characterization of emerging high‐consequence pathogens, supporting pandemic preparedness, vaccine development, and antiviral discovery.
abstract_zh: 摘要 理解病原病毒在天然、可感染状态下的结构特性对于合理开发抗病毒药物和疫苗至关重要。然而,在生物安全三级(BSL-3)条件下进行冷冻电镜(cryo-EM)研究面临重大挑战。在此,我们在BSL-3设施中建立了并验证了一种高端冷冻电镜工作流程,全面整合了设施设计、防护措施、样品处理、冷冻转移系统和去污染协议。为了展示该工作流程的实用性与可重复性,我们采用冷冻电镜断层扫描技术对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2)在天然、活性状态下的结构进行了研究。我们的观察结果证实,未经固定的病毒颗粒表现出与之前在固定或灭活样品中报道的类似多形性特征,验证了这些结构特性是天然特征而非化学固定产生的伪影。此外,还观察到了表面刺突蛋白的空间重新分布。该稳健的BSL-3冷冻电镜工作流程的建立为新兴高危害病原体的结构表征提供了实用蓝图,支持流行病防控、抗病毒药物开发和疫苗发现。

title: Deletion of the Envelope gene attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection by altered spike localization and increased cell-to-cell transmission
abstract: ABSTRACT Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) causes COVID-19, a highly transmissible acute respiratory infection that can result in severe pneumonia and death. Many details of SARS-CoV-2 infection are not fully understood, including the cell biology and host-virus interactions involved in coronavirus assembly and release, in which the Envelope (E) structural protein is instrumental. Deletion of E in other coronaviruses has been shown previously to either attenuate or abrogate infection. To determine the role of E in SARS-CoV-2 virus production and infectivity, we produced a reporter SARS-CoV-2 with or without the E gene deleted using a bacterial artificial chromosome. Replication of ΔE SARS-CoV-2 was attenuated in Vero E6 cells expressing human ACE2 and TMPRSS2 and in human epithelial cell lines. Electron and immunofluorescence microscopy and virology assays showed that ΔE SARS-CoV-2 increased cell surface expression of Spike (S) glycoprotein, leading to reduced S incorporation into ΔE SARS-CoV-2 particles and promotion of increased cell-to-cell transmission that evades neutralizing antibody inhibition. Trans-complementation of E partially rescued ΔE SARS-CoV-2 S incorporation and restored cell-free transmission. In addition to validating the role of E in retention of S in the ER-Golgi intermediate complex (ERGIC), our results showed that a lack of E led to reorganization of the ERGIC and Golgi during SARS-CoV-2 infection. Improved understanding of E in SARS-CoV-2 replication and host pathogenesis may help the development of novel therapeutics. IMPORTANCE Non-Spike coronavirus structural proteins, including Envelope, are conserved, making them potential pan-coronavirus therapeutic targets. Many details about these proteins and their roles in viral replication and host pathogenesis are unknown. In this study, we showed that severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) replicates without Envelope but is attenuated and impaired in virus particle formation, with less Spike incorporated into virions and more Spike expressed on the cell surface compared to wild-type virus. SARS-CoV-2 lacking Envelope transmitted primarily via cell fusion and evaded neutralizing antibodies. In addition, the absence of Envelope resulted in the reorganization of the cell secretory compartment during SARS-CoV-2 infection. A better understanding of how Envelope influences SARS-CoV-2 replication could guide directed design of novel therapeutics for treatment of COVID-19 patients, as well as the potential for pan-coronavirus protection against future coronavirus outbreaks.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the role of the Envelope (E) gene in SARS-CoV-2 replication and infectivity, as many aspects of SARS-CoV-2 infection remain poorly understood, particularly the cell biology and host-virus interactions involved in coronavirus assembly and release.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved producing a reporter SARS-CoV-2 with or without the E gene deleted using a bacterial artificial chromosome to assess its impact on virus production and infectivity. The research was conducted in Vero E6 cells expressing human ACE2 and TMPRSS2, as well as human epithelial cell lines.
analysis.methods: The researchers used bacterial artificial chromosome technology to generate a reporter SARS-CoV-2 with or without the E gene deleted. They then performed electron and immunofluorescence microscopy, along with virology assays, to evaluate the effects of E deletion on Spike (S) glycoprotein expression and virus particle formation.
analysis.main_results: ΔE SARS-CoV-2 showed attenuated replication in Vero E6 cells and human epithelial cell lines. It had reduced Spike incorporation into virions and increased cell surface expression of Spike, which promoted cell-to-cell transmission and evaded neutralizing antibody inhibition.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the absence of Envelope leads to altered Spike localization and increased cell-to-cell transmission, which may provide insights into the mechanisms of SARS-CoV-2 pathogenesis and replication.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results may inform the development of novel therapeutics targeting the Envelope protein, potentially offering new strategies for treating COVID-19 patients and providing pan-coronavirus protection against future outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in vitro using cell lines, which may limit its generalizability to in vivo conditions. However, the evidence is strong as it directly links E deletion to changes in Spike expression and transmission mechanisms.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of the Envelope (E) gene in SARS-CoV-2 replication and infectivity. By deleting the E gene in a reporter SARS-CoV-2 using a bacterial artificial chromosome, the researchers observed that ΔE SARS-CoV-2 exhibited attenuated replication in Vero E6 cells and human epithelial cell lines. Electron and immunofluorescence microscopy, along with virology assays, revealed that the absence of E increased cell surface expression of Spike (S) glycoprotein, leading to reduced S incorporation into virions and enhanced cell-to-cell transmission that evades neutralizing antibodies. These findings suggest that E plays a critical role in S localization and virus particle formation, offering potential insights for developing new therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2. The study's in vitro nature may limit its applicability to real-world scenarios, but the results are robust and directly link E deletion to specific changes in viral behavior.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨包膜(E)基因在严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2复制和感染性中的作用,因为严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染的许多方面仍不明确,特别是与冠状病毒组装和释放相关的细胞生物学和宿主-病毒相互作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究通过使用细菌人工染色体技术生成带有或不带有E基因删除的报告严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2,以评估其对病毒生产和感染性的影响。研究在表达人ACE2和TMPRSS2的Vero E6细胞以及人类上皮细胞系中进行。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用细菌人工染色体技术生成了带有或不带有E基因删除的报告严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2。随后,他们进行了电子显微镜和免疫荧光显微镜检测,以及病毒学检测,以评估E基因删除对刺突(S)糖蛋白表达和病毒颗粒形成的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: ΔE 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2在Vero E6细胞和人类上皮细胞系中显示出复制减弱。其刺突蛋白整合到病毒颗粒中减少,而细胞表面刺突蛋白表达增加,这促进了细胞间传播传播并逃避中和抗体的抑制。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,包膜蛋白的缺失导致刺突蛋白定位改变和细胞间传播传播增加,这可能为理解严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 发病机制和复制机制提供见解。

title: The magnitude and durability of immune response to the SARS-CoV-2 vaccination among children
abstract: BACKGROUND: The declining uptake of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines, combined with evolving schedules and recurrent infections, underscores the need to monitor the durability of hybrid immunity in children. The objective of this study was to assess children's SARS-CoV-2-specific immune responses post-second vaccine dose and to compare immune responses between unvaccinated children and children vaccinated with two or three vaccine doses. METHODS: Three observational cohorts of children aged 3-14 years were followed longitudinally from December 2021 to October 2023 in Montreal, Canada. Two had scheduled serology assessments before their second dose and at one, six and twelve months post-second dose. The other cohort included unvaccinated and vaccinated children, with 2-4 serology assessments, every 2-3 months. Linear mixed models adjusting for infection history were used to assess immune waning post-second dose and differences over time by vaccine status. RESULTS: Controlling for recent infection, anti-spike IgG, anti-receptor binding domain (RBD) IgG, and neutralizing titers against wild-type SARS-CoV-2 declined by six months post-vaccination. For example, average IgG anti-RBD was 1 374.1 BAU/mL one month after dose two, with an estimated decline of -856.1 BAU/mL at six months (95% CI, -1 303.5 to -596.0; p<0.0001). T cell responses showed little evidence of decline over 12 months across all groups with a history of infection. Comparing children by vaccine status, the highest humoral responses were associated with three doses whereas the lowest with unvaccinated status (e.g., crude average two-dose IgG anti-RBD: 920.0 BAU/ml; unvaccinated estimated difference -515.1 BAU/mL; 95% CI, -698.0 to -444.7; p<0.0001). Spike-specific CD4+ T cell responses were lower among the unvaccinated. CONCLUSIONS: Humoral responses declined significantly within six months of vaccination. Cellular responses were comparable across vaccine status groups, yet vaccinated children tended to maintain higher levels for more than one-year post-vaccination. Hybrid immunity could contribute to a more robust and durable cellular response.
journal: Journal of the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the magnitude and durability of immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in children. It follows three observational cohorts aged 3-14 years in Montreal, Canada, from December 2021 to October 2023. The study compares immune responses between unvaccinated children and those vaccinated with two or three doses. Results show that anti-spike IgG, anti-RBD IgG, and neutralizing titers against wild-type SARS-CoV-2 decline significantly within six months post-vaccination. However, T cell responses remain stable across all groups. The authors suggest that hybrid immunity may enhance cellular response durability. These findings have implications for vaccine schedules and strategies to maintain immune protection in children. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational design, and no limitations are explicitly reported.

title_zh: 免疫应答在儿童中对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗接种的强度和持续时间
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: The declining uptake of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines, combined with evolving schedules and recurrent infections, underscores the need to monitor the durability of hybrid immunity in children. The objective of this study was to assess children's SARS-CoV-2-specific immune responses post-second vaccine dose and to compare immune responses between unvaccinated children and children vaccinated with two or three vaccine doses. METHODS: Three observational cohorts of children aged 3-14 years were followed longitudinally from December 2021 to October 2023 in Montreal, Canada. Two had scheduled serology assessments before their second dose and at one, six and twelve months post-second dose. The other cohort included unvaccinated and vaccinated children, with 2-4 serology assessments, every 2-3 months. Linear mixed models adjusting for infection history were used to assess immune waning post-second dose and differences over time by vaccine status. RESULTS: Controlling for recent infection, anti-spike IgG, anti-receptor binding domain (RBD) IgG, and neutralizing titers against wild-type SARS-CoV-2 declined by six months post-vaccination. For example, average IgG anti-RBD was 1 374.1 BAU/mL one month after dose two, with an estimated decline of -856.1 BAU/mL at six months (95% CI, -1 303.5 to -596.0; p<0.0001). T cell responses showed little evidence of decline over 12 months across all groups with a history of infection. Comparing children by vaccine status, the highest humoral responses were associated with three doses whereas the lowest with unvaccinated status (e.g., crude average two-dose IgG anti-RBD: 920.0 BAU/ml; unvaccinated estimated difference -515.1 BAU/mL; 95% CI, -698.0 to -444.7; p<0.0001). Spike-specific CD4+ T cell responses were lower among the unvaccinated. CONCLUSIONS: Humoral responses declined significantly within six months of vaccination. Cellular responses were comparable across vaccine status groups, yet vaccinated children tended to maintain higher levels for more than one-year post-vaccination. Hybrid immunity could contribute to a more robust and durable cellular response.
abstract_zh: 背景:严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗的接种率下降,结合不断变化的接种计划和反复感染,凸显了监测儿童中混合免疫持续时间的必要性。本研究的目的是评估儿童在接种第二剂疫苗后针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的免疫应答,并比较未接种疫苗儿童与接种两剂或三剂疫苗的儿童之间的免疫应答。方法:在加拿大蒙特利尔,对3-14岁儿童进行了三项纵向观察性队列研究,时间跨度为2021年12月至2023年10月。其中两项在接种第二剂前以及接种后1、6和12个月时进行了定期血清学评估。另一项队列研究包括未接种疫苗和接种疫苗的儿童,进行了2-4次血清学评估,间隔2-3个月。使用线性混合模型,调整感染史,以评估接种第二剂后免疫水平的下降情况,并比较不同疫苗状态随时间的变化。结果:在控制近期感染的情况下,针对刺突蛋白的IgG抗体、针对受体结合域(RBD)的IgG抗体以及针对野生型严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的中和抗体,在接种疫苗接种后6个月均出现下降。例如,接种第二剂后一个月,平均IgG抗RBD为1 374.1 BAU/mL,6个月时估计下降了-856.1 BAU/mL(95% CI,-1 303.5至-596.0;p<0.0001)。所有有感染史的组别中,针对刺突蛋白的T细胞反应在12个月内均未明显下降。比较不同疫苗状态的儿童,接种三剂的儿童具有最高的体液免疫反应,而未接种疫苗的儿童则最低(例如,粗略平均两剂IgG抗RBD为920.0 BAU/mL;未接种疫苗估计差异为-515.1 BAU/mL;95% CI,-698.0至-444.7;p<0.0001)。未接种疫苗的儿童中,针对刺突蛋白的CD4+ T细胞反应较低。结论:在接种疫苗接种后6个月内,体液免疫反应显著下降。细胞免疫反应在不同疫苗状态组之间相当,但接种疫苗的儿童在接种疫苗接种后超过一年仍能维持较高的免疫水平。混合免疫可能有助于增强和延长细胞免疫反应。科学与公共卫生意义:细胞免疫反应在不同疫苗状态组之间相当,但接种疫苗的儿童在接种疫苗接种后超过一年仍能维持较高的免疫水平。这些发现可能有助于制定疫苗接种计划,并增强儿童免疫持久性的策略。局限性与证据强度:本研究未报告研究设计的局限性。由于研究的观察性质以及潜在的混杂因素,证据强度为中等。

title: Timing dependent associations of acute phase laboratory and antibody parameters with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection in unvaccinated individuals
abstract: Introduction Post-acute sequelae of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection (PASC) affects a substantial minority of individuals after acute COVID-19, and immune dysregulation is widely implicated in its pathogenesis. Reported associations between SARS-CoV-2-specific antibody responses and PASC have nonetheless been inconsistent. Because antibody levels change rapidly in the weeks after symptom onset, the timing of sampling may itself account for much of this heterogeneity, yet few studies have examined humoral responses along the time axis from symptom onset in combination with routinely available hematological, biochemical, and coagulation parameters. Methods Eight hundred seventy-two serial serum samples were retrospectively analyzed from 213 unvaccinated individuals experiencing their first SARS-CoV-2 infection, sampled between April 2020 and June 2021, before vaccine rollout and before the emergence of Omicron; 13 individuals subsequently met the World Health Organization definition of PASC. Sixty-seven parameters, comprising antiviral antibodies, autoantibodies and immune markers, complete blood count, biochemistry and coagulation tests, were compared between groups within four windows defined by days since symptom onset: ≤ 7, 8–14, 15–28, and > 28 days. Results The pattern of association shifted markedly across windows. Within seven days of onset, innate inflammatory and coagulation markers predominated. Between days 8 and 14, when adaptive humoral responses first become measurable, red cell indices differed between groups, with lower mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration remaining significant when each patient contributed a single value. Anti-spike IgM levels tended to be higher in individuals who later developed PASC, although the difference was not statistically significant. Exploratory multivariable models combining humoral and hematological features discriminated better than either domain alone, although the small number of PASC cases precludes any claim of predictive validity. Discussion These findings identify days 8–14 after symptom onset as a potentially informative window during which acute-phase laboratory parameters, and possibly early humoral responses, differ between individuals who do and do not subsequently develop PASC, and suggest that the timing and quality of the early antibody response, rather than antibody magnitude measured at a single late time point, merit systematic investigation in PASC.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨急性期实验室检测和抗体参数与未接种疫苗个体中严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染后急性期后综合征的时间依赖性关联,因为免疫失调广泛参与其发病机制。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究回顾性分析了2020年4月至2021年6月期间213名未接种疫苗个体在首次严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染期间采集的872份连续血清样本,这些样本是在疫苗推广之前以及奥密克戎变异株出现之前采集的;13名个体后来符合世界卫生组织对PASC的定义。
elements_zh.methods: 在四个由症状出现后天数定义的时间窗口内,比较了包括抗病毒药物抗体、自身抗体、免疫标志物、全血细胞计数、生化检测和凝血检测在内的67个参数:≤7天、8–14天、15–28天和>28天。
elements_zh.main_results: 在不同时间窗口中,关联模式发生了显著变化。在症状出现后7天内,先天性炎症和凝血标志物占主导地位。在症状出现后的第8至14天,当适应性体液免疫反应首次可检测时,各组之间的红细胞指标存在差异,且每个患者仅贡献一个值时,平均红细胞血红蛋白浓度仍保持显著差异。抗刺突蛋白IgM水平在后来发展为PASC的个体中似乎更高,但差异并不具有统计学意义。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,症状出现后第8至14天可能是识别发展为PASC的个体与未发展为PASC的个体之间急性期实验室参数和早期体液免疫反应差异的关键窗口,强调了早期抗体反应的时间和质量的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可能有助于开发更具针对性的监测和PASC诊断策略,强调在临床评估中考虑时间依赖性免疫标志物的必要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于PASC病例数量较少,研究结果的预测有效性受到限制,且回顾性研究设计可能引入偏倚。然而,由于参数分析的全面性和方法的清晰性,证据强度中等。

title: Retrospective and Bibliometric Assessment of SARS-CoV-2 Viral Culture (2020–2025): Navigating Five Years of Technological Shifts, Translational Research and Viral Immune Evasion
abstract: Since 2020, SARS-CoV-2 viral culture has been a pivotal experimental tool for elucidating viral biology and supporting translational research. This study provides a five-year (2020–2025) retrospective and bibliometric mapping of 4405 unique publications retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed. Quantitative science mapping was integrated with a qualitative retrospective assessment of the ten most cited articles to identify influential biological and technological landmarks. The bibliometric results show a publication peak in 2021, with the United States and China as leading contributors. Thematic evolution shifted from foundational viral isolation to variant-specific investigations (Delta and Omicron) and therapeutic development. Retrospective analysis highlights a significant technological transition from standard cell lines to engineered models, including 3D organoids and deep mutational scanning approaches for the characterization of immune escape and viral fitness. Importantly, manual verification identified author name ambiguity as a major methodological limitation distorting productivity metrics. Overall, viral culture remains a critical bridge for validating phenotypic traits and establishing infectivity windows, providing a data-driven framework for future pandemic preparedness.

abstract_zh: 自2020年以来,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2病毒培养已成为阐明病毒生物学并支持转化研究的关键实验工具。本研究对2020–2025年间从Scopus、Web of Science和PubMed中检索到的4405篇独特文献进行了回顾与文献计量学分析。定量科学映射与对十篇被引次数最高的文献的定性回顾评估相结合,以识别有影响力的生物学和技术里程碑。文献计量学结果表明,2021年出现出版高峰,美国和中国是主要贡献国。主题上的进化从基础病毒分离转向针对特定变异株(Delta和Omicron)的研究以及治疗药物的开发。回顾分析强调了从标准细胞系向工程化模型的技术转变,包括3D类器官和深度突变扫描方法,用于表征免疫逃逸和病毒适应性。重要的是,手动验证发现作者姓名模糊是影响生产力指标的主要方法学局限,可能扭曲结果的解释。总体而言,病毒培养仍然是验证表型特征和确定感染窗口期的关键桥梁,为未来大流行病的防控提供了数据驱动的框架。

title: Anxiety levels among college students following the sudden transition of prevention and control strategies against COVID-19
abstract: The mental health of college students is a constant concern. After China implemented an open strategy for addressing coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in December 2022, college campuses became among the main locations for the rapid spread of the epidemic, which resulted in a serious impact on the mental health of college students. From December 2022 to January 2023, a cross-sectional survey was conducted to evaluate the mental health status of college students in Southwest China in a timely manner and to analyze the influencing factors after the sudden change in prevention and control strategies against COVID-19. The Results revealed that the prevalences of anxiety and event-related psychological distress were 16.08% and 29.14%, respectively. Moderate and severe psychological impacts were reported by 29.1% of the participants. Moderate and moderate to severe psychological anxiety were reported by 10.6% and 3.8% of the participants, respectively. College students who were in poor health, such as those who were suffering from chronic diseases (OR = 0.42, 95% CI = 0.249 ~ 0.705) and who had incomplete vaccinations (OR = 2.45, 95% CI = 1.381 ~ 4.362), were more likely to have anxiety. College students who were older (OR = 2.22, 95% CI = 1.014 ~ 4.873), who received incomplete vaccinations (OR = 1.68, 95% CI = 1.009 ~ 2.803), and who had low knowledge level of COVID-19 (OR = 1.46, 95% CI = 1.028 ~ 2.072) were more likely to experience event-related psychological distress. The prolonged COVID-19 epidemic and sudden alterations in prevention and control strategies caused a substantial negative influence on the mental health of college students in China. This study provides insights for the formulation of corresponding psychological intervention measures that could improve the mental health of college students following a sudden change in prevention and control strategies against far-reaching emerging infectious diseases.

After China implemented an open strategy for addressing coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in December 2022, college campuses became among the main locations for the rapid spread of the epidemic, which resulted in a serious impact on the mental health of college students. From December 2022 to January 2023, a cross-sectional survey was conducted to evaluate the mental health status of college students in Southwest China in a timely manner and to analyze the influencing factors after the sudden change in prevention and control strategies against COVID-19. The Results revealed that the prevalences of anxiety and event-related psychological distress were 16.08% and 29.14%, respectively. Moderate and severe psychological impacts were reported by 29.1% of the participants. Moderate and moderate to severe psychological anxiety were reported by 10.6% and 3.8% of the participants, respectively. College students who were in poor health, such as those who were suffering from chronic diseases (OR = 0.42, 95% CI = 0.249 ~ 0.705) and who had incomplete vaccinations (OR = 2.45, 95% CI = 1.381 ~ 4.362), were more likely to have anxiety. College students who were older (OR = 2.22, 95% CI = 1.014 ~ 4.873), who received incomplete vaccinations (OR = 1.68, 95% CI = 1.009 ~ 2.803), and who had low knowledge level of COVID-19 (OR = 1.46, 95% CI = 1.028 ~ 2.072) were more likely to experience event-related psychological distress. The prolonged COVID-19 epidemic and sudden alterations in prevention and control strategies caused a substantial negative influence on the mental health of college students in China. This study provides insights for the formulation of corresponding psychological intervention measures that could improve the mental health of college students following a sudden change in prevention and control strategies against far-reaching emerging infectious diseases.

title: Persistent left ventricular systolic dysfunction at ≥6 months after SARS-CoV-2–associated MIS-C: a systematic review and rare-event meta-analysis
abstract: Background Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) associated with SARS-CoV-2 frequently involves acute myocardial dysfunction. However, the prevalence of persistent left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction at longer-term follow-up remains uncertain. We therefore performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate the prevalence of persistent LV systolic dysfunction at ≥6 months after MIS-C. Methods We included observational cohort studies reporting longitudinal echocardiographic follow-up in children and adolescents aged <21 years with SARS-CoV-2–associated MIS-C. The prespecified primary outcome was persistent LV systolic dysfunction, defined as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) < 55% at ≥6 months. Study-level events and denominators were extracted and harmonized using the number of children who underwent ≥6-month echocardiography as the endpoint-specific denominator. Pooled prevalence was estimated using an intercept-only binomial logistic-normal generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) fitted directly to study-level event counts and denominators without continuity correction. The originally prespecified random-effects logit model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung–Knapp–Sidik–Jonkman confidence intervals, together with alternative continuity corrections and transformation-based approaches, was retained as sensitivity analysis under sparse-event conditions. Results Ten cohorts met the inclusion criteria and contributed to quantitative synthesis, comprising 432 children with echocardiography at ≥6 months. Persistent LV systolic dysfunction occurred in 3 children, corresponding to a crude observed proportion of 0.69% (3/432). In the revised primary continuity-correction-free binomial logistic-normal GLMM, the pooled prevalence was 0.69% (95% CI, 0.22%–2.13%). Given that only three events were observed, this model-based estimate should not be interpreted as a precise estimate of the underlying population prevalence. Continuity-corrected sensitivity models yielded pooled estimates from 1.62% to 2.23%, further demonstrating numerical sensitivity to the treatment of zero-event cohorts. Conclusion Persistent LV systolic dysfunction was infrequently observed among children with MIS-C reassessed by echocardiography at ≥6 months. However, only three events were identified, so the available evidence is insufficient to determine the exact population prevalence with precision. Inference is further limited by heterogeneous follow-up and potential selection bias from nonuniform late imaging. Larger prospective cohorts with standardized long-term surveillance are needed.

title: Neutralization and protective effectiveness of three XBB vaccines in older adults 12 months after booster
abstract: COVID-19 vaccination is a key determinant for optimizing booster strategies in older adults, who remain at high risk for severe outcomes because of immunosenescence and waning immunity. We previously reported neutralizing responses in a prospective cohort of 90 older adults ( ≥ 65 years) at 6 months after boosting with trivalent (Tri-XBB.1.5), bivalent (Bi-Omi-XBB), or tetravalent (Tetra-XBB.1) protein vaccines. 1 In this extended follow-up to 12 months post-vaccination of the same cohort, we assessed neutralizing antibody persistence, decay kinetics, and protective effectiveness against SARS-CoV-2 infection. Detailed methods are provided in the Supplementary Materials.Allparticipants, regardless of infection status after booster vaccination, maintained detectable neutralizing antibodies across the three vaccine cohorts at 12 months post-booster (Fig. 1a, b), with comparable geometric mean titers (GMTs, all p > 0.05). In the Tri-XBB.1.5 cohort (Fig. 1a), the GMTs on day 357 ranged from 313.1 (XEC) to 3,583.0 (BA.5). Compared with day 185, signi fi cant declines were observed for all the variants except D614G, with GMT reductions of 1.7-fold for BA.5, 1.3-fold for XBB.1.5, 1.6-fold for JN.1, 1.2-fold for KP.3, and 1.9-fold for XEC. In the Bi-Omi-XBB cohort (Fig. 1a), the GMTs on day 357 ranged from 452.6 to 2047.0; signi fi cant declines were observed for BA.5 (3.2-fold), XBB.1.5 (2.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the persistence and protective effectiveness of three XBB vaccines in older adults 12 months after booster vaccination, as older adults remain at high risk for severe outcomes due to immunosenescence and waning immunity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study is an extended follow-up of a prospective cohort of 90 older adults (≥ 65 years) who received booster vaccinations with trivalent (Tri-XBB.1.5), bivalent (Bi-Omi-XBB), or tetravalent (Tetra-XBB.1) protein vaccines.
analysis.methods: Neutralizing antibody levels were measured using a standardized assay, and protective effectiveness was assessed by comparing infection rates across the three vaccine cohorts over the 12-month period post-booster.
analysis.main_results: At 12 months post-booster, all participants maintained detectable neutralizing antibodies across the three vaccine cohorts, with comparable geometric mean titers (GMTs, all p > 0.05). Significant declines were observed for all variants except D614G, with GMT reductions of 1.7-fold for BA.5, 1.3-fold for XBB.1.5, 1.6-fold for JN.1, 1.2-fold for KP.3, and 1.9-fold for XEC.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating sustained neutralizing antibody levels across all vaccine cohorts, highlighting the potential for long-term protection against SARS-CoV-2 infection in older adults.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide important insights into the long-term effectiveness of XBB vaccines in older adults, informing booster strategies and vaccine development for sustained immunity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to an abstract-only analysis, and the evidence is based on a single cohort, which may affect generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of detailed statistical analysis and follow-up data.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the persistence and protective effectiveness of three XBB vaccines in older adults 12 months after booster vaccination. The research is motivated by the high risk of severe outcomes in this population due to immunosenescence and waning immunity. The study follows a cohort of 90 older adults who received trivalent, bivalent, or tetravalent protein vaccines. Neutralizing antibody levels were measured using an assay, and protective effectiveness was assessed by comparing infection rates across the vaccine groups. Results show that all participants maintained detectable neutralizing antibodies, with comparable geometric mean titers (GMTs) across the cohorts. However, significant declines were observed for most variants, except D614G. The authors suggest that these findings indicate sustained protection against SARS-CoV-2 infection in older adults. The study has moderate evidence strength due to its abstract-only nature and reliance on a single cohort, which may limit generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估三种XBB 疫苗在加强接种12个月后对老年人的持续性和保护效果,因为老年人由于免疫衰老和免疫力下降仍面临严重后果的高风险。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是对一项前瞻性队列研究的扩展随访,该队列研究包括90名老年人(≥65岁),他们接受了三价(Tri-XBB.1.5)、二价(Bi-Omi-XBB)或四价(Tetra-XBB.1)蛋白疫苗的加强接种。
elements_zh.methods: 通过标准化检测方法测量中和抗体水平,并通过比较接种后12个月内三种疫苗 队列研究的感染率来评估保护效果。
elements_zh.main_results: 在加强接种12个月后,所有参与者均保持对三种疫苗 队列研究的可检测中和抗体,几何平均滴度(GMTs,所有p > 0.05)相当。所有变体(除D614G外)均观察到显著下降,其中BA.5的GMT下降了1.7倍,XBB.1.5下降了1.3倍,JN.1下降了1.6倍,KP.3下降了1.2倍,XEC下降了1.9倍。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为所有疫苗 队列研究中和抗体水平的持续性,强调了在老年人中对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染提供长期保护的潜力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为了解XBB 疫苗在老年人中的长期有效性提供了重要见解,有助于制定加强接种策略和疫苗开发,以维持长期免疫力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于摘要分析,证据基于单一队列研究,这可能影响其普遍性。由于缺乏详细的统计分析和随访数据,证据强度中等。

title: Avascular necrosis of the femur following COVID-19: an updated systematic review
abstract: BACKGROUND: One of the complications of COVID-19 infection is avascular necrosis of the femoral head. To date, various studies have reported a wide range of osteonecrosis of the femoral head in patients with COVID-19. The previous systematic review included only 14 studies. So, this systematic review aims to update the findings of these studies. METHODS: Databases such as PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were systematically searched by two independent researchers on April 1st, 2024. RESULTS: A literature search revealed 1229 records, 161 full-texts were evaluated, and finally, 55 studies remained for systematic review. Fifty-five studies were included in this systematic review. Four studies were cross-sectional studies, six were retrospective studies, and the remaining (45studies) were case reports or case-series studies. Totally, 864 cases were included. Except for 12 studies, 43 studies reported the administration of steroid therapy in included cases. The most common underlying conditions were hypertension, followed by diabetes. In 274 (31.7%) of included cases, AVN was bilateral, and both hips were involved. In some studies, non-surgical treatments-including supplement therapy, anticoagulant therapy, physiotherapy, and hyperbaric oxygen therapy-were administered. Several studies reported symptomatic improvement in patients treated with the core decompression approach. Total hip arthroplasty (THA) was the most commonly used surgical treatment. CONCLUSIONS: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head in cases that have survived COVID-19 should be considered carefully as early diagnosis helps to preserve the joint and its function.
journal: Archives of Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery

title: Bloodstream Isolation of Klebsiella Pneumoniae in Adults Hospitalized with SARS-CoV-2 During the Omicron BA.5 Wave: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background and Objectives: Secondary bloodstream infection in patients hospitalized with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can lengthen admission and increase antimicrobial exposure, yet pathogen-specific evidence from the Omicron period is scarce. We examined how often Klebsiella pneumoniae was recovered from blood among adults admitted with SARS-CoV-2 (severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2) infection during the Omicron BA.5 wave, and which clinical features and outcomes accompanied it. Materials and Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort comprised 395 adults admitted in Timișoara, Romania, from 12 July to 25 September 2022. pneumoniae in blood culture were compared with all remaining patients, whether their cultures showed no growth or another pathogen. Groups were compared with the Mann–Whitney U and Fisher’s exact tests. The association between K. pneumoniae and a hospital stay of at least 14 days was estimated with Firth penalized logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, and admission oxygen saturation. Results: Blood cultures grew K. pneumoniae in 16 patients (4.1%), another pathogen in 73 (18.5%), and nothing in 306 (77.5%). Median length of stay was 17.5 days (IQR (interquartile range) 9.8–25.2) with K. pneumoniae and 9.0 days (IQR 7.0–16.0) in the rest of the cohort (p = 0.006); a stay of at least 14 days occurred in 56.3% versus 28.0% (unadjusted OR 3.31, p = 0.022). The association persisted after adjustment (Firth adjusted OR 3.18, 95% CI 1.14–8.87; p = 0.027; maximum-likelihood estimate 3.25, 95% CI 1.16–9.12; p = 0.025). In-hospital death occurred in 1 of 16 exposed patients (6.3%) and in 61 of 379 others (16.1%; Fisher’s exact p = 0.485); with a single exposed death, the age- and sex-adjusted Firth estimate was imprecise (adjusted OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.04–2.21). pneumoniae bloodstream isolation was infrequent in this Omicron BA.5 cohort but was accompanied by a markedly longer hospital stay. Causality and an effect on mortality cannot be inferred: culture dates, place of acquisition, device exposure, and isolate susceptibility were not available, the untimed exposure is prone to immortal-time bias, and no non-COVID-19 comparator was studied. Prospective surveillance combining time-stamped microbiology with resistance phenotyping is needed.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study investigated the frequency of Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream isolation among adults hospitalized with SARS-CoV-2 during the Omicron BA.5 wave in Romania. The study found that K. pneumoniae was isolated in 4.1% of patients, with a significantly longer hospital stay compared to those without bloodstream infection. The association between K. pneumoniae and prolonged hospitalization remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, and admission oxygen saturation. However, causality and mortality effects could not be inferred due to the lack of detailed microbiology data and the absence of a non-COVID-19 comparator. The study underscores the need for prospective surveillance to better understand the clinical impact of K. pneumoniae in SARS-CoV-2 patients. The evidence is moderate due to the observational design and missing data.

title_zh: Bloodstream Isolation of Klebsiella Pneumoniae in Adults Hospitalized with SARS-CoV-2 During the Omicron BA.5 Wave: A Retrospective Cohort Study
source_body_en: Background and Objectives: Secondary bloodstream infection in patients hospitalized with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can lengthen admission and increase antimicrobial exposure, yet pathogen-specific evidence from the Omicron period is scarce. We examined how often Klebsiella pneumoniae was recovered from blood among adults admitted with SARS-CoV-2 (severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2) infection during the Omicron BA.5 wave, and which clinical features and outcomes accompanied it. Materials and Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort comprised 395 adults admitted in Timișoara, Romania, from 12 July to 25 September 2022. pneumoniae in blood culture were compared with all remaining patients, whether their cultures showed no growth or another pathogen. Groups were compared with the Mann–Whitney U and Fisher’s exact tests. The association between K. pneumoniae and a hospital stay of at least 14 days was estimated with Firth penalized logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, and admission oxygen saturation. Results: Blood cultures grew K. pneumoniae in 16 patients (4.1%), another pathogen in 73 (18.5%), and nothing in 306 (77.5%). Median length of stay was 17.5 days (IQR (interquartile range) 9.8–25.2) with K. pneumoniae and 9.0 days (IQR 7.0–16.0) in the rest of the cohort (p = 0.006); a stay of at least 14 days occurred in 56.3% versus 28.0% (unadjusted OR 3.31, p = 0.022). The association persisted after adjustment (Firth adjusted OR 3.18, 95% CI 1.14–8.87; p = 0.027; maximum-likelihood estimate 3.25, 95% CI 1.16–9.12; p = 0.025). In-hospital death occurred in 1 of 16 exposed patients (6.3%) and in 61 of 379 others (16.1%; Fisher’s exact p = 0.485); with a single exposed death, the age- and sex-adjusted Firth estimate was imprecise (adjusted OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.04–2.21). pneumoniae bloodstream isolation was infrequent in this Omicron BA.5 cohort but was accompanied by a markedly longer hospital stay. Causality and an effect on mortality cannot be inferred: culture dates, place of acquisition, device exposure, and isolate susceptibility were not available, the untimed exposure is prone to immortal-time bias, and no non-COVID-19 comparator was studied. Prospective surveillance combining time-stamped microbiology with resistance phenotyping is needed.

title: Letter to the Editor: Coronavirus disease 2019, multisystem inflammatory syndrome, and children’s hearts: Finding answers with cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
abstract: The article refers to “Persistent long-term subclinical myocardial changes in multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children revealed by cardiac magnetic resonance and galectin-3” by OV et al published in the World Journal of Clinical Pediatrics , multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) associated with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and its cardiovascular complications. MIS-C frequently causes cardiovascular complications, including coronary artery dilatation, low left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction, diastolic dysfunction, myocarditis, and pericardial effusion, decreases over time, usually resolving within 6-9 months after the disease onset. Echocardiographic evaluations reveal mild to moderate LV dysfunction, resolving within two weeks. Severe dysfunction normalizes after approximately 1.5 months. Global longitudinal strain proves valuable for detecting subclinical myocardial damage. Long-term effects based on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) data indicate the persistent myocardial edema and/or fibrosisupto12 months after the initialevent. Signs of interstitial fibrosis were found in 7.7% of patients during a one-year follow-up period. CMRI is an important additional method in the assessment of children who have experienced multisystem inflammatory syndrome in COVID-19, especially in patients with persistent symptoms or abnormal data from other cardiac findings.
