analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the cardiovascular complications of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) associated with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and its long-term effects on cardiac health.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on children who had experienced MIS-C linked to COVID-19, examining their cardiovascular complications and long-term cardiac outcomes through follow-up assessments.
analysis.methods: Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) and galectin-3 measurements were used to assess myocardial changes, while echocardiographic evaluations were conducted to monitor left ventricular (LV) function.
analysis.main_results: Persistent myocardial edema and/or fibrosis were observed in some patients up to 12 months after the initial event, and signs of interstitial fibrosis were found in 7.7% of patients during a one-year follow-up period.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the potential for long-term cardiac damage in children with MIS-C, emphasizing the importance of CMRI in detecting subclinical myocardial changes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results suggest that CMRI should be considered for assessing long-term cardiac effects in children with MIS-C, particularly those with persistent symptoms or abnormal findings from other cardiac tests.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational nature and potential for bias, but the evidence is supported by CMRI data and follow-up assessments, providing moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the cardiovascular complications of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) associated with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and its long-term effects on cardiac health. Using cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) and galectin-3 measurements, the research reveals persistent myocardial edema and fibrosis in some patients up to 12 months post-onset, with interstitial fibrosis observed in 7.7% during a one-year follow-up. The findings suggest that CMRI is valuable for detecting subclinical myocardial damage in children with MIS-C, especially those with ongoing symptoms or abnormal cardiac findings. However, the study's observational design and potential for bias limit the confidence in its conclusions, though the evidence is supported by CMRI data and follow-up assessments, offering moderate confidence in the results.

elements_zh.methods: 使用心脏磁共振成像(CMRI)和半乳糖凝集素-3测量来评估心肌变化,同时通过超声心动图评估来监测左心室(LV)功能。
elements_zh.main_results: 一些患者在初始事件后12个月内仍观察到持续的心肌水肿和/或纤维化,一年随访期间,7.7%的患者出现了间质性纤维化的迹象。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果突显了多系统炎症综合征在儿童中可能存在的长期心脏损伤风险,强调了心脏磁共振成像(CMRI)在检测亚临床心肌变化中的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果表明,对于患有MIS-C且有持续症状或其它心脏检查异常发现的儿童,应考虑使用CMRI评估长期心脏效应。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其观察性质和潜在的偏倚,但研究结果得到了心脏磁共振成像数据和随访评估的支持,为研究发现提供了中等程度的可信度。

title: A Pilot Surveillance Program to Identify Emerging SARS-CoV-2 Variants in International Travelers Arriving at a Major International Airport: Prospective Cohort Evaluation
abstract: Background: Testing arriving international travelers for COVID-19 paired with whole-genome sequencing (WGS) may identify new introductions of SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern in California, enabling a timely public health response. Traveler genomic surveillance may be a way to improve gaps in worldwide disease genomic surveillance. Objective: This paper aimed to describe a pilot surveillance program to identify SARS-CoV-2 variants in arriving international travelers at San Francisco International Airport (SFO). Methods: The California Department of Public Health implemented a pilot program at SFO to voluntarily test arriving international travelers for COVID-19 from June 2021 to November 2021 to identify SARS-CoV-2 variants. Arriving international travelers were offered self-collect COVID-19 antigen tests upon arrival at SFO. Travelers with positive COVID-19 antigen tests or with COVID-19 symptoms were recommended to self-collect and mail an additional specimen for diagnostic molecular testing. WGS of SARS-CoV-2 was performed on RNA extracts from positive tests to identify variants. Results: In total, 2.1% (19,008/892,558) of all arriving international travelers at SFO from 133 different countries of departure enrolled in the program. The COVID-19 test positivity among this group was 0.7% (33/5038), and the weekly test positivity range, 0% to 1.5%, was lower than the weekly test positivity across the state of California during the same time frame. Arriving international travelers departing from Turkey (3/145, 2.1%), Mexico (7/602, 1.2%), and the United Kingdom (6/626, 1.0%) had the highest test positivity. Of the 14 positive molecular tests, 10 (71.4%) were sequenced, and all were found to belong to the SARS-CoV-2 Delta B.1.617.2 lineage, the most prevalent SARS-CoV-2 variant in California and worldwide at the time. Conclusions: Voluntary testing of arriving international travelers paired with WGS was operationally and logistically feasible. Although the number of sequenced positive COVID-19 specimens in this program was limited, the lessons learned from this pilot informed improvements to subsequent iterations of traveler viral genomic surveillance in California and highlighted the potential value of traveler viral genomic surveillance to support early identification and characterization of emerging infectious diseases entering a region.

title_zh: A Pilot Surveillance Program to Identify Emerging SARS-CoV-2 Variants in International Travelers Arriving at a Major International Airport: Prospective Cohort Evaluation
source_body_en: Background: Testing arriving international travelers for COVID-19 paired with whole-genome sequencing (WGS) may identify new introductions of SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern in California, enabling a timely public health response. Traveler genomic surveillance may be a way to improve gaps in worldwide disease genomic surveillance. Objective: This paper aimed to describe a pilot surveillance program to identify SARS-CoV-2 variants in arriving international travelers at San Francisco International Airport (SFO). Methods: The California Department of Public Health implemented a pilot program at SFO to voluntarily test arriving international travelers for COVID-19 from June 2021 to November 2021 to identify SARS-CoV-2 variants. Arriving international travelers were offered self-collect COVID-19 antigen tests upon arrival at SFO. Travelers with positive COVID-19 antigen tests or with COVID-19 symptoms were recommended to self-collect and mail an additional specimen for diagnostic molecular testing. WGS of SARS-CoV-2 was performed on RNA extracts from positive tests to identify variants. Results: In total, 2.1% (19,008/892,558) of all arriving international travelers at SFO from 133 different countries of departure enrolled in the program. The COVID-19 test positivity among this group was 0.7% (33/5038), and the weekly test positivity range, 0% to 1.5%, was lower than the weekly test positivity across the state of California during the same time frame. Arriving international travelers departing from Turkey (3/145, 2.1%), Mexico (7/602, 1.2%), and the United Kingdom (6/626, 1.0%) had the highest test positivity. Of the 14 positive molecular tests, 10 (71.4%) were sequenced, and all were found to belong to the SARS-CoV-2 Delta B.1.617.2 lineage, the most prevalent SARS-CoV-2 variant in California and worldwide at the time. Conclusions: Voluntary testing of arriving international travelers paired with WGS was operationally and logistically feasible. Although the number of sequenced positive COVID-19 specimens in this program was limited, the lessons learned from this pilot informed improvements to subsequent iterations of traveler viral genomic surveillance in California and highlighted the potential value of traveler viral genomic surveillance to support early identification and characterization of emerging infectious diseases entering a region.

title: Cryptic spread of SARS-CoV-2 undermined targeted travel restrictions
abstract: Abstract The effectiveness of travel restrictions in mitigating the spread of novel viral variants remains understudied, particularly in regions with sparse genomic surveillance. We evaluated the efficacy of these restrictions in Western Asia, where countries sequenced less than one percent of SARS-CoV-2 cases in 2021, focusing on Iraq’s travel ban on India and the tourist travel restriction. We generated 535 SARS-CoV-2 whole-genome sequences from clinical samples collected in Duhok, Iraq, between June 2021 and March 2022, encompassing the Delta and Omicron variant waves. Using discrete Bayesian phylogeographic modeling, we reconstructed spatiotemporal viral spread patterns to determine whether travel restrictions delayed the introduction of the variants into the country, postponed community transmission onset, or altered the geographic sources of viral introductions over time. We found that the Delta variant was introduced into Iraq three months before the targeted travel ban was enacted, predominantly from Western and Southern Asia, whereas the Omicron variant was introduced despite the tourist travel restriction already being in place. We also show that both variants had established community transmission within the country despite travel restrictions, rendering these measures ineffective. Analysis of travel restrictions on a global scale reveals similar patterns of limited efficacy in mitigating the introductions of novel SARS-CoV-2 variants, challenging the usefulness of such measures.

title_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2隐秘传播削弱了针对性旅行限制的有效性
source_body_en: Abstract The effectiveness of travel restrictions in mitigating the spread of novel viral variants remains understudied, particularly in regions with sparse genomic surveillance. We evaluated the efficacy of these restrictions in Western Asia, where countries sequenced less than one percent of SARS-CoV-2 cases in 2021, focusing on Iraq’s travel ban on India and the tourist travel restriction. We generated 535 SARS-CoV-2 whole-genome sequences from clinical samples collected in Duhok, Iraq, between June 2021 and March 2022, encompassing the Delta and Omicron variant waves. Using discrete Bayesian phylogeographic modeling, we reconstructed spatiotemporal viral spread patterns to determine whether travel restrictions delayed the introduction of the variants into the country, postponed community transmission onset, or altered the geographic sources of viral introductions over time. We found that the Delta variant was introduced into Iraq three months before the targeted travel ban was enacted, predominantly from Western and Southern Asia, whereas the Omicron variant was introduced despite the tourist travel restriction already being in place. We also show that both variants had established community transmission within the country despite travel restrictions, rendering these measures ineffective. Analysis of travel restrictions on a global scale reveals similar patterns of limited efficacy in mitigating the introductions of novel SARS-CoV-2 variants, challenging the usefulness of such measures.
abstract_zh: 摘要 旅行限制在遏制新型病毒变异株传播方面的有效性尚未得到充分研究,尤其是在基因组监测病例稀少的地区。我们评估了这些限制在西亚的影响,其中2021年各国对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2病例的基因组测序率低于1%,重点关注伊拉克对印度实施的旅行禁令和旅游旅行限制。我们从2021年6月至2022年3月在伊拉克杜胡克收集的临床样本中生成了535个严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2全基因组序列,涵盖了Delta和Omicron变异株的传播浪潮。利用离散贝叶斯系统发育地理建模,我们重建了病毒的时空传播模式,以确定旅行限制是否延迟了变异株进入该国,推迟了社区传播的开始,或是否改变了病毒引入的地理来源随时间的变化。我们发现,Delta变异株在旅行禁令实施前三个月已进入伊拉克,主要来自西亚和南亚,而Omicron变异株则在旅游旅行限制已实施的情况下仍被引入。我们还表明,尽管有旅行限制,这两种变异株已在该国建立了社区传播,使这些措施无效。对全球旅行限制的分析显示,这些措施在遏制新型严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株引入方面的效果有限,挑战了此类措施的实用性。

title: P-462: Increased incidence of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) during COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Abstract Introduction The COVID-19 pandemic led to strict measures and healthcare shifts, delaying diagnosis of conditions like type 1 diabetes (T1D). In children, this increased DKA at diagnosis, often more severe, likely due to reduced access to care and fear of infection during the pandemic. Objectives To compare the severity and frequency of DKA in new-onset type 1 diabetes mellitus patients and in patients with previous diagnosis of T1D in a referral Pediatric hospital during and before the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods This retrospective cohort study reviewed medical records of children with DKA at a referral Pediatric hospital between April/2018 and December/2019 (pre-pandemic period) and between April/2020 and December/2021 (pandemic period). We analyzed demographics, clinical features, hospital stay, and laboratory data, excluding incomplete records. The means, percentages, and variability were calculated, and the chi-squared test and Fisher’s exact test were applied accordingly. Results We analyzed 55 patients with 74 DKA admissions, comparing pre-pandemic (Group 1) and pandemic (Group 2) periods. The Gender distribution shifted toward females. Age and diagnosis patterns showed trends but no significant differences. Table 1 shows the characteristics of Group 1 and 2. Conclusions Our study found a 39% rise in patients and 85% in admissions, There were a marked increase in DKA cases during the pandemic period, consistent with international data, but without differences in severity, though with a trend toward more ventilation and dialysis. Most cases were moderate to severe, reflecting delayed diagnosis.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study aimed to compare the severity and frequency of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) in new-onset type 1 diabetes mellitus patients and in patients with previous diagnosis of T1D in a referral Pediatric hospital during and before the COVID-19 pandemic. The focus was on SARS-CoV-2 and its impact on DKA incidence and severity in children with T1D.

The means, percentages, and variability were calculated, and the chi-squared test and Fisher’s exact test were applied accordingly.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found a 39% rise in patients and 85% increase in DKA admissions during the pandemic period compared to the pre-pandemic period. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study did not report significant differences in severity, though there was a trend toward more ventilation and dialysis. The evidence does not provide detailed information on the mechanisms behind the increased incidence or the long-term implications of delayed diagnosis.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest the need for improved surveillance and early diagnosis of type 1 diabetes in children during pandemics. The implications highlight the importance of maintaining access to healthcare services and monitoring for delayed diagnoses of T1D, which can lead to more severe DKA cases.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the incidence and severity of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) in children with type 1 diabetes (T1D). It compares data from pre-pandemic (April 2018–December 2019) and pandemic (April 2020–December 2021) periods at a referral Pediatric hospital. The results show a 39% increase in patients and 85% rise in DKA admissions during the pandemic, with a trend toward more ventilation and dialysis. However, no significant differences in severity were observed. The study underscores the need for improved surveillance and early diagnosis of T1D in children during public health crises, as delayed diagnosis may contribute to more severe DKA cases.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本研究为回顾性分析,审查了2018年4月至2019年12月(疫情前)和2020年4月至2021年12月(疫情期间)期间在一家转诊儿科医院就诊的儿童DKA病例的医疗记录。分析包括人口学特征、临床表现、住院时间和实验室数据,排除不完整的记录。计算了均值、百分比和变异情况,并相应应用了卡方检验和费舍尔精确检验。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 本研究发现,疫情期间患者数量增加了39%,DKA入院数量增加了85%。DKA病例数量显著增加,与国际数据一致,但未观察到严重程度的差异,尽管有向更多需要通气和透析的趋势。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 本研究未报告严重程度的显著差异,尽管有向更多需要通气和透析的趋势。年龄和诊断模式显示出趋势,但无显著差异。证据未提供关于DKA病例增加机制或诊断延迟长期影响的详细信息。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果表明,在疫情期间需要改善对儿童类型1糖尿病的诊断和早期干预。这些发现强调了保持医疗服务可及性以及监测类型1糖尿病延迟诊断的重要性,因为这可能导致更严重的DKA病例。

title: Dysfunctional neutrophil response in COVID-19 infection varies by subtype.
abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 virus significantly evolved, with several new strains being identified. Transmissibility has increased with each strain, corresponding with a decrease in mortality. We previously demonstrated novel dysfunctional neutrophil responses in patients with the Alpha variant of COVID-19 compared with control patients with community-acquired pneumonia. We investigated if strain variation altered neutrophil dysfunction we had previously observed. Patients with COVID-19 not requiring intensive care were recruited between January 2021 and May 2022 from the Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham; 41 patients had the Alpha variant, 32 had the Delta variant, and 14 had the Omicron variant. Neutrophils isolated from whole blood were investigated for phagocytosis of labelled Streptococcus pneumoniae, Transwell migration toward IL-8, neutrophil extracellular (NET) formation, and surface phenotype. Neutrophil phagocytosis was significantly increased in the Delta variant (vs Alpha, P = 0.0012; vs Omicron P = 0.0209). Transwell migration was also significantly reduced in patients with the Omicron variant (vs Alpha P = 0.0002; vs Delta, P = 0.0129). There was a significant reduction in NET formation from patients with Omicron (vs Alpha, P = 0.0031; vs Delta, P = 0.0231). Compared with patients with Alpha, neutrophils from those with Omicron had reduced expression of CD10 (P = 0.0004), CD54 (P = 0.0015), CD62L (P = 0.0013), and CD11c (P < 0.0001). CXCR2 expression was higher in neutrophils from patients with the Omicron variant compared with those with Alpha (P = 0.0001). Neutrophil function and phenotype differ among the variants of COVID-19 infection in hospitalized patients. Neutrophil changes suggest more accurate migration in patients with the Omicron variant, leading to decreased neutrophil host-mediated tissue damage. This may contribute to the overall milder clinical Omicron phenotype. Ongoing research and review of therapies remain important as the virus evolves.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether strain variation of SARS-CoV-2 altered neutrophil dysfunction previously observed in patients with the Alpha variant. The research focused on patients with non-intensive care COVID-19 infections recruited from the Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham between 2021 and 2022. Neutrophil function was assessed through phagocytosis, migration, NET formation, and surface phenotype. Results showed increased phagocytosis in Delta variant patients, reduced migration in Omicron variant patients, decreased NET formation in Omicron patients, and altered surface marker expression. The findings suggest that neutrophil changes in Omicron may lead to reduced host-mediated tissue damage, potentially explaining its milder clinical phenotype. The study provides insights into variant-specific immune responses but does not address its limitations.

title: Long COVID prevalence among U.S. adults: A state-level ecological analysis of associations with SARS-CoV-2 incidence, COVID-19 hospitalization rates, COVID-19 vaccine coverage, and multimorbidity
abstract: BACKGROUND: Long COVID has emerged as a major public health concern in the United States, yet geographic variation in its prevalence remains poorly understood. This study examines how state-level differences in COVID-19 vaccination, SARS-CoV-2 infection burden, severity of acute COVID-19 (measured by hospitalization rates) and multimorbidity burden relate to adult Long COVID prevalence in the United States. METHODS: We conducted an ecological analysis using data from the 2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), from which we estimated state-level prevalence of self-reported Long COVID among adults. These estimates were linked with publicly available data on SARS-CoV-2 incidence, COVID-19 hospitalizations, COVID-19 vaccine coverage, and a multimorbidity indicator (defined as ≥3 chronic conditions associated with increased risk of severe COVID-19, e.g., diabetes, obesity, chronic kidney disease). Multivariable linear regression models were used to assess the association between these factors and Long COVID prevalence, adjusting for state age and sex distributions. Rubin's rules were applied to propagate the uncertainty in the estimates of Long COVID and COVID-19 vaccine coverage through regression analyses. RESULTS: All examined factors-including SARS-CoV-2 incidence, COVID-19 hospitalization, COVID-19 vaccine coverage, and multimorbidity prevalence-varied by state. In univariable analyses, vaccine coverage and multimorbidity prevalence were significantly associated with Long COVID prevalence. In the multivariable model, vaccine coverage and SARS-CoV-2 incidence were significant; however, after accounting for uncertainty in Long COVID and vaccine coverage estimates, only higher vaccine coverage remained significantly associated with lower Long COVID prevalence. CONCLUSIONS: Higher State-level variation in COVID-19 vaccine coverage was consistently associated with lower adult Long COVID prevalence. These ecological findings support further investigation of vaccination and other state-level determinants of Long COVID burden and may inform population-level strategies for addressing Long COVID.

Rubin’s rules were applied to propagate the uncertainty in the estimates of Long COVID and COVID-19 vaccine coverage through regression analyses. Results All examined factors—including SARS-CoV-2 incidence, COVID-19 hospitalization, COVID-19 vaccine coverage, and multimorbidity prevalence—varied by state. In univariable analyses, vaccine coverage and multimorbidity prevalence were significantly associated with Long COVID prevalence. In the multivariable model, vaccine coverage and SARS-CoV-2 incidence were significant; however, after accounting for uncertainty in Long COVID and vaccine coverage estimates, only higher vaccine coverage remained significantly associated with lower Long COVID prevalence. Conclusions Higher State-level variation in COVID-19 vaccine coverage was consistently associated with lower adult Long COVID prevalence. These ecological findings support further investigation of vaccination and other state-level determinants of Long COVID burden and may inform population-level strategies for addressing Long COVID.

title: Randomised controlled phase I trial of a SARS-CoV-2 monoclonal antibody.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: SARS-CoV-2 infection remains a threat to vulnerable groups. Neutralising monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) have shown efficacy in the treatment and prevention of COVID-19, but most mAbs have lost activity against recent Omicron strains. METHODS: We previously isolated a receptor binding domain-specific mAb from a COVID-19 convalescent donor, PDI204, which retained activity against several early Omicron strains. This randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase I clinical trial enrolled healthy adults (n = 32) to receive PDI204 intravenously (IV) at three different doses (200, 600, 1200 mg) or intramuscularly (IM) at 300 mg. RESULTS: PDI204 was safe and tolerable with only Grade 1 and 2 adverse events. High serum levels of PDI204 were detected in PDI204-dosed participants with a median elimination half-life of 17.7 days (IQR 16.3-22.1). Boosted neutralising activity and Fc receptor binding were observed in serum against ancestral and Omicron BA.5 SARS-CoV-2 strains, but not against the later Omicron strain XBB.1.5. IM-dosed subjects had peak PDI204 levels in serum 2-6 days later than IV-dosed subjects. Entry of PDI204 into saliva from blood was low and variable, and primarily detected in participants receiving 600 mg or 1200 mg doses. Three of 32 people acquired COVID-19 within 90 days of dosing, two receiving PDI204 and one in a placebo recipient. CONCLUSION: Overall, the mAb PDI204 was safe but lost activity against later Omicron strains and did not prevent COVID-19 during this trial.

title: Identification of small-molecule inhibitors of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD–ACE2 interaction by structure- and affinity-based screening
abstract: The receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein mediates viral entry through its interaction with angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), making it an attractive target for antiviral intervention. However, the broad and relatively shallow ACE2-binding interface presents a challenge for small-molecule inhibitor discovery. In this study, we explored conserved regions outside the ACE2-binding interface as potential druggable sites for small-molecule inhibitors targeting the SARS-CoV-2 RBD. Structure-based virtual screening was performed using the structure of the SARS-CoV-1 RBD as a structural surrogate, and selected compounds were evaluated using a newly established affinity-based assay on diazirine-modified amorphous carbon plates. Evaluation of 175 virtual hits identified eight RBD-binding compounds. Among them, only RABI-1 inhibited RBD-ACE2 interaction in a Calu-3 cell-based binding assay without affecting ACE2 expression or cell viability. Evaluation of structural analogs of RABI-1 led to the identification of RABI-3, which showed stronger inhibitory activity compared with RABI-1. In addition, RABI-3 inhibited the interaction between ACE2 and RBDs derived from multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants in an AlphaLISA immunoassay and suppressed pseudovirus infection in Calu-3 cells. These findings support the feasibility of targeting regions of the RBD outside the ACE2-binding interface as a strategy for identifying small-molecule inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 entry.

title: Duration and determinants of SARS-CoV-2 RNA positivity in hospitalized patients in Guinea: a prospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background This study aimed to determine the duration of SARS-CoV-2 RNA positivity and identify factors associated with delayed RNA clearance among hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Conakry, Guinea. Methods We conducted a prospective cohort study of patients with RT-qPCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection hospitalized in Conakry between January 2021 and January 2022. Patients were followed longitudinally until documented RNA clearance or censoring due to early outcome or loss to follow-up. Whole-genome sequencing was performed on eligible positive samples using the COVID-19Seq protocol, followed by mutation analysis with Nextclade. Factors associated with RNA clearance were assessed using multivariable generalized Gamma parametric survival regression within an accelerated failure time framework, with time ratios (Exp[β]) and two-sided P values < 0.05. Results Among 330 patients (median age, 39 years; IQR, 27–58; 56.7% male), 311 (94.2%) were followed to complete RNA clearance, whereas 19 (5.8%), primarily older ICU patients, had incomplete follow-up. Clinical presentations were mild (33.3%), moderate (30.6%), or asymptomatic (28.2%). Median RNA positivity duration was 9.0 days (IQR, 8.0–12.0; range, 3–91). Older age (≥ 60 years; Exp[β] = 1.16, P = 0.003), unemployment/farming/manual labor (Exp[β] = 1.14, P = 0.012), and ICU admission (Exp[β] = 1.32, P = 0.007) were independently associated with prolonged RNA positivity. Mild disease was associated with faster clearance than asymptomatic infection (Exp[β] = 0.83, P = 0.001). Among 14 sequenced samples, Omicron (35.7%), Alpha (28.6%), Eta (7.1%), and other lineages were identified. Conclusion Older age, occupational characteristics, and ICU admission were associated with prolonged SARS-CoV-2 RNA positivity, whereas mild disease was associated with faster RNA clearance. These findings support risk-stratified monitoring of hospitalized COVID-19 patients in resource-limited settings.

title: Investigating the impact of the Covid-19 epidemic on mortality and fertility indicators in Qom province and comparing it with national indicators from 2019 to 2023
abstract: Objective (s): Communicable and non-communicable diseases are always associated with many impacts on fertility rates, mortality, and disease burden. The present study aimed to investigate the impact of COVID-19 on fertility and mortality indicators. Methods: The present study was a mixed-method study that was conducted in two phases: a descriptive cross-sectional study and a review study. In the descriptive phase, statistical data were reviewed during 3 time periods before the COVID epidemic (March 2017 to March 2020), during the epidemic (March 2020 to March 2021), and after the epidemic (March 2021 to March 2023) for 24 months. In the second phase, a review study was conducted on the impact of the COVID-19 epidemic on mortality and fertility indicators, as well as maternal-fetal outcomes in Iran over the past years, which was searched through the electronic databases PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Persian Database (SID) for articles up to 2023. The source of the study of outcomes and complications related to the mother and newborn was obtained through a review study. Data analysis was performed using descriptive statistics in SPSS software and expressed using numbers, percentages, and graphs. Results: The general fertility rate in the pre-epidemic period was estimated at about 3.5%, which decreased to 1.3% during and after the epidemic . The stillbirth rate in the pre-epidemic period was reported to be approximately 4.6%, which decreased to 3.8% in the post-epidemic period. The crude birth rate in the pre-epidemic and post-epidemic periods was also 1.4% and 1.05%, respectively. In terms of maternal outcomes during and after the COVID-19 epidemic , most pregnant mothers faced the risk of cesarean section, premature birth, and prolonged hospital stay. In terms of neonatal outcomes, fetal heart rate abnormalities, hospitalization in the neonatal intensive care unit, and the need for resuscitation in the first minute were the most reported outcomes. Vaccination coverage decreased during and after the epidemic . Conclusion: The study findings showed that fertility and crude birth rates have decreased during and after the epidemic . Also, during the Covid-19 period, maternal and fetal complications such as respiratory complications, preterm labor, premature rupture of membranes, preeclampsia, coagulation disorders, and cardiopulmonary disorders of pregnant mothers and newborns increased. Therefore, awareness raising to prevent any type of infection during pregnancy that can affect the occurrence of pathological consequences in the mother and newborn, as well as improving and continuing prenatal care, seems necessary.

title: Time to sustained control of the effective reproduction number as a failure-time estimand: a county-level analysis of the first SARS-CoV-2 wave in the United States.
abstract: Subnational analyses of emerging pathogen transmission typically model the reproduction number (Rt) as a continuous outcome and estimate average associations with its level. Operationally, however, response planning depends on a different quantity: which jurisdictions bring transmission below the epidemic threshold (Rt<1), and how quickly. We formulate time to control as a failure-time estimand and show that doing so exposes a structural feature that linear regression does not accommodate: a jurisdiction cannot enter the risk set until enough cases accumulate to estimate Rt. Cases accumulate faster where transmission is faster, so entry time depends on the outcome process itself and on factors that drive early spread. We account for this outcome-dependent observability using a mixed-effects Cox proportional hazards model with calendar-time left truncation and state-level Gaussian frailties, applied to 2,956 US counties observed between January 22 and July 15, 2020. The primary event was defined as the first three-day sustained reduction of mean Rt below one. Control was rare (171 counties, 5.8%). Each standard-deviation increase in log population density was associated with a lower rate of control (hazard ratio 0.54; 95% confidence interval 0.44 - 0.67) and higher policy stringency with a faster rate (HR 1.50; CI 1.09 - 2.05). Evaluating jurisdictions by their rate of reaching an operational target - rather than by average transmission level - provides a clearer, decision-relevant metric for prospective allocation decisions and public health interventions. Keywords: SARS-CoV-2, COVID-19, reproduction number, survival analysis, Cox model, county-level, United States, policy stringency, population density.

title: Catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome after COVID-19 mRNA vaccination: A case report
abstract: ObjectiveAntiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a common acquired thromboinflammatory disease and catastrophic APS (CAPS) its most rare and lethal variant. The objective of this report is to describe a case of probable CAPS triggered after vaccination with an mRNA vaccine in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic.MethodsThis is a descriptive case report conducted at a Brazilian university hospital, involving a single 40-year-old patient admitted with dysarthria, gross hematuria, signs of pulmonary embolism, and a large intracavitary cardiac thrombus. He had a history of multiple past venous thrombotic events, but investigations for malignancy had consistently yielded negative results. Approximately 48 hours earlier, he had received the second dose of the Pfizer® mRNA vaccine (Pfizer-BioNTech BNT162b2).After infections and concomitant autoimmune diseases were ruled out, thrombocytopenia and positive serologic testing for APS raised the possibility of CAPS, and treatment was promptly initiated with anticoagulation, corticosteroids, low-dose aspirin, and hydroxychloroquine. Main outcome measures were organ involvement, laboratory abnormalities, imaging findings, and clinical response to treatment.ResultsAfter therapeutic measures were instituted, the patient showed laboratory improvement - restoration of renal function and increased platelet count - as well as clinical improvement, with resolution of neurological deficits. Follow-up testing revealed persistent triple positivity for APS-related serologies.ConclusionsThis emblematic report brings a rare complication of APS in association with immunization using an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, presenting clinical features that resemble those described in other CAPS cases documented in the CAPS Registry. Additional reports of immune-mediated diseases induced by vaccine platforms have also been described, suggesting pathophysiological mechanisms that remain incompletely understood, particularly molecular mimicry. Immunization against COVID-19 and other pathogens should not, however, be discouraged, as vaccines continue to play a fundamental role in preventing potentially severe infectious diseases. Instead, scientific research should be encouraged in order to better understand which individuals are more predisposed to such a severe complication.

title: VaccineScout: A Computational Framework for Guiding the Composition and Valency of SARS-CoV-2 Vaccine Updates
abstract: The continual evolution of SARS-CoV-2 necessitates periodic vaccine updates to maintain immunity against newly emerging variants. However, vaccine design remains largely guided by experimental serological studies, and there is no publicly available computational framework to help systematically prioritize vaccine variants and guide valency selection. Here, we analyze over 14 million SARS-CoV-2 genomes collected globally between 2021 and 2025 and find that over half of spike amino acid sequences (primary vaccine target) observed during the first six months after vaccine selection were already circulating at the time of selection, compared with only 5-10% of sequences during the subsequent six months. These findings provide quantitative support for annual COVID-19 vaccine updates. We further show that circulating variant prevalence and open-source variant fitness predictors can both effectively rank circulating variants by their future prevalence. Motivated by these findings, we developed VaccineScout, a computational framework that recommends vaccine candidates by minimizing the average spike amino acid substitution distances to the forecasted prevalence of circulating variants. VaccineScout also helps determine vaccine valency by quantifying diminishing returns as additional variants are introduced. Retrospective analyses showed that VaccineScout-recommended candidates either matched U.S. Food and Drug Administration recommendations or had lower average spike sequence distances to future variants and higher fitness. In addition, their spike distances to future variants were comparable to an oracle selection informed by future prevalence, indicating near-optimal performance by this metric. Together, VaccineScout introduces an in silico framework for systematically prioritizing SARS-CoV-2 vaccine candidates for costly downstream experimental validation.

title: Keep the peace? The early politics of Covid-19 and the limits of partisan influence on public opinion
abstract: Crises often call for swift and far-reaching government action that depends on broad public acceptance to be effective. While political disagreement is commonly seen as undermining support, its actual impact on public attitudes remains contested. This study examines public opinion during the COVID-19 pandemic in Germany – a context that shifted from early cross-party unity to later politicization. Combining original media data on partisan messaging and panel survey data from 2020, we assess how the emergence of partisan criticism shaped public acceptance of pandemic response policies. Although increasing partisan politicization was associated with declining public acceptance of pandemic measures, we find no evidence that this relationship was driven by partisan cue-taking. Instead, citizens adjusted their party preferences rather than their policy views in response to disagreement with their preferred party. These findings highlight the limits of partisan persuasion, and the growing importance of citizens’ own evaluations as elite consensus erodes.

title: Evaluation of dentists' fear, anxiety, and work-life balance during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Aim: This study aimed to determine the fear and anxiety levels and work-life balance of postgraduate dental residents during the COVID-19 pandemic and to examine the relationships among these variables. Methodology: This descriptive, cross-sectional study used a correlational design. The study included 188 of 348 postgraduate dental residents (54%) at five public universities in Ankara, Türkiye, who completed an online survey. Data were collected using the COVID-19 Fear Scale, the COVID-19 Anxiety Scale, and the Work-Life Balance Scale. Data were analyzed using the Mann–Whitney U, Kruskal–Wallis H, one-way ANOVA, and Spearman correlation tests. Results: The mean scores were 16.41 ± 5.21 for fear, 6.37 ± 2.33 for anxiety, and 37.26 ± 10.19 for work-life balance. Fear and anxiety levels were higher among female and younger dentists and among those who considered COVID-19 a serious disease. Fear levels were also higher among pedodontists, those who had received COVID-19 training, and those who found the work environment inadequate for disease prevention. Work-life balance levels were significantly lower among those who found the precautions insufficient and were weakly correlated with COVID-19 knowledge (r = 0.180) and the perception of COVID-19 as a serious disease (r = 0.164). No relationship was found between work-life balance and COVID-19-related fear and anxiety. Conclusion: Fear and anxiety among postgraduate dental residents during the COVID-19 pandemic were associated with sex, age, specialty, training, and perceived workplace adequacy, but not with work-life balance. Creating working conditions that reduce fear and anxiety and support work-life balance is therefore important. The results can be used to develop policies regulating the working conditions of dentists in the post-COVID period.

source_records.abstract: Aim: This study aimed to determine the fear and anxiety levels and work-life balance of postgraduate dental residents during the COVID-19 pandemic and to examine the relationships among these variables. Methodology: This descriptive, cross-sectional study used a correlational design. The study included 188 of 348 postgraduate dental residents (54%) at five public universities in Ankara, Türkiye, who completed an online survey. Data were collected using the COVID-19 Fear Scale, the COVID-19 Anxiety Scale, and the Work-Life Balance Scale. Data were analyzed using the Mann–Whitney U, Kruskal–Wallis H, one-way ANOVA, and Spearman correlation tests. Results: The mean scores were 16.41 ± 5.21 for fear, 6.37 ± 2.33 for anxiety, and 37.26 ± 10.19 for work-life balance. Fear and anxiety levels were higher among female and younger dentists and among those who considered COVID-19 a serious disease. Fear levels were also higher among pedodontists, those who had received COVID-19 training, and those who found the work environment inadequate for disease prevention. Work-life balance levels were significantly lower among those who found the precautions insufficient and were weakly correlated with COVID-19 knowledge (r = 0.180) and the perception of COVID-19 as a serious disease (r = 0.164). No relationship was found between work-life balance and COVID-19-related fear and anxiety. Conclusion: Fear and anxiety among postgraduate dental residents during the COVID-19 pandemic were associated with sex, age, specialty, training, and perceived workplace adequacy, but not with work-life balance. Creating working conditions that reduce fear and anxiety and support work-life balance is therefore important. The results can be used to develop policies regulating the working conditions of dentists in the post-COVID period.

title: The Activation of NF-κB by the SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein and Its Role in Epigenetic Age Acceleration, Inflammaging, and, Finally, Senescence
abstract: Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) occurs when an individual's DNA methylation-predicted biological age is older than their actual chronological age. EAA is associated with neurological disease, amongst many other diseases. A series of studies, indexed in Medline, identify that COVID-19 and long COVID are both associated with EAA. Pathogenesis occurs primarily via the spike protein (SP). Through Toll Like Receptor 2 (TRL2) and MyD88-mediated response, SP activates nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB), to initiate pro-inflammatory responses and promote inflammation. SARS-CoV-2 infection causes methylation and demethylation profile alterations in DNA and telomere attrition, which associates with COVID-19 severity. Post COVID-19 syndrome (Long COVID) is also associated with EAA and telomere attrition. Alterations of the methylome during EAA contribute to cellular senescence, which is linked to autoimmunity, and, furthermore, to cancer. In this paper, we investigate the role of NF-κB activation in EAA. We identify that nucleosome alterations can occur not only with COVID-19 and Long COVID but also following administration of the SARS-Cov-2 mRNA vaccines. We analyse in depth the mechanisms that implicate NF-κB to cause these alterations. We identify the critical role of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), which regulate NF-κB activation through scaffolds, decoys, and feedback loops, in modulating type I interferon expression, premature aging, inflammaging and senescence. We discuss the consequences of these processes on the overall health of the human population. The mRNAs in the COVID-19 vaccine and the transcribed spike protein persist in time, promoting chronic activation of NF-κB and other pathogenic pathways.

title: Mass spectrometric profiling of plasma and erythrocyte glycerophospholipids and oxylipins in patients hospitalized with coronavirus disease 2019
abstract: Abstract Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is associated with systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, and altered lipid metabolism; however, paired characterization of plasma and erythrocyte lipid profiles remains limited. This exploratory case–control study evaluated an LC–linear ion-trap tandem mass spectrometry (LC–IT-MS/MS) workflow for profiling selected glycerophospholipids and oxidized fatty-acid mediators in paired plasma and erythrocyte samples from 30 hospitalized patients with moderate-to-severe COVID-19 and 30 healthy controls. Samples were subjected to nitrogen-protected biphasic chloroform–methanol extraction, and lipid species were characterized using chromatographic retention behavior, multistage fragmentation, and spectral-library comparison. Quantification was performed using class-representative calibration and class-matched internal standards, while group differences were evaluated using univariate analysis, effect-size estimation, false-discovery-rate adjustment, and exploratory principal component analysis. The method showed acceptable analytical performance, with linearity over 1–100 ng/mL (r 2 = 0.9951–0.9992), limits of quantification of 0.70–1.00 ng/mL, intra-day precision of 3.8–12.5%, and recoveries of 86.4–108.7%. COVID-19 was associated with compartment-specific lipid alterations, including decreased plasma lysophosphatidylcholines and plasmenyl-phosphatidylethanolamines; LPC 20:5 and LPC 20:3 decreased by approximately fourfold, while the combined abundance of six plasmenyl-phosphatidylethanolamine species decreased by 52.7%. In erythrocytes, PE 18:1/22:6 increased 1.5-fold (126.2 versus 82.5 μg/mL), whereas total lysophosphatidylethanolamines and phosphatidylinositols decreased 4.3-fold and 2.5-fold, respectively. Erythrocyte 9-HpOTrE, 5-HETE, and 13-HOTrE increased by 3.9, 3.6, and 2.0-fold, respectively, and exploratory principal component analysis showed separation between COVID-19 and control samples. Paired plasma–erythrocyte LC–IT-MS/MS profiling therefore identified group-associated, compartment-specific changes in glycerophospholipids and oxidized lipid mediators consistent with altered membrane-lipid remodeling and oxidative lipid metabolism in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. These associations require confirmation by untargeted quantitative LC–MS/MS using authentic standards and validation in independent, clinically characterized cohorts before considering biomarker, stratification, or monitoring applications.

title: Risk of Shoulder Injury Related to Vaccine Administration for COVID-19 and Influenza Vaccinations
abstract: Importance: The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine identified a critical evidence gap regarding the risk of shoulder injury related to vaccine administration (SIRVA) after COVID-19 vaccination. Objective: To compare the risk of SIRVA after COVID-19 vs influenza vaccinations in adults. Design, Setting, and Participants: This population-based cohort study included individuals aged at least 18 years who received a COVID-19 or influenza vaccination administered via intramuscular deltoid injection between August 1, 2023, and April 30, 2024, at Kaiser Permanente Southern California. Data were analyzed from June 2024 to September 2026. Exposure: Receipt of COVID-19 vaccination or influenza vaccination. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary outcome was incident SIRVA, defined as shoulder symptoms beginning at or before 7 days and persisting more than 30 days after vaccination, identified using a validated natural language processing algorithm. Incidences were calculated per 10 000 vaccinations. Adjusted relative risks (RRs), risk differences, and 95% CIs were estimated using robust Poisson regression with inverse probability of treatment weighting. Results: A total of 1 366 362 individuals (mean [SD] age at vaccination, 58.4 [18.2] years; 782 994 female [57.3%]) across 1 901 588 vaccinations were included (1 076 609 vaccinations [56.7%] were administered to females). Among 1 830 636 vaccinations in the primary analysis, 252 SIRVA cases were identified as follows: 110 cases (0.018%) after 596 614 COVID-19 vaccinations and 142 cases (0.012%) after 1 234 022 influenza vaccinations. An additional 13 SIRVA cases (0.018%) were identified among 70 952 simultaneous COVID-19 and influenza vaccinations. Most COVID-19 vaccines were Pfizer-BioNTech messenger RNA (667 455 of 667 566 [99.98%]), and influenza vaccines were predominantly standard-dose (866 530 of 1 304 974 [66.40%]) or high-dose (438 183 of 1 304 974 [33.58%]) inactivated quadrivalent formulations. SIRVA incidence was higher after COVID-19 than influenza vaccination, at an incidence of 1.84 (95% CI, 1.53-2.22) vs 1.15 (95% CI, 0.98-1.36) per 10 000 vaccinations, corresponding to an adjusted absolute increase of 0.67 cases (95% CI, 0.15-1.19) per 10 000 vaccinations (adjusted RR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.16-2.28). Among adults 65 years or older, SIRVA incidence was 2.11 (95% CI, 1.67-2.67) per 10 000 for COVID-19 vaccination and 1.63 (95% CI, 1.28-2.07) per 10 000 for high-dose influenza vaccination (adjusted RR, 1.41; 95% CI, 0.92-2.15). Conclusions and Relevance: Results of this cohort study suggest that although SIRVA was rarely associated with both vaccines, COVID-19 vaccination was associated with approximately 7 additional cases per 100 000 vaccinations compared with influenza vaccination. Among adults aged 65 years or older, SIRVA risk did not differ significantly between COVID-19 and high-dose influenza vaccination. The small absolute risk of SIRVA should be considered alongside the established benefits of COVID-19 and influenza vaccination in preventing severe disease and hospitalization.

title: PABbind: A Hierarchical Geometric Framework for Mutation-Involved Antigen−Antibody Interaction Prediction and SARS-CoV-2 Immune Escape Assessment
abstract: Abstract Antibody therapies exhibit remarkable specificity and therapeutic potential, yet their efficacy can be compromised by rapidly emerging antigen mutations that enable immune escape. Therefore, predicting how antigen variants alter antibody recognition is critical for assessing antibody durability, but experimental evaluation of large-scale mutation combinations remains challenging. Here, we develop PABbind, a hierarchical geometric deep-learning model that integrates sequence and structural information to predict antigen−antibody interaction changes using wild-type protein−protein interaction (PPI) structures and mutant sequences. By simultaneously incorporating sequence and structural information and leveraging pretraining on general mutant PPI datasets, PABbind accurately predicts immune escape effects of antigen variants against antibodies using wild-type PPI structures only, enabling large-scale screening of antigen mutations. PABbind demonstrates favorable performance on mutant PPI benchmarks and enables prediction of variant-specific immune escape scores for SARS-CoV-2 antibodies, therefore providing an effective computational framework for large-scale assessment of SARS-CoV-2 antigen variants.

title: Timing of Long COVID Improvement in Prospectively Followed RECOVER-Adult Participants.
abstract: BACKGROUND Long COVID (LC) is widespread; however, limited information has been reported on the likelihood that symptoms remit over time. OBJECTIVE To evaluate the likelihood of improvement among persons with likely LC. DESIGN Prospective, multisite cohort study (RECOVER-Adult [Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery]). SETTING 83 U.S.-based sites across 33 states; Washington, DC; and Puerto Rico. PARTICIPANTS 1019 persons in RECOVER-Adult with likely LC (LC Research Index [LCRI] ≥11) 12 months after first SARS-CoV-2 infection. MEASUREMENTS The primary outcome was time until 2 consecutive study visits with LCRI less than 11. Secondary outcomes were time until LCRI measure reduced 50% or more and quality of life was good or better, and LCRI decreased to 0. Unadjusted estimates of cumulative incidence and adjusted marginal cumulative incidence by age, sex, SARS-CoV-2 wave, and LC subtype were reported across all follow-up time points. RESULTS An estimated 36.2% (95% CI, 33.0% to 39.5%) met the primary outcome by 24 months after infection, and 50.1% (CI, 46.1% to 54.0%) met the primary outcome by 36 months. An estimated 56.4% (CI, 52.2% to 60.4%) and 26.9% (CI, 23.3% to 30.5%), respectively, met the 2 secondary outcomes by 36 months. Among persons who still reported likely LC at 18 months and 24 months after first infection, relative timing of subsequent symptom improvement was similar. LIMITATION Findings in this observational cohort are interpretable in a population with prevalent likely LC and do not address causal relationships between individual characteristics and symptom improvement. CONCLUSION Among persons with likely LC 12 months after initial SARS-CoV-2 infection, one half experience meaningful reductions in symptoms by 36 months, whereas a quarter experience complete remission of symptoms. These findings underscore both the potential for natural recovery and the urgent need for placebo-controlled therapeutic intervention trials. PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE National Institutes of Health.

title: Honeybee (Apis mellifera) venom and its bioactive peptides tertiapin and apamin modulate the proteome of SARS-CoV-2-infected cells
abstract: The continuing emergence of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) variants highlights the need for host-directed antiviral strategies with specific molecular mechanisms. Honeybee (Apis mellifera) venom (HBV) contains bioactive peptides with immunomodulatory and membrane-active properties, yet their effects on SARS-CoV-2 infection remain insufficiently characterized. Here, we investigated the antiviral activity and proteomic impact of whole HBV and two venom-derived peptides, apamin (APA) and tertiapin (TERT), in human angiotensin-converting enzyme 2-expressing HEK293 cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 spike-pseudotyped lentiviral particles. Cell viability and membrane integrity assays showed that HBV, APA, and TERT exerted limited cytotoxicity at the tested concentrations. In pseudovirus infectivity assays, HBV displayed the strongest inhibitory effect, reducing viral infectivity to 61.3% at 2 μg/mL, whereas APA reduced it to 73.3% at 0.5 μg/mL, and TERT showed weaker inhibitory activity. Comparative nano-liquid chromatography matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization tandem mass spectrometry revealed treatment-associated remodelling of the host-cell proteome. A shared signature of 215 proteins across HBV-, APA-, and TERT-treated infected cells was enriched in binding and catalytic activity, translational proteins, metabolite interconversion enzymes, cytoskeletal proteins, and pathways linked to integrin, Wnt, interferon, and Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription signalling. Protein-protein interaction analysis highlighted functional clusters associated with cytoplasmic translation, viral mRNA translation, and the Sec61 translocon complex, with EFTUD2, EPRS1, and HSPA4 emerging as central hubs. HBV treatment additionally promoted immune-related and interferon-stimulated gene products, including factors involved in innate antiviral defence, cytoskeletal organization, ion transport, and membrane structural reinforcement. These findings suggest that HBV reduces SARS-CoV-2 pseudovirus infectivity through a multifactorial host-directed mechanism involving antiviral signalling, cellular architecture, and proteostasis, supporting further investigation of bee venom-derived compounds as antiviral agents.

title: Health Resource Allocation in Jiangxi Province Before and After the COVID-19 Pandemic (2015–2024): An Entropy-Weighted TOPSIS and Rank-Sum Ratio Assessment
abstract: Abstract Background The equitable allocation of health resources is a fundamental determinant of population health outcomes. To examine how a major public health emergency reshapes the regional distribution of health resources, this study evaluated health resource allocation in Jiangxi Province before and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods Per-1,000-population health resource data for 11 prefecture-level cities in Jiangxi Province from 2015 to 2024 were used. Entropy-weighted TOPSIS and the rank-sum ratio (RSR) method were applied for a comprehensive evaluation. The study period was divided into a pre-pandemic window (2015–2019) and a post-pandemic window (2020–2024) to compare resource allocation before and after the outbreak. Results Both methods indicated that the overall level of health resource allocation in Jiangxi improved markedly after the pandemic. Provincial per-1,000-population beds, practicing (assistant) physicians, registered nurses, and health-care expenditure rose by 38.6%, 40.9%, 44.9%, and 40.8%, respectively, while inter-city dispersion (coefficient of variation) was roughly halved. The entropy weight of health-care expenditure surged from 6.9% to 23.3% (a 16.4-percentage-point increase). Nanchang and Pingxiang consistently ranked in the top two in both periods; Fuzhou and Yichun improved markedly, whereas Yingtan and Ganzhou declined. Conclusions The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the expansion and equalization of health resources in Jiangxi, with fiscal input emerging as a new principal dimension of disparity. Sustained, equity-oriented fiscal redistribution is needed to consolidate gains in less-developed regions.

title: Long-term outcomes of COVID-19-related versus non-COVID-19-related post-intubation tracheal stenosis: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Post-intubation tracheal stenosis (PITS) is a clinically challenging condition requiring multidisciplinary bronchoscopic and surgical management. Its incidence increased markedly in recent years, particularly following the rise in patients requiring prolonged invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) during the pandemic period. Whether the underlying etiology influences stenosis characteristics, treatment strategies, and long-term outcomes remains insufficiently understood. Methods This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 111 patients who developed PITS following IMV between March 2020 and November 2021 and were followed for a minimum of three years. Patients were categorized by etiology: COVID-19-related ( n = 54) and non-COVID-19 ( n = 57). Demographic characteristics, stenosis features (type, grade, length, and location), bronchoscopic and surgical treatment modalities, and long-term clinical outcomes were compared between groups. Results Baseline characteristics were largely similar between groups, except for a higher prevalence of multiple comorbidities in the non-COVID group (57.9% vs. Intubation duration was significantly longer in the post-COVID group (21 vs. 15 days, p = 0.005). Stenosis characteristics and treatment modalities did not differ significantly between groups. At 3-year follow-up, bronchoscopic success rates (58.6% vs. 62.2%), surgical success rates (73.3% vs. 81.8%), restenosis rates (20.0% vs. 13.6%), tracheostomy dependence (9.2% vs. 5.3%), and mortality (14.8% vs. 17.5%) were all comparable between groups ( p > 0.05). Conclusion When post-COVID and non-COVID PITS patients are compared, findings suggest that etiology may not significantly influence the long-term clinical outcomes of PITS. These findings support an individualized approach to treatment based on anatomical and clinical factors, regardless of etiology. Larger prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm these results. Clinical trial registration Not applicable.

title: Working conditions and nurses' mental health in Latin America and the Caribbean during the COVID-19 pandemic: a multinational cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background The COVID-19 pandemic placed unprecedented pressure on health systems across Latin America and the Caribbean. Although studies have documented adverse working conditions and psychological distress among healthcare workers, evidence focused specifically on nursing personnel has largely been derived from single-country studies, limiting understanding of regional patterns. Analyses spanning multiple countries remain limited. This study aimed to describe the working conditions and mental health symptoms reported by nursing staff in work and home environments during the COVID-19 pandemic across Latin America and the Caribbean. Methods A cross-sectional, multinational study was conducted among nursing professionals in 20 Latin American countries between July 2022 and April 2025. Self-report measures assessed working conditions, institutional support, training, occupational recognition, emotional symptoms at work and at home, and burnout. Descriptive analyses and Pearson’s chi-square tests were performed. Cramér’s V (Vc) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) was used to estimate the magnitude and precision of associations between emotional symptoms reported at work and at home. Results A total of 6,986 nurses participated. Overall, 16.2% had temporary contracts. 21.3% held multiple jobs, and more than half reported that their income was insufficient to avoid poverty (51.8%) or to cover household needs (52.9%). Another 41.8% had a COVID-19 infection, although only 37.2% were recognized as having an occupational illness, and 14.3% received additional benefits. Job reassignment occurred in 30.7% of cases, and 9.3% were laid off. Statistically significant associations were observed between emotional symptoms reported at work and at home (χ2, p < 0.001). The largest associations were observed for irritability (Vc = 0.566, 95% CI 0.550–0.582), depression (Vc = 0.562, 95% CI 0.547–0.577), difficulty concentrating (Vc = 0.548, 95% CI 0.532–0.564), and fatigue (Vc = 0.512, 95% CI 0.492–0.531). Conclusions Nursing staff in Latin America experienced adverse working conditions during the pandemic, characterized by contractual instability, insufficient wages, limited institutional recognition, and high exposure to biological risk. Emotional symptoms showed moderate to large associations across work and home settings, highlighting the need for policies that strengthen workforce protection, occupational recognition, and mental health support.

title: Lexical salience and inference boundaries in Kompas.com COVID-19 reporting during 2021
abstract: Abstract Lexical prominence in a news archive does not by itself establish moral panic. This study reassesses the documented analytical record of an earlier corpus analysis of Kompas.com COVID-19 reporting during 2021. It distinguishes reproducible arithmetic from reported lexical measurements and unverified descriptions of software outputs. The accessible empirical materials are the manuscript's tables, narrative and four embedded figures; the raw and cleaned news records, processing scripts and eight separately cited Voyant exports were not available in the revision materials. Monthly entries sum to 22,531 headline records and 649 article records, compared with stated totals of 22,491 and 740. These sums verify internal discrepancies rather than the underlying corpus size. Three embedded count labels rank COVID at 3,160, cases at 1,298 and health at 805, but their counting unit remains unresolved. The documented associations foreground pandemic, prevention and institutional vocabulary without establishing hostility, disproportionate concern or audience anxiety. Descriptions of segmented or non-chronologically ordered Voyant displays cannot support calendar trends, and the underlying displays require recovery before independent inspection. Unresolved selection rules, translation procedures, denominators and co-occurrence settings prevent reproduction of the central corpus findings. The contribution is a case-specific account of evidence requirements connecting lexical description, contextual moral attribution and social consequences, rather than an empirically validated model of moral panic. Record reconciliation and recovery of the original analytical materials remain necessary before corpus-level claims can be verified.

title: Incidence and risk factors of acute respiratory illness associated with influenza, COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus within a birth cohort study
abstract: ABSTRACT Influenza virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are leading causes of acute respiratory infections (ARIs). New Zealand’s coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) public health measures disrupted the circulation of these viruses in 2020–2021, creating a rare opportunity to explore the impact of potential immunity gaps on age-specific infection risk. We analyzed data from 843 participants aged between 0 and 4 years enrolled in the Southern Hemisphere Influenza and Vaccine Effectiveness Research and Surveillance 3 (SHIVERS-III) birth cohort, a longitudinal community-based study in New Zealand, during 2020–2024. During the respiratory season, weekly surveillance captured ARI symptoms and severity. Nasal swabs were collected from symptomatic participants and tested for viral RNA by RT-PCR. Incidence rates (IRs) and incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were estimated for the surveillance period and adjusted for age, sex, ethnic group, socioeconomic status, and influenza vaccination status. No influenza or SARS-CoV-2 infections were detected in 2020 and 2021. From 2021 to 2024, RSV had the highest IR during the surveillance period (63.2/100 person-years [PY]; 95% CI, 56.6–69.8), followed by SARS-CoV-2 (39.3/100 PY; 95% CI, 34.5–44) and influenza (35.7/100 PY; 95% CI, 29–42.3). Age influenced infection risk: infants <6 months had the lowest incidence of influenza and RSV, potentially reflecting maternally derived immunity and limited exposure. Risk increased after 6 months of age, peaking at age 1 year for RSV and at age 2 years for influenza. Influenza vaccination lowered symptomatic influenza risk (IRR 0.66; 95% CI, 0.44–1.00). In the New Zealand community setting in the post-COVID-19 era, individual respiratory virus illness patterns differ in children aged 0–4. Influenza vaccine shows protection, and age influences virus-specific risk. IMPORTANCE Influenza virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are major causes of acute respiratory illness in early childhood, yet current understanding is largely reliant on hospital-based surveillance that underestimates the broader community burden. This study addresses this limitation by providing comprehensive, community-based estimates of incidence, severity, and symptom profiles across these viruses within a single longitudinal birth cohort. By leveraging the unique epidemiological context created by pandemic-related disruptions, it offers important insights into how changes in exposure influence subsequent infection risk and virus circulation. The direct comparison of three major respiratory viruses within the same population highlights distinct age-related risk patterns and disease characteristics. In addition, our research provides real-world evidence of the reduced risk of influenza-associated acute respiratory illness among vaccinated children. These findings strengthen the evidence base for age-targeted immunization strategies and improve understanding of early-life respiratory virus epidemiology.

title: eLife Assessment: Inhibiting the interaction between the mitochondrial receptor Tom70 and SARS CoV 2 Orf9b with small molecules
abstract: The SARS CoV 2 accessory protein Orf9b is in a complex monomer-dimer equilibrium that influences its interactions with the host mitochondrial receptor Tom70. This interaction is critical for viral suppression of a Type-1 interferon response during infection. Modulating this equilibrium with a small molecule, either by stabilizing the Orf9b homodimer or blocking its interaction with Tom70, represents a promising strategy for restoring interferon signaling and the antiviral response. To build tool molecules that could test this concept, we performed two screens: a crystallographic fragment screen against the Orf9b homodimer and a high-throughput fluorescence polarization screen for competitors of an Orf9b-derived peptide binding to Tom70. Fragment screening revealed two binding sites with potential to be developed into an inhibitor: one located at the peripheral dimer interface and the other just outside the lipid-binding channel that defines the central dimer interface. Functionalization of the fragments outside of the lipid-binding channel with hydrophobic moieties stabilized the Orf9b homodimer thereby indirectly inhibiting association with Tom70. In parallel, the high throughput screen for competitive inhibitors of the Tom70:Orf9b interaction discovered a separate series of molecules. These molecules display dynamic structure activity relationship (SAR) and could be improved in the future to modulate the interaction between Tom70 and potentially a wide range of substrates. Collectively, these results demonstrate the feasibility of two distinct strategies to manipulate the Orf9b-Tom70 equilibrium, which is critical to the host response to SARS CoV 2 infection.

This interaction is critical for viral suppression of a Type-1 interferon response during infection. Modulating this equilibrium with a small molecule, either by stabilizing the Orf9b homodimer or blocking its interaction with Tom70, represents a promising strategy for restoring interferon signaling and the antiviral response. To build tool molecules that could test this concept, we performed two screens: a crystallographic fragment screen against the Orf9b homodimer and a high-throughput fluorescence polarization screen for competitors of an Orf9b-derived peptide binding to Tom70. Fragment screening revealed two binding sites with potential to be developed into an inhibitor: one located at the peripheral dimer interface and the other just outside the lipid-binding channel that defines the central dimer interface. Functionalization of the fragments outside of the lipid-binding channel with hydrophobic moieties stabilized the Orf9b homodimer thereby indirectly inhibiting association with Tom70. In parallel, the high throughput screen for competitive inhibitors of the Tom70:Orf9b interaction discovered a separate series of molecules. These molecules display dynamic structure activity relationship (SAR) and could be improved in the future to modulate the interaction between Tom70 and potentially a wide range of substrates. Collectively, these results demonstrate the feasibility of two distinct strategies to manipulate the Orf9b-Tom70 equilibrium, which is critical to the host response to SARS CoV 2 infection.

title: Risk of retinal vascular occlusion following COVID-19 vaccination: A meta-analysis of nearly 15 million individuals.
abstract: BACKGROUND Retinal vascular occlusion is a rare ocular condition reported following coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination. However, the association between vaccination and retinal vascular occlusion remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the frequency and risk of retinal vascular occlusion following COVID-19 vaccination. METHODS Four electronic databases were systematically searched through August 2026. Observational studies reporting retinal vascular occlusion after COVID-19 vaccination were included. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to estimate pooled event proportions and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Potentially overlapping study populations were assessed, and study quality was evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. RESULTS Five studies comprising 14,877,781 reported participants were included. The pooled proportion of retinal vascular occlusion events among vaccinated individuals was 0.02% (95% CI: 0.00%-0.07%; I2 = 99.5%). The overall association between vaccination and retinal vascular occlusion was not statistically significant (RR = 2.12, 95% CI: 0.65-6.90; P = .213), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 96.8%). However, separate analyses showed statistically significant associations for retinal artery occlusion (RR = 2.03, 95% CI: 1.17-3.51) and retinal vein occlusion (RR = 2.26, 95% CI: 2.08-2.47), without a significant difference between subtypes (P = .696). No significant associations between retinal vascular occlusion and vaccine were observed in sex-specific analyses. Among vaccine types, ChAdOx1/AstraZeneca showed a significant association (RR = 2.00, 95% CI: 1.60-2.50), based on a single study, whereas pooled associations for other vaccines were nonsignificant. CONCLUSION Retinal vascular occlusion events following COVID-19 vaccination were rare. Although the overall association was not statistically significant, separate arterial and venous analyses showed significant associations. Substantial heterogeneity, potential confounding, and differences in contributing studies limit definitive conclusions. Further research is needed to clarify these findings.

title: SARS-CoV-2 exposure in deer increases with use of human-modified habitat
abstract: Abstract Deer can transmit severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) to humans and harbour human-extinct variants. Despite this public health threat, ecological mechanisms driving exposure patterns in deer populations remain poorly understood. Our objective was to identify behavioural risk factors by linking serostatus of individual deer to their movement and space use using multilevel logistic regression. We examined serosurveillance data of white-tailed (Odocoileus virginianus) and mule deer (O. hemionus) wearing global positioning system devices across an urban–rural gradient in the United States (1151 individuals, 20 sites, 8 states). Seropositivity was positively associated with average human footprint index and negatively associated with average SARS-CoV-2 human wastewater concentration. Seropositivity was not associated with time spent in GAP-modelled deer habitat. Together, these findings provide evidence that human-to-deer transmission could be a primary source of deer SARS-CoV-2 exposure and deer populations may struggle to maintain transmission without repeated spillover from humans. Integrating human and environmental indices with movement behaviours and space use can thus clarify pathways that facilitate cross-species transmission in wildlife.

title: Tocilizumab Use and Outcomes in Hospitalized COVID-19 Patients During the Initial Pandemic Peak in Peru: A Real-World Retrospective Study
abstract: Background: Tocilizumab was used as emergency treatment for COVID-19 in Peru during 2020, before randomized clinical trial evidence supporting its use became available. Documenting real-world experiences of its implementation in resource-constrained health systems provides relevant insights for pandemic preparedness. Methods: Retrospective cohort study of 242 patients hospitalized with COVID-19 who received tocilizumab at seven sites in Peru (March–September 2020). Clinical characteristics, tocilizumab use, and adverse events were described (primary objective). A Cox proportional-hazards model was used as a secondary analysis to explore the association between tocilizumab initiation within the first 3 days of hospitalization (days 1–3) vs. later and all-cause mortality. Results: 79.8% (n = 193) patients were male; mean age was 59.0 years (SD: 13.0); 43.0% died. The median cumulative tocilizumab dose was 400 mg (IQR: 400–600 mg), lower than the currently recommended weight-based regimen (8 mg/kg; maximum 800 mg per infusion); 86.4% received a single dose. In the adjusted Cox model, early tocilizumab use was not significantly associated with mortality (HR: 1.09; 95%CI: 0.67–1.75; p = 0.72). The proportional-hazards assumption was met globally. Adverse events of any cause (not assessed for causality) were recorded during hospitalization in 56 (23.1%) patients; the most frequent MedDRA category was respiratory, thoracic, and mediastinal disorders (n = 16). Conclusions: This Peruvian cohort documents how tocilizumab was used, in terms of timing and dose, during the first pandemic wave in a resource-constrained setting. In the absence of an untreated comparator, these data do not allow inferences on the contribution of tocilizumab to mortality, ICU admission, or adverse events.

Methods: Retrospective cohort study of 242 patients hospitalized with COVID-19 who received tocilizumab at seven sites in Peru (March–September 2020). Clinical characteristics, tocilizumab use, and adverse events were described (primary objective). A Cox proportional-hazards model was used as a secondary analysis to explore the association between tocilizumab initiation within the first 3 days of hospitalization (days 1–3) vs. later and all-cause mortality. Results: 79.8% (n = 193) patients were male; mean age was 59.0 years (SD: 13.0); 43.0% died. The median cumulative tocilizumab dose was 400 mg (IQR: 400–600 mg), lower than the currently recommended weight-based regimen (8 mg/kg; maximum 800 mg per infusion); 86.4% received a single dose. In the adjusted Cox model, early tocilizumab use was not significantly associated with mortality (HR: 1.09; 95%CI: 0.67–1.75; p = 0.72). The proportional-hazards assumption was met globally. Adverse events of any cause (not assessed for causality) were recorded during hospitalization in 56 (23.1%) patients; the most frequent MedDRA category was respiratory, thoracic, and mediastinal disorders (n = 16). Conclusions: This Peruvian cohort documents how tocilizumab was used, in terms of timing and dose, during the first pandemic wave in a resource-constrained setting. In the absence of an untreated comparator, these data do not allow inferences on the contribution of tocilizumab to mortality, ICU admission, or adverse events.

title: Neutralising Antibodies Response Against SARS-CoV-2 Among People Living With HIV in Dar- es-Salaam Tanzania
abstract: Background: Coronavirus Disease 2019 has become endemic and is no longer a global health emergency. However, it remains significant for people living with HIV, whose immune dysregulation may impact antibody responses. Hence this study assessed neutralizing antibody capacity against SARS-CoV-2 variants among HIV-infected adults in Tanzania to inform sero-surveillance and pandemic readiness.Methods: Seventy HIV-positive adults (≥18 years) were enrolled (53 vaccinated, 17 unvaccinated). These were compared with 89 individuals who were HIV negative (71 vaccinated and 18 unvaccinated). Neutralizing antibodies were quantified using a surrogate virus neutralization assay, with ≥27.7% inhibition defined as protective. Factors associated with neutralization were analyzed using modified Poisson regression (STATA v15), and group differences assessed using Kruskal-Wallis tests (Prism 9), with significance at P .9999. Also, the median percentage of neutralizing capacity among the relatively healthy HIV infected individuals (>500 CD4 count) was lower (28%) compared those who were HIV negatives (98%), within the vaccinated group (P<.0001) and 29% vs 80% for unvaccinated sub-groups (P<.005).Conclusion: Neutralising antibodies declined significantly across newer SARS-CoV-2 variants among HIV-infected individuals. Moreover, neutralizing capacity was significantly lower among immune competent HIV-positive participants compared to their HIV negative counterparts. We recommend ongoing sero-surveillance to enable timely action.
