While initial radiological research focused on parenchymal lung disease, a paradigm shift has identified pulmonary vascular abnormalities—specifically endotheliitis, microthrombosis, and maladaptive angiogenesis—as critical drivers of the Long COVID phenotype. The disease is characterized by “endotheliitis,” where direct viral entry via ACE2 receptors precipitates a pro-coagulant state and the formation of in situ microthrombi. This is further complicated by immunothrombosis involving neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) and the presence of amyloid-like fibrin microclots that are resistant to natural breakdown. Additionally, structural remodeling through intussusceptive angiogenesis and “vascular pruning” (the loss of distal capillaries) reduces the effective surface area for gas exchange. Conventional CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) often fails to detect these microvascular changes, despite patients exhibiting severe symptoms. However, advanced modalities provide deeper insights. Dual-energy CT (DECT) reveals persistent, wedge-shaped perfusion defects even in morphologically normal lung parenchyma. Quantitative CT (QCT) allows for the measurement of “vascular pruning,” showing a significant reduction in small vessel volume (PBV5). Hyperpolarized xenon-129 MRI (Hp-XeMRI) has identified a hallmark Red blood cell (RBC):barrier defect, indicating impaired gas transfer from the alveoli to red blood cells—a finding that persists even when standard CT and pulmonary function tests are normal. Functional techniques like V/Q SPECT and phase-resolved functional lung (PREFUL) MRI further confirm a “mottled” perfusion pattern indicative of diffuse small vessel vasculopathy. This review emphasizes that Long COVID involves a distinct vascular phenotype that requires functional and quantitative imaging for accurate diagnosis. Adherence to the 2025 international consensus guidelines—recommending imaging 3 months post-infection and the use of paired inspiratory/expiratory protocols—is essential for standardizing care and differentiating vascular from airway-related symptoms.

title: Novel Occupational and Environmental Risk Factors for SARS-CoV-2 Infection Among Coal Miners: Longitudinal Cohort Study
abstract: Background Miners are essential rural workers who may work in close proximity to others in inadequately ventilated environments and cannot telecommute or work flexible hours, rendering them vulnerable to SARS-CoV-2 transmission. Exposure to particulate air pollution may also be associated with an increased risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection and mortality. Chronic exposure to particulate matter causes overexpression of the alveolar angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 receptor, facilitating SARS-CoV-2 entry into lung epithelial cells. Objective We tested the hypothesis that coal miners with higher levels of self-reported particulate matter exposure assessed separately for occupational dust, residential wood burning, and shared transportation have a greater risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection than miners with lower exposure. Methods We conducted a longitudinal study from February 2021 to March 2022 involving 169 surface coal miners in New Mexico and 61 in Wyoming. Seropositivity was determined by measuring immunoglobulin G antibodies to the nucleocapsid protein of SARS-CoV-2 in plasma samples at baseline and at 3, 6, and 12 months after study enrollment. Predictor variables were self-reported exposure to occupational dust, wood burning, and shared transportation. The outcome variable was postbaseline incident seropositivity, defined as any new positive antibody result following enrollment during the 12-month study period. We used logistic regression and Firth-penalized likelihood for analysis; the multivariable model used the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator model selection method. Multivariable models were adjusted for sex, race and ethnicity, mine site (state), COVID-19 vaccination status, and baseline (prevalent) seropositivity. Results The study included 230 miners—44% (101/230) Hispanic and 13% (29/230) American Indian, mostly men (202/230, 88%), and 73% (169/230) from New Mexico and 27% (61/230) from Wyoming. At baseline, 23% (52/230) of participants reported COVID-19 vaccination; 25% (58/230) reported high baseline dust exposure, 18% (41/230) reported burning wood very often, and 23% (54/230) reported sharing transportation very often. Higher self-reported mining dust exposure was associated with lower odds of incident seroconversion, but the association was not significant after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio 0.42, 95% CI 0.17-1.07; P=.07). No incident seroconversions occurred among participants reporting frequent residential wood burning (0/35, 0%), and wood-burning frequency was not associated with incident seroconversion. Shared transportation frequency was also not associated with incident seroconversion. Conclusions Self-reported occupational dust exposure was not associated with higher odds of incident SARS-CoV-2 seroconversion in miners; point estimates instead suggested lower odds. This unexpected finding most likely reflects unmeasured workplace factors rather than a protective effect of dust; because individual respirator use and work microenvironment data were not collected, no causal inference can be drawn. Our results highlight the need for additional research on how occupational and environmental exposures interact with infectious disease dynamics in essential rural workforces.

title: Genomic surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 in Cote d’Ivoire, 2024 - 2025; diversification of JN.1 derived lineages and detection of the recombinant XFJ.1
abstract: Abstract Although the COVID-19 public health emergency ended in 2023, SARS-CoV-2 continues to circulate and diversify. Genomic surveillance therefore remains essential, particularly in regions underrepresented in global databases. We characterized the SARS-CoV-2 lineages circulating in Côte d’Ivoire in 2024-2025. Nasopharyngeal samples were collected from patients with influenza-like illness or severe acute respiratory infection within the national sentinel surveillance network. SARS-CoV-2 RNA was detected by multiplex real-time RT-qPCR, and specimens with a cycle threshold ≤ 30 underwent targeted sequencing of the Spike (S) gene on the Oxford Nanopore platform. Consensus sequences were assigned to Nextstrain clades with Nextclade. Of 9,622 specimens tested, 207 were positive (2.1% in 2024; 2.2% in 2025), and 158 yielded high-quality S-gene sequences. All belonged to BA.2.86/JN.1 descendants. Clade 24A predominated in 2024 (70.4%) and was replaced in 2025 by clades 24H (44.2%) and 25H (23.4%). The recombinant XFJ.1 became the most frequent lineage in 2025 (23.4%). Lineage diversity was highest in 2025 and lowest in 2024. These results show a continued diversification of JN.1-derived lineages and support sustained, geographically expanded genomic surveillance in West Africa. Keywords: SARS-CoV-2, genomic surveillance, JN.1, recombinant XFJ.1, Côte d’Ivoire

title: SARS-CoV-2 and the Gut: From Viral Persistence to Post-Infectious Gut–Brain Disorders
abstract: COVID-19 is a multisystem disease with important gastrointestinal (GI) involvement. Diarrhea, nausea or vomiting, reduced appetite, and abdominal pain are among the most frequently reported GI manifestations during acute infection, although their prevalence varies across populations, viral variants, disease severity, and study designs. The biological basis of intestinal involvement is supported by the expression of angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) and host proteases required for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) entry into intestinal epithelial cells. Viral RNA and antigens have also been detected in intestinal tissues after respiratory clearance, indicating persistence of viral material in some individuals; these findings do not by themselves demonstrate replication-competent virus. Uncommon but potentially severe GI complications include acute mesenteric ischemia, ischemic colitis, gastrointestinal bleeding, ileus, intestinal perforation, and acute pancreatitis. Although COVID-19 is associated with worse outcomes in acute pancreatitis, direct viral causation remains uncertain. Persistent GI manifestations have also emerged as an important component of post-COVID disease. Studies using Rome criteria have identified new-onset disorders of gut–brain interaction, including irritable bowel syndrome, functional dyspepsia, functional diarrhea, and functional constipation. Candidate mechanisms include intestinal viral antigen persistence, epithelial barrier dysfunction, sustained immune activation, gut microbial dysbiosis, and altered tryptophan–serotonin signaling; most links remain associative rather than causally established. Altered microbial signaling may also contribute to mucosal inflammation and disturbances in gut–lung and gut–brain communication. Overall, current evidence supports GI involvement in both acute and post-acute COVID-19. Further studies integrating microbiome, metabolic, and immune profiling are needed to clarify the mechanisms underlying post-COVID GI disorders and identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

title: Quantifying the contribution of policy measures to COVID-19 dynamics across 126 countries
abstract: COVID-19 provides an unprecedented opportunity to evaluate the contribution of public health and social measures (PHSMs) to controlling transmission and inform responses to future emerging respiratory pathogens. We analysed SARS-CoV-2 transmission across 126 countries spanning multiple epidemic waves and diverse policy environments during periods when PHSMs were the primary interventions available to influence the epidemic. By explicitly representing key epidemiological drivers of transmission and measuring reductions in residual transmission scaling after incorporating OxCGRT policy time-series data, we isolated the effect of PHSMs on transmission. PHSMs frequently explained a substantial proportion of the observed variation in transmission intensity, with particularly strong effects seen in many high-income countries. In countries with strong evidence for policy effects, reductions in transmission reached 60-80% or above, although the individual policies responsible for these effects varied considerably. Harmonised analyses considering the effect of community mobility showed comparably strong effects in a similar subset of countries.

title: Unravelling the role of polyadenylate binding protein (PABPC1) in the SARS-CoV-2 life cycle
abstract: As the SARS-CoV-2 virus continues to evolve, the emergence of new variants reduces the effectiveness of existing treatments and vaccines, highlighting the need for alternative strategies to combat infection. This thesis investigates how targeting human proteins, such as PABPC1, affects SARS-CoV-2 infection. It shows that PABPC1 interacts with an important viral protein and helps control the movement of viral components inside infected cells. As a result, the body’s early antiviral responses are diminished and viral replication is promoted. By identifying the PABPC1 as a potential target, this research provides insights into more durable host-directed antiviral approaches against evolving variants.

title: Integrated Plasma Proteomic and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Profiling of Three COVID-19 Second-Booster Regimens: An Exploratory Analysis of a Randomized Phase IV Trial
abstract: Background: Waning vaccine-induced immunity and the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants have prompted the evaluation of alternative booster strategies. We investigated the systemic immune profiles associated with three second-booster regimens in adults previously vaccinated with three doses of an inactivated vaccine. Methods: This exploratory analysis was nested within a randomized phase IV trial comparing homologous CoronaVac (ICV), intramuscular Ad5-nCoV (IM), and inhaled Ad5-nCoV (IH) boosting. Serum antibody responses were assessed, 119 plasma samples underwent Olink inflammatory-protein profiling, and 24 peripheral blood mononuclear cell samples were analyzed by single-cell RNA sequencing. title: Clustering Genetically Closely Related SARS-CoV-2 Lineages that Share the Same Relative Effective Reproduction Number Using BIC–Based Model Selection
abstract: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has evolved continuously, producing a large number of viral lineages. Natural selection favors lineages with advantageous mutations, and these lineages increase in frequency, replacing previously circulating lineages. Several lineage replacement models have been developed to estimate the relative effective reproduction number of circulating lineages. When a large number of lineages are circulating in a population simultaneously, the number of model parameters representing viral transmissibility increases, making it difficult to explore mutations affecting viral transmissibility. Therefore, clustering viral lineages with similar genetic backgrounds and the same relative effective reproduction numbers may help us explore the genetic and phenotypic relationships among circulating lineages. In this paper, we present a new algorithm called FindPart-w-ε, which identifies groups of genetically closely related viral lineages that share the same relative effective reproduction numbers from temporal count datasets of observed viral lineages. We formalize groups of genetically closely related viral lineages using ε-connected partitions, and FindPart-w-ε searches for an ε-connected partition that minimizes the Bayesian information criterion. By applying the algorithm to datasets of SARS-CoV-2 lineage counts from the United States of America and the United Kingdom, we showed that FindPart-w-ε improves the interpretability of the resulting lineage partitions while retaining major lineage-specific transmissibility patterns.

title: Association of IL-8 and IL-8R1 gene polymorphisms with COVID-19 mortality
abstract: Abstract Background Host genetic factors contribute to the heterogeneity of clinical outcomes in Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). Interleukin-8 (IL-8) and its receptor IL-8R1 (CXCR1) play key roles in inflammatory responses and cytokine-mediated tissue damage during severe SARS-CoV-2 infection. This study investigated the association of IL-8 rs4073 and rs2227306, as well as IL-8R1 rs2234671 polymorphisms, with COVID-19 mortality in an Iranian population. Methods A total of 328 hospitalized COVID-19 patients, including 178 recovered and 150 deceased individuals, were enrolled. Genotyping of IL-8 rs4073, IL-8 rs2227306, and IL-8R1 rs2234671 polymorphisms was performed using polymerase chain reaction–restriction fragment length polymorphism (PCR-RFLP), and selected samples were confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Genotype and allele frequencies were compared between groups, and logistic regression models were applied to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Multilocus genotype combination analysis was also conducted. Results The IL-8R1 rs2234671 polymorphism showed a significant association with COVID-19 mortality. Carriers of the G allele exhibited an increased risk of death compared with CC homozygotes under codominant, dominant, overdominant, and log-additive inheritance models (all P < 0.05). The strongest association was observed under the dominant model (OR = 3.29, 95% CI = 1.55–6.99, P = 0.0014). In contrast, IL-8 rs4073 and rs2227306 polymorphisms showed no statistically significant associations with mortality when analyzed individually. Multilocus genotype combination analysis suggested that specific combinations involving IL-8R1 rs2234671 may influence clinical outcomes, although these findings require further validation. Conclusions Our findings indicate that the IL-8R1 rs2234671 polymorphism is associated with COVID-19 mortality in the studied Iranian population, supporting the importance of IL-8/CXCR1-mediated inflammatory pathways in disease progression. Although individual IL-8 polymorphisms were not significantly associated with mortality, combined genetic effects may contribute to outcome variability. However, the proposed functional mechanisms remain to be experimentally validated. Larger multi-ethnic studies and functional investigations are needed to validate these associations and clarify their biological significance. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Risk Factors for Incident Diabetes After SARS-CoV-2 Infection Across Variant Eras: Findings From the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C) COVID-19 Enclave
abstract: Abstract Background: SARS-CoV-2 infection has been associated with incident diabetes, but the influence of evolving clinical and population characteristics across the pandemic remains unclear. The objective was to identify factors associated with incident diabetes after COVID-19 and assess differences across variant eras. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study, analyzing 528,710 adults with COVID-19 and without pre-existing diabetes using data from the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative COVID-19 Enclave. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated demographics, comorbidities, variant era, COVID-19 severity and socioeconomic factors associated with incident diabetes within one year following acute COVID-19. Results: Increasing age, male sex (OR 1.32, 95% CI 1.27-1.38), higher BMI, cardiometabolic conditions, and hospitalization for COVID-19 were associated with incident diabetes risk. Risk was higher among Black (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.41-1.59) and Hispanic individuals (OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.55-1.77), and those living in areas with high poverty rates (OR 1.13, 95% CI 1.15-1.32). Compared with the ancestral period, risk was lower in Alpha (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.82-0.92) and Delta eras (OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85-0.98), but similar during Omicron (OR 1.01, 95% CI 0.93-1.09). The ancestral cohort included more Black and Hispanic individuals and greater socioeconomic disadvantage, whereas later cohorts were increasingly non-Hispanic White, less disadvantaged, and had more comorbidities. Conclusions: Incident diabetes risk after COVID-19 was associated with cardiometabolic and sociodemographic factors and remained similar in the Omicron and ancestral periods. Shifting sociodemographic characteristics across variant eras suggests that changing healthcare engagement may influence the populations represented in contemporary electronic health record data. · Why did we undertake this study? We sought to understand how infection- and patient-related factors influence incident diabetes risk after COVID-19 across variant eras. · What is the specific question(s) we wanted to answer? We evaluated the association of infection-related, clinical, and sociodemographic factors with incident diabetes and whether risk differs across pandemic eras. Incident diabetes risk was associated with increasing age, male sex, cardiometabolic comorbidities and sociodemographic risk factors. There was no evidence of difference in risk between the ancestral and Omicron variant eras, however the populations represented in EHR data shifted over time. · What are the implications of our findings? Temporal trends likely reflect changes in healthcare utilization and population representation, underscoring the need for targeted screening and cautious interpretation of observational data.

title: P-455: Establishing a pediatric and adolescent type 1 diabetes clinic at a Kenyan sub-county hospital during COVID-19: a six-year experience from Mariakani, Kilifi county
abstract: In Kilifi County, Kenya, children with type 1 diabetes (T1D) previously travelled long distances to Coast General Teaching & Referral Hospital (CGTRH) in Mombasa or to Kilifi Sub-County Hospital. The 2020 COVID-19 lockdown cut off this access, prompting establishment of a decentralized pediatric T1D clinic at Mariakani Sub-County Hospital (MSCH), serving Kaloleni, Rabai and surrounding areas. To describe the six-year growth, outcomes and psychosocial interventions of the T1D clinic in a resource-limited Kenyan sub-county hospital. Retrospective review of MSCH clinic records from May 2020 to April 2026. The clinic was set up with mentorship from CGTRH and support from the Changing Diabetes in Children programme. Enrolment, retention, mortality with causes, and psychosocial interventions were reviewed. The clinic opened in May 2020 with 22 children and has cumulatively enrolled 69; 58 are currently active and mostly clinically stable aged between 2-19 years. Seven deaths were recorded (three during COVID-19); causes included diabetic ketoacidosis, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, malnutrition with wounds, and sepsis. Psychosocial interventions included placing a 16-year-old with T1D, Down syndrome and epilepsy who was rejected by mainstream schools for comorbidity in a special-needs boarding school. Escalating parental neglect of an adolescent to the sub-county children’s office and probation offices; advocating vocational training pathways for adolescents unable to attend mainstream school; and rehabilitating a malnourished 15-year-old (15 kg, low hemoglobin) who returned to school. A mentor-supported, decentralized T1D clinic at a sub-county hospital can sustain pediatric T1D care in coastal Kenya, with outcomes extending beyond glycemic control to school re-entry, child protection and vocational advocacy. The model is scalable to other Kenyan sub-county hospitals to close the rural access gap.

title: Changes in Respiratory Microorganism Distribution and Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns in Intensive Care Units: A Comparative Analysis Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate changes in the distribution of microorganisms isolated from respiratory tract specimens and antimicrobial resistance patterns in intensive care units (ICUs) before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. Microbiological data from respiratory tract specimens obtained from patients admitted to the ICUs of a state hospital between January 1, 2019, and April 30, 2021, were retrospectively reviewed. The study period was divided into the pre-pandemic period (January 1, 2019–February 29, 2020) and the pandemic period (March 1, 2020–April 30, 2021). A total of 634 patients and 757 respiratory tract isolates were included. The median age was 79 years (IQR: 66–85), and 55.2% of the patients were male. was the most frequently isolated microorganism overall, followed by Klebsiella spp., Pseudomonas spp., Escherichia coli, and Staphylococcus aureus. Overall microorganism distribution differed significantly between the pre-pandemic and pandemic periods (p<0.001). Antimicrobial resistance analyses were performed for the most frequently isolated bacterial pathogens. No significant changes were observed in resistance rates among Pseudomonas spp. Among Acinetobacter spp. isolates, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole resistance increased significantly during the pandemic period. Among Klebsiella spp. isolates, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole resistance increased significantly. These findings indicate that the COVID-19 pandemic period was associated with changes in respiratory microorganism distribution and selected antimicrobial resistance patterns in ICUs.

title: Long COVID: A Modified Delphi Consensus on Definition, Burden, Diagnosis and Management in Southeast Asia
abstract: Long COVID is a heterogeneous post-infectious condition following acute severe acute respiratory syndrome-coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection. Ongoing uncertainty around its definition, burden, diagnosis and management complicates clinical recognition and care in Southeast Asia. A modified Delphi consensus study was conducted with twelve experts from six Southeast Asian countries to develop regional guidance on long COVID. Consensus was predefined as ≥ 80% agreement, corresponding to at least 10 of 12 experts selecting the same response in multiple-choice questions or indicating agreement on Likert-scale questions (e.g. agree/strongly agree, most important/more important, relevant/highly relevant). Questions that reached consensus were removed from the subsequent round, while unresolved questions were revised, consolidated, or expanded. In the final round, a post hoc descriptive category, ‘moderate endorsement’, was applied to Likert-scale questions that had not reached consensus, with ‘important’ as the midpoint category of the five-point importance scale (‘most important’ to ‘least important’), to capture responses judged important but falling short of the consensus threshold. Consensus was reached for all ‘definition’, ‘burden’ and ‘management’ theme questions and most ‘diagnosis’ questions. Experts defined long COVID as unexplained symptoms persisting for > 3 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection, distinct from post-acute COVID-19, with no minimum severity threshold requirement. Long COVID was recognised as affecting approximately 6%–10% of individuals after SARS-CoV-2 infection, consistent with published WHO and KSID estimates; clinical evaluation and symptom-guided testing were recommended for its diagnosis. Hospitalisation during acute COVID-19 was identified as a risk factor for developing long COVID. The experts recommended multidisciplinary, symptom-directed care, rehabilitation, pacing and follow-up. Vaccination and reinfection prevention were supported as important long COVID risk-reduction strategies, and early antiviral treatment should be considered to prevent severe acute illness and hospitalisation in high-risk individuals. Consensus was not reached on the past medical history required for diagnosis; moderate endorsement was observed for booster status, absence of early antiviral treatment, pre-COVID health assessment and standardised patient-reported outcome tools. This Delphi study provides a practical regional consensus framework for long COVID in Southeast Asia.

title: Nasopharyngeal Microbiome Profiles of SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR Positive and Negative Outpatients in Guayaquil, Ecuador
abstract: The nasopharyngeal microbiome contributes to respiratory health and may influence host responses to respiratory viral infections, including SARS-CoV-2, yet its association with viral detection remains incompletely understood, particularly in outpatients from Latin America. In this cross-sectional study, adult outpatients undergoing SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR testing in Guayaquil, Ecuador, were consecutively recruited between 2 and 7 June 2021, and their nasopharyngeal microbiome was characterized using 16S rRNA gene (V3–V4) sequencing. Microbiome diversity, taxonomic composition, differential abundance, and predicted functional profiles were compared between RT-PCR positive (n = 41) and RT-PCR negative (n = 17) individuals. Compositional analyses used 57 samples after taxon filtering (41 RT-PCR positive and 16 RT-PCR negative). No differences by RT-PCR status were detected in alpha or beta diversity, and no taxa or predicted pathways were differentially abundant; alpha- and beta-diversity results were unchanged after accounting for collection date. Both groups displayed similar microbial communities dominated by Corynebacterium sp. and Staphylococcus sp., which together with Cutibacterium sp. formed the core microbiome. These findings indicate that SARS-CoV-2 detection was not associated with major alterations in the taxonomic composition or predicted functional profiles of the nasopharyngeal microbiome in this outpatient Ecuadorian cohort, although smaller effects cannot be excluded given the size of the RT-PCR negative group.

These findings indicate that SARS-CoV-2 detection was not associated with major alterations in the taxonomic composition or predicted functional profiles of the nasopharyngeal microbiome in this outpatient Ecuadorian cohort, although smaller effects cannot be excluded given the size of the RT-PCR negative group.

title: Mental health trajectories before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic among patients attending a psychosomatic internal medicine clinic in Japan: A retrospective quantitative study.
abstract: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has exacerbated anxiety and depression globally, particularly among individuals with mental health conditions and chronic illnesses. However, the extent to which these mental health effects have persisted following the pandemic remains unclear. This study examined changes in mental health before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic among first-time patients attending a psychosomatic internal medicine clinic in Japan. The legal reclassification of COVID-19 to "Class5" status under Japan's Infectious Diseases Control Law, which took effect on May 8 2023, serves as the benchmark marking the beginning of the post-pandemic era, designated as the beginning of the post-pandemic period. The General Health Questionnaire (GHQ)-30, State-Trait Anxiety Inventory, and Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D) were used to assess general mental health, state and trait anxiety, and depressive symptoms, respectively. Participants were classified into pre-pandemic (n = 87), during-pandemic (n = 322), and post-pandemic (< 1 year: n = 75 and 1-2 years: n = 68) groups. The Mann-Whitney U test was used to compare mental health outcomes across the study periods. A total of 552 participants completed the survey (237 men and 315 women; mean age: 44.57 ± 19.56 years). Within 1 year after the pandemic, GHQ total mean scores, sleep disturbance, anxiety and dysphoria, and CES-D mean scores were significantly higher than those in the pre-pandemic group (GHQ total: 16.32 vs 13.57, P = .015; sleep disturbance: 3.70 vs 2.65, P < .001; anxiety and dysphoria: 3.14 vs 2.35, P = .016; CES-D: 26.53 vs 21.39, P = .005). Sleep disturbance scores were also significantly higher within 1 year after the pandemic than during the pandemic (3.70 vs 3.19, P = .015) but were significantly lower in the 1 to 2 years post-pandemic group than in the within-one-year post-pandemic group (2.65 vs 3.70, P = .022). These findings suggest that symptoms of anxiety, depression, and sleep disturbance persisted during the early post-pandemic period but gradually improved over time. Particularly, sleep disturbance remained one of the most persistent mental health concerns, highlighting the importance of continued attention to the mental health of patients with psychosomatic disorders following the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Recent positive psychosocial experiences are linked to SARS-CoV-2 IgG immune memory in adults exposed to adverse childhood experiences
abstract: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are associated with altered immune function in adulthood including elevated susceptibility to viral infection, chronic inflammation, and poorer COVID-19 disease outcomes. Meanwhile, protective experiences have been associated with better immune profiles, although few studies have examined this in the context of high ACEs. In a community-based sample of middle-aged (35-59y) adults with high average 10-item ACE scores (mean(SD)=4.2(2.9)) and who self-reported at least one COVID-19 vaccine dose or one COVID-19 illness (N=72), we tested whether early life ACEs and current protective and compensatory experiences (C-PACEs) in adulthood were associated with reduced anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike protein subunit 1 receptor binding domain (S1-RBD) IgG antibody levels. In covariate-adjusted analyses, higher childhood ACE scores were associated with lower levels of log2-transformed anti-S1-RBD IgG antibodies (β=−0.17±0.06 per ACE event, p=0.005). Analyses examining adult C-PACE scores documented an elevation in anti-S1-RBD IgG (β=0.09±0.03 per C-PACE point, p=0.001). Follow-up analyses did not detect moderation of the effect of ACEs by C-PACEs (interactive term β=0.17, p=0.296). In an exploratory mediation analysis, the estimated indirect effect through C-PACEs was not statistically supported (β=−0.07, 95% bootstrap CI [−0.167, 0.004], p=.113). These results suggest that SARS-CoV-2 IgG immune memory may be linked to protective experiences in adulthood, which are inversely correlated with childhood ACEs.

title: Metformin and Severe Post‐ COVID ‐19 Outcomes Among Individuals With Diabetes Mellitus
abstract: AIMS: We evaluated the relationship between metformin, one of the most commonly prescribed medications for individuals with diabetes, and COVID-19 sequelae. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We evaluated a retrospective cohort of individuals in the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative with Type 2 diabetes mellitus and COVID-19 who were prescribed metformin or a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor (DPP4i) at least 30 days before the onset of acute COVID-19 between 1 October 2021, and 15 November 2023. We compared the 12-month cumulative incidence of Long COVID diagnosis (ICD-10 U09.9: Post COVID-19 condition, unspecified), probable Long COVID (based on a model-derived phenotype), and mortality between individuals prescribed metformin versus DPP4i. We applied Super Learner and targeted maximum likelihood estimation to obtain risk ratios while adjusting for covariates of interest. RESULTS: In our sample of 53 332 individuals with Type 2 diabetes and COVID-19, we found that metformin prescription was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality after COVID-19 (adjusted risk ratio [aRR]: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.51, 0.73). We also observed that metformin users, compared to DPP4i users, had a slightly lower risk of probable Long COVID (aRR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.81, 0.94) but did not detect a significant relationship with the clinically defined outcome of Long COVID diagnosis (aRR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.68, 1.20). CONCLUSIONS: These findings support the hypothesis that metformin prescription during acute COVID-19 may be associated with lower mortality among adults with diabetes.

title: Changes in Subjective Mortality Due to COVID-19 and Its Vaccination: The Influence on Saving Behavior in Japan
abstract: Abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic, while broad social anxiety spread, some individuals might have perceived a heightened risk of dying in the near future, whereas the subsequent rollout of vaccines might have provided a sense of relief by lowering these short-term mortality expectations. This study explored how COVID-19 and vaccination influenced subjective mortality and saving behavior. Referring to the life cycle model, we hypothesized that an increase in subjective mortality due to COVID-19 negatively affects and a decrease in mortality due to vaccination positively affects saving. In January 2022, we conducted an online survey in Japan with 3500 individuals aged 20–79 years who were working or whose spouses were working. We analyzed the determinants of the share of savings in income. Considering the endogeneity of subjective mortality, we estimated the savings equation using the instrumental variable method, conducting analyses for the full sample as well as for two specific groups: those under 65 and those aged 65 and over. The analysis revealed that individuals who felt their mortality increased due to the pandemic exhibited lower savings in the full sample and the 65-and-over age group. Those who felt that their mortality decreased after vaccination tended to save more. However, vaccination alone did not significantly affect savings. Regarding the experience of COVID-19 infection, it showed no significant impact on savings for the full sample and those under 65, whereas it exhibited a significant positive impact exclusively for the sample aged 65 and over at the 10% level. JEL Classification D10, I10, J10

title: Polyaniline-based fluorescence nucleic acid biosensor for SARS-COV-2 RNA monitoring: from analytical validation to wastewater analysis
abstract: Rapid, selective nucleic acid detection is essential for environmental surveillance and public health monitoring. This study presents a label-free fluorescent biosensor based on polyaniline (PANI) functionalized with a DNA probe for SARS-CoV-2 RNA recognition. UV irradiation conditions and probe concentration were optimized to improve fluorescence performance. The biosensor discriminated complementary from non-complementary RNA sequences at concentrations as low as 10−10 mM. Concentration-dependent fluorescence quenching was observed over 10−10 – 10−6 mM, yielding a strong logarithmic calibration fit (R2 = 0.9934). Blank-based limits of detection and quantification were statistically estimated at 1.83 × 10−6 and 6.11 × 10−6 mM, respectively, pending experimental validation. Principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering confirmed spectral discrimination between sensing stages and RNA concentrations. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry, and ATR-FTIR provided complementary evidence of interfacial modifications following DNA functionalization and RNA hybridization. Sensor stability was additionally assessed over 21 days to investigate fluorescence-response reproducibility. Application to purified RNA extracts from municipal wastewater and spent hemodialysis dialysate yielded relative fluorescence-response amplitudes of 92.3% and 15.1%, respectively, indicating distinct matrix-dependent effects rather than concentration-based analytical recoveries. Comparison with RT-qPCR measurements showed a strong association (R2 = 0.9025), supporting the platform’s applicability to environmental samples. Overall, the PANI–DNA biosensor offers a promising amplification-free sensing strategy for SARS-CoV-2 RNA recognition and wastewater-based epidemiology, although further validation of analytical sensitivity, matrix tolerance, and operational robustness remains necessary.

title: Assessment of Logistics Performance Indicators in Network SMES during the COVID-19 Pandemic: The Case of Tomaszów County, Poland
abstract: The issue of small and medium-sized (SME) enterprises has been widely covered in both domestic and international literature. In Poland, sector accounts for 99.8% of the activities of all enterprises. Theoretical analysis and he research discussed in the article was carried out on a sample of network companies from the SME sector and enterprises located in smaller towns and villages in the Łódź Voivodeship (outside the Łódź agglomeration) in Poland, which not often feature in the literature on the subject, Studies also focused on the analysis of the economic performance of the Łódź Voivodeship, especially of the Tomaszów County during the COVID-19 crisis. The article has been based, among others, on: literature on the subject, reports of the Polish Agency for Enterprise Development (PARP), BVL reports, practical knowledge about logistics shared by logistics companies on their websites and own research, which was carried out in the form of surveys among enterprises in the SME sector in the Łódź Voivodeship, and selected statistics. The explored indicators concerning the quality of transport and logistics were at a good level. Although they slightly deteriorated during the COVID-19 pandemic, the decline remained within the range of 0–3%.
journal: International Journal of Energy Economics and Policy

title: Strategi Kampanye Komunikasi Publik Satgas Covid-19 Nasional dalam Penanganan Covid-19
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia generated significant impacts on public health and the national economy, reflected in rising confirmed cases, economic contraction, and increasing unemployment resulting from physical distancing policies. These conditions required society to adapt to new behavioral norms through structured and effective public communication. This study aims to analyze the public communication campaign strategy implemented by the National COVID-19 Task Force in managing the pandemic and to identify the supporting and inhibiting factors influencing its implementation. The research employed a qualitative approach within a constructivist paradigm using a case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with the public communication division and community members and were analyzed interpretatively. The findings indicate that the campaign strategy was systematically designed with informative and persuasive objectives to enhance public awareness and encourage behavioral change. Messages were science-based and delivered by credible communicators with authentic voices. Furthermore, stakeholder mapping was conducted to strengthen collaborative support, contributing to the development of active and sustainable public participation in pandemic management.

title: COVID-19 diagnosis using a decision tree algorithm
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is a respiratory infection for which chest X-ray (CXR) imaging can provide an accessible screening modality. This study investigates an interpretable computer-aided screening pipeline for distinguishing COVID-19-positive from normal CXR images. Methods: The pipeline combines Otsu-based lung segmentation, morphological refinement, seven Hu invariant shape moments, training-fold z-score normalization, and a class-weighted Decision Tree. A cohort of 2,600 CXR images (1,000 COVID-19-positive and 1,600 normal) was evaluated using stratified five-fold cross-validation. The retained experimental record reports 98.6% accuracy, 97.8% precision, 98.6% recall (sensitivity), and 98.2% F1-score. The pooled confusion matrix shows TP=986, FN=14, FP=22, and TN=1578, corresponding to 98.6% accuracy and 97.8% precision. ROC/AUC analysis yielded AUC = 0.987 ± 0.004 under the image-level evaluation protocol. Conclusion: The findings indicate that a low-dimensional, shape-based descriptor combined with an interpretable Decision Tree can discriminate COVID-19-positive from normal CXR images under the present internal image-level protocol. Because the cohort was not partitioned at the patient or source level and no independent external cohort was retained in the study record, the results are considered preliminary proof-of-concept evidence rather than clinically validated diagnostic performance.

title: Social and Political Differences in COVID-19 Vaccination and Vaccine Readiness Among RN-to-BSN Nursing Students
abstract: Background: Research demonstrates a strong relationship between healthcare professionals’ vaccine attitudes and behaviors and the vaccination behaviors of patients, family, and friends. Positive vaccine attitudes among healthcare professionals are associated with vaccine uptake among patients and non-patients. Relatedly, vaccine hesitancy among healthcare professionals is associated with decreases in vaccine uptake. Understanding and addressing vaccine hesitancy among healthcare professionals, such as nurses, is a critical public health issue. Purpose: This study examines social and political differences between COVID-19 fully vaccinated (FV) and not fully vaccinated (NFV) nursing students. Methods: An online survey was distributed to investigate the social (i.e., age, gender, race/ethnicity, and religious affiliation) and political (political affiliation) differences in COVID-19 vaccination among RN-to-BSN nursing students. Among the NFV, readiness for COVID-19 vaccination and reasons for vaccine hesitancy were also assessed. The final analytic sample included 192 respondents. Descriptive and bivariate analyses were conducted to identify whether socio-demographic and political differences existed between COVID-19 FV and NFV nursing students. title: Immunogenicity of COVID-19 vaccines in the upper respiratory tract: a comparative study of Pfizer-BioNTech and Johnson & Johnson vaccines among Ugandan adults
abstract: Abstract Background COVID-19 vaccination has been shown to elicit robust systemic immune responses against SARS-CoV-2. However, little is known about vaccine-induced mucosal responses in the upper respiratory tract (URT), particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. Here, we characterized nasal and peripheral blood immune responses among Pfizer-BioNTech and Johnson & Johnson (J&J) COVID-19 vaccine recipients in Uganda. Methods This was an observational prospective cohort sub-study evaluating URT and systemic T cell responses in 21 Ugandan adults receiving either a single dose of J&J Ad26.COV2. S ( n = 7) at enrolment or two doses of Pfizer-BioNTech BNT162b2 ( n = 14) at enrolment and week 4 Study visits. T-cell responses were characterized by flow cytometry using nasopharyngeal (NP) swabs and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) samples collected at enrolment, weeks 4 and 12. Changes in immune responses over time and differences between vaccine groups were evaluated using linear mixed models and non-parametric Mann-Whitney test respectively. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results Overall, we observed a significant increase in the proportions of CD8 + T cells in the nasal mucosa ( p = 0.0500) and peripheral blood ( p = 0.0484). Additionally, CD8 + tissue-resident memory (TRM) T cells identified by co-expression of CD69 and CD103, showed an increased abundance in the upper respiratory tract ( p = 0.2469), accompanied by a simultaneous significant decrease in their proportions in blood ( p = 0.0300) following vaccination. Comparison of immune responses between the two vaccine groups at 4 weeks after the first vaccination dose for Pfizer and only dose for J&J revealed significantly higher immune cell counts of CD45+ ( p = 0.0182), CD3+ ( p = 0.0136), CD4+ ( p = 0.0091), and CD8+ ( p = 0.0182) among J&J recipients compared to Pfizer-BioNTech. CD4 + CD69+ TRM T cell abundance was also significantly higher in J&J recipients ( p = 0.0182). Conversely, Pfizer-BioNTech recipients showed higher proportions of SARS-CoV-2-specific nasal CD8 + T cells expressing IFN-γ, perforin, and TNF at week 4 while J&J recipients revealed increased proportions of CD8 + T cells expressing IFN-γ and CD107a (both p = 0.0500) compared to Pfizer-BioNTech recipients at week 12. Conclusion Our findings demonstrate that both J&J and Pfizer-BioNTech vaccines induced nasal and systemic T cell responses in Ugandan adults, with response patterns varying by vaccine platform and time point. While J&J vaccination was associated with higher early nasal immune cell abundance, Pfizer-BioNTech vaccination elicited distinct immune responses, with changes observed across study visits. These data highlight the need to better understand mucosal immunity to COVID-19 and other vaccines, especially in low- and middle-income settings.

title: Changes in WIC Participants' Experiences During and After the COVID-19 Pandemic.
abstract: OBJECTIVE To evaluate Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) participants' food security, adequacy of cash value benefits (CVB), and WIC Electronic Benefit Transfer card and app satisfaction during (2021) and after (2023) the COVID-19 pandemic. DESIGN Cross-sectional surveys. SETTING 11 US WIC agencies. PARTICIPANTS WIC participants, 2021 (n = 25,808; 4.5% response rate), 2023 (n = 20,542; 5.5% response rate). MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE(S) Food security, food assistance, CVB adequacy, WIC card and app satisfaction. ANALYSIS Generalized linear mixed models, with time as a fixed effect and state as a random effect; significance was set at P < 0.05; models were adjusted for age, race, education, and work status. RESULTS In 2023, food insecurity prevalence was higher than in 2021 (56.8% vs 72.8%, P < 0.001). Pandemic-Electronic Benefit Transfer (33.5% vs 30.6%, P < 0.001) and school meals (29.0% vs 19.6%, P < 0.001) were lower in 2023 than in 2021; food from family/friends (24.0% vs 32.7%, P < 0.001), food pantries (25.4% vs 33.0%, P < 0.001), and Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program participation (42.0% vs 44.5%, P < 0.001) were higher; and perception of CVB adequacy (15.0% vs 31.6%, P < 0.001), satisfaction with the WIC card (3.43 vs 3.69, P < 0.001), and the app (3.35 vs 3.60, P < 0.001) were higher in 2023 than in 2021. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS Although participants altered their food assistance patterns from 2021 to 2023, food insecurity was higher in 2023 as pandemic-related programs ended. Higher WIC card and app satisfaction may reflect WIC's modernization efforts.
journal: Journal of nutrition education and behavior

title: Belom Bahadat and the future of a sustainable COVID-19 response in Indonesia
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has demonstrated that the response to a public health crisis depends not only on government policies and healthcare system capacity but also on the social and cultural values of the community. The Belom Bahadat philosophy of the Dayak Ngaju people emphasizes the spirit of mutual cooperation ( gotong royong ), mutual respect, equality, responsibility, and care for others. This study aims to understand the significance of Belom Bahadat regarding COVID-19 vaccination behavior and to interpret its connections to the second principle of Pancasila, Talcott Parsons’ AGIL scheme, and SDGs 3, 11, and 13. A qualitative approach was employed, involving interviews with five members of the Dayak Ngaju community in Palangka Raya City. Interview transcripts were analyzed thematically and interpreted through the AGIL framework. The results indicate that Belom Bahadat can be understood as a socio-cultural resource that fosters solidarity, collective responsibility, protection of family and community, and adaptability in the face of crisis. However, vaccination behavior is also influenced by government recommendations, workplace and travel requirements, social influence, risk perception, and understanding of vaccine safety and efficacy. These findings suggest that local values have the potential to complement culturally sensitive health governance and communication. Conceptually, this study links Belom Bahadat , AGIL, Pancasila, and the SDGs by integrating qualitative insights gained from conversations with the five participants. The connection to SDG 13 is presented as a conceptual link regarding adaptation and resilience, rather than as empirical evidence of climate action measures.

title: Sex differences in inflammation, mitochondrial function and energy sensing during early recovery from COVID 19 in older adults
abstract: Abstract SARS-CoV-2 infections induce mitochondrial dysfunction and exacerbate systemic inflammation. In the present study, sex differences were investigated among post-COVID-19 patients during the early recovery phase, as emerging evidence indicates that sex critically influences post-COVID-19 outcomes, particularly in older adults. Mitochondrial dysfunction, energy stress signaling through AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), and inflammatory dysregulation represent pathogenic mechanisms implicated in prolonged recovery. In this study, we analyzed peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and plasma from aged male and female patients during early post-COVID-19 recovery (1–4 weeks after obtaining a negative SARS-CoV-2 PCR test), comparing them to an inflammatory control group. Female post-COVID-19 patients exhibited elevated circulating TNF-α levels and a trend toward increased mRNA levels of proinflammatory interleukins IL-1β and IL-18 in PBMCs, accompanied by enhanced acetylation and decreased activity of mitochondrial superoxide dismutase 2 (SOD2). Both sexes displayed increased phosphorylation of AMPK, suggesting altered energy-sensing pathways. Mitochondrial gene expression was upregulated in female post-COVID-19 patients, potentially indicating compensatory responses to energy deficits. These findings reveal sex-dependent inflammatory and mitochondrial alterations during early recovery, suggesting a mechanistic link to the higher prevalence of long COVID-19 in women. These findings emphasize the need for sex-specific therapeutic approaches targeting mitochondrial and immunometabolic dysfunction in post-COVID-19 patients.

title: SARS-CoV-2 Period Seroprevalence Study on Cancer Healthcare Workers in a Rural Cancer Care Network
abstract: Introduction: Healthcare workers (HCWs), especially cancer care teams, are at an increased risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection, which may be amplified in rural areas. Therefore, we aimed to determine SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence among HCWs in our rural cancer care network. Methods: We conducted a multisite, longitudinal, three-part SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence study within the MaineHealth Cancer Care Network between November 2020 and April 2023, spanning metropolitan (one site), micropolitan (four), and rural (six) practices in south-central Maine and eastern New Hampshire. Follow-up was completed in January 2024. We followed 435 HCWs who provided cancer care during the pandemic. Participants reported their own medical history and that of household members and job duties, completed Occupational Risk and End-of-Study surveys, and underwent serial SARS-CoV-2 antibody testing. Results: In Part 1, the primary outcome SARS-CoV-2 period seroprevalence rate was 1.6% (3/192; 95% CI 0.5–4.5%). Nearly 8% of participants and 10% of their household members reported immunocompromising conditions. We observed persistence of spike protein antibody response >2,500 U/mL over the course of the study. Survey response rates were high and remarkably consistent, given the diversity of participants. Outside the workplace, our care team members practiced a high level of personal safety measures during the pandemic. Conclusion: Our findings showed a low SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence, consistent with the national and international data reported early in the pandemic. We also observed higher-than-expected immunocompromising conditions in rural HCWs and their households. These results underscore the importance of longitudinal sero-surveillance, particularly for high-risk rural healthcare networks.

title: Environmental circulation of airborne SARS-CoV-2 particles in intensive care rooms
abstract: Abstract Background: Airborne transmission is a major concern in intensive care units (ICUs). This study aimed to identify the determinants of airborne and surface contamination in ICU rooms occupied by patients with COVID-19 associated respiratory failure. Methods: Observational study in a tertiary care hospital comprising six ICUs with diverse architectural layouts and HVAC systems. We modeled the dispersion of respiratory particles in five rooms using computational fluid dynamics (CFD). Air and surface samples were collected at predefined locations in 19 rooms occupied by 28 patients testing positive for SARS-CoV-2. Risk factors associated with environmental contamination were identified using classification tree analysis. Results: Measured HVAC airflow rates were substantially lower than programmed values in three ICUs. CFD simulations suggested that exhaled particles initially rose above the patient, accumulated beneath the ceiling, and subsequently dispersed in the room. SARS-CoV-2 was detected in 14/64 (22%) air samples and 60/134 (45%) surface samples. The most important determinants of environmental contamination were patient viral load, room characteristics, and mode of respiratory support. Environmental contamination was more frequent in rooms with low airflow rates and extraction vents located outside the room. Conclusion: In our ICUs, the main factors associated with environmental detection of SARS-CoV-2 particles were patient airway viral load, the flow rate and location of the exhaust ventilation system, and the use of mechanical ventilation. These results could help guide the renovation or construction of intensive care rooms.

title: Temporal dynamics of antigen-specific T cell expansion in primary SARS-CoV-2 infection
abstract: Abstract Quantifying T cell response during primary infection in humans is crucial for understanding adaptive immunity. Leveraging a controlled human challenge to SARS-CoV-2, we characterized antigen-specific T cell response within and across individuals. Notably, individual clones reached similar maximum frequencies despite differences in the timing of their peak expansion. Mathematical modeling showed that this observation is consistent with precursor frequency, but not TCR signal strength, as the source of inter-clonal variability. Single-cell profiling revealed distinct temporal programs for CD4 + and CD8 + T cells, with CD4 + cells expanding earlier but contracting to a lower frequency. Clones with similar receptors, likely recognizing the same antigen, expanded at similar times. Together, these findings highlight how clone-intrinsic properties such as precursor frequency and lineage shape T cell clonal kinetics. These insights provide a quantitative framework for understanding T cell response in humans, with implications for vaccine design.

title: A retrospective comparative study of antenatal care services before and during the COVID-19 pandemic in rural Gadag district India
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted the delivery and utilization of essential maternal health services worldwide. Restrictions on movement, fear of infection, transportation difficulties, and changes in healthcare service delivery may have affected access to antenatal care (ANC), particularly in rural communities. This study aimed to compare selected indicators of antenatal care service provision and utilization between the Pre-COVID-19 and COVID-19 periods among women residing in selected rural villages of Gadag Taluk, Karnataka. A community-based retrospective comparative study was conducted among 360 eligible women from five selected rural villages of Gadag Taluk. Participants were categorized according to whether their pregnancy occurred during the pre-COVID-19 or COVID-19 study period. Data were collected through household-based interviews using a pretested semi-structured questionnaire. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the data, and the chi-square test was used to compare selected categorical variables between the two periods. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Among the 360 women included in the study, 172 (47.8%) belonged to the pre-COVID-19 group, and 188 (52.2%) belonged to the COVID-19 group. ANC registration in the MCP card declined significantly from 84.9% pre-COVID-19 to 48.4% during the pandemic (χ2=51.532, p < 0.001). The proportion of women receiving ANC check-ups also decreased from 90.7% to 84.6% ( p < 0.001), with significant delays in the timing of the first, second, third, and fourth ANC visits ( p < 0.05 for all). Doctor-led ANC consultations decreased from 96.5% to 78.7%, whereas consultations by ANMs increased from 0.6% to 21.3% (χ2=42.502, p < 0.001). The receipt of food grains from Anganwadi centres declined substantially from 96.5% to 29.8% (χ2=166.360, p < 0.001), while iron sucrose administration decreased from 54.7% to 18.1% (χ2=50.830, p < 0.001). Adherence to four or more ANC visits declined from 83.7% pre-COVID-19 to 65.4% during the pandemic (χ2=15.692, p < 0.001), and IFA tablet receipt decreased from 99.4% to 86.2% (χ2=22.725, p < 0.001). Awareness of ambulance services and tetanus toxoid vaccination remained relatively stable between the two periods. The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with significant disruption of antenatal care service provision and utilization in the study villages in rural areas of study area. Reductions in ANC registration, adherence to recommended visits, doctor-led consultations, nutritional support, iron sucrose administration, and IFA supplementation indicate substantial interruptions in routine maternal healthcare. However, ambulance service awareness and tetanus toxoid vaccination remained relatively stable, suggesting resilience in the selected essential services.

title: EFEITOS NEGATIVOS DA PANDEMIA DE COVID-19: ESTUDO DE CASO EM UMA ESCOLA DE EDUCAÇÃO BÁSICA EM PLANALTINA DF NEGATIVE EFFECTS OF THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC: A CASE STUDY IN A BASIC EDUCATION SCHOOL IN PLANALTINA DF
abstract: As transformações ocorridas com o avanço do Novo Coronavírus, causador da doença COVID-19, provocaram diversas mudanças, atingindo várias áreas da sociedade, seja ela econômica, social e, até mesmo, a educacional. Diante das medidas de distanciamento social, toda a comunidade escolar foi desafiada a se adaptar ao novo contexto, do ensino remoto. O presente trabalho tem como objetivo um estudo de caso sobre os impactos negativos da pandemia e suas consequências na escola CED Stella em Planaltina - DF e como a aprendizagem pode ter sido prejudicada com o cancelamento das aulas presenciais. A metodologia apresenta uma abordagem quali-quantitativa, tratando-se de uma pesquisa básica de observação por meio de questionários. Foi realizada em turmas do Ensino Fundamental e Ensino Médio e com seus respectivos professores, no período pós-pandêmico (1° semestre de 2022). Também foi investigada a situação da evasão escolar. Nos resultados foram identificados impactos negativos da pandemia e com sérias consequências na aprendizagem dos alunos. Ficou clara também a importância em todo o processo de ensino e aprendizagem da presença do professor como mediador do conhecimento. Em relação à evasão escolar, somente dados de 2019 foram compartilhados, indicando uma evasão de 23,2% no 9° ano. Por fim, os prejuízos durante o ensino remoto foram percebidos tanto por discentes quanto docentes e é urgente a necessidade de pensar em estratégias que possam minimizar ou diluir essas deficiências.

title: How Did COVID-19 Affect Urban Slums?
abstract: Abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic, slum settlements received significant attention for their vulnerabilities. To mitigate risks of disease transmission and containment measures, experts called for community-driven solutions. But such approaches frequently neglect pre-existing structures of local leadership in these settlements. How did India’s slum leaders respond to the pandemic? What factors shape their success in helping residents? To answer these questions, we conducted a phone survey of 321 slum leaders in two north Indian cities during India’s stringent 2020 national lockdown. Our survey reveals striking continuities with pre-pandemic politics. Slum leaders persist in their problem-solving roles but tilt efforts toward pandemic response activities. Their effectiveness in doing so remains informed by the same factors that shape efficacy during “normal times,” notably their education and degree of embeddedness in party networks. Finally, pre-pandemic disparities in slum-level infrastructural development shape how much residents must depart from social distancing guidelines to secure essential services.

But such approaches frequently neglect pre-existing structures of local leadership in these settlements. How did India’s slum leaders respond to the pandemic? What factors shape their success in helping residents? To answer these questions, we conducted a phone survey of 321 slum leaders in two north Indian cities during India’s stringent 2020 national lockdown. Our survey reveals striking continuities with pre-pandemic politics. Slum leaders persist in their problem-solving roles but tilt efforts toward pandemic response activities. Their effectiveness in doing so remains informed by the same factors that shape efficacy during “normal times,” notably their education and degree of embeddedness in party networks. Finally, pre-pandemic disparities in slum-level infrastructural development shape how much residents must depart from social distancing guidelines to secure essential services.

title: ‘Reaching and Teaching’: Understanding the Supercomplexity of Primary Teachers’ Work in an Area of High Social Deprivation During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract This chapter explores the supercomplexity of primary teachers’ work in four northern English schools serving communities of high social deprivation during the COVID-19 pandemic. Based on a multiple case study, it shows how teachers’ safeguarding, pastoral and welfare roles expanded during the pandemic, requiring sustained family engagement amid overlapping social, economic and digital disadvantage and in response to shifting policy guidance. Framed by Barnett’s (2000a) notion of supercomplexity, the analysis identifies five overlapping themes: evolving definitions of vulnerability, mediating learning through homes, the emotional labour of care, rapid pedagogical and organisational adaptation and re-evaluation of educational aims beyond high-stakes accountability. While teachers demonstrated remarkable adaptability; developing hybrid provision, restructuring Early Years pedagogy and prioritising wellbeing, the moral weight of this labour remained largely unrecognised in policy. This chapter argues for teacher education and system design that centre adaptability, relational care and professional judgement, positioning teachers as co-constructors of educational meaning and essential agents in building resilience for future crises.
journal: Schools and Families on the Frontline

title: Widening the Gap? The Impact of COVID-19 Restrictions on Education for Students With Special Educational Needs and Disabilities in an English Special School
abstract: Abstract This study explores how COVID-19 restrictions impacted on the provision of education for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), from the point of view of four parents and the headteacher at a special school in the North of England. Thematic analysis of the data through Bronfenbrenner’s bioecological theory and Biesta’s domains of education contextualised the effects of school closures and policies on the people and systems that students engage with, as well as how they both interact with one another. While existing research has largely examined the impact of school closures and remote learning, this case study highlights the critical role of specialist provision in supporting families and maintaining student wellbeing. Findings reveal how the pandemic exacerbated existing inequalities and exposed the marginalisation of SEND learners within policy and practice. The study calls for a radical reframing of education through a social model of disability, advocating for inclusive environments and pedagogies. Although focused on only one special school, insights offer valuable lessons for mainstream and specialist settings alike. Wellbeing must be embedded in educational policy and practice to better support all learners moving forward.
journal: Schools and Families on the Frontline

title: Reimagining Secondary Schools as a Result of the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Qualitative Study
abstract: Abstract This chapter reports the findings of a qualitative study that set out to examine the experiences and priorities of English state-funded secondary schools during the COVID-19 pandemic. It considers how historical and contemporary policy eras have shaped the capacities of schools to respond to the challenges posed by the pandemic. Research took place within three schools with different types of governance: an inner-city new build that is part of a multi-academy trust, a Faith School and a Maintained School. It purposively recruited staff across a range of roles (senior leader, teaching and non-teaching support) to gain a complete picture of school approaches. Findings were as follows: going into the pandemic, each school identified challenges around staff recruitment, budgetary pressures, social deprivation and an increasing special educational needs and disabilities register. In the early days of school closure, schools utilised their existing pastoral structures to support children and families with varying degrees of success. As the pandemic evolved, all staff found themselves taking on new activities outside of their remit, which enabled a better understanding of the families and communities that they served. The authors conclude that in taking almost total responsibility for the welfare of pupils and their families during the pandemic, participating schools – whatever their governance – continued to resist neoliberal-driven educational policy that focuses purely on the classroom and excellent teaching. Learning from the pandemic suggests that there is a strong case to re-imagine schools as integral to communities and furthermore, that there is an appetite to achieve this.
journal: Schools and Families on the Frontline

title: Skeletal Muscle Cell Necrosis in Individuals with SARS-CoV-2 Infection: An Autopsy Study
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 infection is linked to systemic symptoms beyond the respiratory tract, including muscle weakness, muscle pain, and fatigue (1). The underlying histopathological reasons for the involvement of skeletal muscle in coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) remain incompletely understood. In the present study, we examined skeletal muscle obtained at autopsy from a subgroup of people who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 and assessed the degree of myofiber necrosis, inflammation, and the immunohistochemical reactivity for the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein. The main morphological finding was degeneration and necrosis of myofibers often in a focal or discontinuous manner affecting single fibers or a group of fibers, while neighboring fibers were fairly well preserved. The inflammatory infiltrates were generally scarce. The immunoreactivity for the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein varied. There was no clear correlation between the intensity of the staining and the severity of the myofiber necrosis. Necrotic changes were found in both the groups that had been hospitalized for a long time and those that had been hospitalized for a short time or not at all, which suggests that critical illness myopathy cannot account for all the lesions observed. These results point to an atypical pattern of skeletal muscle damage in individuals who are positive for SARS-CoV-2 at the time of autopsy, a pattern that is mostly free from inflammation, and thus calls for further investigation into neurogenic, vascular, and other indirect mechanisms of muscle damage during both the acute and the post-acute phases of COVID-19.

title: Impact of the coronavirus disease 2019 ( COVID ‐19) pandemic and stringency index on the dispensation of human immunodeficiency virus post‐exposure prophylaxis in Brazil: A retrospective study
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic substantially affected healthcare systems worldwide and may have compromised access to human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) prevention strategies, including post-exposure prophylaxis (HIV-PEP). However, evidence regarding temporal changes in HIV-PEP dispensation and their association with restrictive governmental measures in Brazil remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the dynamics of HIV-PEP dispensation in Brazil before, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic and to investigate its temporal association with the COVID-19 Stringency Index. METHODS: This retrospective epidemiological study used secondary data from the Brazilian Ministry of Health HIV-PEP Monitoring Panel between 2018 and 2024. The study period was categorized into pre-pandemic (until February 2020), pandemic (March 2020 to May 2023) and post-Public Health Emergency of International Concern (post-PHEIC; from June 2023 onward) periods. An interrupted time-series analysis (ITSA) using negative binomial regression was performed to evaluate temporal changes in HIV-PEP dispensation, including immediate-level changes and changes in trends associated with the pandemic and post-PHEIC periods. Additional generalized linear mixed-effects models were used to evaluate factors associated with the volume of recorded HIV-PEP dispensation events, with a random intercept for Brazilian state. Data on the COVID-19 Stringency Index were obtained from the Oxford COVID-19 Government Response Tracker. Exploratory analyses using negative binomial regression and Spearman correlation were performed to evaluate the temporal association between the Stringency Index and HIV-PEP dispensation. RESULTS: From 2018 to 2024, 863 201 HIV-PEP dispensation events were recorded in Brazil, most frequently in the Southeast region (54%). Consensual sexual exposure accounted for most dispensation events (69%), followed by accidents involving biological material (26%). Before the pandemic, HIV-PEP dispensation showed an increasing temporal trend (rate ratio [RR] = 1.019; 95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 1.015, 1.024). At the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, an immediate reduction in the number of recorded HIV-PEP dispensation events was observed (RR = 0.657; 95% CI: 0.604, 0.714). The volume of dispensations subsequently resumed an increasing trajectory during both the pandemic (RR = 1.016; 95% CI: 1.014, 1.018) and post-PHEIC periods (RR = 1.013; 95% CI: 1.006, 1.020), although the observed trajectory remained below the pre-pandemic trajectory. In the adjusted mixed-effects model, the expected number of recorded HIV-PEP dispensation events was lower during both the pandemic (RR = 0.74; 95% CI: 0.71, 0.76) and post-PHEIC periods (RR = 0.75; 95% CI: 0.71, 0.79). In the primary temporal model, the Stringency Index was inversely associated with HIV-PEP dispensation (RR = 0.968; 95% CI: 0.961, 0.974). However, this association was no longer statistically significant after the pandemic onset was incorporated into the segmented sensitivity model (RR = 0.990; 95% CI: 0.980, 1.001), indicating that the association was not robust across all model specifications. CONCLUSION: HIV-PEP dispensation in Brazil showed an increasing trend before the COVID-19 pandemic, followed by an immediate reduction at pandemic onset and a subsequent recovery that remained below the model-based counterfactual trajectory. Although the Stringency Index was inversely associated with HIV-PEP dispensation in the primary exploratory model, this association was not statistically significant after adjustment for pandemic onset. These findings should therefore be interpreted as temporal associations rather than evidence of independent or causal effects.

title: Determinants of Auto-medication among People with Symptoms Related to COVID-19 in Yaoundé, Cameroon: A Qualitative Study
abstract: Background: Since the emergence of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), many people with symptoms suggestive of the disease have followed therapeutic routes outside the formal healthcare system. Auto-medication, the use of any remedy without the advice of a health professional, is widespread in sub-Saharan Africa. Understanding why people avoided formal care during COVID-19 remains essential for preparedness against future epidemics. This study aimed to analyse the determinants of auto-medication among people with symptoms related to COVID-19 in Yaoundé, Cameroon. Methods: A phenomenological qualitative study was conducted between July and September 2020. Data were collected through the triangulation of three techniques: direct observation in four households in different neighbourhoods of Yaoundé, semi-structured individual interviews with 12 purposively selected residents (until saturation), and one 90-minute focus group discussion with 10 participants (4 women, 6 men). Data were analysed thematically and interpreted through the Health Belief Model (HBM) and commitment theory. Results: Participants were informed about the symptoms and barrier measures of COVID-19, so auto-medication did not stem from a lack of knowledge. Seven of the 12 interviewees usually treated flu-like symptoms with herbal remedies, four used roadside drug sellers and one used a health facility. Determinants were behavioural, psychological, socio-economic, socio-cultural and health-system-related. Through the HBM lens, two opposite pathways led to the same behaviour: participants who denied or minimised the disease saw no need for formal care, while those who feared it saw the hospital itself as a threat. In both cases, the perceived barriers to formal care (isolation and lost income, stigma, fear of contamination in hospitals and the non-return of bodies for religious burial) outweighed its perceived benefits, whereas home remedies were seen as familiar, affordable and within personal control. Cues to action came mainly from neighbours, relatives, social media and religious figures rather than from health authorities. Conclusion: Auto-medication was a reasoned response to the perceived costs of formal care rather than simple ignorance. Future epidemic responses should lower these costs through income support during isolation, community-based and home-based testing, safe and dignified burials designed with religious leaders, visibly safe health facilities, and partnerships with trusted community messengers and informal drug providers.
journal: International Journal of TROPICAL DISEASE & Health

title: Can Financial Incentives Reduce Declared COVID-19 Vaccine Refusal? Survey Evidence from Poland
abstract: Aim: To examine the declared potential of financial public-policy instruments among Polish vaccine refusers and identify behavioural factors associated with vaccination status. Methodology: A cross-sectional CAWI survey (Poland, 2021, N = 800) distinguished four vaccination attitude levels. Declared responses to financial instruments were tested with non-parametric methods, incentive susceptibility with rank correlation and linear regression, and vaccination status with exploratory models. Findings: The vaccination lottery was rated low across all groups. Differences among the vaccinated, the hesitant, and those intending to get vaccinated were not significant. For vaccine refusers, no tested financial incentive was rated as likely to change their reported decision; loss-framed incentives were rated higher than gain-framed ones, yet both remained near the lower end of the scale. Implications: The results indicated the limited declared potential of individual financial incentives among vaccine refusers, raising questions about the efficiency of public spending for this group. Originality/value: The article adds a behavioural perspective to research on COVID-19 vaccination incentives. Refusers placed little importance on financial benefits, while exploratory models linked vaccination status to vaccine safety beliefs, severe COVID-19 in someone close, and political identification.
