title: Spatially autocorrelated and clustered associations between short-term exposure to PM2.5 and daily reported confirmed COVID-19 cases across the contiguous United States, 2020–2022
abstract: Background Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is a highly transmissible respiratory infection that has caused a global pandemic. Evidence for the effect of short-term PM 2.5 exposure on COVID-19 incidence varied across regions, and few studies have used advanced spatial analysis methods to examine spatial autocorrelation or clustering in these associations to improve estimation accuracy and identify highly susceptible geographic regions. Methods In this study, we used a novel three-stage strategy, including generalized additive model (GAM) and the newly developed estimation-error-based scan statistic (EESS) and multivariate conditional meta-autoregression (MCMAR), to fill the gap across the contiguous United States. Results We found there was significant spatial heterogeneity ( I 2 = 67.416 % , P < 0.001 ), autocorrelation ( ρ = 0.972 , P < 0.001 ), and clustering (four clusters were discovered, P ≤ 0.011 ) in the associations between short-term exposure to PM 2.5 and daily reported confirmed COVID-19 cases. Considering the spatial autocorrelation and the spatial clustering effectively improved the fitting results of meta-regression. The pooled relative risk (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CI) for per 10 μg/m 3 increase in PM 2.5 were 1.0341 and (1.0308, 1.0375). The RRs (95% CIs) for per 10 μg/m 3 increase in PM 2.5 were 1.0107 (1.0074, 1.0140), 1.1770 (1.1551, 1.1992), 1.0005 (0.9984, 1.0026), 1.0719 (1.0566, 1.0875), and 1.1032 (1.0798, 1.1270) in baseline and clusters 1–4, respectively. By 30 June 2022, a total of 1,761,726 (95% CI: 1,583,970–1,916,779; accounting for 2.06%, 95% CI: 1.85–2.24%) COVID-19 cases were found to be related to elevated PM 2.5 exposure relative to the WHO annual mean PM 2.5 guideline threshold of 5 μg/m 3 across the contiguous United States. The eastern region and central region exhibited greater RR, greater attributable risk percentage, and more attributable cases than the western coastal region. Conclusion There was significant spatial heterogeneity, autocorrelation, and clustering in the associations between short-term exposure to PM 2.5 and daily reported confirmed COVID-19 cases across the contiguous United States.

title: P-04: Incidence of pediatric type 1 diabetes beyond the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Abstract Introduction In Germany, as in many countries, the incidence of pediatric type 1 diabetes (T1D) increased during the first years after the COVID-19 emergence (2020-2022), especially in young children. Objectives To follow the course of pediatric T1D incidence in Germany beyond the acute COVID-19 pandemic. Methods Data of children and adolescents aged 0.5-17 years from the German multicenter Diabetes Prospective Follow-up (DPV-) registry, capturing >90% of pediatric cases with diabetes, with clinical onset of T1D between 2011 and 2025 were analyzed. Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for the single years 2020-2025 and for the whole period were estimated based on the pre-pandemic trend from 2011-2019. Results 43,649 children and adolescents were included (55.1% male, 25.3% with migration background). Median age at diagnosis was 9.8 years pre- and post-pandemic, but 9.3 years during the acute pandemic (2020-2022). T1D incidence increased from 17.6 [95%-CI: 16.9-18.3] in 2011 to 22.1 [21.3-22.8] cases / 100,000 person-years in 2019 (relative annual increase: 2.1% [0.8-3.4]). Based on this trend, the observed incidence was significantly higher than expected in 2020 (IRR: 1.15 [1.09-1.21]), 2021 (1.23 [1.17-1.29]) and 2022 (1.15 [1.09-1.20]), but significantly lower than expected in 2023 (0.93 [0.89-0.98]), 2024 (0.84 [0.80-0.89]) and 2025 (0.85 [0.81-0.90]). The IRR for 2020-2025 combined was 1.02 [1.00-1.04], p=0.058. The age-stratified IRRs for 2020-2025 combined were 1.22 [1.17-1.27] in children aged <6 years, 1.01 [0.98-1.04] in children aged 6-<12 years and 0.90 [0.87-0.93] in adolescents aged 12-<18 years. Conclusions These preliminary data suggest that there is no substantial persistent increase in T1D incidence beyond the expected level when combining all years since the COVID-19 pandemic. Together with the temporary decrease in onset age and the different IRRs by age group this suggests a wave-like T1D incidence pattern that might have (nearly) normalized as of 2025.

title: Integrated Molecular and Serological Epizootic Monitoring of SARS-CoV-2 and Influenza A Virus in Animals in Kazakhstan
abstract: Respiratory viruses with broad host ranges are relevant to veterinary epidemiology, biological safety, and One Health surveillance. This retrospective study integrated companion-animal and wildlife records to examine two complementary surveillance questions: SARS-CoV-2 detection in dogs and cats with close human contact, and influenza A virus detection across a broader multispecies panel that included wild birds. We analyzed 256 archived animal samples collected in Kazakhstan during 2022–2023, comprising 158 dogs, 76 cats, and 22 animals of other domestic and wild species. A previously developed in-house multiplex RT-qPCR assay was used to detect SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus RNA, and a previously developed in-house SM-antigen-based ELISA was used to assess SARS-CoV-2-associated serum reactivity. SARS-CoV-2 RNA was detected in 104/256 samples (40.6%; 95% CI, 34.8–46.7), including 68 dogs and 36 cats. Influenza A virus RNA was detected in four wild birds (1.6%): two partridges and two mallards. According to the assay-specific classification recorded in the source dataset, 34 sera were reactive, 14 were doubtful, and 208 were non-reactive. All SARS-CoV-2 RT-qPCR-positive samples were ELISA-non-reactive; all reactive or doubtful ELISA results occurred among RT-qPCR-negative animals. Dogs and cats did not differ significantly in SARS-CoV-2 RT-qPCR positivity, ELISA reactivity, or Ct distributions. Because the ELISA had not been formally validated for the animal species studied, reactivity was not interpreted as confirmed SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity. The archived 2022–2023 dataset therefore provides a historical baseline for multispecies respiratory-virus surveillance in Kazakhstan and supports cautious integration of molecular and serological data.

title: COVID-19 in the Village
abstract: Abstract This chapter examines why frontline health workers played such uneven roles in India’s rural COVID-19 response. Focusing on Accredited Social Health Activists, Anganwadi workers, and Auxiliary Nurse Midwives, it conceptualizes frontline workers as hybrid actors positioned between local communities and the state. Drawing on interviews with workers and officials, a multistate survey, and grassroots video documentation, the chapter shows that pandemic responses rose or fell with hybrid actors’ social standing and institutional support. Many frontline health workers were doubly constrained—by weak backing from state agencies and by entrenched inequalities of caste, class, and gender—leaving them exposed, overburdened, and unable to deliver reliable care or welfare. Others were doubly empowered, combining bureaucratic authority with community trust, and so were able to mobilize resources, enforce public health measures, and extend assistance more equitably. The chapter argues that inequalities affecting frontline workers are a central but overlooked feature of crisis response and identifies the conditions under which local intermediaries might reduce, rather than reproduce, social exclusion.

title: Health resort-based versus home-based rehabilitation for post-COVID-19 syndrome
abstract: Background Post-COVID-19 syndrome, presents a significant rehabilitation challenge due to the multifaceted nature of symptoms, including dyspnea, fatigue, and cognitive dysfunction. Objectives This study aimed to compare the effect of an intensive Health Resort-based rehabilitation program versus a monitored home-based rehabilitation program in patients with Post-COVID-19 syndrome. Methods Patients with confirmed Post-COVID-19 syndrome were assigned to either a Health Resort-based rehabilitation program ( N = 33), which included inhalation therapy, aquatic and land-based exercises; or a home-based rehabilitation program ( N = 33). Assessments were performed at baseline, post-treatment, and at 3- and 6-month follow-ups. Outcome measures included quality of life, perceived dyspnea, motor function, perceived pain, fatigue, psychological status and cognitive function. Results Linear mixed effects regression model analysis revealed that both interventions improved symptoms. Statistically significant time-by-group interactions indicated that the Health Resort-based rehabilitation group achieved greater improvements compared to the home-based rehabilitation group in perceived dyspnea, bilateral hand grip strength, and anxiety. Both groups showed comparable improvements in fatigue, pain, functional limitations due to dyspnea, lower limb function, cognitive function, and quality of life, with benefits maintained during follow-up. Conclusions Both Health Resort-based and home-based rehabilitation are effective modalities of care delivery for Post-COVID-19 syndrome management, where integrated and multimodal interventions are required, with the Health Resort-based rehabilitation option providing additional benefits.

title: Beyond vestibular recovery: Functional gait improvement through sensorimotor adaptation after COVID-19
abstract: Introduction: Vestibular neuritis leads to deficits in postural control and gait stability. Recovery is often assumed to depend on restoration of vestibular function; however, emerging evidence suggests that functional mobility may improve through adaptive sensorimotor mechanisms even in the presence of persistent vestibular deficits. This study examined the relationship between vestibular recovery and functional improvements in postural control and gait following rehabilitation that included adaptation exercises and habituation, with and without biofeedback, in a patient recovering from a COVID-19 infection. Methods: A 54-year-old patient with vestibular neuritis, diagnosed 3 weeks after contracting COVID-19, underwent a personalized rehabilitation program emphasizing gaze stabilization, dynamic balance, and gait adaptability. Assessments were conducted at baseline (T0), 6 weeks (T1), and 6 months (T2). Outcome measures included the Dizziness Handicap Inventory (DHI), Activities-specific Balance Confidence (ABC) scale, Zur Balance Scale, and Dynamic Gait Index (DGI). Vestibular function was assessed using the video head impulse test to assess vestibular-ocular reflex VOR) gain and the functional head impulse test (fHIT). Results: Substantial improvements were observed in functional domains despite incomplete vestibular recovery. DHI improved from 40 % to 0 %, and ABC increased from 35 % to 97.5 %. Postural control improved from 66 % of normal for the age-matched group to 100 %. Gait performance normalized, with the DGI increasing from 17 (fall risk) to 24. In contrast, VOR gain on the affected side improved only partially (0.3–0.73), and fHIT improved from 30 % initially to 80 % at 6 months. This difference indicates that recovery of gait and postural control exceeded the degree of peripheral vestibular restoration. Conclusions: Functional recovery following vestibular neuritis after COVID-19 infection may be driven more by sensorimotor adaptation than by normalization of vestibular input. These findings challenge a vestibular-centric model of recovery and highlight the importance of targeting dynamic stability and gait adaptability in rehabilitation.

title: A Refined Search of SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease Inhibitors as COVID-19 Antivirals
abstract: Abstract MPI8 was among one of the first SARS-CoV-2 main protease (MPro) inhibitors with strong antiviral potency. Building on its peptidomimetic aldehyde scaffold, we retained the P2 3-cyclohexylalanine and P3 O-tert-butylthreonine elements, which support S2 binding, S-subsite engagement, and likely cellular permeability, and varied the S4/S1′ substituents and covalent warheads. SAR and co-crystal structures identified compact N-terminal carbamates or amides bearing cyclopropane, isopropyl, or trifluoromethyl groups as favorable S4 binders. Benzoxazole/benzothiazole-carbonyl groups and acyloxymethyl ketones were explored as S1′-engaging motifs, with one benzoxazole-containing structure confirming tight S1′ packing by crystal structure. Nitrile and 2-amino-2-oxyacetyl warheads provided viable alternatives to the parent aldehyde. Combining optimized S4 groups with alternative warheads or S1′ motifs yielded multiple inhibitors more potent than MPI8. Notably, MPI-131 showed an IC50 of 1.7 nM, strong antiviral potency, and CC50 of 60.2 μM, placing it among the most potent MPro inhibitors reported.

title: CALCULADORA DE EVOLUÇÃO DA COVID-19 NO SCRATCH
abstract: A disseminação da Covid-19 no Brasil provocou um aumento significativo na quantidade de infectados e mortos em 2020. Por este motivo, propomos um estudo sobre a evolução dos modelos epidemiológicos básicos aplicados ao ensino de Matemática. Estudaremos sobre os modelos SIR, SEIR e SECIAR. A partir do modelo SIR, incluímos o grupo dos expostos, gerando o modelo SEIR. Com base neste novo modelo SEIR, acrescentamos a classe dos contaminados e assintomáticos, dando origem ao SECIAR. As simulações realizadas para cada modelo representam períodos de evolução da doença. Utilizaremos o método de Runge-Kutta de primeira ordem para calcular as iterações. A inserção dessa problemática em sala de aula pode produzir resultados satisfatórios quanto ao ensino das operações básicas e demais assuntos relacionados. Por isso, recorremos às equações de diferenças. A calculadora criada no Scratch foi utilizada para determinar os valores das variáveis em determinado período. Os gráficos obtidos no Octave foram fundamentais para a confirmação dos resultados da calculadora. Com isso, estamos reformulando um tema do Ensino Superior, com o objetivo de aplicação na Educação Básica.

title: Bayesian Spatio-temporal Modeling of Multi-Site Wastewater Surveillance Data
abstract: Wastewater surveillance provides population-level evidence of infectious disease activity. As surveillance expands across multiple sites, repeated measurements must be analyzed jointly while accounting for differences among sites and the public health regions they represent. We develop a Bayesian spatio-temporal framework that decomposes wastewater measurements into a shared epidemic curve, spatially correlated regional deviations, persistent site effects, and within-site temporal dependence. This hierarchical decomposition accommodates unequal observation windows and sampling schedules, allowing regional trajectories to be compared while preserving site-level heterogeneity. A direct marginal spatial covariance specification further separates the magnitude of regional variation from the strength of association between neighboring regions, providing distinct interpretations of these two sources of spatial variation. We also introduce region-specific time shifts to distinguish regional leads and lags in epidemic timing from differences in signal levels and local fluctuations. Simulation studies demonstrate the recovery of these components and show that omitting true time shifts can lead to increased estimates of residual temporal variation. Application to Ontario SARS-CoV-2 wastewater surveillance data reveals persistent site heterogeneity, within-site temporal dependence, and spatial association among neighboring regions. Regional timing differences are more pronounced during the first year of Omicron than in the XBB-and-later period.

title: A systematic benchmarking of deep transfer learning architectures and optimization strategies for COVID-19 detection from lung ultrasound images
abstract: Introduction The COVID-19 pandemic imposed severe burdens on global health infrastructure, underscoring the urgent need for rapid, reliable, and scalable diagnostic technologies. Conventional radiological modalities such as chest X-rays and computed tomography (CT) face critical deployment barriers, including ionizing radiation exposure, elevated procedural costs, and substantial infection-control risks in resource-constrained settings. Lung ultrasound (LUS) presents a compelling alternative owing to its portability, absence of ionizing radiation, and suitability for point-of-care application; however, systematic analysis of deep learning architectures optimized for LUS-based COVID-19 classification remains limited. Methods To address this gap, this study presents a comprehensive benchmarking framework in which 13 pretrained convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures—AlexNet, VGG-16, VGG-19, ResNet-50, ResNet-101, ResNet-152, DenseNet-121, DenseNet-169, DenseNet-201, InceptionV3, Inception-ResNetV2, MobileNetV2, and Xception—were evaluated under seven gradient-based optimization strategies: SGD, Adagrad, RMSProp, Adadelta, Adam, AdaMax, and Nadam. Transfer learning was applied uniformly across all architectures to compensate for the limited scale of the publicly available POCOVID-Net dataset, which comprised 455 LUS frames from confirmed COVID-19 cases and 226 frames from non-COVID subjects. In addition, geometric transformation-based data augmentation was employed to mitigate the effects of class imbalance and improve inter-patient generalization. Results Among the architecture–optimizer combinations evaluated under the hold-out scenario, DenseNet-121 with the Adam optimizer achieved perfect classification with 100% accuracy, surpassing all previously reported LUS-based COVID-19 detection methods evaluated under comparable single-dataset conditions. Given the risk that a single hold-out split may overstate performance, rigorous stratified 5-fold cross-validation was subsequently performed on this best-performing hold-out model to ensure robustness and address concerns regarding overfitting. This yielded a mean accuracy of 99.11% ± 0.35%, sensitivity of 99.41% ± 0.31%, specificity of 99.18% ± 0.38%, F1-score of 99.36% ± 0.29%, and AUC of 99.45% ± 0.25%. Discussion/Conclusion Despite consistently strong performance across both evaluation schemes, these results were derived from a single, limited-diversity public dataset and, therefore, represent a methodological benchmark rather than a validated estimate of real-world performance. External multicenter validation is necessary before clinical application of the model. Nonetheless, the evaluated DenseNet-121 framework holds practical utility as a rapid triage aid and complementary screening tool within clinical workflows, particularly in low-resource environments where CT infrastructure is unavailable.

title: Respiratory muscle strength, lung function and persistent symptoms of COVID-19 in hospitalized and non-hospitalized individuals one year after infection
abstract: Introduction: COVID-19, emerging in 2019, caused millions of cases and left many patients with persistent symptoms, such as fatigue and shortness of breath, affecting daily functioning and quality of life. Objectives: To evaluate respiratory muscle strength, lung function, and persistent COVID-19 symptoms in hospitalized and non-hospitalized individuals one year after infection. Methods: A cross-sectional study included 160 participants (80 hospitalized, 80 non-hospitalized) in Fortaleza, Ceará (2021–2024). Assessments included manovacuometry, spirometry, and a questionnaire on persistent symptoms by organ system. Results: Participants’ mean age was 55.8 ± 15.87 years and BMI 28.85 ± 4.85 kg/m2. Comorbidities were present in 37.5% of hospitalized participants, mainly cardiovascular diseases (27.5%). Persistent symptoms occurred in 42.5% of hospitalized and 45% of non-hospitalized individuals (p = 0.716). Fatigue was more frequent in non-hospitalized participants (42.5% vs. Hospitalized individuals showed lower forced vital capacity (FVC) (60.01 ± 11.14%) compared to non-hospitalized (89.02 ± 10.94%, p = 0.021). Predictors of persistent symptoms included BMI (OR: 1.07, p = 0.001) and comorbidities (OR: 2.08, p = 0.040) in hospitalized participants, and acute-phase symptoms (OR: 4.05) and comorbidities (OR: 2.00) in non-hospitalized participants. Conclusions: One year post-infection, persistent symptoms were common, with fatigue predominating in non-hospitalized individuals. Hospitalized participants showed greater restrictive lung impairment. Predictors of prolonged symptoms differed between groups, highlighting the need for tailored follow-up strategies. Post- Acute COVID-19 Syndrome. Respiratory Function Tests.

title: Latent classes of family vulnerability and associations with parental functioning during the COVID-19 pandemic.
abstract: This study examined prepandemic patterns of family vulnerability and their associations with parental outcomes during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using longitudinal data from 918 families in Norway, recruited through family counseling services, we applied latent class analysis to 16 indicators spanning contextual (e.g., socioeconomic disadvantage), interpersonal (e.g., low support, interparental conflict), and personal (e.g., mental health problems) domains. Analyses were conducted separately for families where parents lived together and those where parents lived apart. Across both family structures, three distinct vulnerability classes emerged: a well-adapted group (low risk) and two elevated-risk groups differing by domain. Among families living apart, the elevated-risk classes included a low collaboration group and a complex risk group characterized by cumulative vulnerabilities. Among families living together, elevated-risk classes included an interpersonal risk group and a contextual risk group. During the pandemic, families in the complex risk and contextual risk groups reported significantly higher parenting stress and poorer mental health than well-adapted families, whereas low collaboration and interpersonal risk groups were not consistently linked to poorer outcomes. Findings underscore the importance of considering multidimensional vulnerability patterns and family structure when assessing risk and tailoring interventions to support families during large-scale disruptions. title: Para-Aortic Adipose Tissue and Severe COVID-19: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Obesity is a well-established risk factor for severe COVID-19, largely mediated by chronic inflammation originating from adipose tissue. The role of para-aortic adipose tissue (PAT)—a component of perivascular adipose tissue in COVID-19 severity remains poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the association between PAT area and the severity of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, and whether it provides information beyond established clinical and laboratory factors. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 279 hospitalized patients with confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia. Based on disease severity, patients were divided into moderate and severe groups. PAT area was measured semi-automatically on a single chest CT slice. Sequential multivariable logistic regression models were fitted: Model 1 (PAT alone), Model 2 (PAT + age + sex), Model 3 (primary; PAT + age + sex + BMI), Model 4 (Model 3 + smoking + diabetes + hypertension), and Model 5 (Model 4 + CRP + NLR). Collinearity was assessed using the variance inflation factor (VIF). Effect estimates for PAT were expressed per 0.1 cm2 increase. Results: In the unadjusted model (n = 279), PAT area was associated with severe COVID-19 (OR 1.19 per 0.1 cm2; 95% CI 1.01–1.40; p = 0.038). After adjustment for age and sex, the association was no longer significant (OR 1.10; 95% CI 0.91–1.33; p = 0.325). In the primary model adjusted for age, sex, and BMI (n = 279, with multiple imputation for missing BMI, CRP, and NLR), PAT was not independently associated with severe disease (OR 0.95; 95% CI 0.77–1.17; p = 0.644), while BMI (OR 1.10 per 1 kg/m2; 95% CI 1.04–1.16; p = 0.001), age (OR 1.03; 95% CI 1.01–1.05; p = 0.003), and male sex (OR 1.81; 95% CI 1.00–3.28; p = 0.057) remained associated. The association between PAT and severity was non-linear (p for non-linearity = 0.042). Firth-corrected estimates were virtually identical (OR 0.96; 95% CI 0.79–1.18; p = 0.705), and no influential observations were identified. Conclusions: In this cohort, PAT area measured on a single chest CT slice was not independently associated with severe COVID-19 after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI. The association was non-linear, and the linear estimate was unstable across models due to varying effective sample sizes. BMI, age, and male sex remained the strongest factors. Prospective studies using volumetric or attenuation-based measures of perivascular adipose tissue are needed to clarify its role.

source_records.title: Para-Aortic Adipose Tissue and Severe COVID-19: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
source_records.abstract: Background/Objectives: Obesity is a well-established risk factor for severe COVID-19, largely mediated by chronic inflammation originating from adipose tissue. The role of para-aortic adipose tissue (PAT)—a component of perivascular adipose tissue in COVID-19 severity remains poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the association between PAT volume and the severity of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and to evaluate its potential as a predictor of severe COVID-19. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 279 hospitalized patients with confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia. Based on disease severity, patients were divided into moderate and severe groups. PAT volume was measured around the aorta semi-automatically on a single chest computed tomography. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging data were analyzed. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were performed to assess the predictive value of PAT volume. Results: Patients with severe COVID-19 were significantly older, had higher body mass index. PAT volume differed significantly between groups, with a greater proportion of higher values in the severe group. Severe cases also exhibited significantly elevated levels of C-reactive protein, ferritin, and D-dimer, and lower oxygen saturation. Correlation analysis revealed significant associations between PAT volume and age, BMI, ferritin, the extent of lung involvement and SpO2. Multivariable logistic regression confirmed that log-transformed PAT volume was independently associated with severe COVID-. The optimal threshold for initial PAT volume was 0.35 cm3 (sensitivity: 51.2%, specificity: 67.1%). Conclusions: PAT volume is independently associated with severe COVID-19, and values exceeding 0.35 cm3 may serve as a predictor of disease severity in hospitalized patients.

title: Effect of Intranasal Administration of SARS-CoV-2 ORF8 Accessory Protein on the First Line of Antioxidant Defense in Male BALB/c Mice
abstract: Several viruses, including severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), induce the production of reactive oxygen species, which damage host cells and facilitate viral replication. The main differences between this coronavirus and SARS-CoV-2 lie in their spike, ORF3a, and ORF8 proteins. ORF8 is an accessory protein associated with immune evasion and the induction of severe inflammation, but little is known about its effect on the first line of antioxidant defense: superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT). In this chapter, we describe the effect on the first line of antioxidant defense following inoculation of the heterologous SARS-CoV-2 protein ORF8 into male BALB/c mice. We administered 25 μg of ORF8 protein in 25 μL intranasally on three occasions, with a seven-day interval between inoculations. At two and eight weeks postinoculation (short-term and long-term, respectively), SOD and CAT enzyme activities were analyzed in various tissues (hepatic, pulmonary, renal, prefrontal cortex, and cardiac). For SOD activity in the lungs and kidneys, TIME had a significant effect (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01, respectively). Regarding the CAT results, a significant ORF8 × TIME interaction was found in the prefrontal cortex (p < 0.05). In the lungs and heart, TIME had a significant effect (p < 0.01 and p < 0.05, respectively). With these data, it is clear that inoculation with the ORF8 protein induces oxidative stress in various organs and triggers the activation of the primary antioxidant defense line in the kidneys, lungs, and heart in the short term; additionally, the prefrontal cortex is affected over time, and there is an interaction between the ORF8 × TIME factors.

title: Riesgos laborales en profesionales de la salud bucal durante la pandemia de COVID-19: revisión sistemática Occupational risks among oral health professionals during the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre los riesgos laborales de los profesionales de la salud bucal durante la pandemia de COVID-19 y las medidas propuestas para controlarlos. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones, ensayos clínicos, estudios transversales y retrospectivos. Resultados: el riesgo biológico por aerosoles, gotas y contacto estrecho fue el principal riesgo descrito, seguido de las exposiciones a sangre y punzocortantes y del riesgo psicosocial, con agotamiento profesional y percepción elevada de riesgo. Las medidas incluyeron triaje, equipos de protección, control de aerosoles y colutorios previos al procedimiento. Conclusión: la pandemia aumentó y diversificó los riesgos laborales en odontología, por lo que se requieren protocolos permanentes de bioseguridad y de protección de la salud mental.

title: COVID-19 in the States
abstract: Abstract This chapter analyzes how the COVID-19 pandemic tested democratic capabilities at the subnational level. It argues that the crisis exposed not only core dimensions of state capacity but also the relational forms of power needed to secure public cooperation in highly unequal societies. It shows that national-level analyses overlook these dynamics by focusing narrowly on formal democracy and fixed bureaucratic resources, whereas the subnational level better captures how state agencies interact with civil society to coordinate high-touch health and welfare responses. It explains why state governments in India became the central actors during the pandemic and how political competition, state–society relations, and local institutions shaped state performance in health and welfare responses. These factors were key in mobilizing resources, inducing compliance, and mitigating inequalities. In doing so, the chapter demonstrates that subnational democratic capabilities are critical both for crisis response and for strengthening equitable state action more broadly.

title: Symptom-based phenotypes and health-related quality of life in Spanish patients with long COVID: a latent class analysis
abstract: Long COVID presents with heterogeneous, fluctuating symptoms that markedly reduce health-related quality of life (HRQol). This study aimed to identify symptom-based subgroups of patients with Long COVID using Latent Class Analysis (LCA) and to compare health-related quality of life across the identified classes. A cross-sectional study was conducted in Salamanca, Spain. Adults with Long COVID per WHO criteria were recruited from primary care and a specialized post-COVID unit. Sociodemographic, clinical, and symptom data ( ad hoc checklist) were collected; HRQoL was assessed using the SF-36. Latent Class Analysis identified symptom-based groups; model selection was based on BIC, entropy, and interpretability. Classes were compared on sociodemographic, clinical, and HRQoL variables. A total of 304 participants were included in the analysis (68.1% women; mean age 52.7 ± 11.9 years). Four classes were identified: Class 1 (28.9%) high multisystem symptom burden; Class 2 (20.1%) low symptom burden; Class 3 (25.3%) moderate neuropsychiatric and sleep-related symptoms; and Class 4 (25.7%) moderate physical-respiratory symptoms. HRQoL differed across classes in all SF-36 domains ( p < 0.001). Class 1 had the lowest scores [physical functioning 34.97 (95% CI: 32.56–37.38); vitality 28.98 (27.21–30.75); social functioning 26.31 (23.27–29.34); mental health 38.14 (35.61–40.67)], whilst Class 2 had the highest scores [52.36 (50.84–53.88); 46.85 (44.47–49.23); 47.07 (44.41–49.72); and 50.04 (48.04–52.04), respectively]. PCS and MCS scores were also lower in Class 1 [30.73 (28.50–32.96) and 35.07 (31.93–38.22), respectively] and higher in Class 2 [48.49 (46.32–50.65) and 48.49 (45.76–51.23), respectively]. Classes 3 and 4 showed intermediate patterns of quality of life, with lower scores in Class 3 compared with Class 4 in terms of social functioning, emotional role and mental health. LCA identified four distinct latent classes based on symptoms, which differ in symptom burden and predominant symptom patterns, and are associated with differences in health-related quality of life. These findings provide a better understanding of the clinical heterogeneity of long COVID. However, the classes are exploratory and sample-specific. The results need to be replicated in independent cohorts and in longitudinal studies. Clinical trial registration Clinicaltrials.gov , Identifier NCT05819840.

title: Robust T and B cell activation is associated with rapid clearance of infectious SARS-CoV-2
abstract: The immunologic correlates of rapid clearance of SARS-CoV-2 shedding are not well understood, partly due to challenges of collecting samples early after infection and the fact that most studies do not measure infectious virus. Here, we performed mass cytometry profiling of peripheral blood cells collected from people 4-6 days after onset of symptoms from acute SARS-CoV-2 infection who underwent daily nasopharyngeal testing for SARS-CoV-2 culture positivity. We identified broad and coordinated activation of innate and adaptive immune cells in unvaccinated individuals with primary infection. Faster clearance of infectious virus shedding was associated with robust adaptive immune cell activation and proliferation, namely among cytotoxic CD8+, CD4+, and γδ T cells and plasmablasts. In contrast, vaccinated individuals who rapidly cleared breakthrough infection showed minimal cellular immune activation. Our findings identify early immune correlates of rapid clearance of infectious SARS-CoV-2 shedding that may inform future prevention and therapeutic approaches to reduce disease burden and transmission.

title: Neurofunctional Outcomes After Pediatric SARS-CoV-2 Infection and Acute Interferon-Related Gene Expression: An Exploratory Observational Pilot Study
abstract: Long-term neurofunctional outcomes after pediatric SARS-CoV-2 infection remain incompletely understood, particularly in relation to acute antiviral immune responses. This exploratory observational pilot study assessed neurofunctional performance approximately six months after infection and its association with acute nasopharyngeal interferon-related gene expression. Sixteen children aged 3–10 years with RT-qPCR-confirmed mild COVID-19 underwent cognitive, gross motor, and functional exercise assessments. Transcript abundance of IFNA2, IFNB1, IFNL2/3, IFI6, and OAS2 was evaluated by qPCR. Five children (31.25%) scored below the age-specific MMSE cutoff, and five of 14 children (35.71%) had below-average TGMD-2 performance. Thirteen completed the ISWT, achieving 53.95 ± 13.55% of the individually predicted distance. IFNB1, IFI6, and OAS2 were detected in all acute-phase samples, whereas IFNA2 and IFNL2/3 were not detected. No statistically significant associations were identified between the detected transcripts and subsequent neurofunctional outcomes. Although the small sample size, absence of pre-infection assessments, and lack of an uninfected comparison group limit interpretation of the findings, this pilot study provides preliminary descriptive data integrating acute mucosal interferon-related gene expression with subsequent neurofunctional assessments in children, supporting further investigation in larger, controlled cohorts.

title: Rates of Diabetes Diagnoses and Diabetic Ketoacidosis Episodes Before Versus During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: ObjectivesTo determine whether the incidence of new-onset diabetes mellitus (DM) differed before and during the COVID-19 pandemic, and to compare the severity of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) at diagnosis.We hypothesized that DM incidence increased during the COVID-19 pandemic, with a corresponding rise in DKA severity. MethodsWe performed a retrospective analysis of youth (ages 0-18 years) newly diagnosed with DM at a single, freestanding children's hospital in Orlando, Florida.Patients diagnosed prior to the COVID-19 pandemic (September 2017-March 2020) were compared to those diagnosed during the COVID-19 pandemic (March 2020-September 2022).Outcomes included incidence of DM stratified by type (type 1 versus type 2), DKA rates and severity at diagnosis, and subgroup analyses by ethnicity and insurance status. ResultsThe overall incidence of pediatric DM increased during the COVID-19 pandemic without a significant rise in DKA rates or severity.When stratified, only youth with type 2 diabetes showed a significantly higher incidence during the pandemic.Increases in DM diagnoses also were observed among non-privately insured youth and those of Hispanic background. ConclusionsThe COVID-19 pandemic was associated with higher rates of pediatric DM diagnoses, particularly among socioeconomically vulnerable populations without a corresponding increase in DKA severity.These findings suggest a shift in clinical presentation and highlight the disproportionate impact of the pandemic on disadvantaged groups.Further research is warranted to evaluate the long-term influence of COVID-19 on pediatric DM incidence and presentation.

title: Experiences of health professionals in Fiji with the provision of medical oxygen during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: AIM: Access to timely medical oxygen is a global concern. During the COVID‐19 pandemic, oxygen demand increased substantially in Fiji. This study examined health professionals' experiences of medical oxygen availability in Fiji's health system during the COVID‐19 pandemic, drawing on frontline staff perspectives to identify lessons for strengthening oxygen systems and pandemic preparedness. METHODS: Semi‐structured interviews were conducted with 17 health professionals, including doctors, nurses, and biomedical and logistics staff, working across Fiji. Transcripts were analysed using inductive reflexive thematic analysis. Coding by multiple researchers was refined through two triangulation workshops. RESULTS: Four inter-related themes were identified. The theme of "oxygen" itself captured challenges related to access, clinical use, pulse oximetry and lack of policy guidance. "Health systems" reflected constraints in logistics and planning, data management, human resources, guidelines and training, leadership and governance, and communication. "Professional impacts" described effects on patient management and ethical dilemmas during extreme demand. "Personal impacts" highlighted stress, grief and loss alongside gratitude, solidarity and resilience. CONCLUSION: Oxygen is an essential medicine. Challenges remain in ensuring equitable access during crises. The findings underscore significant frontline staff impacts and resilience, and the need for planning and investment to strengthen oxygen access and health system preparedness in resource constrained settings.

title: Percepções sobre a Covid-19 entre pessoas com e sem sequelas no ano de 2023
abstract: Este trabalho investigou as percepções associadas à Covid-19 entre pessoas com e sem sequelas da doença. A amostra foi composta por 1.251 participantes, com idade média de 42,8 anos (DP=13,09) e provenientes das cinco regiões do país. Foi utilizado um questionário composto por questões sociodemográficas, uma pergunta sobre a infecção e a presença de sequelas por Covid-19. Também foi usada a técnica de evocação livre de palavras, empregando-se o termo indutor “Covid-19”. O convite para a participação foi feito através de divulgação nas redes sociais e a coleta de dados aconteceu por meio de uma plataforma virtual. A amostra foi dividida em dois grupos: com sequelas (G1) e sem sequelas (G2). No primeiro quadrante foi possível observar uma percepção negativa geral sobre a Covid-19, mas houve peculiaridades em relação ao grupo com sequelas. Nesse grupo, as evocações negativas foram relatadas primeiramente e em maior frequência, além de serem mencionados sentimentos que indicaram uma vivência afetiva mais intensa. No segundo quadrante, os termos mais evocados remetem, além das experiências individuais, a aspectos sociopolíticos presentes ao longo da pandemia. No terceiro quadrante, o grupo com sequelas apresentou evocações relacionadas às características da doença, a exemplo dos sintomas. No quarto quadrante foram mencionados aspectos mais generalistas, com destaque, pela primeira vez, da presença de uma evocação positiva no primeiro grupo, e afetos negativos no segundo grupo. Em razão da frequência das evocações e sua localização entre os quadrantes, nota-se que o grupo com sequelas se sobressaiu, o que indica a necessidade de maior acompanhamento desse público. Os achados reforçam a necessidade de intervenções direcionadas às pessoas com sequelas da Covid-19, contemplando aspectos psicológicos relacionados à vivência prolongada do adoecimento.

title: INTERAÇÕES SOCIAIS E ENSINO: DURANTE A PANDEMIA DE COVID-19
abstract: Este ensaio aborda a questão das interações sociais e sua influência no ensino, tematizando o período de pandemia da covid-19, no qual vivenciamos o distanciamento social, a impossibilidade de termos aulas presenciais e, consequentemente, a diminuição das relações sociais. O estudo teve como objetivo entender como a interação social, no período de afastamento presencial, influenciou os processos de ensino e de aprendizagem. Trata-se de uma pesquisa bibliográfica, de abordagem qualitativa, que teve como principal referência teórica o autor Lev Semenovich Vygotsky. Constatou-se que, na pandemia, devido ao afastamento dos alunos do meio escolar, a aprendizagem foi impactada visto que muitos alunos tiveram dificuldades de estudar e pesquisar sozinhos, além de não terem acesso às tecnologias digitais. Evidenciou-se que a aprendizagem dos alunos se ancora nas mediações semióticas e nos signos repassados pelos professores ou outros influenciadores. Essas constatações reforçam a importância da escola como o lugar no qual os alunos se constituem como sujeitos, na e pela linguagem, a partir da relação com o outro. Conclui-se que a interação social, presencial ou virtual, é fator determinante para os processos de ensino e de aprendizagem. Por isso, indica-se que as escolas propiciem uma interação efetiva entre docentes e discentes, independente do contexto histórico.

Trata-se de uma pesquisa bibliográfica, de abordagem qualitativa, que teve como principal referência teórica o autor Lev Semenovich Vygotsky. Constatou-se que, na pandemia, devido ao afastamento dos alunos do meio escolar, a aprendizagem foi impactada visto que muitos alunos tiveram dificuldades de estudar e pesquisar sozinhos, além de não terem acesso às tecnologias digitais. Evidenciou-se que a aprendizagem dos alunos se ancora nas mediações semióticas e nos signos repassados pelos professores ou outros influenciadores. Essas constatações reforçam a importância da escola como o lugar no qual os alunos se constituem como sujeitos, na e pela linguagem, a partir da relação com o outro. Conclui-se que a interação social, presencial ou virtual, é fator determinante para os processos de ensino e de aprendizagem. Por isso, indica-se que as escolas propiciem uma interação efetiva entre docentes e discentes, independente do contexto histórico.

title: Analysis of the effect of COVID‐19 on crude oil and agricultural commodity market relationships
abstract: Abstract This study examines the COVID‐19 pandemic's effect on relationships between crude oil and agricultural commodity markets. Using a Time‐Varying Parameter Vector Autoregressive model, we find strong volatility transmission, with Brent, WTI, corn, and soybean prices acting as net shock transmitters, while cotton and wheat are net receivers. Dynamic Time Warping further identifies co‐movement and temporal lead‐lag relationships across markets. A Bayesian Structural Time Series model shows that COVID‐19 is associated with a statistically significant 5.8% increase in market connectedness. These findings indicate that market linkages intensified during the pandemic, suggesting that shocks in one market can generate spillover effects across interconnected markets.
journal: Journal of the Agricultural and Applied Economics Association

title: ОЦІНКА ОСОБЛИВОСТЕЙ ВПЛИВУ ПАНДЕМІЇ COVID-19 НА ПОКАЗНИКИ ЗАХВОРЮВАНОСТІ НА НЕІНФЕКЦІЙНІ ХВОРОБИ
abstract: The purpose of the study is to study the influence of COVID-19 on the development and course of non-infectious diseases (NIDs). Materials and Methods of the Study. An analysis of 200 medical records of outpatients was conducted, of which COVID-19 was diagnosed by polymerase chain reaction in 195 people for the period 2020–2025. The statistical method and the method of system analysis were used. After COVID-19, patients developed a number of NCDs that were not diagnosed before the coronavirus disease: arterial hypertension, ischemic heart disease (IHD), type 2 diabetes, obesity, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, oncological pathology, depression. It was found that age and place of residence have a statistically significant relationship with the presence of chronic diseases. The results obtained indicate the presence of an association between the severity of COVID-19 and the development of new NCDs, with the largest proportion of new diseases observed with a moderate course. The analysis showed a statistically significant relationship between the severity of COVID-19 and the emergence of new non-communicable diseases. Statistically significant changes were noted for IHD and psycho-emotional disorders (depression/anxiety). At the same time, for depressive and anxiety states, a significant increase in the number of new cases was observed after COVID-19 (9.0 % versus 0.5 % before COVID), which may indicate a pronounced impact of the infection on mental health. The impact of COVID 19 on CVD is multi-level and is not limited to the acute phase of infection. Even after recovery, a significant proportion of patients may face long-term changes that require medical supervision, lifestyle modification, and control of chronic diseases. The formation of effective prevention and monitoring strategies is a key direction for the development of medicine in the post-pandemic world, since COVID 19 has left a long-term “cardiological and psychological trace” that will require attention in the coming years. It is recommended to increase the attention of family doctors to monitoring the health status of post-COVID patients, especially with the aim of preventing cardiovascular and psychological disorders.

title: Impact of COVID-19 Infection and Vaccination on Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus: A Prospective Analysis From the Zoster Eye Disease Study
abstract: PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to assess the interplay between 2 important viral infections and their management, herpes zoster ophthalmicus (HZO) and COVID-19. METHODS: A subanalysis from the Zoster Eye Disease Study, a prospective randomized controlled study examining prophylactic valacyclovir in HZO, and data collected on COVID-19 vaccination and infection from July 2020 were evaluated. Participants were included if enrolled from January 1, 2019, ensuring that their 18-month follow-up overlapped with the COVID-19 pandemic. Recurrence was defined as new or worsening stromal keratitis without ulceration, endothelial keratitis, iritis, dendritiform epithelial keratitis, or stromal keratitis with ulceration requiring a substantial increase or recommencement of topical steroid therapy. RESULTS: A total of 402 participants were included in the analysis. Attenuated zoster vaccination live was given to 35 (8.7%) and recombinant zoster vaccine to 40 (10.0%) before study commencement. No difference was observed in incidence or severity of COVID-19 infection in those with previous zoster vaccination, and no difference was observed in those treated with valacyclovir prophylaxis. COVID-19 infection occurred in 71 participants (17.7%) during the study period, and COVID-19 vaccination was received by 170 participants (42.3%). No association was observed between HZO recurrence and COVID-19 infection (P = 0.39) or vaccination (P = 0.75) during the 18-month follow-up. The study was powered to detect a hazard ratio of 1.19 for COVID-19 infection or vaccine-associated recurrence. CONCLUSIONS: No significant association was observed between zoster vaccination or valacyclovir use and COVID-19 incidence or severity. In addition, no significant increase in HZO recurrence was observed following COVID-19 infection or vaccination.

title: Impacto de la COVID-19 en los servicios y las políticas de salud de América Latina Impact of COVID-19 on health services and health policies in Latin America
abstract: Objetivo: analizar el impacto de la COVID-19 en los servicios de salud pública de América Latina y las políticas adoptadas. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la pandemia interrumpió los servicios esenciales de rutina, incluidas la atención materna y odontológica, y amplió vulnerabilidades previas de sistemas fragmentados y desiguales. Las respuestas incluyeron la reorganización de servicios, la telesalud, la protección de las cadenas de suministro, medidas no farmacológicas y planes de vacunación con prioridades distintas. La recuperación fue parcial. Conclusión: la pandemia evidenció la fragilidad de los sistemas de salud latinoamericanos y la necesidad de políticas que garanticen la continuidad de la atención esencial.

title: The influence of ensemble size and composition on the performance of combined real-time COVID-19 forecasts
abstract: During infectious disease outbreaks, short-term forecasts can play an important role for both decision makers and the general public. While previous research has shown that combining individual forecasts into an ensemble improves accuracy and consistency, practical guidance for organisers of multi-model prediction platforms on how to construct an ensemble has been scarce. In particular, it is not entirely clear how ensemble performance relates to the size of the underlying model pool, a relevant question when relying on voluntary contributions from modelling teams that face competing priorities. Furthermore, the exact composition of an ensemble forecast may influence its performance. Ensembles can either include all models equally or, alternatively, discriminate based on past performance or other characteristics. Using data from the European COVID-19 Forecast Hub we investigated these questions, with the aim of offering practical guidance to organisers of multi-model prediction platforms during infectious disease outbreaks. We found that including more models both improved and stabilised aggregate ensemble performance, while selecting for better component models did not yield any particular advantage. Diversity among models, whether measured numerically or qualitatively, did not have a clear impact on ensemble performance. These results suggest that for those soliciting contributions to collaborative ensembles there are more obvious gains to be made from increasing participation to moderate levels than from optimising component models.

title: Human-Centric Social Sensing for IoT-Enabled COVID-19 Situational Awareness: DistilBERT-Based Emergency Signal Discovery
abstract: Internet of things (IoT)-enabled public health systems need timely indicators from both device data and human-generated streams. Social media can supply upstream observations during emergencies, but noisy language complicates their validation against official surveillance. We construct daily emergency signals from Weibo posts and test whether they add leading information about official COVID-19 case counts. The analysis covers 39.6 million COVID-19-related posts in Weibo-COV 2.0 from January to April 2020. Distilled bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (DistilBERT), fine-tuned with keyword pseudo-labels, performs binary emergency screening and classifies symptom-, resource-, and policy-related subtypes. Postlevel metrics report agreement with keyword-derived pseudo-labels, not accuracy against independent human annotations; no such benchmark was available. Daily indicators are extrapolated from stratified samples of 500 posts. Their finite-sample uncertainty is reported, and alternative sample sizes represent theoretical precision bounds rather than empirical downstream stability. Validation uses stationarity tests, VAR lag selection, BH-corrected Granger predictability tests, HC1-robust OLS regressions, Johansen rank diagnostics, and a rank-one VECM sensitivity fit. A complete rerun with the stated settings reproduced all empirical outputs, while formula-derived quantities and theoretical bounds were recomputed. Binary and multiclass weighted $F1$ -scores on pseudo-labeled held-out data are 0.927 and 0.880, respectively. At a one-day lag, emergency signals improve the statistical explanation of later cases ( $F=24.68$ , adjusted $p\lt 0.001$ ); symptom signals are strongest ( $F=26.87$ ). The seven-day coefficient is 1.623 ( $p\lt 0.001$ ), and subtype decomposition raises $R^{2}$ from 0.636 to 0.665. Because the Johansen trace test rejects both rank restrictions, $\alpha =-0.2965$ (29.6%/day) remains a descriptive VECM sensitivity estimate. A keyword baseline attains higher aggregate fit ( $R^{2}=0.691$ ), so the evidence does not establish transformer dominance. DistilBERT instead contributes semantic subtype discovery with less manual rule design. The resulting IoT contribution is an interoperable analytics layer for aggregate alerts, not a new sensing device, protocol, or edge architecture.

title: Structural and Functional Differences in the Brains of Individuals with Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19: A Systematic Review of Neuroimaging Findings
abstract: Abstract Post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) is a heterogeneous condition characterized by a panoply of symptoms presenting after a SARS-CoV-2 infection and persisting for months or years, with no alternative explanation. Many symptoms of PASC, such as fatigue or cognitive complaints, are neurological in nature, and various changes in the brain associated with COVID-19 have been proposed as plausible mechanisms. This systematic review summarizes structural and functional brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and positron emission tomography (PET) findings in adults with PASC. Three databases (PubMed, Scopus, and Europe PMC) were searched, and 34 studies met eligibility criteria and were included in the review. Most PASC patients were female and had a history of mild to moderate acute COVID-19 on average three to thirty months prior to image acquisition, with common symptoms including fatigue, cognitive impairment, and olfactory dysfunction. Included studies varied widely in imaging modality, control group characterization, sample size, and time since infection, but were largely cross-sectional in design. Significant differences in PASC compared with controls were reported for grey and white matter volume, cortical thickness, white matter microstructure, functional connectivity, cerebral perfusion, blood-brain barrier permeability and cerebral gliosis, and glucose metabolism, among other measures, and many of these outcomes correlated with symptom burden and clinical measures. The most consistent findings were cerebral hypometabolism (especially frontotemporal) and hypoperfusion, blood-brain barrier disruption, alterations in white matter microstructure, and changes in multiple metrics in the cerebellum. Findings for volume and cortical thickness in most regions and connectivity alterations were bidirectional and inconsistent. Because most data are cross-sectional, longitudinal, multimodal studies are needed to establish whether these brain changes contribute causally to PASC symptoms.

source_records.title: Structural and Functional Differences in the Brains of Individuals with Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19: A Systematic Review of Neuroimaging Findings
source_records.abstract: Abstract Post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) is a heterogeneous condition characterized by a panoply of symptoms presenting after a SARS-CoV-2 infection and persisting for months or years, with no alternative explanation. Many symptoms of PASC, such as fatigue or cognitive complaints, are neurological in nature, and various changes in the brain associated with COVID-19 have been proposed as plausible mechanisms. This systematic review summarizes structural and functional brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and positron emission tomography (PET) findings in adults with PASC. Three databases (PubMed, Scopus, and Europe PMC) were searched, and 34 studies met eligibility criteria and were included in the review. Most PASC patients were female and had a history of mild to moderate acute COVID-19 on average three to thirty months prior to image acquisition, with common symptoms including fatigue, cognitive impairment, and olfactory dysfunction. Included studies varied widely in imaging modality, control group characterization, sample size, and time since infection, but were largely cross-sectional in design. Significant differences in PASC compared with controls were reported for grey and white matter volume, cortical thickness, white matter microstructure, functional connectivity, cerebral perfusion, blood-brain barrier permeability and cerebral gliosis, and glucose metabolism, among other measures, and many of these outcomes correlated with symptom burden and clinical measures. The most consistent findings were cerebral hypometabolism (especially frontotemporal) and hypoperfusion, blood-brain barrier disruption, alterations in white matter microstructure, and changes in multiple metrics in the cerebellum. Findings for volume and cortical thickness in most regions and connectivity alterations were bidirectional and inconsistent. Because most data are cross-sectional, longitudinal, multimodal studies are needed to establish whether these brain changes contribute causally to PASC symptoms.

title: Olfactory training for COVID-19–related smell loss: the smell trial
abstract: Abstract Background Olfactory dysfunction (OD) after SARS-CoV-2 infection is common and can be prolonged and disabling, but evidence for effective treatments remains limited. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 12-week olfactory training (OT) in adults with post-COVID-19 OD. Methods In this single-centre, randomized, controlled, assessor-blinded trial, adults aged ≥18 years with ≥3 months of ongoing OD after SARS-CoV-2-infection and impairment on Sniffin’ Sticks identification (SSI) testing were randomly assigned to 12 weeks of OT or no intervention. Because the protocol was developed during the pandemic under contemporaneous infection-control recommendations, olfactory testing was performed by drawing an odor line on single-use filter paper strips without directly presenting the reusable Sniffin’ Stick pen under the nose. This procedure was feasible for SSI and Sniffin’ Stick discrimination (SSD), but not for the Threshold assessment, which therefore was omitted. A prespecified modified Sniffin’ Sticks total score (mSST; SSI + SSD) was used as primary outcome; primary endpoint was change in mSST from baseline to 12 weeks. Results Seventy-seven participants were screened through October 31, 2024. Of these, 70 were randomly assigned, and 68 completed the randomised phase and were included in the per-protocol analysis (OT n = 38; no intervention n = 30). OT improved mSST compared with natural course, with a significant time-by-group interaction (F(1,66) = 29.95, p 6 and >12 months. Participants from the control group who subsequently underwent OT during the exploratory extension phase showed significant improvements in mSST, SSI, and SSD scores. No serious adverse events occurred. Conclusions Twelve weeks of structured OT produced significant and clinically relevant improvements in psychophysical olfactory outcomes in adults with post-COVID-19 OD. The exploratory extension phase further supported improvement after delayed training initiation. OT appears to be a safe, practical, and scalable treatment option for post-COVID-19 OD. Trial registration Trial registration number: NCT05421221; URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05421221 ; Trial registration date: 13 June 2022.

title: Clinical Effect of Syp. Kankasava in Patients With COVID-19: A Preliminary Observational Study
abstract: COVID-19 commonly presents with cough and respiratory distress. Kankasava is a classical Ayurvedic fermented formulation traditionally used for respiratory complaints. However, direct clinical evidence for its use in COVID-19 remains limited, and it should not replace evidence-based COVID-19 treatment or oxygen support. Objective: To describe the change in cough, breathlessness, and recorded oxygen-related clinical score among COVID-19 patients treated with Syp.
journal: Intemed International Journal of Research in Integrated Medical Sciences (IJ-RIMS)

title: REPERCUSSÕES DAS MEDIDAS DE ENFRENTAMENTO À COVID-19 (SARS-COV-2) NO DESENVOLVIMENTO PSICOSSOCIAL E NA ALFABETIZAÇÃO DE ESTUDANTES: UMA REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA
abstract: Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar as repercussões das medidas de enfrentamento à COVID-19 no desenvolvimento psicossocial e na aprendizagem da leitura e da escrita de crianças em ciclo de alfabetização (6 a 8 anos), com atenção a contextos de vulnerabilidade social e regional. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura científica nacional, com pergunta estruturada pela estratégia PICo e busca no portal Oasisbr (português, 2021-2026). Combinaram-se duas buscas encadeadas: a terceira (518 registros), triada apenas entre artigos, e a quarta, com descritores regionais (86 registros, todos contidos na terceira), triada em todos os formatos. Após a aplicação dos critérios de exclusão e a leitura integral dos textos, treze estudos (cinco artigos, uma tese, quatro dissertações e três trabalhos de conclusão de curso) compuseram o corpus, analisado por Análise de Conteúdo em quatro categorias inspiradas em Piaget, Vygotsky, Wallon e na noção de vulnerabilidade social, com avaliação do nível de evidência. Os estudos indicam desempenho em leitura e escrita abaixo do esperado em crianças de baixa renda após o período pandêmico, barreiras de acesso ao ensino remoto (materiais impressos, mensagens por aplicativo e conectividade limitada) e desigualdades que, em parte, antecediam a pandemia; evidências empíricas diretas sobre a dimensão socioafetiva foram escassas, e o contexto amazônico foi contemplado por um único estudo empírico, realizado em Boa Vista (RR), centrado na imigração venezuelana. O corpus é composto, em sua maioria, por teses, dissertações, trabalhos de conclusão de curso, revisões e relatos, de nível de evidência baixo a moderado, e concentrado em uma única instituição. Conclui-se que há indícios consistentes, porém limitados, de prejuízos na aprendizagem, sendo necessários estudos longitudinais, com grupos de comparação, sobre o desenvolvimento socioafetivo e sobre a realidade amazônica, de modo a subsidiar políticas de recomposição das aprendizagens.

title: Drivers and barriers influencing healthcare provider antiviral prescribing decisions for patients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19: a discrete choice experiment
abstract: Objectives Effective antivirals for coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) are available, yet uptake among eligible high-risk patients remains limited. This study quantified the impact of patient characteristics on healthcare providers (HCPs)’ stated preferences for antiviral prescribing for outpatients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19.Methods US HCPs completed an online survey, including a discrete choice experiment (DCE) with nine attributes: patient-reported symptom severity, patient antiviral request, drug-drug interactions [DDIs], and clinical risk factors. HCPs also responded to direct elicitation items varying by concomitant medication use. Using choice data from the DCE, stated preferences were analyzed using hierarchical Bayesian modeling to estimate relative importance (RI) for each attribute. Exploratory subgroup analyses compared RI by prescribing volume and practice setting. Direct elicitation data were summarized descriptively.Results HCPs included in the analyses (N = 684) were from three practice settings: emergency (33.0%), primary (37.6%), and urgent (29.4%) care. Patient-reported symptom severity was the most influential attribute driving antiviral prescribing decisions (RI = 23.9%), followed by immunocompromised status (RI = 18.2%) and patient age (RI = 15.3%). Patient request for antiviral therapy (RI = 9.2%) and potential DDIs (RI = 4.2%) had comparatively lower influence on prescribing decisions. RI estimates varied by practice setting and antiviral prescribing volume. In direct elicitation, most HCPs selected a highly effective oral antiviral, but some preferred alternative therapies when patients were using concomitant medications requiring interruption or dose adjustment.Conclusion Although guidelines identify underlying medical conditions as key risk factors for severe COVID‐19 progression, HCP prescribing decisions were more strongly influenced by patient‐reported symptom severity than several established clinical risk factors, highlighting opportunities for HCP education on evidence-based antiviral prescribing and DDI management.

title: Global Impact of the COVID ‐19 Pandemic on Cancer Mortality: An Analysis of 54 Countries
abstract: The extent and direction of the impact of COVID-19 pandemic disruptions on cancer mortality remain unclear. We assessed observed versus expected cancer mortality from 2020 to 2023 across 54 countries in 14 regions, by cancer type. Using WHO Mortality Database, we calculated age-standardized mortality rates (ASMRs) for adults (≥ 20 years) from all cancers combined and specifically for lung, pancreatic, breast, and leukemia. Expected ASMRs for 2020-2023 were projected from 2015 to 2019 using Estimated Annual Percent Change. Rate ratios (RRs) of observed versus expected ASMRs were stratified by year, age group, cancer type, country, and region. The analysis included over 2.3 million annual cancer deaths across 54 countries. Lung cancer was the leading cause of death in 45 countries. Eastern Europe had the highest mortality in 2020-2023, with Hungary reporting the highest ASMR (222.6/100,000). Overall, observed mortality was lower than expected (RR < 1). Differences were modest in 2020 but widened by 2023. The largest discrepancies were for breast cancer (RR 0.62-1.19) and leukemia (0.67-1.18), while lung (0.87-1.16) and pancreatic cancers (0.91-1.20) showed smaller differences. Regional variation was notable, with Western Asia showing the widest difference from expected. Differences in expected mortality were limited for poor-prognosis cancers, while breast cancer and leukemia were more affected during long-term healthcare disruptions. Regional disparities illustrate the negative impact of compounding crises on cancer mortality and underscore the need for resilient systems to protect cancer care during emergencies.

title: High vaccine coverage and non-pharmaceutical interventions decreased hospitalizations and deaths due to the Omicron variant in Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada
abstract: The Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador (NL) had high vaccination coverage, and few infections were reported prior to the establishment of the Omicron variant. We investigated whether changes in the timing and rate of booster dose administration could have reduced severe disease outcome and reliance on non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) during the Omicron wave in NL. We used a vaccination-stratified epidemiological model calibrated to serology data to investigate the impact of vaccination relative to counterfactual vaccination strategies under actual, strict and no NPI scenarios. Compared with a Canadian vaccination rate scenario, the actual vaccination rollout in NL was estimated to have prevented approximately 519 hospitalizations and 122 deaths from December 15, 2021 to December 15, 2022, corresponding to reductions of 25.9\% and 30.9\%, respectively. These reductions reflected contributions from NL's higher initial primary series coverage (81.3\%), higher final booster dose coverage (57.3\%), and the implementation of various NPIs for 89 days after the Omicron BA.1 variant became established. Earlier and faster administration of booster doses reduced the duration of strict NPIs required to achieve hospitalization targets. Our findings show how the timing and rate of vaccination rollout can complement NPIs to reduce severe disease and the duration for which strict NPIs are required.

title: The role of overgeneralized autobiographical memories and inflammatory markers in stress symptoms associated with the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Objective To investigate the characteristics of pandemic-related stress symptoms among frontline healthcare workers involved in COVID-19 prevention and control, as well as the roles of overgeneralized autobiographical memory (OGM) and inflammatory markers in these symptoms. Methods Using convenience sampling, 52 frontline healthcare workers (exposure group) and 55 non-frontline healthcare workers (control group) who participated in COVID-19 prevention and control efforts at the Guannan Campus of Lianyungang First People’s Hospital between March 2020 and March were selected.Assessments were conducted using the Posttraumatic Stress Disorder Checklist (PCL-C), the Autobiographical Memory Test (AMT), and the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ), and serum levels of IL-1β, IL-2, IL-6, IL-8, IL-18, and C-reactive protein (CRP) were measured.Statistical analyses were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test, Spearman’s rank correlation, and bootstrap stratified regression analysis. Results In the exposure group, significant differences compared to the control group were observed in PCL-C avoidance (Z = −1.984, P = 0.047), hypervigilance (Z = −2.020, P = 0.043), OGM total score (Z = −4.379, P 0.05). Stratified regression showed significant associations of OGM total score and CRP with PCL-C vigilance (β = 0.299, P = 0.005; β = 0.587, P 0.05). Conclusion Frontline healthcare workers during the COVID-19 pandemic showed higher stress symptoms and elevated inflammatory markers, OGM and CRP, compared to a control group. OGM and CRP were linked to pandemic-related stress, while IL-1β, although elevated, lacked independent predictive power. CRP showed the strongest correlation with stress symptoms, suggesting it could be a key biological marker for understanding pandemic-related stress.

title: Tourism Recovery and Structural Resilience in Indonesia After COVID-19
abstract: Indonesia’s inbound tourism experienced a severe pandemic contraction followed by a rapid but nonlinear recovery between 2019 and 2025. This study examined the depth, speed, and remaining gap of that recovery using a longitudinal quantitative descriptive design based on official BPS-Statistics Indonesia data. Annual international visitor arrivals were analyzed through year-on-year growth, a 2019-based recovery index, recovery gaps, and phase-specific comparisons. Arrivals fell from 16.11 million in 2019 to 1.56 million in 2021 before rising to 15.39 million in 2025. The recovery index increased from 9.68 at the 2021 trough to 95.53 in 2025, leaving a gap of 0.72 million visits, or 4.47%, below the pre-pandemic benchmark. The findings show that Indonesia achieved substantial demand restoration, while growth moderated as the market approached its former scale. However, restored visitor volume does not automatically indicate structural resilience. Stronger resilience requires market diversification, crisis preparedness, digital capability, financial and workforce adaptability, and sustainable destination management. The study provides an empirical framework for distinguishing numerical tourism recovery from broader organizational, institutional, and destination-level resilience for future shocks and long-term sustainable tourism development strategies.

title: Persistent Immune Dysregulation Following Acute SARS-CoV-2 Infection in an Experimental Model
abstract: A dysregulated immune system has been hypothesized to be one of the main drivers for the debilitating Long COVID sequelae that patients report. Due to the invasive nature of sampling human lung tissue, there is a need to further characterize the pulmonary immune environment that may be promoting the pulmonary LC sequelae. This dissertation utilizes a mouse-adapted SARS-CoV-2 virus to characterize the post-acute phase of the infection in the lung. We first characterized the lung immune cell populations at 30 and 60 days post-MA30 infection. Here, we detected persistent innate immune infiltration, which included macrophages, eosinophils, and dendritic cells, along with T cell activation and exhaustion, which is further countered by the expansion of regulatory T cells. Importantly, no evidence of a contagious virus was found; persistent viral RNA was detected in the lungs, most likely driving pulmonary immune responses. When challenged with Pseudomonas aeruginosa at 30 DPI, MA30 surviving mice demonstrated enhanced bacterial clearance driven by amplified macrophage and neutrophil responses. These findings suggest that post-acute immune dysregulation enhances immunity against secondary pathogens, while potentially causing future complications. There are also various studies that report novel onset allergic asthma following severe COVID-19, and yet the exact mechanisms behind the occurrence have not been revealed. We aimed to investigate whether, at 60 days post the acute infection, if the immune remodeling would result in an exacerbated allergic response when exposed to a cocktail of allergens: dust mites, ragweed, and aspergillus. Despite significantly increased lung eosinophil populations at 60DPI, the MA30+triple allergen-challenged mice did not have an exaggerated allergic response when compared to the triple allergen-challenged controls. All together, these findings demonstrate that a severe SARS-CoV-2 infection can remodel the pulmonary innate and adaptive immune cell populations in a manner that enhances host defense against secondary bacterial challenge, while raising important questions about the future consequences of persistent pulmonary inflammation.

title: Is the Pandemic Over? The Lasting Impact of COVID-19 on Teachers of Color in Chicagoland Schools
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has had enduring effects on educators’ professional lives, with particularly pronounced consequences for Teachers of Color (ToCs) in urban school contexts. This mixed-methods study examines how educators in Chicagoland schools experienced, interpreted, and responded to changes in well-being, professional identity, and healing during and after the pandemic. Survey data from 56 educators and narrative interviews with a subset of participants were analyzed using descriptive statistics, a teacher-adapted Ecological Systems Framework, and Razfar et al.’s (2024) Seven Dimensions of Narrative Analysis. Findings indicate widespread declines in educator well-being, including heightened stress, burnout, emotional exhaustion, and challenges to work–life balance. Comparative analyses further suggest that Teachers of Color experienced disproportionate and sustained impacts. Narrative findings reveal that participants situated pandemic-related experiences within broader structures of racial inequity rather than as individual deficits. Across ecological levels, educators described patterns of racialized visibility, institutional silence, health disparities, neighborhood disinvestment, and inequitable distributions of emotional and professional labor. The study identified four interconnected themes: pandemic disruption and identity fracture among educators; structural racialized trauma across ecological systems; societal inequities as a source of pandemic-related trauma; and collective recognition and narrative healing. Findings further demonstrate that collective narrative spaces characterized by shared storytelling, solidarity, and recognition functioned as important sites for meaning-making, identity reconstruction, and healing. This study advances a synthesis framework that integrates Ecological Systems Theory, Critical Race Theory, and narrative inquiry to explain how educators experience disruption, interpret those experiences through narrative, and engage in processes of healing and identity reconstruction. The findings suggest that educator well-being is not solely an individual outcome but a socially, relationally, and structurally mediated process. Implications highlight the need for equitycentered, healing-oriented approaches that move beyond individual wellness frameworks to address the systemic conditions shaping educators’ experiences.
