title: Disentangling enforced and voluntary behaviour change during the COVID-19 Pandemic, the Netherlands, 2020 to 2023
abstract: BACKGROUNDEffective pandemic mitigation relies on population behaviour change. To understand how to achieve this, it is important to not only consider restrictive policies that enforce behaviour change but also consider voluntary responses to changes in pandemic severity and behavioural advice.AIMThe current study investigates to what extent change in protective behaviour during the COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands can be attributed to self-guided behaviour change (in response to changes in pandemic severity), adherence to government behavioural advice, or compliance with restrictive policies.METHODSWe analysed survey and mobility data on seven protective behaviours from 2020 to 2023. Using time-series and mixed-effects models, we examined associations between pandemic severity (hospitalisations), government behavioural advice, and restrictive policies with these behaviours. Control variables included seasonality, pandemic duration and demographic characteristics.RESULTSPandemic severity was consistently associated with increases in protective behaviour, while the impact of behavioural advice and restrictive policies varied. Moreover, the estimated influence of behavioural advice and restrictive policies was substantially reduced when including pandemic severity in the models.CONCLUSIONThe consistent association between pandemic severity and protective behaviours indicates that people changed their behaviour in order to protect themselves and others, even without government advice or restrictive measures. Behaviour change could be further promoted through behavioural advice and/or restrictive policies, although the estimated impact of these approaches varied substantially between target behaviours. These results highlight the importance of voluntary behaviour change and accounting for type of behaviour change when designing and evaluating mitigation policies.

title: Reduced Plasma Bradykinin and an Elevated Angiotensin converting enzyme/Bradykinin Ratio are Associated with Disease Severity in COVID-19: A Retrospective Study of 224 Severity-Stratified Patients
abstract: Abstract Objectives: Dysregulation of kallikrein-kinin system (KKS) has been suggested to play a role in the pathophysiology of Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and contribute to COVID-19-related inflammation, coagulation, vasodilatation, and vascular permeability. Therefore, in the present study, plasma levels of bradykinin, a major KKS peptide, and angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE), a primary enzyme degrading bradykinin were investigated. Subjects and Methods: In this retrospective study, plasma bradykinin was measured by ELISA method in a stratified cohort of 224 COVID-19 patients spanning the full WHO severity range, from asymptomatic infection to critical illness. Unlike most previous studies limited to hospitalized patients, ACE was also quantified in the same specimens, enabling calculation of the ACE/bradykinin ratio. Results: Plasma bradykinin levels progressively decreased across the five severity strata. Severe/critical patients had significantly lower levels than asymptomatic/mild patients (p < 0.001), while mild pneumonia patients had lower levels than those with mild symptomatic disease (p < 0.001). Bradykinin levels did not differ between severe and critical illness (p = 0.348). Conclusions: In this study, bradykinin showed a strong negative correlation with disease severity, whereas the ACE/bradykinin ratio showed a strong positive correlation with the severity of COVID-19 suggesting a potential utility of the ACE/bradykinin ratio as a marker of disease severity.

title: Control in crisis: the dynamic of formal and informal social control in the transmission of COVID-19 in Hong Kong
abstract: Scholars in sociology and criminology emphasize the importance of both formal and informal control in maintaining social order. However, limited research has explored the dynamic interaction between these two forms of control. This study addresses this gap by investigating whether formal control created a supportive framework that enhances the effectiveness of neighborhood informal social control in curbing the local transmission of disease during the early phase of the COVID-19 epidemic in Hong Kong. The outcome variable is block-level aggregation of COVID-19 cases reported between January 23 and November 22, 2020, in Hong Kong. Neighborhood-level informal social control is measured using two variables derived from the Hong Kong Panel Study of Social Dynamics, while formal control is operationalized through government-imposed social distancing policies. Poisson regression models are used to assess the association between block-level COVID-19 cases and neighborhood informal social control at various levels of formal control. The findings reveal that informal social control significantly reduced virus transmission, but only in the presence of strong formal control. The results offer valuable insights into how forms of control work in the crisis.

title: Care Experiences of People with COPD during the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Although there is a substantial body of literature focused on the pathophysiology regarding chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and COVID-19, there remains limited exploration of the healthcare experiences of patients with COPD during the pandemic. This study explores the challenges patients with COPD (PWC) experienced during the pandemic, including access to care, the efficacy of virtual COPD care, and mental health impacts. We performed a cross-sectional survey of 200 individuals with COPD recruited through respirologists' offices and local lung health groups on social media from Southwestern Ontario, Canada, who accessed care since the COVID-19 pandemic. The study included 200 participants, most aged 30–49. Fear of COVID-19 led 68% to delay or cancel in-person visits. 95% of participants accessed alternative care (online/phone), but barriers such as technology access, difficulty using technology, and language issues were common. Increased sadness was prevalent among those unable to maintain in-person care. The pandemic exacerbated mental health and disrupted care access for PWC, increasing reliance on virtual care despite significant barriers. Future programs should address technology access and digital literacy to better support patients. This study identified key challenges faced by people with COPD during COVID-19, including reduced in-person care, increased reliance on virtual care, and barriers related to technology access and digital literacy.

title: Clinical and pathogenetic heterogeneity of anxiety disorders in COVID-19 survivors
abstract: OBJECTIVE To analyze the clinical and pathogenetic heterogeneity of anxiety disorders in COVID-19 survivors to inform differentiated therapeutic approaches. MATERIAL AND METHODS A comparative, observational, prospective study included 90 patients, with the presence of anxiety symptoms after a SARS-CoV-2 infection. The sample was divided into two groups: Group 1 (n=63), treatment-naïve patients; and Group 2 (n=27), patients with a history of anxiety or affective disorders (F32.0-F42.0) before SARS-CoV-2 infection. Clinical-psychopathological and psychometric assessments included the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A) and Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D), the Generalized Anxiety Disorder questionnaire (GAD-7), and the A.M. Vein autonomic disorder questionnaire. RESULTS Anxiety severity reached moderately severe levels (median scores on HAM-A: 24-25; GAD-7: 16). Asthenia was observed in 87.8% of patients, and cognitive impairment ('brain fog') occurred in 77.8%. Autonomic disorders (A.M. Vein average score 37.4-37.9) included cardiac (53.3%), gastrointestinal (17.8%), and pain syndromes. Three clinically relevant primary psychopathological syndromes were identified: anxiety-asthenic (61.2%), anxiety-hypochondriacal (31.1%), and anxiety-depressive (7.7%). The organic pathway (neuroinflammation) was predominant in the pathogenesis. The somatogenic pathway was associated with autonomic dysfunction and pain syndromes, while the psychogenic (nosogenic) pathway contributed to the development of anxiety-hypochondriacal and anxiety-depressive syndromes. CONCLUSIONS Anxiety disorders in the post-COVID period are highly heterogeneous and require differentiated therapeutic approaches. Pharmacotherapy, including antidepressants and neurometabolic therapy, is indicated for the organic subtype, while psychotherapy should be prioritized for the psychogenic subtype.
journal: S S Korsakov Journal of Neurology and Psychiatry

source_records.abstract: OBJECTIVE To analyze the clinical and pathogenetic heterogeneity of anxiety disorders in COVID-19 survivors to inform differentiated therapeutic approaches. MATERIAL AND METHODS A comparative, observational, prospective study included 90 patients, with the presence of anxiety symptoms after a SARS-CoV-2 infection. The sample was divided into two groups: Group 1 (n=63), treatment-naïve patients; and Group 2 (n=27), patients with a history of anxiety or affective disorders (F32.0-F42.0) before SARS-CoV-2 infection. Clinical-psychopathological and psychometric assessments included the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A) and Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D), the Generalized Anxiety Disorder questionnaire (GAD-7), and the A.M. Vein autonomic disorder questionnaire. RESULTS Anxiety severity reached moderately severe levels (median scores on HAM-A: 24-25; GAD-7: 16). Asthenia was observed in 87.8% of patients, and cognitive impairment ('brain fog') occurred in 77.8%. Autonomic disorders (A.M. Vein average score 37.4-37.9) included cardiac (53.3%), gastrointestinal (17.8%), and pain syndromes. Three clinically relevant primary psychopathological syndromes were identified: anxiety-asthenic (61.2%), anxiety-hypochondriacal (31.1%), and anxiety-depressive (7.7%). The organic pathway (neuroinflammation) was predominant in the pathogenesis. The somatogenic pathway was associated with autonomic dysfunction and pain syndromes, while the psychogenic (nosogenic) pathway contributed to the development of anxiety-hypochondriacal and anxiety-depressive syndromes. CONCLUSIONS Anxiety disorders in the post-COVID period are highly heterogeneous and require differentiated therapeutic approaches. Pharmacotherapy, including antidepressants and neurometabolic therapy, is indicated for the organic subtype, while psychotherapy should be prioritized for the psychogenic subtype.

title: Legitimacy Boundaries in Crisis: Online Learning Adoption in Ultra-Orthodox Schools During COVID-19
abstract: Abstract The restrictions imposed on the citizens of Israel with the outbreak of COVID-19 forced educational institutions to adopt online channels for distance learning. The ultra-Orthodox society, bound by its suspicious and disapproving approach to the use of media, especially among teenagers and children, had to deal with the new circumstances and decide its course of action to resolve this conflict. The present study investigates whether, and to what extent, online channels were used in ultra-Orthodox educational institutions in their various subsections, and what were parents’ and teachers’ considerations, attitudes, and perceptions regarding the adoption of online learning in either COVID-19 or in any future similar emergencies. The article combines quantitative and qualitative methods based on a survey among a representative sample of parents of primary school-aged children (N=395) and semi-structured interviews (N=45) with parents and teachers in ultra-Orthodox schools. The results show that 14% of all parents in the sample use Zoom for distance learning. Furthermore, significant differences were found between the different sub-currents, with the Chabad stream being the most popular (94%), followed at a large margin by the Sephardic public (15%), Lithuanian (13%), and Hasidic (4%). Differences were also found between the sub-currents in terms of parents’ willingness to use online learning channels in the future, and correlations were found between parents’ level of conservatism/modernism, learners’ gender identity, their age and willingness to use online learning channels. However, almost none of the participants saw this period as an opportunity for pedagogical development related to the potential of studies in the online spaces, but as a limitation that requires coping and necessary adaptation to minimize the damage.

title: Public Health Service Delivery During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Experiences from Katutura State Hospital in Namibia
abstract: The goal of this assessment is to make people aware of the dangers of the COVID-19 pandemic. COVID-19 was initially identified in China in December 2019, and it was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in January 2020, making it a global pandemic. A pandemic, according to the World Health Organisation (WHO), is "an epidemic occurring worldwide, or over a very wide area, crossing international boundaries and usually affecting a large number of people". This Pandemic left the planet and its inhabitants in states of turmoil and distress. The Corona Virus, also known as the COVID-19 Pandemic, made health-care delivery for both patients and health personnel, difficult for hospitals and health centres in Namibia. The study examined the global lockdown caused by the pandemic. The pandemic had a significant impact on service delivery. As a result of these situations, hospital service delivery was jeopardised. This study was conducted at Katutura State Hospital using a qualitative method with a sample size of 20 doctors and enrolled nurses. Descriptive analysis was used, with an interview guide serving as the study instrument. The study was limited by the number of participants. The investigation discovered that service delivery was severely impacted, particularly in the pharmacy sector, and that the virus slowed down all aspects of the institution. It is recommended that if patients should anticipate delays, informing them in advance would reduce unnecessary contact volume.

title: O SOFRIMENTO PSICOLÓGICO NA AUSÊNCIA DOS RITUAIS DE DESPEDIDA NA PANDEMIA DA COVID-19: UMA REVISÃO DE LITERATURA PSYCHOLOGICAL SUFFERING IN THE ABSENCE OF FAREWELL RITUALS IN THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC: A LITERATURE REVIEW
abstract: A pandemia causada pelo novo coronavírus fez com que o mundo adotasse o distanciamento e isolamento social como medida não farmacológica para a contenção da disseminação do vírus para que não houvesse o colapso do sistema de saúde. Contudo, milhares de mortes ocorreram e o sofrimento psicológico foi inevitável na ausência dos rituais de despedida na pandemia da Covid-19. A partir de revisão de literatura, o objetivo deste estudo foi investigar o sofrimento psicológico da pessoa que não teve a oportunidade de vivenciar os rituais de despedida dos indivíduos vitimados pela Covid-19. Realizou-se um levantamento bibliográfico, por meio dos sistemas informatizados de busca: SciELO, PePSIC e no buscador Google Acadêmico, no período de 2019 a 2021. Os resultados revelaram a importância cultural dos rituais de despedida ao longo da história, marcada por mudanças e ciclos, e as consequências psicológicas causadas pela interrupção abrupta desses rituais nos indivíduos impactados pela Covid-19, bem como as dificuldades e desafios encontrados na experiência da morte e, consequentemente, a contribuição da psicoterapia como suporte à travessia que o indivíduo deve construir em sua experiência. Concluiu-se que, mediante a tantas situações derivadas e desencadeadas no contexto pandêmico, é necessário encontrar condições favoráveis para a superação e a reorganização psíquica, pois os rituais de despedida são fundamentais para a elaboração da perda e do luto.

title: Uncertainty-aware haplotype quantification at subclonal resolution
abstract: Haplotypes are defined as stretches of DNA with a set of small variants, which are single/multiple nucleotide variants and small indels, or genes that are inherited as a single piece from the same parent. This doctoral thesis investigates the development & implementation of a generic model for uncertainty aware quantification of haplotypes at subclonal levels and further explores potential applications. Using variant allele frequencies as observed evidences from sequencing data, a Bayesian latent variable model is employed to compute _a posteriori_ estimates of haplotype combinations. The first part of this thesis contains a manually curated benchmark dataset of 99 samples and it shows that our approach excels at identification of correct HLA types and proves the best performance as compared to the other state-of-the-art algorithms, thereby proving the applicability of the approach to HLA typing. The second part of this thesis then focuses on a different area, which is quantification of virus variants in mixtures. An example mixture is given as a co-infection of an individual by multiple variants of a virus species, e.g. Using a simulated dataset that mimics pandemic progress and a real dataset that contains known coinfections of delta and omicron variants of SARS-CoV-2, the approach does not only accurately report virus variants but also informs about additional variants of the virus. This finding is strengthened with the evaluation of a laboratory generated mixture of five HIV-1 strains, showing that the approach is not bound to a specific virus species. This work adopts the use of pangenome graph based alignments in order to take into account genetic variation. As a result, read aligment is improved and more accurate variant calls are acquired, thus having a direct impact on the downstream processes that includes the operation of the Bayesian model. In addition to identification of haplotypes, Orthanq may shed light on potentially new haplotypes, for example novel HLA types or virus variants, with the aid of extensive visualizations that are automatically generated. The model is implemented under the framework ORThogonal evidence based HAplotype Quantification (ORTHANQ) as an open source computational tool, written in Rust programming language.

title: Nonparametric testing for socio-economic health inequalities: an application to covid-19 deaths
abstract: This paper develops a non-parametric test statistic for assessing the equality of the health concentration curve and the 45-degree line, which represents perfect equality. Specifically, the test compares the health concentration curve, C(p,Y), with the line p for p∈(0,1) using an L2 metric. In addition, we propose alternative tests for detecting pro-rich and pro-poor health inequalities based on metrics other than L2. We employ a non-parametric estimator for C(p,Y) and establish the asymptotic properties of the tests, including their size and power. A Monte Carlo simulation study demonstrates the strong finite-sample performance of the tests, with robust size and power across various data-generating processes. Finally, to illustrate the practical relevance of the proposed methods, we apply them to U.S. data to test for inequality in COVID-19 deaths across and within U.S. states, comparing the health concentration curves of these outcomes to the 45-degree line. Our empirical findings reveal varying levels of health inequality across states, with some states showing pro-rich inequality where wealthier individuals experience lower death rates. The results highlight the critical role of socioeconomic disparities in shaping the impact of COVID-19, particularly in states with high poverty rates and lower incomes.

title: The World Health Organization's Reform After COVID ‐19: Between Old Habits and a New Normal
abstract: ABSTRACT The COVID‐19 pandemic subjected the World Health Organization (WHO) to its sternest test. While the rationale for its existence became clearer than ever, widespread criticism of its pandemic response eroded its standing, already compromised by previous health emergencies and a highly competitive global health landscape. Since 2020, calls to reform the WHO have intensified, echoing past initiatives that drew significant scholarly attention. However, studies on WHO reform often lack breadth and analytical benchmarks while failing to consider the preferences of member states and other principals. This article fills these gaps by examining key stakeholders in post‐COVID‐19 WHO reform efforts and explaining how the initiatives undertaken relate to the notions of robustness, effectiveness and democracy. Our analysis relies on original interviews with officials and observers, public records and secondary literature. Findings suggest that the WHO Secretariat and member states have identified synergies between robustness, effectiveness and democracy, although emphases have varied and trade‐offs have also emerged. Despite uneven progress and overlooked institutional weaknesses, the post‐COVID‐19 reform agenda maintains significant momentum. Going forward, it will require a deeper reflection on the WHO's role in global health governance and how to weather the United States' retreat from multilateralism.

title: Peripheral Oxygen Extraction Is Reduced During Submaximal Exercise in Post-COVID-19 Condition
abstract: BACKGROUND Studies in post-COVID-19 condition following hospitalisation have focused on maximal exercise, with limited insight into submaximal responses that better reflect daily activities. We compared central haemodynamic, ventilatory, and peripheral muscle oxygen extraction responses during submaximal exercise between individuals with post-COVID-19 condition and healthy age-matched controls. METHODS Twelve participants with post-COVID-19 condition, who were assessed 624 (593, 729) days following hospitalisation (median (IQR) length of stay: 7 (4.7, 11.7) days) and seven age-matched healthy controls (59±11 years) completed a 4-min constant-load exercise test at 80% of peak cycling workload. Cardiac output (CO), oxygen uptake (V̇O2), and ventilatory efficiency (V̇E/V̇CO2) were assessed throughout exercise. Arteriovenous oxygen content difference was calculated using the Fick equation (C(a-v)O2 = V̇O2/CO). RESULTS Post-COVID-19 condition participants exhibited a lower (p=0.03) mean±SD C(a-v)O2 compared with healthy controls (135±29 vs. 171±46mLO2·L−1 blood). No significant differences were observed between post-COVID-19 condition and controls for V̇O2 (1.9±0.3 vs. 2.1±0.7L·min−1), V̇E/V̇CO2 (26.6±3.0 vs. 27.5 ± 2.4), or CO (12.7± 3.0 vs. 11.1± 3.6L·min−1), indicating similar central cardiovascular and ventilatory responses between groups, despite a numerically greater cardiac output in the post-COVID-19 condition group (11±4% higher). In contrast, RER and V̇E/V̇O2 were significantly higher in healthy controls than in post-COVID-19 condition participants, indicating divergent ventilatory behaviour despite preserved V̇E/V̇CO2. CONCLUSION Post-COVID-19 condition following hospitalisation is characterised by reduced peripheral oxygen extraction during submaximal exercise, alongside no significant difference in cardiovascular responses and preserved ventilatory efficiency with respect to carbon dioxide elimination, compared with healthy controls. Although RER and V̇E/V̇O2 were higher in healthy controls, indicating some divergence in ventilatory behaviour between groups, this did not reflect impaired ventilatory efficiency in post-COVID-19 condition. These findings indicate that differences in exercise responses at workloads representative of daily living are possibly peripheral rather than central, supporting rehabilitation strategies targeting skeletal muscle oxidative function.

title: Back to normal? The enduring effects of COVID-19 lockdowns on wellbeing
abstract: We investigate the immediate and longer-term impacts of COVID-19 lockdowns on overall life satisfaction and eight domains of subjective wellbeing, addressing the lack of evidence on whether these effects persist after lockdowns end. Leveraging quasi-natural variation in the timing and duration of local lockdowns across Australia and using long-horizon individuallevel panel data spanning the pre-pandemic, pandemic and post-pandemic periods, we employ individual fixed-effects models with time and location fixed effects to identify the causal effects of lockdowns. Our results show that lockdowns substantially reduce overall life satisfaction and satisfaction with employment opportunities and community, while increasing satisfaction with free time. These effects are strongest closer to the lockdown period and diminish over time. The effects are also non-linear, with most wellbeing outcomes affected only when lockdown exposure exceeds approximately two months in the preceding year. While effects on free time and community satisfaction are short-lived, negative effects on overall life satisfaction and satisfaction with employment opportunities persist for up to four years. We also identify delayed negative effects on satisfaction with financial circumstances, home, neighbourhood, and health, alongside a delayed positive effect on personal safety satisfaction. Heterogeneity analysis reveals larger effects among younger individuals, positive immediate effects on financial satisfaction only among lower-income households, and contrasting effects on health satisfaction across genders. These findings highlight the importance of considering lockdown duration and longer-term wellbeing effects in future pandemic responses.

source_records.abstract: We investigate the immediate and longer-term impacts of COVID-19 lockdowns on overall life satisfaction and eight domains of subjective wellbeing, addressing the lack of evidence on whether these effects persist after lockdowns end. Leveraging quasi-natural variation in the timing and duration of local lockdowns across Australia and using long-horizon individuallevel panel data spanning the pre-pandemic, pandemic and post-pandemic periods, we employ individual fixed-effects models with time and location fixed effects to identify the causal effects of lockdowns. Our results show that lockdowns substantially reduce overall life satisfaction and satisfaction with employment opportunities and community, while increasing satisfaction with free time. These effects are strongest closer to the lockdown period and diminish over time. The effects are also non-linear, with most wellbeing outcomes affected only when lockdown exposure exceeds approximately two months in the preceding year. While effects on free time and community satisfaction are short-lived, negative effects on overall life satisfaction and satisfaction with employment opportunities persist for up to four years. We also identify delayed negative effects on satisfaction with financial circumstances, home, neighbourhood, and health, alongside a delayed positive effect on personal safety satisfaction. Heterogeneity analysis reveals larger effects among younger individuals, positive immediate effects on financial satisfaction only among lower-income households, and contrasting effects on health satisfaction across genders. These findings highlight the importance of considering lockdown duration and longer-term wellbeing effects in future pandemic responses.

title: LINKING SUSTAINABILITY PERFORMANCE TO STOCK RESILIENCE DURING AND AFTER COVID-19 CRISIS: EVIDENCE FROM SOUTHEAST ASIA
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic severely disrupted markets. While sustainability performance measured by ESG scores theoretically buffers against shocks, its efficacy in emerging markets with nascent sustainability frameworks remains underexplored. Method: We analyze a balanced panel of 1,395 observations from 279 non-financial Southeast Asian firms (2020–2024). Using OLS, lagged, and fixed effects models, we compare the impact of sustainability performance on stock resilience during the 2020–2022 and post-pandemic (2023–2024) periods. Findings: Sustainability performance (ESG scores) significantly enhanced stock resilience during the pandemic. However, this protective effect dissipated post-pandemic. Results confirm a statistically significant improvement in overall resilience following the crisis, as investors redirected their focus toward traditional financial fundamentals such as profitability and leverage. Conclusion: Sustainability performance acts as situational crisis insurance. Its risk-mitigation value is highly salient during systemic uncertainty but diminishes under stable market conditions. Novelty/Originality of this article: Unlike prior single-phase studies in developed economies, this research provides longitudinal evidence on the dynamic, state-dependent nature of sustainability performance across crisis and recovery phases within Southeast Asia’s early-stage ESG landscape.

title: NYC’S Unsettled COVID-19 Era Labor Market: The Case for an Active Labor Market Policy
abstract: This report combines an analysis of the current state of New York City’s changing labor market with a survey and examination of the city’s workforce system – the vast array of agencies, training programs, and support services designed to help jobseekers find work and careers. Unlike many cities and the nation overall, New York City has yet to recover from pandemic-induced job loss, with a particularly severe impact on lower-income workers of color and working parents. What is needed is an active labor market policy that takes a comprehensive approach, plans and coordinates across the four branches to connect with workers and businesses, education institutions and training providers, and identifies and builds many more career pathways and the ladders and supports needed to help workers climb those ladders. And that needs to be coupled with public and private policies to raise wages and job quality and to encourage and support businesses in adapting to a regime of better wages and jobs.

title: Pandemic road safety: how COVID-19 policies shaped crash severity in England
abstract: Background COVID-19 pandemic restrictions changed travel volume, road-user composition and the traffic environment, but evidence on crash severity across distinct policy phases remains limited. We examined fatal or serious outcomes across 14 England policy periods. Methods Official police-reported collision, vehicle and casualty records for 2019–2022 were linked at crash level. The binary outcome was fatal or serious versus slight crash severity. We fitted a complete-sample, unweighted logistic regression adjusted for vehicle, road, environmental, temporal and police-force factors, using calendar-week cluster-robust CIs. Marginal standardisation estimated adjusted probabilities and risk differences; non-linear weekly trends were assessed in sensitivity analysis. Results Among 384 472 crashes, 81 931 (21.3%) were fatal or serious. Adjusted probability of a fatal or serious crash was 20.5% (95% CI 20.2% to 20.7%) before the pandemic, 22.0% (21.0% to 23.0%) during the first national lockdown and 22.6% (22.3% to 22.9%) during postrestriction follow-up. Absolute differences were +1.52 and +2.08 percentage points, respectively. Both associations remained positive after nonlinear weekly adjustment, but only the first-lockdown association remained statistically significant with police force by year controls. Motorcycle involvement (OR 3.17, 95% CI 3.07 to 3.28) and single-vehicle crashes (OR 2.45, 95% CI 2.39 to 2.51) had larger associations. Discussion and conclusion Policy-period associations were heterogeneous and modest in absolute magnitude. Vehicle involvement and crash context had stronger associations. Findings are observational and do not establish causal policy effects.

title: Digital Health Surveillance in Public Health Emergencies: Testing the DPDP Act, 2023 Against India's COVID-19 Experience
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the adoption of digital health surveillance across India, prompting government bodies to deploy contact tracing applications, location tracking and geo-fencing to manage public health risks. These rapid technological interventions, however, raised serious constitutional and data privacy concerns, particularly about the handling of sensitive health information without robust statutory backing. This paper evaluates India’s pandemic-era digital health measures through the constitutional lens of K.S. Union of India (2017) and assesses the evolution of the governing legal framework. It shows how the legacy framework under the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the IT Rules, 2011 proved structurally incapable of regulating State-led health surveillance. The paper then examines the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules, 2025, scrutinising in particular the broad ‘legitimate use’ exceptions for public health emergencies, the State exemptions, data principal rights and executive oversight of the Data Protection Board. It argues that while the DPDP Act provides a long-awaited statutory base, significant regulatory gaps remain. To ensure that public health interventions respect fundamental rights, the paper proposes statutory safeguards, binding emergency protocols and enhanced judicial and institutional oversight.
journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities

title: Design and Validation of Multiplexed Respiratory RT-LAMP assay for the differentiation of SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) in COVID-19 Pandemic Samples from Western Kenya.
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the importance of widespread, accessible viral surveillance to ensure pandemic-preparedness. The rapid diagnosis of respiratory infections is crucial not only for effective patient management but also to inform ongoing surveillance for the detection of outbreaks. Reverse transcriptase-Loop mediated isothermal amplification (RT-LAMP) assays are an attractive alternative to reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) for rapid, decentralised testing in resource limited settings due being rapid and low cost. Here we present the design and evaluation of a multiplexed RT-LAMP assay for the simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and Respiratory Syncytial Virus via the incorporation of fluorescently labelled LAMP probes. Mid-nasal swabs collected from 175 participants on the day of enrolment in the MALCOV Cohort study in Kisumu, Kenya were used in the evaluation of the RT-LAMP assay. Overall, 114 SARS-CoV-2, six Influenza A, two Influenza B and zero RSV samples were identified in the cohort by the Allplex SARS-CoV-2/FluA/FluB/RSV RT-PCR kit (Seegene Inc) reference test, in addition to 53 negatives. Sensitivity and specificity of the RT-LAMP assay (SARS-CoV-2/FluA/RSV) when compared to RT-PCR was 82.64% [CI95%:74.70-88.92%] and 100% [CI95%:93.40-100%] at 40 minutes for all samples respectively. The mean time to a positive result was 11minutes, highlighting the speed of this technology compared to the more commonly used RT-PCR. RT-LAMP enables rapid multi-pathogen detection with comparable diagnostic accuracy to RT-PCR.

title: Diabetes Mellitus with COVID-19 Complication: A Review
abstract: 374 Acute coronavirus syndrome-2 is causing the present outbreak of COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2). Social, vocational, economic, physical, and mental health all suffer as a result. Other lithium interference is affected in a similar way. In this review chapter, we are looking at diabetes, and COVID-19 has certain health-related consequences for individuals. COVID-19 improves hyperglycemic circumstances in a variety of domains, including insulin, lipopolysaccharides, RAAS, ROS, and IL-6, according to the research. Furthermore, we are conducting quick testing of their mechanisms, which includes a typical list of medicines licensed for treating COVID-19 and diabetes mellitus (DM). Small papers for type 1 DM have been gathered, and the best results are still feasible; therefore, further study is needed to get the best results.

title: COVID-19: una aproximación pluridisciplinar
abstract: El SARS-Cov-2, agente causante de la COVID-19, es la hidra del siglo XXI, un monstruo de muchas cabezas que no solo ha constituido un problema médico, sino un imponente desafío sanitario a todos los niveles. Esta obra intenta abarcar los aspectos concernientes a la COVID-19 desde una óptica pluridisciplinar, lo que da cabida a los saberes científico-técnicos, humanísticos, sociales y jurídicos, además de atender como primordial los aspectos clínicos relevantes, medicina preventiva, salud pública e industria. La obra es diferencial y única, heterogénea, plural y amplia; contempla desde cuestiones básicas hasta otras de carácter más complejo: desarrollo de antivirales, tratamiento farmacológico, papel de las nanotecnologías en el diagnóstico y, de forma extensa, las vacunas frente al SARS-CoV-2, la solución principal frente a la pandemia. El volumen va dirigido a especialistas en la(s) materia(s), universitarios de distintas áreas, alumnos y público en general.

title: [Surgery in transition: Impact of the early COVID-19 pandemic on visceral surgery in Germany].
abstract: BACKGROUND Changes in visceral surgical care in Germany during the early COVID-19 pandemic have not yet been sufficiently described. To date, data on in-hospital mortality and postoperative complications remain limited. MATERIAL AND METHODS In this retrospective analysis, anonymized administrative data from the Federal Statistical Office of Germany (Destatis) for the period from 2018 to 2021 were evaluated comparatively, focusing on the most frequently performed visceral surgical procedures nationwide. Demographic characteristics, procedure volumes, length of hospital stay on regular wards and intensive care units, postoperative complications, and in-hospital mortality were analyzed. RESULTS A total of approximately 2.1 million procedures were recorded over the 4-year study period. Compared with the pre-pandemic years 2018 and 2019, procedure volumes decreased by approximately 9% in 2020 and 2021, respectively. The average length of stay in the intensive care unit and in hospital decreased during the pandemic. Postoperative complications, including pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, sepsis, and peritonitis, increased during the pandemic years compared with the preceding years. Overall in-hospital mortality in visceral surgery increased from 2.43% in 2018 to 2.55% in 2020 and 2.53% in 2021. In particular, in-hospital mortality in colorectal surgery increased from 7.37% in 2019 to 7.95% in 2021, while the mortality among COVID-19-positive patients following colorectal procedures reached 48%. In contrast, mortality rates in esophageal, hepatic, and pancreatic surgery remained largely unchanged. CONCLUSION During the COVID-19 pandemic, Germany experienced a substantial reduction in the volume of visceral surgical procedures and hospital length of stay, while postoperative complications and in-hospital mortality increased. A potential causal relationship with SARS-CoV-2 cannot be established based on the available data. These findings emphasize the importance of systematically evaluating the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on surgical care in Germany and of developing evidence-based strategies to maintain surgical capacity and patient safety during future pandemics.

Compared with the pre-pandemic years 2018 and 2019, procedure volumes decreased by approximately 9% in 2020 and 2021, respectively. The average length of stay in the intensive care unit and in hospital decreased during the pandemic. Postoperative complications, including pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, sepsis, and peritonitis, increased during the pandemic years compared with the preceding years. Overall in-hospital mortality in visceral surgery increased from 2.43% in 2018 to 2.55% in 2020 and 2.53% in 2021. In particular, in-hospital mortality in colorectal surgery increased from 7.37% in 2019 to 7.95% in 2021, while the mortality among COVID-19-positive patients following colorectal procedures reached 48%. In contrast, mortality rates in esophageal, hepatic, and pancreatic surgery remained largely unchanged. CONCLUSION During the COVID-19 pandemic, Germany experienced a substantial reduction in the volume of visceral surgical procedures and hospital length of stay, while postoperative complications and in-hospital mortality increased. A potential causal relationship with SARS-CoV-2 cannot be established based on the available data. These findings emphasize the importance of systematically evaluating the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on surgical care in Germany and of developing evidence-based strategies to maintain surgical capacity and patient safety during future pandemics.

title: Baseline Severity and Early Multiorgan Failure to Predict In-Hospital Mortality in Critically Ill COVID-19 Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background: Intensive Care Unit (ICU) mortality remains high among patients with severe coronavirus disease. Static admission severity scores may fail to capture the dynamic clinical trajectory of critically ill patients. We hypothesized that early multiorgan failure (MOF) at 24 hours would improve mortality discrimination beyond admission severity alone. Methods: Retrospective, single-center cohort study of 345 adults with severe COVID-19 pneumonia admitted to a Spanish ICU (March 2020-December 2022). The primary outcome was all-cause in-hospital mortality. Univariate comparisons between survivors and non-survivors were performed, followed by multivariable logistic regression to identify independent predictors of mortality. Three sequential models were constructed and compared by Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC-ROC) discrimination. Results: Overall, in-hospital mortality was 20.6%. Non-survivors were older and had higher Simplified Acute Physiology Score (SAPS) II and Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE) II scores (p<0.001). MOF at 24 hours was more frequent among non-survivors than survivors (88.4% vs. The baseline model (age, sex, Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), hypertension, and SAPS II) achieved an AUC of 0.798 (95% CI 0.742-0.852). The final model incorporating MOF at 24 hours achieved an AUC of 0.812 (95% CI 0.754-0.860); early MOF nearly tripled the odds of death (OR 2.78, 95% CI 1.22-6.33, p=0.015). Conclusions: Combining baseline severity with early multiorgan dysfunction provides a simple, interpretable approach to mortality risk stratification in critically ill COVID-19 patients; however, external validation is needed before it can inform escalation-of-care or treatment-limitation decisions in clinical practice.

title: P-503: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the diagnosis and clinical presentation of type 1 diabetes mellitus in children referred to a tertiary public hospital in Rio de Janeiro
abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) presents acutely and may lead to diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). During the COVID-19 pandemic, diagnostic delays and increased DKA frequency were reported. To compare clinical and epidemiological characteristics of children referred to a tertiary public hospital in Rio de Janeiro for new onset TIDM before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. Retrospective study of patients at the time of diagnosis of T1DM (2018–2021), divided into two groups: pre-pandemic (G1: 2018–2019) and pandemic (G2: 2020–2021). Variables included sex, age, DKA at diagnosis, duration of symptoms prior to diagnosis, and family history (FH). In G2, COVID-19-related data included symptoms and testing. A total of 49 children were included (G1 n=15; G2 n=34). No differences were observed between groups in: mean age at diagnosis (94.3±49.2 vs 89.0±56.4 months; p=0.3683); sex distribution [53% female (n=8), 47% male (n=7) vs 47% female (n=16), 53% male (n=18); p=0.9244]; frequency of family history of T1DM [26% (n=4) vs 28% (n=7); p=0.1145] and type 2 diabetes [50% (n=7) vs 50% (n=14); p=0.2551]; mean duration of symptoms prior to diagnosis (24.0±28.8 vs 31.1±45.5 days; p=0.9564); and frequency of DKA at diagnosis [60% (n=9) vs 70% (n=23); p=0.4485]. In G2, 23% (n=8) reported COVID-19 symptoms, 12% (n=4) had a positive test, and 26% (n=9) had household contact. The time from symptom onset to diagnosis was prolonged regardless of the pandemic period, despite the expectation of longer delays and, consequently, a higher frequency of DKA diagnoses during the pandemic. This may reflect low clinical suspicion of T1DM in children, unchanged during the pandemic. Additionally, the number of COVID-19 cases was low and unlikely to have influenced the presentation of T1DM. These findings highlight the need for larger-scale studies to clarify the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the diagnosis and clinical presentation of T1DM.

title: P-06: Increased DKA at type 1 diabetes onset during the COVID-19 pandemic without evidence of delayed diagnosis or worse glycemic outcomes
abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that the COVID-19 pandemic altered the epidemiology of type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) with both increases in the number of new onset diagnoses and the incidence and severity of Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) at presentation. To evaluate DKA incidence at T1DM onset and its association with demographic and clinical characteristics, comparing pandemic with pre- and post-pandemic periods. Retrospective longitudinal study including 76 pediatric patients with newly diagnosed T1DM (2018–2025) at a tertiary center. Data included age, sex, BMI, and symptom duration. DKA was defined according to ISPAD criteria. Statistical analysis used chi-square, Mann–Whitney and odds ratios. Overall DKA incidence was 60.5% (46/76), with a mean age at diagnosis of 8.8 years, a male predominance of 60.5%, and a mean symptom duration of 24.5 days. Children under 5 years of age exhibited the highest DKA rates (86.6%) and a significantly greater risk of severe presentation (OR 4.9; p 0.05). No statistical association was observed between the increased incidence of DKA and delayed diagnosis. One-year follow-up HbA1c levels were similar between the pandemic and post-pandemic cohorts (8.58 ± 1.1% vs. 8.60 ± 1.4%; p = 0.96). The pandemic was associated with increased DKA at T1DM onset, not explained by delayed diagnosis or baseline patient characteristics. The subsequent decline may be related to older age at diagnosis. Glycemic control at 1 year remained unchanged. Early recognition of T1DM symptoms remains essential to prevent severe presentations during healthcare disruptions

title: P-01: Temporal trends and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the clinical presentation of type 1 diabetes in children: a 2018–2024 cohort
abstract: T1D incidence is rising, with presentation changes post-COVID-19. DKA at diagnosis remains a major concern. Longitudinal data on temporal trends and seasonality in middle-income pediatric populations are limited. To analyze temporal trends, clinical characteristics, DKA frequency, and seasonality in children with T1D (2018–2025). Retrospective cohort of 76 children diagnosed with T1D at a tertiary center. Data included age, sex, BMI, DKA, and diagnosis date, stratified by pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods. Incidence increased by 200% during the pandemic (15.0 cases/yr) vs. pre-pandemic baseline (5.0 cases/yr), remaining 80% higher post-pandemic (9.0 cases/yr). Mean age was 8.8 years, 60.5% male. Overall DKA frequency was 60.5%. DKA rates were significantly higher during the pandemic (73.3%) vs. post-pandemic (44.4%; p=0.018; OR 3.44). A seasonal peak occurred in Q3 (July-September; 29.8% of cases). Mean 1-year HbA1c was similar between pandemic and post-pandemic cohorts (8.58% vs 8.60%; p=0.96). Recent follow-up showed an overall mean HbA1c of 8.8%, with 25% of patients at the <7.0% target. A structural shift in T1D incidence occurred, with a 200% pandemic surge not yet returning to baseline. The pandemic significantly increased severe DKA risk (OR 3.44), independent of symptom latency. Children <5 years remain the most vulnerable. Despite acute initial severity, long-term glycemic control was not negatively impacted by the pandemic, though low target achievement (25%) highlights the urgent need for improved chronic management and early symptom recognition.

title: Mental health outcomes following COVID-19- associated caregiver loss in children and adolescents: a six-year evidence gap
abstract: By May 2022, an estimated 10.5 million children worldwide had lost a parent or caregiver to COVID-19. We found only two cohorts with quantitative mental-health data: one in Iran and the South African Orphanhood and Caregiver Loss Among Adolescents and Youth study. Both reported more psychiatric and psychosocial difficulties among bereaved children than controls. In Iran, internalizing symptoms, post-traumatic stress, and suicidal ideation increased during follow-up, and no participant received mental-health care. In South Africa, likely mental disorder declined in both groups but remained more common among bereaved participants; suicidal ideation or attempts rose slightly in the bereaved group while falling among controls. Social support, food insecurity, and domestic violence were associated with outcomes. These children were bereaved during school closures, social isolation, disrupted mourning, and financial strain, when usual sources of support were often reduced. Yet few were identified and followed over time. Research funding priorities and fragmented health, education, mortality, and child-protection systems may have contributed to this gap. Many children bereaved in the first pandemic waves are now adolescents or young adults, but their longer-term mental-health course remains largely unknown. They should be identified, followed, and offered support according to clinical and family need.

title: Experiences of individually tailored physical exercise in COVID-19-induced postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome: A qualitative content analysis
abstract: Background Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS) is a phenotype of post-COVID-19 Condition (PCC), characterised by orthostatic intolerance and a range of debilitating symptoms. Exercise is a frequently implemented intervention in the treatment of POTS and PCC. However, patients’ experiences with exercise as a therapeutic modality remain largely unexplored. This study aimed to explore the experiences of individuals diagnosed with PCC and POTS who underwent an individually tailored physical exercise intervention. Methods A qualitative study design with an inductive approach was applied. Twenty-three participants who completed a feasibility study, involving semi-supervised tailored exercise, were recruited for individual interviews. Data were collected using a semi-structured interview guide and analysed through qualitative content analysis. Results Five main categories emerged, underscoring the importance of individualised design of exercise programs, flexible modalities, and continuous support from physiotherapists with expertise in PCC and POTS. Participants experienced improvements in physical, mental, and social functioning, although setbacks and symptom fluctuation were common. Strategies for energy management, alongside informal and formal support, were identified as facilitators and reduced barriers to exercise as a treatment. Psychological dimensions, including hope, motivation, goal setting, emotional adaptation, acceptance, and coping strategies, were central to participants’ experiences. The combination of the intervention structure, therapeutic support, and effective strategies was perceived as contributing to the intervention’s effectiveness, and many participants viewed exercise as a key pathway to recovery. Conclusions This study highlights the need for a flexible and individualised rehabilitation approach in COVID-19-induced POTS. Moreover, exercise should be closely monitored by a physiotherapist with condition-specific expertise, who not only adapts the exercise to symptom fluctuations but also addresses diverse psychosocial needs and individual resources. The participants’ experiences indicate that a holistic, multidisciplinary, and person-centred rehabilitation model may support recovery and contribute to improved long-term wellbeing in individuals with PCC and POTS.

title: COVID-19 as a Compound Hazard: Emergency Managers Experiences in Compound Disaster Management
abstract: Abstract The health impacts of the coronavirus pandemic (COVID-19) have been widely documented; however, less is known about the impacts of the COVID-19 response on emergency managers who were part of the COVID-19 response while continuing with their everyday disaster job, too. Interviews were conducted in late 2021 with state emergency management planners from 21 states to discuss their experience handling COVID-19 and other disasters concurrently. The 158 disasters declared during the COVID-19 pandemic give us a unique view of compound hazard events that include a long-duration hazard with a large geographic footprint. Experiences from emergency managers serving during COVID-19 were able to shine a light on activities and policies that helped and hindered their efforts to serve their communities most effectively. Common issues encountered were related to coordination, lack of training in roles, a need for more resources in rural areas, more planning for long duration events, and mental health resources.

title: ДЕРМАТОЛОГИЧЕСКИЕ ОСЛОЖНЕНИЯ ФАРМАКОТЕРАПИИ COVID-19: КЛИНИЧЕСКИЕ ВЫЗОВЫ И ДИФФЕРЕНЦИАЛЬНАЯ ДИАГНОСТИКА (ОБЗОР)
abstract: Пандемия COVID-19 привела к широкому применению и внедрению большого количества фармакологических средств, сопровождаясь возникновением побочных эффектов. Среди них можно выделить дерматологические осложнения. Дерматологические осложнения наиболее часто связаны с противовирусными препаратами (ремдесивир, фавипиравир), противомалярийными средствами (гидроксихлорохин) и антибиотиками (азитромицин). Спектр проявлений варьирует от легких макулопапулезных и уртикарных экзантем до тяжелых состояний, включая острый генерализованный экзантематозный пустулез (AGEP) и синдром Стивенса–Джонсона.

title: Prevalence of Musculoskeletal Symptoms in Post-COVID-19 Patients
abstract: Background: Coronavirus disease 2019 can affect several body systems, and musculoskeletal symptoms may persist after recovery from the acute infection. Pain and other musculoskeletal complaints can create additional challenges during the post-COVID-19 recovery period. Objective: To determine the frequency and distribution of musculoskeletal symptoms among post-COVID-19 patients. Methodology: This observational cross-sectional study was conducted from June to September 2021 after ethical approval from the Lyallpur Institute of Management Sciences, using purposive sampling to recruit 120 individuals with previous COVID-19 infection, of whom 70 met the eligibility criteria. Participants were aged 30 to 55 years, had recovered from COVID-19 with a negative test, reported musculoskeletal symptoms, and had manual muscle testing grades 1–3, while smokers, those with autoimmune conditions, those >55 years, and participants still positive or under quarantine were excluded. Data were collected through a demographic form, self-developed screening questionnaire, 0–5 verbal pain scale, Musculoskeletal Health Questionnaire, and Standardised Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire, administered through face-to-face interviews. The Musculoskeletal Health Questionnaire assessed overall musculoskeletal health (0–56), while the Nordic Questionnaire identified symptoms across different anatomical regions. Descriptive statistics, including frequencies, percentages, and appropriate measures for numerical variables, were used to summarize demographic characteristics, pain intensity, Musculoskeletal Health Questionnaire scores, and musculoskeletal symptoms. Results: Of the 70 participants, 50 (71.4%) reported very severe pain, 14 (20%) reported the worst possible pain, and 6 (8.6%) reported severe pain. Neck and shoulder symptoms were reported by all participants (100%), followed by upper-back symptoms (98.6%) and lower-back symptoms (94.3%). Knee symptoms were reported by 81.4% of participants, while ankle, elbow, and wrist symptoms were reported by 68.6%, 57.1%, and 54.3%, respectively. Hip symptoms were reported by 42.9% of participants. Conclusion: Musculoskeletal symptoms were frequently reported among the post-COVID-19 patients included in this study, particularly in the neck, shoulder, upper-back, and lower-back regions. These findings highlight the importance of assessing musculoskeletal complaints during post-COVID-19 follow-up. Larger prospective studies incorporating objective functional assessments are needed to determine symptom progression and rehabilitation needs.
journal: Healer Journal of Biomedical and Health Sciences

title: Body Mass Index and Mortality in Adults Hospitalized with COVID-19 at a Tertiary Referral Hospital in Northern Jordan, 2020–2021: A Single-Center Retrospective Secondary Analysis
abstract: Background and Objectives: A previous analysis of the same Jordanian hospital cohort reported obesity as nonsignificant in a broad mortality model but did not characterize BMI dose–response or nonlinearity. We examined BMI and in-hospital mortality in a focused secondary analysis of adults hospitalized during 2020–2021. Materials and Methods: The archived extract contained 1399 adults and 559 deaths. The primary exposure was obesity (BMI ≥ 30 vs. Logistic regression adjusted for age using a four-knot restricted cubic spline, sex, and smoking status; an expanded model additionally included comorbidities. Modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted risk ratios. Results: Mortality was 41.4% with obesity and 38.8% without obesity. The primary adjusted OR was 1.124 (95% CI 0.892–1.416; p = 0.322) and adjusted RR was 1.066 (0.938–1.212; p = 0.327). BMI-category and spline global tests were nonsignificant, but intervals were wide at the extremes. Conclusions: No statistically clear BMI–mortality association was identified in this selected early-pandemic hospitalized cohort. The findings do not establish equivalence and may not transfer to later pandemic eras; interpretation is limited by unresolved derivation differences from the parent cohort and unavailable acute-severity and timing variables.

title: Vacinação infantil pós-COVID-19: desafios, hesitação e o movimento antivacina
abstract: A hesitação vacinal representa um desafio para a saúde pública, especialmente no período pós-pandemia de covid-19, diante da redução da adesão à vacinação infantil e da disseminação de informações falsas e discursos antivacina. Este estudo teve como objetivo investigar a baixa adesão à vacinação em crianças e adolescentes no período pós-covid-19 e a influência do movimento antivacina. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura. A busca foi realizada nas bases de dados PubMed, LILACS e SciELO, considerando artigos publicados entre 2021 e 2025, nos idiomas português e inglês. Após a aplicação dos critérios de inclusão e exclusão, dez artigos compuseram a amostra final. Os resultados apontaram que a hesitação e a recusa vacinal estão associadas a múltiplos fatores, incluindo o medo de efeitos adversos, as preocupações com a segurança e a eficácia das vacinas, a desconfiança nas instituições de saúde, a circulação de desinformação, as crenças pessoais e as experiências anteriores dos responsáveis. Por outro lado, a recomendação dos profissionais de saúde, a comunicação acolhedora e as intervenções educativas demonstraram potencial para favorecer a aceitação vacinal. Conclui-se que a baixa adesão à vacinação infantil não pode ser atribuída exclusivamente ao movimento antivacina ou à falta de conhecimento, sendo necessária uma abordagem multifatorial que fortaleça a confiança, amplie o acesso à informação confiável e qualifique a comunicação entre profissionais de saúde e responsáveis.

title: Agglomeration and Regional Performance and Innovation Dynamics in Italy Across the Covid-19 Shock
abstract: Regional disparities remain a central issue in economic geography, particularly within the European Union, where territorial cohesion is a key policy objective. This study examines the joint dynamics of agglomeration, economic performance, and innovation across Italian macro-regions (NUTS-1) over the period 2017–2023, focusing on the structural break induced by the COVID-19 pandemic. Building on the New Economic Geography framework, and in particular the contributions of Philippe Martin, the analysis combines a panel interaction model with β-convergence, σ-convergence, and spatial autocorrelation measures (Moran's I), providing a comprehensive assessment of regional dynamics. The results reveal heterogeneous patterns. Innovation exhibits convergence, suggesting a gradual diffusion of knowledge across regions. In contrast, GDP shows limited convergence, indicating persistent disparities, while agglomeration displays divergence, reflecting increasing spatial concentration after 2020. Furthermore, econometric results indicate that the effect of agglomeration on both GDP and innovation strengthens in the post-COVID period. Overall, the findings point to an asymmetric adjustment process: while innovation converges, economic performance and spatial structures remain characterised by persistence and cumulative agglomeration forces.

title: Psychological burden, subjective complaints and their impact on the progression of verbal fluency in COVID-19 survivors and healthy controls: a longitudinal analysis
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the longitudinal change of verbal fluency after COVID-19 and potential influencing factors in a community-based sample. Within the COVIMMUNE-Clin study at the University of Bonn Medical Center, participants with a mild course of COVID-19 (n = 52), a severe course (n = 52), and healthy controls (n = 55) were compared. This focused secondary analysis examined verbal fluency as a distinct cognitive outcome within the broader study. Semantic and lexical verbal fluency, assessed using the Vienna Verbal Fluency Test (WIWO), as well as psychological burden measured by the ICD-10 Symptom Rating Scale (ISR) and subjective complaints assessed with the Everyday Cognition-12 (ECog-12) questionnaire, were administered at the first visit and again after 12 months. A linear mixed model was employed, incorporating Group (mild, severe and healthy controls) and Visit as fixed effects, with Subject and the Intercept as random effects. ISR and ECog-12 were each incorporated into separate models as fixed effects. Group and psychological burden had an impact on semantic fluency, in a way that more severe disease and higher psychological burden were associated with lower performance. Contrary to the hypothesis, verbal fluency did not significantly change over 12 months. Across models, verbal fluency types showed distinctive patterns, which is reflected by the fact that psychological burden and subjective complaints only showed an association with semantic fluency performance. Lexical fluency showed no significant effects of these constructs and was primarily positively influenced by education. COVID-19 disease severity, psychological burden, and subjective complaints were associated with semantic fluency. These findings support further research on whether verbal fluency measures, in combination with self-reported symptoms, may contribute to practical assessment approaches following COVID-19. Specific details of the study design are included at the German Clinical Trials Registry (primary registry trial identifier: DRKS00023806; registration date: March 16, 2021, cross-referenced at World Health Organization’s International Clinical Trials Registry Platform [ICTRP]).

title: Transcranial direct current stimulation combined with aerobic exercise for motor, mood and cognitive symptoms in long COVID: a randomized, sham-controlled feasibility trial
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The COVID-19 pandemic left millions of people with persistent disorders. Among these, long COVID is frequently associated with motor, mood, and cognitive impairments, significantly reducing quality of life. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility of a randomized, sham-controlled trial of a two-week protocol combining transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) and aerobic exercise in individuals with long COVID, against pre-specified criteria for recruitment, retention, adherence, assessment burden, acceptability and safety. Motor, mood and cognitive outcomes were exploratory. METHODS AND MATERIALS: Participants were randomized (1:1) to real (2 mA, 30 min, left M1) or sham tDCS, both combined with treadmill exercise (64–76% max heart rate). Randomization used a computer-generated sequence, with allocation concealed in sealed opaque envelopes; participants and outcome assessors were blinded. The protocol comprised 13 sessions: baseline, 10 interventions, and two follow-ups. Feasibility was assessed through resources, management, and safety; clinical outcomes included motor, mood, and cognitive functions. RESULTS: Of 76 individuals contacted, 44 were assessed for eligibility and 10 were randomized (5 per group). All participants completed the intervention and post-intervention reassessment, and 8 completed the follow-up (80% retention). Adherence was high, and assessments remained under 120 minutes. All participants reported perceived benefits after the intervention (90% at follow-up); no serious adverse events occurred, and mild adverse effects were reported by all participants in both groups (most commonly drowsiness, tingling and fatigue), with no between-group differences. Fatigue decreased in both groups, with no significant between-group differences in any clinical outcome. CONCLUSION: A randomized, sham-controlled trial of tDCS combined with aerobic exercise in long COVID is feasible, and the protocol was safe and acceptable. The pre-specified feasibility criteria were met, supporting progression to an adequately powered trial with adjustments to recruitment strategies and delivery format.

title: Higher Diagnostic Yield of Sputum Versus Oropharyngeal Swabs for Viral Pathogens in Hospitalized Non-COVID-19 Community-acquired Pneumonia
abstract: Rapid and accurate pathogen detection is crucial for managing community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and guiding infection control. Among 229 hospitalized adults with paired specimens, multiplex PCR detected respiratory viruses in 65% of sputum samples compared with 39% of oropharyngeal swabs, indicating higher diagnostic yield with sputum in moderate-to-severe CAP.

title: Perfil sociodemográfico, condições de acolhimento e histórico relacionado à COVID-19 de adolescentes institucionalizados: estudo transversal
abstract: ABSTRACT | OBJECTIVE: To describe the sociodemographic profile, care conditions, and COVID-19-related history of institutionalized adolescents. METHODS: This is a descriptive cross-sectional study conducted with 37 institutionalized adolescents in July 2023 across four municipal care facilities in northeastern Brazil, using variables related to sociodemographic, care conditions, and COVID-19 history. The data were analyzed descriptively. RESULTS: A predominance of males (59.5%) was observed, with a mean age of 14.7 years (SD=1.7); the majority identified as mixed-race (51.4%), without a partner (64.9%), heterosexual (78.4%), without a religion (45.9%), and with a mean of 8.1 years of schooling (SD=2.1). Clinical/pandemic characterization showed that the majority had not contracted COVID-19 (78.4%). However, among those who had COVID-19 (21.6%), some required hospitalization (5.4%) and experienced sequelae or complications such as “shortness of breath” (16.2%). The care conditions showed that adolescents were under care in male-only facilities (62.2%), with a mean institutionalization period of 3.6 years (SD=4.6) and an average of 2.8 stays in care (SD=2.3); the main reasons for admission included family instability (29.7%), drug involvement (29.7%), and family abandonment (24.3%), among others. CONCLUSIONS: The study results show that males, mixed-race individuals, heterosexuals, those without a religion, with a mean of 8.1 years of schooling, and without a partner comprise the population of institutionalized adolescents in the municipality.

title: Inverted advantage: Technology adoption and the achievement paradox in Bangladesh secondary schools during COVID-19
abstract: Abstract This study examines how digital access, socio-economic conditions, and institutional support interacted to shape learning continuity and academic outcomes among secondary school students in Bangladesh during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using a mixed-methods design, the study utilizesdata from 446 students and qualitative insights from teachers, parents, and school stakeholders across rural and urban contexts. The findings show that learning disruption was not driven by digital access alone but by the interaction of structural and institutional factors as well. Rural students faced significant barriers related to connectivity, device access, and institutional capacity, while urban students, despite higher access, experienced uneven engagement shaped by socio-economic conditions. Academic performance declined during school closures and recovered only partially after reopening, with persistent inequalities across different contexts. The study develops an integrated analytical framework linking digital access, socio-economic conditions, and institutional support, demonstrating how these dimensions jointly produce and sustain educational inequality. The findings highlight the need for policy approaches that go beyond infrastructure expansion to address affordability, instructional capacity, and institutional resilience.
journal: Journal of Education and e-Learning Research

title: BLENDED LEARNING MANAGEMENT DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC
abstract: This study used a qualitative approach with descriptive method. Data were collected through observation in the madrasah environment, interviews with teachers and madrasah head, and review of learning documents. The analysis was conducted through the stages of data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing to obtain a complete picture of the practice of Blended Learning in both institutions. The results show that both madrasas have done careful planning by adjusting the curriculum and providing supporting facilities for online learning, such as internet networks and digital devices. In its implementation, MAN 1 Pangandaran applies a shift system between offline and online learning alternately every day, while MAS YPP Jamanis Parigi mostly applies full face-to-face learning with additional online activities according to teacher needs. In the evaluation stage, both implement web-based assessment to ensure objectivity and efficiency of the assessment process. Overall, the implementation of Blended Learning has proven to be an adaptive and effective solution in maintaining the quality of madrasah learning amidst the limitations of the pandemic, as well as showing the flexibility of educational institutions in dealing with dynamic learning system changes.

title: Structural Resilience and Institutional Response: An Empirical Study of Economic Recovery Pathways in UK Cities Following the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: The study empirically examines city-level data in the UK for 2019-2023, systematically accounting for the spatial divergence and the drivers of it along three main lines of inquiry: the recovery of incomes, the recovery of welfare spending, and the recovery of regional inequality following the COVID-19 pandemic, using a fixed-effects panel model approach. The results show a strong “Matthew Effect” in the recovery after the pandemic. Higher-skilled, industrial and institutional cities like metros and tech cities like Cambridge had a stronger performance regarding income and welfare security, even having net positive growth. Concurrently, this agglomerative effect deepened regional disparities and intra-metropolitan inequities. Correspondingly, this agglomeration effect resulted in growing inequities both between regions and within large cities. The study suggests that the pandemic was far from a uniform shock but reinforced the spatial disparity of the UK economy as a result of a myriad of structural and institutional changes. Policies need to transcend the limiting growth paradigm focused on maximizing efficiency and implement a competitiveness-oriented development pathway that includes regional equity. This can be done by focusing investments in education, digital infrastructure and industrial policies to stem further geographical inequality.

source_records.title: Structural Resilience and Institutional Response: An Empirical Study of Economic Recovery Pathways in UK Cities Following the COVID-19 Pandemic
source_records.abstract: The study empirically examines city-level data in the UK for 2019-2023, systematically accounting for the spatial divergence and the drivers of it along three main lines of inquiry: the recovery of incomes, the recovery of welfare spending, and the recovery of regional inequality following the COVID-19 pandemic, using a fixed-effects panel model approach. The results show a strong “Matthew Effect” in the recovery after the pandemic. Higher-skilled, industrial and institutional cities like metros and tech cities like Cambridge had a stronger performance regarding income and welfare security, even having net positive growth. Concurrently, this agglomerative effect deepened regional disparities and intra-metropolitan inequities. Correspondingly, this agglomeration effect resulted in growing inequities both between regions and within large cities. The study suggests that the pandemic was far from a uniform shock but reinforced the spatial disparity of the UK economy as a result of a myriad of structural and institutional changes. Policies need to transcend the limiting growth paradigm focused on maximizing efficiency and implement a competitiveness-oriented development pathway that includes regional equity. This can be done by focusing investments in education, digital infrastructure and industrial policies to stem further geographical inequality.

title: Genetic predisposition, perceived threat and burden, and sex differences in changes in anxiety symptoms across the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Several meta-analyses have shown that the COVID-19 crisis and the efforts to contain the virus have had a significant impact on mental health, leading to an increase in anxiety-related symptoms, especially in the first phase of the pandemic. The present paper aimed to investigate the development of anxiety symptoms throughout the course of the pandemic in a non-clinical sample. Using longitudinal data from the German TwinLife panel, the study investigates how stressor-related perceptions of threat and burden mediated the development of anxiety symptoms while acknowledging individuals’ genetic susceptibility to developing anxiety symptoms, as well as sex differences. The study expands the understanding of pandemic-specific processes by incorporating pre-pandemic anxiety levels. Anxiety symptoms remained remarkably stable during the pandemic in relation to pre-pandemic anxiety levels, underscoring the relevance of pre-pandemic differences in anxiety as pandemic risk factors. Genetic predispositions explained differences in initial anxiety levels and in perceived threat and burden, but not in anxiety change over time, which calls for research on the environmental factors through which these predispositions are realized. Females showed higher initial anxiety, and perceived threat and burden mediated changes in anxiety significantly only in females. Whether these sex differences in mediation reflect distinct mechanisms remains to be tested in future studies.

title: Confucian culture and crisis governance in East Asia: Evidence from COVID-19 policy attitudes
abstract: This study examines how Confucian cultural orientations shape public support for crisis governance in East Asia. Using Asian Barometer Survey Wave 6 data from Japan, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, and Vietnam, it models familialism, collectivism, harmony, and hierarchism as latent traits via item response theory and relates them to COVID-19 policy attitudes using fixed-effects ordinal regression. Confucian orientations are strongest in Vietnam and Singapore. Collectivism and hierarchism are associated with greater trust in government pandemic information, more favorable evaluations of crisis management, and stronger support for emergency measures. Harmony is associated only with support for emergency measures; familialism shows no significant association. The findings suggest that Confucian culture does not operate as a unified orientation toward authority; relational obligation and morally grounded deference are the principal cultural channels shaping public responses to state action during crises.

title: Association between PHQ-9-measured depressive symptoms and a positive AD8 screen among older adults during the COVID-19 pandemic: a large cross-sectional study in China
abstract: The association between depressive symptoms and possible cognitive impairment among older adults during the COVID-19 pandemic warrants further investigation. This cross-sectional study examined the association between depressive symptoms measured using the PHQ-9 and a positive AD8 screen among older adults in China, including whether the association departed from linearity. In this cross-sectional study, participants aged 60 years or older were recruited through quota sampling in 120 cities selected using a non-probability approach across China. The PHQ-9 scale was used to assess depressive symptoms, and the AD8 was used to screen for possible cognitive impairment or possible dementia. Logistic regression, restricted cubic spline regression analyses, and subgroup analyses were conducted to examine the association between depressive symptoms and a positive AD8 screen. Among 1,026 participants, 483 (47.1%) screened positive on the AD8. The fully adjusted logistic regression analysis revealed a significant association between PHQ-9 scores and a positive AD8 screen (OR, 95% CI: 1.34, 1.05–1.71, per 1 SD increase). The restricted cubic spline analysis indicated a nonlinear association between depressive symptoms and a positive AD8 screen ( P for overall < 0.001; P for nonlinear < 0.001). Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested differences in the association between depressive symptoms and a positive AD8 screen by living-alone status and chronic illness. This cross-sectional study identified a nonlinear association between depressive symptoms measured using the PHQ-9 and a positive AD8 screen among older adults during the COVID-19 pandemic. These findings suggest that depressive symptoms may help identify older adults who could benefit from further cognitive assessment and closer clinical attention.
