title: Understanding the Market Volatility during COVID-19 and Global Financial Crisis through ARCH/ GARCH Modelling of Conventional and Islamic Indices
abstract: This study investigated the volatility and predictability of Islamic and conventional stock indices during two significant crises; the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2007-08 financial crisis. Using ARCH/GARCH models, the study examined the volatility behaviour of both types of indices, while ARMA/ARIMA models are employed to disclose their predictability and autoregressive characteristics. The findings revealed that Islamic indices exhibited unique resilience to financial shocks. Specifically, Islamic indices showed reduced sensitivity to initial market disruptions in both crises, suggesting greater stability compared to conventional indices. However, both Islamic and conventional indices experienced sustained volatility in prolonged crises, highlighting the need for robust risk management strategies. The study addressed a critical gap by examining how these crises affected the volatility of Islamic and conventional indices, identifying similarities and differences in their volatility patterns during periods of financial turmoil. The findings also highlight the stabilizing role of Islamic finance principles and offer important implications for investors, policymakers, and regulators in enhancing market resilience and designing effective crisis-response strategies.

title: Relationship between Profile, Quality of Life and Burden of Older People With Dementia’s Caregivers during the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: This study was to verify the quality of life and caregiver burden of older people with dementia during the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (COVID-19) pandemic, and the clinical and sociodemographic factors associated with them. This cross-sectional study was conducted remotely and included Brazilian older people with a mild to moderate stage of dementia and their family caregivers. The caregivers reported older people’s clinical and sociodemographic characteristics. Caregiver characteristics were also collected. The sample comprised 37 pairs of older adults and caregivers, involving older adults with a mean age of 77.5 years old and caregivers who were mostly women (86.5%). Only caregiver years of study and caregiver burden significantly influenced caregiver quality of life. Caregiver distress related to older people’s behavior symptoms, older people’s behavioral symptoms and caregiver quality of life influenced caregiver burden. These caregivers have a fair quality of life and moderate to mild burden during the COVID-19 pandemic. The fewer years of study, the higher quality of life the caregiver presents. The lower caregiver quality of life, the higher caregiver distress related to behavioral symptoms, and the older people’s behavioral symptoms, the higher the caregiver burden is.

title: Epigenetic aging during the COVID-19 pandemic: A prospective longitudinal study with prepandemic baseline data in children, adolescents, and adults.
abstract: Psychosocial stress is a risk factor for aging-related diseases. The COVID-19 pandemic placed a psychosocial burden on individuals, potentially increasing the risk for aging-related diseases for which epigenetic clocks are used as early biomarkers. Based on four epigenetic clocks (DunedinPACE, GrimAge2, Horvath, and PedBE), we investigated whether epigenetic aging changed during the pandemic and whether these changes were associated with objective and subjective pandemic-related stressors and preexisting individual risk factors for poorer physical and mental health. We used prospective longitudinal data (n = 1,028), including repeated salivary DNA collection from children (n = 359, MAGE = 9.5 y), adolescents (n = 385, MAGE = 15.5 y), and adults (n = 284, MAGE = 24.3 y). Saliva was collected before the first phase of containment measures in Germany in March 2020 and after the second phase in 2021. We observed significant increases in epigenetic age acceleration (PedBE: b = 0.17, P < 0.0001; GrimAge2: b = 0.08, P < 0.0001) and pace of aging (DunedinPACE: b = 0.13, P < 0.0001) across all age groups. Prepandemic physical health and parental socioeconomic status, but not objective pandemic stressors, were significantly associated with this change. In adolescents, higher perceived pandemic burden was associated with a larger increase in pace of aging (DunedinPACE: b = 0.04, P = 0.01). Together, these findings suggest that prepandemic individual risk factors for poorer physical and mental health are accompanied by measurable increases in epigenetic aging during the COVID-19 pandemic, with adolescence representing a sensitive phase to its psychosocial burden.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Photo quality in political Twitter during COVID-19
abstract: Photo quality on social media has received little published research attention, despite the critical role that images play in social media. While photo quality is an inherently subjective evaluation, it is also based upon standards that are widely shared by professionals. This study builds upon professional standards of photo quality to analyze images on Twitter, a popular social media app. Since the COVID-19 pandemic placed increased demands on political social media to inform the public, this study focused on the use of images on Twitter from political leaders in the US during 2020. This study created a reliable rubric to evaluate photo quality, confirmed through intercoder reliability testing. Of 471 tweets from US governors that included photographs, 34 percent were of professional quality. Quantitative analysis linked high-quality photos to larger states, images including the governor’s face and images with patriotic themes. Qualitative analysis described how photographs utilized color, lighting, and angles to enhance messages.

title: FORMATIVE PROCESS OF GRADUATE STUDENTS IN NURSING IN THE CONTEXT OF COVID-19
abstract: Objective: to report the experience of remote teaching in an academic master’s degree course during the covid-19 pandemic. Methods: this is a descriptive study, experience report type, experienced from October to December 2020 in a mandatory subject of the Postgraduate Program in Nursing of a Public University in the state of Pará. Results: The educational activities took place synchronously and asynchronous, from virtual classes and texts for reading, all of that was possible by the use of educational technological strategies in the experienced pandemic scenario. Remote teaching required students and teachers to adapt to the new classroom routine in their homes, adapting the study environment and appropriate equipment for this context. Even with the challenges faced, the establishment of the remote learning process added skills among those involved, improvement of tools and digital transformation of the conventional classroom. Conclusion: remote teaching was efficient and provided opportunities for pedagogical mediations, promoting collaborative learning among students. It also revealed the need for training for those involved in the process.

title: Effects of Increased and Decreased Cognitive Social Capital on Depressive Symptoms Along the Income Gradient During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Evidence from Asymmetric Fixed-Effects Models
abstract: Social capital is considered to protect health when facing natural hazard-related disasters and pandemics. We further differentiated the effects of increased and decreased cognitive social capital (measured using generalized trust, trust in neighbors, trust in local government officials, and reciprocity) on depressive symptoms in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic and examined the moderating effect of household income on these effects, while controlling for unobserved time-invariant factors. Using follow-up data from the 2018 and 2020 China Family Panel Studies (N = 14,908), we conducted asymmetric fixed-effects regression. We found that decreased generalized trust and decreased reciprocity were associated with greater depressive symptoms, whereas their increased components were not associated with depressive symptoms. Furthermore, decreased equivalized household income exacerbated the effect of decreased reciprocity on greater depressive symptoms. Therefore, attention should be paid to preventing cognitive social capital decline to safeguard mental health during a pandemic, especially for people with declining household income. Future studies and policies should consider the distinct health effects of increased and decreased social capital when facing a pandemic.
journal: International Journal of Disaster Risk Science

title: Navigating resilience and barriers in mental health care: retrospective accounts of ethnic minority older adults during the COVID-19 pandemic in remote Northern Thailand
abstract: Ethnic minority older adults living in remote mountainous areas may face substantial barriers to accessing mental health care, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, limited evidence exists regarding their experiences of mental health care and the factors influencing service utilization in these underserved communities. This study explored the retrospectively recalled experiences of ethnic minority older adults and their caregivers in navigating mental health care during the COVID-19 pandemic and the continuing consequences of these experiences in remote Northern Thailand. A qualitative study design was used. Face-to-face, in-depth interviews were conducted with 22 participants, including 11 ethnic minority older adults with mental health problems and 11 family caregivers. Although interviews were conducted between January and March 2024, participants were asked to retrospectively describe their experiences with mental health care during the COVID-19 pandemic and any continuing consequences in the post-pandemic period. Data were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis. Two overarching themes and eleven sub-themes were identified. The first theme, Challenges in providing mental health care for ethnic minority older adults with mental health problems , described barriers related to limited mental health literacy, restricted access to mental health services and technology, geographic isolation, perceived disparities in service provision, inadequate caregiver preparedness, and the psychological consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic. The second theme, Perceptions and expectations of mental health care , reflected the importance of culturally responsive care, cultural and spiritual practices, family support, alternative approaches to care, and strategies for improving mental health service delivery. Participants also described resilience through family relationships, community engagement, and cultural resources that supported coping during the pandemic. Ethnic minority older adults in remote communities retrospectively described multiple barriers to accessing and utilizing mental health services during the COVID-19 pandemic. At the same time, family support, community participation, and cultural and spiritual practices were perceived as important resources for coping with mental health challenges. These findings suggest the importance of culturally responsive and accessible mental health services that are aligned with the needs and contexts of ethnic minority communities.

title: REGISTROS DE VISITAS DOMICILIARES NA ATENÇÃO PRIMÁRIA À SAÚDE NO BRASIL ANTES, DURANTE E APÓS A PANDEMIA DE COVID-19, 2019–2025
abstract: Objetivo: descrever a evolução anual dos registros de visitas domiciliares realizadas na Atenção Primária à Saúde (APS) no Brasil de 2019 a 2025, por região e unidade da federação, e relacioná-la ao número de agentes comunitários de saúde (ACS). Método: estudo ecológico descritivo de série temporal anual, com os totais anuais (12 meses) do Sistema de Informação em Saúde para a Atenção Básica e a média anual de ACS do Cadastro Nacional de Estabelecimentos de Saúde. Calcularam-se variações percentuais, índice com base em 2019 e registros por ACS por mês, comparando 2019–2022 e 2022–2025 em relação à emergência sanitária. Resultados: os registros cresceram 123,6% entre 2019 e 2025, mais de 2019 a 2022 (74,2%) do que de 2022 a 2025 (28,4%), depois da queda de 2020. O Sul cresceu 48,8%, bem abaixo das demais regiões. Com o número médio de ACS pouco alterado até 2024 e menor em 2025, os registros por ACS passaram de 91,8 para 219,8 por mês. source_records.abstract: Objetivo: descrever a evolução anual dos registros de visitas domiciliares realizadas na Atenção Primária à Saúde (APS) no Brasil de 2019 a 2025, por região e unidade da federação, e relacioná-la ao número de agentes comunitários de saúde (ACS). Método: estudo ecológico descritivo de série temporal anual, com os totais anuais (12 meses) do Sistema de Informação em Saúde para a Atenção Básica e a média anual de ACS do Cadastro Nacional de Estabelecimentos de Saúde. Calcularam-se variações percentuais, índice com base em 2019 e registros por ACS por mês, comparando 2019–2022 e 2022–2025 em relação à emergência sanitária. Resultados: os registros cresceram 123,6% entre 2019 e 2025, mais de 2019 a 2022 (74,2%) do que de 2022 a 2025 (28,4%), depois da queda de 2020. O Sul cresceu 48,8%, bem abaixo das demais regiões. Com o número médio de ACS pouco alterado até 2024 e menor em 2025, os registros por ACS passaram de 91,8 para 219,8 por mês. Conclusão: os registros mais que dobraram com pouca variação da força de trabalho até 2024, o que pede acompanhar o registro por agente e distinguir visita realizada de item registrado.

title: KIỂM SOÁT ĐƯỜNG HUYẾT NỘI VIỆN VÀ TỬ VONG Ở BỆNH NHÂN COVID-19 CÓ ĐÁI THÁO ĐƯỜNG TYPE 2 TẠI BỆNH VIỆN BỆNH NHIỆT ĐỚI, THÀNH PHỐ HỒ CHÍ MINH, 2021-2022
abstract: Mục tiêu: Mô tả đường huyết nội viện và mối liên quan với tử vong ở bệnh nhân COVID-19 có đái tháo đường type 2. Đối tượng và phương pháp: Nghiên cứu hồi cứu, mô tả có phân tích trên 154 bệnh nhân COVID-19 có đái tháo đường type 2 điều trị tại Bệnh viện Bệnh Nhiệt đới, thành phố Hồ Chí Minh từ tháng 6/2021 đến tháng 9/2022. Kết quả: Có 31/154 bệnh nhân tử vong, chiếm 20,1%. Đường huyết lúc nhập viện trung bình là 243 ± 152 mg/dL; đường huyết trung bình nội viện là 223 ± 55 mg/dL. Có 121 bệnh nhân có đường huyết trung bình nội viện > 180 mg/dL, chiếm 78,6%. Nhóm tử vong có đường huyết trung bình nội viện cao hơn nhóm hồi phục, lần lượt là 244 ± 47 mg/dL và 217 ± 55 mg/dL; p = 0,015. Đường huyết trung bình nội viện > 180 mg/dL gặp ở 30/31 bệnh nhân tử vong và 91/123 bệnh nhân hồi phục, có liên quan với tử vong trong phân tích đơn biến với OR = 10,55; 95% CI: 1,38-80,54; p = 0,006. Kết luận: Đường huyết trung bình nội viện > 180 mg/dL thường gặp ở bệnh nhân COVID-19 có đái tháo đường type 2 và có liên quan với tử vong trong phân tích đơn biến. Cần theo dõi sát đường huyết ở nhóm bệnh nhân này trong quá trình điều trị.

title: Mortalidade proporcional de indígenas e não indígenas brasileiros antes, durante e após a pandemia de covid-19
abstract: Objetivo: analisar o perfil da mortalidade na população indígena e não indígena no Brasil, antes, durante e após a pandemia de COVID-19. Métodos: estudo descritivo com dados do Sistema de Informações sobre Mortalidade referentes aos óbitos entre povos indígenas e não indígenas no Brasil, no período de 2018 a 2022. Calculou-se o excesso de óbitos e a mortalidade proporcional de indígenas e não indígenas brasileiros, segundo características sociodemográficas e causas básicas de morte. Resultados: os povos indígenas apresentaram expressivo excesso de óbitos, com pico em 2021. A mortalidade proporcional foi elevada entre os indígenas menores de 1 ano, em contraste com a estabilidade observada entre os não indígenas da mesma faixa etária. No período analisado, os óbitos entre os povos indígenas concentraram-se na região Norte, no sexo masculino e antes dos 60 anos, enquanto os não indígenas apresentaram maior mortalidade proporcional após os 60 anos, especialmente durante e após a pandemia. As principais causas de óbito na população indígena foram doenças infecciosas e parasitárias, doenças crônicas não transmissíveis e causas externas, o que reforça o contexto pandêmico e a transição epidemiológica do grupo. Conclusões: as desigualdades sociais, a negação da equidade no acesso à saúde, entre outros fatores, refletem-se na manutenção da elevada mortalidade prematura entre os povos indígenas, agravada pela pandemia.
authors: Ana Carolina Micheletti Gomide Nogueira de Sá

title: La vida cotidiana de las personas mayores de Manizales (Colombia) en tiempos de COVID-19
abstract: Este estudio tuvo como objetivo comprender la vida cotidiana de las personas mayores de la ciudad de Manizales en relación a los cambios en sus interacciones y prácticas sociales durante el periodo de la emergencia sanitaria por COVID-19. Se desarrolló un enfoque cualitativo con alcance descriptivo, basado en entrevistas semiestructuradas y un grupo focal con la participación de hombres y mujeres mayores. El análisis, de carácter inductivo y desde una perspectiva fenomenológica, permitió interpretar las experiencias desde la voz propia de los participantes. Los hallazgos evidenciaron que, aunque la vida cotidiana se vio interrumpida por el riesgo de contagio, surgieron transformaciones significativas, como la reducción de círculos sociales, cambios en la percepción del cuidado y la seguridad, visibilización de desigualdades por edad y estigmas hacia la vejez. También se identificó una falta de reconocimiento de las personas mayores como sujetos con capacidad de agencia. Asimismo, se reafirma el papel fundamental de la familia, la sociedad y el Estado en su protección, y se destaca el creciente interés de esta población por adquirir competencias en el uso de dispositivos tecnológicos.

title: [Gender and age characteristics of cases of disability during the pandemic of coronavirus infection in Moscow].
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has been a global stress factor for population health in most countries, including Russia. The high prevalence and economic burden of diseases make it important to study the regional characteristics of population morbidity among different population groups. The aim of this study was to identify the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on temporary disability cases among residents of Moscow by gender and age, based on data from a primary healthcare organization. The assessment was based on data from 2019 to 2024. The dynamics of the total number of disability cases from 2019 to 2024, as well as their distribution by gender and age categories, were analyzed. The «disability coefficient» was calculated for the entire attached population and for specific gender and age groups. The average duration of days of disability due to respiratory diseases during the study period was also evaluated. It can be stated that the female part of the working population was more likely to apply for disability leaves, and the 35-49 age group had the highest number of temporary disability cases. There were no significant differences in the duration of temporary disability cases between men and women.

title: Post-ARDS Pulmonary Fibrosis: From Molecular Mechanisms to Clinical Management
abstract: Abstract Background Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a severe inflammatory lung injury caused by various factors, including infection, trauma and shock. The predominant pathological alteration in its late stages is pulmonary fibrosis (PF), characterised by progressive extracellular matrix deposition, architectural destruction and functional impairment. Particularly in COVID-19-induced ARDS, PF incidence has markedly increased, making it a major sequela impacting patients’ long-term quality of life. Methods This review systematically examines post-acute lung injury (ALI)/ARDS PF through three perspectives: pathogenesis, prediction and treatment. Results Mechanistically, the fibrotic process involves epithelial injury and mesenchymal transition, fibroblast activation with aberrant extracellular matrix remodelling, dysregulated inflammation with immune cell involvement and clinical management-related factors. For prediction, various biomarkers (including growth factors, matrix proteins and inflammatory markers) and imaging features (particularly high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics) demonstrate clinical value. Integrated multiparameter models incorporating artificial intelligence show promise for early identification and risk stratification of high-risk patients. Therapeutic strategies encompass anti-inflammatory approaches (e.g., corticosteroids and antioxidants), antifibrotic agents (pirfenidone and nintedanib), cell-based therapies (mesenchymal stem cells and exosomes) and emerging genetic/RNA interventions. However, specific preventive and therapeutic approaches tailored to the post-ALI/ARDS PF population remain inadequate in clinical practice. Conclusions Future research should focus on elucidating underlying mechanisms, refining early-warning systems, exploring personalised treatments and facilitating clinical translation. The ultimate goal is to transition from traditional supportive care to proactive prevention through enhanced clinical surveillance, early prediction and rational intervention, thereby preventing fibrosis progression and improving outcomes in ARDS survivors.

title: Models, designs, and impact of virtual wards: a scoping review.
abstract: OBJECTIVE This scoping review maps international evidence on the models, design features, and reported impacts of virtual wards, addressing technology-enabled approaches that deliver hospital-level care in patients' homes. INTRODUCTION Virtual wards expanded rapidly during and after COVID-19, offering hospital-level monitoring and multidisciplinary care at home. Despite their growth, definitions and designs remain inconsistent, and evidence on their impact may vary. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA This review included studies involving adults (≥18 years) receiving hospital-level care at home through a virtual ward, as well as health care professionals and unpaid carers involved in delivering or supporting such care. Studies exclusively focused on people aged under 18 years were excluded. The concept of interest was virtual wards, defined as health care approaches that remotely monitor patients who would typically require hospital-level care, supported by digital technologies and structured escalation and de-escalation processes. The context encompassed health care delivery outside traditional inpatient hospital settings, where virtual wards were implemented for admission avoidance, early supported discharge, or both. Eligible evidence included English-language primary research studies, systematic and scoping reviews, program evaluations, and relevant gray literature published from 2019 onwards. METHODS Two searches were conducted following JBI methodology and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). An initial search (May 2023) and an updated search (January 2024) were run across 6 databases: CINAHL (EBSCOhost), Embase (Ovid), Emcare (Ovid), HMIC (Ovid), MEDLINE (Ovid), PsycINFO (ProQuest). The Health Services Journal (HSJ) was also searched, alongside targeted gray literature sources, including GrayNet, British Library, NHS, and World Health Organization (WHO) websites. Dual screening, piloted data extraction, and narrative mapping with frequency counts were conducted. RESULTS Thirty-one sources (12 from databases, 19 from gray literature) were included. Virtual wards were commonly designed for admission avoidance, early discharge, or both. Most were acute-led, with some joint models; only 1 operated 24/7. Reported features included multidisciplinary input, personalized care plans, escalation protocols, and technologies such as telephone, messaging, video, and wearable monitoring. Documented impacts included improved communication, patient-centered care, cost savings, reduced readmissions, the challenges of digital exclusion, variable discharge criteria, and workforce sustainability. Overall, these findings highlight implications for both patients and health care teams. CONCLUSION Virtual wards have been presented in the literature as a promising model for implementing digitally enabled hospital-level care at home. To achieve sustainable impact, services require clear admission/discharge criteria, co-design with stakeholders, robust governance, reliable technology, and multidisciplinary workforce planning. Further research is needed to evaluate issues of efficacy, cost, and scalability.

The concept of interest was virtual wards, defined as health care approaches that remotely monitor patients who would typically require hospital-level care, supported by digital technologies and structured escalation and de-escalation processes. The context encompassed health care delivery outside traditional inpatient hospital settings, where virtual wards were implemented for admission avoidance, early supported discharge, or both. Eligible evidence included English-language primary research studies, systematic and scoping reviews, program evaluations, and relevant gray literature published from 2019 onwards. METHODS Two searches were conducted following JBI methodology and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The Health Services Journal (HSJ) was also searched, alongside targeted gray literature sources, including GrayNet, British Library, NHS, and World Health Organization (WHO) websites. Dual screening, piloted data extraction, and narrative mapping with frequency counts were conducted. RESULTS Thirty-one sources (12 from databases, 19 from gray literature) were included. Documented impacts included improved communication, patient-centered care, cost savings, reduced readmissions, the challenges of digital exclusion, variable discharge criteria, and workforce sustainability. Overall, these findings highlight implications for both patients and health care teams. CONCLUSION Virtual wards have been presented in the literature as a promising model for implementing digitally enabled hospital-level care at home. To achieve sustainable impact, services require clear admission/discharge criteria, co-design with stakeholders, robust governance, reliable technology, and multidisciplinary workforce planning. Further research is needed to evaluate issues of efficacy, cost, and scalability.

title: Application Research on mRNA Vaccine Technology in Infectious Disease Prevention and Control
abstract: Compared with inactivated, subunit, and DNA nucleic-acid approaches, mRNA vaccines do not enter the nucleus and carry no risk of genomic integration; they are translated in the cytoplasm and can jointly induce humoral and cellular immunity. In vitro transcription and cell-free production also markedly shorten the interval from sequence acquisition to vaccine output. This paper summarizes the configurations of non-replicating, self-amplifying, and circular RNA vaccines, as well as the characteristics of PRR-mediated immune activation, and reviews key process technologies including the 5′ cap, UTRs, pseudouridine modification, dsRNA removal, and LNP delivery. At the application level, the discussion centers on the billion-scale administration of SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines, booster immunization, and variant-component updating, while also reviewing progress and limitations in pipelines for influenza, rabies post-exposure prophylaxis, HIV, hepatitis B, and other diseases, and analyzing their public health significance in shortening emergency response windows and tracking strain drift. IVT purity, ultracold-chain requirements, and accessibility in resource-limited regions remain the main constraints. Self-amplifying/circular RNA, multivalent combination vaccines, and inhalable mucosal delivery may help move this platform from a “single pandemic response” toward broader infectious disease prevention and control practice.
journal: International Journal of Public Health and Medical Research

title: Predicting key viral mutations from within-host deep sequencing data
abstract: Rapid SARS-CoV-2 evolution drives continuous epidemic waves, harming vaccine protection and exerting heavy burden to population health. Predicting virus evolution holds the key for current and future medical countermeasures against infectious diseases by allowing well-matching vaccines and timely epidemic response. However, due to its high genetic diversity, fast transmissibility and evolutionary rate, accurate and timely prediction of SARS-CoV-2 evolution remains a challenge. To address this, we developed a computational framework, Beth-2, to predict key mutations of SARS-CoV-2 through analyzing within-host viral genome deep sequencing data. We leveraged the early fitness signals of variants exhibited within-host and their fitness pattern between-host to infer the emerging mutations with fitness potential. In retrospective data validation, 98.6% of the key SARS-CoV-2 mutations on receptor binding domain could be detected by our model with a median lead time of 9 mo before they reached predominance at population level. Among the 26 prospectively predicted mutations, 69% of them exhibited significantly enhanced transmissibility and five showed significant immune escape from plasma of subjects who received COVID-19 mRNA vaccine collected 6 mo after the prediction time. The mutations predicted by Beth-2 that are functionally enhanced include F456L, the defining mutation of multiple current circulating lineages, including KP.3, NB.1.8.1, and XFG. The model captures mutations of high fitness potential under the natural immune environment of host and is applicable to other pathogens. The framework can be implemented along with the existing genome surveillance network and offers an efficient and effective instrument for vaccine preparation and epidemic response.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

title: VENAS2: Bidirectional Mutation Modeling for Genomic Surveillance Reveals Reversions and Hidden Transmission Links in Pathogens
abstract: Accurately resolving pathogen evolution is essential for genomic surveillance, yet existing approaches often assume unidirectional mutation accumulation and fail to capture reversions that obscure lineage classification and transmission dynamics. Here we present VENAS2, a scalable framework that integrates genomic, temporal and geographic information to construct spatiotemporal evolutionary networks while explicitly modeling bidirectional mutational processes. Applied to 7.25 million SARS-CoV-2 genomes from GISAID between December 2019 and June 2024, VENAS2 reconstructed the evolutionary history of SARS-CoV-2 and precisely inferred the temporal dynamics of major variants of concern. Further application to the Viridian dataset revealed 4,654 distinct genomic sites with at least one potential reversion event, providing a systematic view of potential reversion signals during viral evolution. Extending to Mycobacterium tuberculosis, VENAS2 delineated major lineages and identified over threefold additional transmission clusters beyond conventional genomic distance-based methods, uncovering hidden links enriched for drug-resistant strains. These results demonstrate VENAS2's capacity to uncover cryptic evolutionary processes across viruses and bacteria, providing a generalizable platform that bridges genomic surveillance with actionable public health response.

title: Trends of delayed healthcare access in ocular injuries: a multicenter study in community hospitals, Central Thailand.
abstract: AIM To determine the annual trends and risk factors for delayed access to care in community hospitals across Central Thailand-an area with high occupational injury risk. METHODS This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed data from four community hospitals in Central Thailand over six years (October 1, 2018-September 17, 2024). Patients aged ≥20y with ocular injuries, identified via International Classification of Diseases-10 (ICD-10) codes, were included. Demographics, injury characteristics, and care-seeking behaviors were recorded. Delayed access was defined as presentation >24h post-injury. Linear and logistic regression models were used to identify associated risk factors. Annual fiscal trends were analyzed to assess year-to-year patterns in delayed healthcare access. RESULTS Among 6571 ocular injury cases, 4034 (61.4%) were male, with median age 43y [interquartile range (IQR) 31-57y], and 3983 (79.3%) were manual laborers. Delayed healthcare access was observed in 2426 cases (36.9%). Significant risk factors included age ≥60y [aOR: 1.55; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.32-1.82], visits to F2-level hospitals [adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 2.03; 95%CI: 1.73-2.38], and outpatient visits (aOR: 14.01; 95%CI: 12.18-16.12). In F2 hospitals, subgroup analysis revealed a U-shaped reduction in delayed healthcare access for ocular injuries during the COVID-19 pandemic (2019-2021), adjusted for age and gender. CONCLUSION This first in-depth study of ocular injuries in Central Thailand's community hospitals found persistently high delayed presentations, with older age, F2 hospital visits, and outpatient department (OPD) attendance as key contributing factors. The trend during the COVID-19 pandemic highlights the important role of lower-tier community hospitals in providing prompt and accessible care for patients. Strengthening healthcare infrastructure and public awareness is essential to ensure timely care and reduce preventable vision-related complications.

title: Viral Immunomodulation as a Potential Driver of Trained Immunity: Emerging Mechanisms of Innate Immune Memory and Antiviral Protection
abstract: The discovery of trained immunity has challenged the longstanding view that immunological memory is restricted to the adaptive immune system. Trained immunity refers to the capacity of innate immune cells to undergo long-term functional reprogramming following exposure to microbial, endogenous, or environmental stimuli, resulting in enhanced responses to subsequent challenges. Trained immunity is mediated by epigenetic and metabolic remodeling, including changes in chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and cellular metabolism. Recent studies further demonstrate that these memory-like properties can also be established in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), providing a basis for their long-term persistence. While Bacillus Calmette–Guérin (BCG) and β-glucan are the best-characterized inducers of trained immunity, increasing evidence indicates that viral infections and viral vaccines can also induce durable innate immune reprogramming. Epidemiological studies have demonstrated heterologous protective effects associated with vaccinia, measles, and oral polio vaccines, while cytomegalovirus infection and severe SARS-CoV-2 infection have been linked to long-lasting alterations in innate immune function. Notably, many of these viruses possess potent immune evasion mechanisms that suppress interferon signaling, modulate NF-κB activation, disrupt antigen presentation, and alter myeloid cell function. We propose that viral immune evasion and immunomodulatory strategies may promote trained immunity by triggering compensatory metabolic, epigenetic, and transcriptional reprogramming that persists after resolution of infection. This review summarizes the historical development and molecular basis of trained immunity and examines emerging evidence linking viral infections and viral vaccines to innate immune memory. We further discuss the potential roles of virus-induced autophagy and long non-coding RNAs as mechanistic bridges connecting viral infection, immune reprogramming, and trained immunity. Understanding how viral infections shape innate immune memory may provide new opportunities for antiviral therapies, vaccine design, and broad-spectrum immune protection.

title: Timing of vaccine-associated anaphylaxis and implications for post-vaccination observation period: A systematic review and Canadian surveillance data analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND The post-vaccination observation period ensures the rapid identification and clinical management of immediate adverse events following immunization, including anaphylaxis. Recommended observation periods vary internationally. In Canada, a 15 min observation period is standard. This systematic review assesses the empirical basis for these recommendations and the potential impact of varying observation period durations. OBJECTIVE To describe time to onset of anaphylaxis following immunization and provide an empirical basis to evaluate variable post-vaccination observation period durations. METHODS This study combined mixed methods to capture the available evidence base. A systematic review following PRISMA guidelines searched Embase and MEDLINE from inception to March 6, 2023, for studies reporting time to onset of anaphylaxis within 30 min of vaccination. Anaphylaxis reports submitted to the Canadian Adverse Events Following Immunization Surveillance System (CAEFISS) were also analyzed. RESULTS Of 44 studies reporting 1365 cases of anaphylaxis, 1229 (90%) had recorded onset time, of which 802 (65%) occurred within 30 min. Among cases with sufficient temporal detail (n = 305), 236 (77%) had onset within 15 min; of 113 cases with 5-min interval data, 61% had onset within 5 min. Findings were broadly consistent across COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 vaccines, age groups, and levels of diagnostic certainty. Among 2193 CAEFISS reports, the median onset time was 12 min; 78% (n = 1702) occurred within 30 min, 80% (n = 1363) of which occurred within 15 min, and 46% (n = 628) of those within 5 min. Results were similar across age groups and vaccine types. CONCLUSIONS Vaccine-associated anaphylaxis most commonly presents within 15 min of vaccination. A routine 15-min observation period would be expected to capture most (77-80%) events occurring within 30 min.

title: Consistent dietary adherence in children and adolescents with celiac disease reflected in anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA and IgG: through diagnostic advancements and epidemiological challenges.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE Recent ESPGHAN guidelines permit the omission of duodenal biopsies in the diagnosis of celiac disease (CeD) in children with tTG-IgA≥10× upper limit of normal, regardless of clinical symptoms. This non-invasive approach may compromise dietary adherence through underestimating disease severity and questioning the diagnosis by families. We monitored serologic response in biopsy-based vs. no-biopsy cohorts using both tTG-IgA and tTG-IgG. A second aim was to investigate subjective and objective factors associated with dietary adherence, including during the period of the COVID restrictions. METHODS Between 2020-2025, 190 children and adolescents with CeD were followed according to ESPGHAN guidelines. Biopsy-based and no-biopsy cohorts were compared in terms of clinical and demographic factors, laboratory results and dietary adherence. A targeted COVID-19 questionnaire was completed by 159 families. RESULTS tTG-IgA levels normalized within 6 months in 55% of patients and after 12 months in 89%. tTG-IgG titers showed similar dynamics, with slightly faster early decline (74% normalized at 6 months), and were indispensable in 4 children (2.1%) with IgA deficiency. Antibody decline was comparable for the biopsy and no-biopsy groups. Only 13% of children exhibited nonadherence, mostly as a single episode. The no-biopsy group had a statistically higher incidence of anemia. The COVID-19 disease course was predominantly mild (94%), with gastrointestinal complications in 3 cases. The perceived impact of COVID-19-related lockdown on dietary adherence was self-reported as neutral in 65% and positive in 26% of families. CONCLUSIONS The no-biopsy approach sustained excellent antibody normalization rates, as measured by both tTG-IgA and tTG-IgG. Nonadherence was rare and mostly associated with adolescence, peer influence, challenged family/social structure, limited parental supervision, poor choice of school meals, and comorbidities. The importance of targeted educational interventions and follow-up is emphasized.

title: C‐terminal engineered human H‐chain ferritin for peptide loading within the protein nanocage
abstract: Abstract Self‐assembling proteins are widely used in bionanotechnology due to their biocompatibility, non‐toxicity, structural stability, and easy functionalization. Ferritins (Fts) are particularly attractive systems, as they assemble into highly ordered nanocages with a hollow internal cavity. Their assembly and disassembly can be modulated by various protocols, such as changes in pH or the use of denaturing agents, enabling their application in molecular encapsulation and drug delivery. However, the efficiency of encapsulation remains challenging, often resulting in low or heterogeneous loading and incomplete protein recovery. Here, we load peptides into the core of the human H‐chain ferritin ( hHFt ) by genetically fusing them to the C‐terminus of the Ft subunit, a region facing the inner cavity. As model peptides, we used fragments derived from the SARS ‐ CoV ‐2 Spike protein sharing similar physicochemical properties but different charges. The structure of the functionalized nanocages was assessed using techniques like transmission electron microscopy, native gel electrophoresis, and X‐ray crystallography. High‐resolution structural analysis revealed interesting conformational changes in the hHFt BC ‐loop associated with C‐terminal functionalization, while the overall nanocage architecture is preserved. Additionally, NMR measurements of the transverse relaxation ( T 2 ) of a target peptide demonstrated that the nanocages do not expose the fused peptides under native conditions, but upon disassembly, can efficiently expose them, demonstrating that C‐terminal genetic functionalization of ferritin nanocages is a robust and effective approach for nanobiotechnological applications.

title: Epidemiological Characteristics and Clinical Outcomes of Vaccine-associated Urticaria: A Retrospective Cross-sectional Analysis of the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System Database (1990-2025).
abstract: INTRODUCTION Urticaria is a commonly reported cutaneous adverse event following vaccination, which may range from mild self-limiting reactions to more severe hypersensitivity manifestations. Monitoring vaccine-associated urticaria is important for ongoing vaccine safety surveillance and pharmacovigilance. However, large-scale population-based analyses evaluating demographic characteristics, vaccine associations, onset intervals, and severity patterns remain limited. AIM The aim of the study was to analyze reports of urticaria in the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) database between 1990 and 2025 and evaluate demographic characteristics, vaccine type distribution, onset intervals, temporal trends, and seriousness patterns. METHODOLOGY A retrospective observational study was conducted using data from the VAERS database. Reports of urticaria submitted between January 1990 and March 2025 were included. The variables analyzed included age, sex, vaccine type, onset interval, and seriousness classification. Descriptive statistics were generated using frequencies and percentages, and comparative analyses were performed between serious and nonserious reports. RESULTS A total of 61,996 urticaria reports were identified during the study period. Most reports occurred among adults aged 18-49 years and females. Most reports were classified as nonserious and occurred within the early postvaccination period. COVID-19 vaccines accounted for the highest proportion of reports, followed by influenza and measles, mumps, and rubella vaccines. Temporal analysis demonstrated a marked increase in reporting during 2021, followed by declining trends thereafter. Comparative analysis identified differences in demographic and clinical characteristics between serious and nonserious reports. CONCLUSION Urticaria is a frequently reported adverse event following vaccination, with identifiable demographic, temporal, and clinical patterns. Most reports were nonserious and occurred shortly after vaccination, although differences were observed between serious and nonserious reports. Continued pharmacovigilance and future studies incorporating detailed clinical data are needed to better understand factors associated with vaccine-related urticaria.

title: [THE STRUCTURAL AND DYNAMIC CHARACTERISTICS OF THE DISEASES OF BLOOD CIRCULATION ORGANS IN THE KYRGYZ REPUBLIC].
abstract: The diseases of circulatory system continue to occupy leading positions in structure of morbidity and mortality of population, remaining one of key public health problems. The purpose of the study is to investigate dynamics of primary morbidity and prevalence of diseases of circulatory system by main nosological forms among adult and adolescent population of the Kyrgyz Republic in 2018-2024. The study used official data from the Center for E-Health Care that was analyzed using retrospective, statistical and comparative analytical methods. It was found that indicators of primary morbidity and prevalence were characterized by pronounced variability with greatest increase in 2022, against the background of decrease in 2020-2021, that may be due to changes in availability of medical care in period of COVID-19 pandemic. The highest levels of morbidity and prevalence were found for hypertension, coronary heart disease and cerebrovascular diseases. Some nosologies, including myocardial infarction and other peripheral vascular diseases, demonstrated sharp increase in indicators, suggesting changes in disease detection and health care seeking behavior of population. The obtained results confirm necessity to improve system of monitoring, prevention and early detection of cardiovascular diseases, especially among high-risk groups.

title: [THE TRENDS OF DEVELOPMENT OF SYSTEM OF PROTECTION OF REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH OF GIRLS-ADOLESCENTS OF ST. PETERSBURG].
abstract: The article presents results of comprehensive analysis of gynecological morbidity of girls-adolescents 15-17 years old in St. Petersburg in 2019-2024. It is established, on the basis of preventive examinations data, that average level of pathological affect made up to 105.04‰ and had pronounced trend to decreasing (β=-4.07; p=0.048). The comparative historical analysis demonstrated improvement of reproductive health indicators by 1.9 times as compared to basic data for 1996-1997. The characteristic of structure of gynecological morbidity of modern girls-adolescents in megalopolis is predominance of menstrual disorders (90.7% of newly diagnosed cases). At that, low medical activity of girls-adolescents continues that is proved by high percentage of newly diagnosed diseases detected only during preventive examinations (29.0%) and as well as significant prevalence of general morbidity over primary one. It is established that in St. Petersburg indicators of morbidity are 2.3-2.6 times higher than the National average indicators that is related to better accessibility of medical care and more efficient system of preventive examinations in the megalopolis. The analysis of the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on gynecological morbidity of girls-adolescents revealed significant decreasing of appealability in 2020 and subsequent incomplete reestablishment of indicators that testifies structural changes in pattern of medical activity of girls-adolescents. The study confirms efficiency of the system of protection of reproductive health of girls-adolescents in St. Petersburg but at the same time indicates at necessity to further enhance medical activity of girls-adolescents and to develop target preventive programs.

title: [THE MODERN DEMOGRAPHIC CHANGES IN THE KYRGYZ REPUBLIC].
abstract: The article presents results of analysis of medical demographic indicators of the Kyrgyz Republic in 2016-2024. The study was carried out concerning dynamics of population size, natality, mortality and migration processes based on statistical data from the National Statistical Committee and the Center of E-Health Care. The regional differences in demographic trends were revealed. The high natality is specific for Southern regions, while in Northern regions its steady decreasing was fixed. It is established that COVID-19 pandemic had short-term impact on mortality growth in 2020. Despite positive natural increase, its pace is decreasing that requires elaboration of state demographic policy and mechanisms stimulating natality, population health promotion and development of regional health care infrastructure. In 2022-2023 migration flows demonstrated positive balance that reflects changes in social economic priorities of population. The main motives for migration remain low wages, limited career opportunities and uncertainty about future. The obtained results confirm necessity of systematic approach to prognostication of demographic processes and development of measures stabilizing medical demographic situation in the Republic.

title: Molecular detection of Human Metapneumovirus among geriatric patients presenting with acute respiratory tract infection in Ibadan, Nigeria
abstract: Abstract Acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) are among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and viruses are primarily responsible for these infections. The Human Metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a respiratory pathogen that was first identified in 2001 in the Netherlands, and has since been recognized as one of the major viral causes of respiratory infections. The clinical manifestations of hMPV infection are typically asymptomatic or mild in healthy adults, however, for high-risk populations, such as children less than 5 years, older people, immunocompromised individuals, and patients with underlying chronic conditions, hMPV infection can lead to severe clinical manifestations, such as pneumonia. Despite its substantial health burden, hMPV is not routinely tested for and monitored in many countries, there are also no approved vaccines or antiviral treatments, and management of the infection remains supportive. The recurrent hMPV related outbreaks in recent years and its potential to cause pandemics, particularly in the post-COVID-19 era, highlights the urgent need for improved surveillance and targeted interventions. Oropharyngeal and nasal swab samples were collected from five hundred and twenty four (524) geriatric patients comprising of outpatient individuals presenting with symptoms of acute respiratory tract infection (ARTI) and those attending the clinic for routine health checks recruited as asymptomatic controls from the period of April 2024 to May 2025. The samples were tested for the presence of Human metapneumovirus using a semi-nested Polymerase chain reaction targeting the Nucleoprotein (N) gene of the virus. Thirty six (6.9%) of the 524 samples were positive for Human Metapneumovirus infections with a significantly (p = 0.004) higher rate among symptomatic participants (5.2%). The difference in the rate of hMPV positivity between age groups and gender was not statistically significant (p = 0.707; p = 0.344 respectively). The three symptoms most commonly reported among hMPV positive cases in our study were cough (30.6%), fever (25%), and headache (25%); however the comparison of clinical symptoms across all the participants showed that chills and sore throat were the only symptoms statistically significant with hMPV positivity (p = 0.006; p = 0.023 respectively). HMPV positivity peaked during the month of July with the highest number of infections detected in symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals within that month. This study highlights the impact of hMPV among the geriatric population in Ibadan, Nigeria, indicating a necessity for more accurate and dependable estimates of the incidence of hMPV-associated disease in the older adult population.

title: Epidemiology of foodborne pathogens in Europe with special emphasis on the Republic of Croatia
abstract: This review evaluates the occurrence and epidemiological trends of major foodborne zoonotic pathogens in the European Union, with particular emphasis on the Republic of Croatia, over the period 2020-2024. Using the One Health framework, data were synthesised from annual zoonosis reports of the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), complemented by targeted national and regional studies. Following a temporary, pandemic-related decline in 2020, largely attributable to COVID-19 related disruptions in surveillance and behavioral changes, notification rates for most foodborne pathogens rebounded and stabilised at pre-pandemic or higher levels. Campylobacteriosis remained the most frequently reported zoonosis, while salmonellosis persisted at consistently high levels, with notable shifts in serovar distribution, including the emergence of Salmonella Infantis. Listeriosis, although less frequent, demonstrated the highest hospitalisation and case fatality rates, with a continued upward trend. Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) infections increased substantially, partly due to improved molecular diagnostics and enhanced surveillance sensitivity. Unlike existing consolidated EFSA/ECDC reports, this review highlights the importance of regional data for identifying localised hotspots and more precisely understanding transmission dynamics. This more detailed perspective emphasises the need for continuous, integrated surveillance across the human, veterinary, and environmental sectors to effectively address evolving, region-specific risks related to pathogen adaptation, antimicrobial resistance, and climate-related pressures within the food supply chain.

title: Understanding health behaviors and resilience during pandemics: a systematic review of ethical, cognitive, and existential dimensions
abstract: Pandemic events such as HIV/AIDS and COVID-19 destabilize not only public health systems but also the philosophical and ethical frameworks through which individuals interpret illness. Health behavior influenced by contagion challenges definitions of identity, perceptions of truth, moral reasoning, and core bioethical principles, including autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, and justice. This study employs a triadic lens, such as ontology, epistemology, and axiology, to examine how pandemic crises transform embodied experience, cognition, ethical response, and value-laden behavioral choices. From there, the consequences for health behavior are analyzed within both phenomenological and bioethical domains. Using a phenomenological framework, the study draws on interdisciplinary data, including clinical case reports, psychosocial literature, and first-person narratives. Philosophical constructs from Husserl, Merleau-Ponty, and Carel inform the mapping of existential vulnerability, cognitive distortion, and value formation. Bioethical principles from Beauchamp and Childress guide the interpretation of moral tensions arising in pandemic behavior, while public health ethics frameworks (e.g., Kass) contextualize collective obligations. Psychiatric presentations during COVID-19 provide illustrative grounding for abstract principles. Motivations and frameworks for pandemic health behaviors are reported as outcomes. A review of 134 articles helped frame the cognitive and ethical terrain of pandemic prevention and dissemination. Pandemics cause overlapping disruptions across ontological, epistemological, axiological, and bioethical levels. Embodied identity becomes fragmented by diagnostic classification, social distancing, and existential uncertainty, raising tensions between autonomy and relationality. Cognitive processing is hindered by emotional stress, misinformation, and isolation, leading to distorted perceptions of truth and reduced rationality, which complicates beneficent and non-maleficent decision-making. Moral behavior reflects value-based tensions—altruism, denial, concealment, stigma—negotiated within shifting contexts of personal risk, communal obligation, and distributive justice. These patterns illustrate how existential dislocation, epistemic fragmentation, and moral ambiguity shape lived experience and ethical behavior during a pandemic. Phenomenology offers vital insights into the human impact of pandemics by examining how relational, cognitive, and ethical dimensions shape illness experiences and health behaviors. Integrating bioethical principles clarifies why individuals struggle with autonomy, responsibility, and fairness during crises. To support recovery and coherence, public health governance must move beyond biomedical control toward emotionally attuned, ethically grounded care that emphasizes relational responsibility, moral imagination, and justice-oriented policy.

title: Phase II randomized non-inferiority trial comparing the humoral immunogenicity of NDV-HXP-S and BNT162b2 vaccines in Brazil
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) prompted an unprecedented global vaccine development response and accelerated regulatory pathways for clinical vaccine development. Despite the end of the public health emergency, sustained preparedness, including the availability of scalable and affordable vaccine platforms, remains essential. This was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled and non-inferiority Phase II clinical trial, to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of a fifth-dose booster of NDV-HXP-S 10 μg, an egg-derived, inactivated COVID-19 vectored-vaccine virus using the Newcastle disease virus (NDV) expressing stabilized prefusion S protein from the Wuhan-Hu-1 strain of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), versus BNT162b2 30 μg. Healthy participants aged 18–59 years ( n = 200) or ≥ 60 years ( n = 200) were randomized at a 1:1 ratio to receive a single intramuscular dose on Day 1. Primary immunogenicity endpoints (per-protocol) were the Day 29 geometric mean titer (GMT) ratio of the 50% neutralizing titer (NDV-HXP-S/BNT162b2) against SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan-Hu-1 and the difference in seroconversion proportions (≥ 4-fold rise if seropositive at baseline, or NT 50 > lower limit of quantification if seronegative). Non-inferiority margins were a point estimate ≥ 0.80 for GMT ratio, the lower bound of the one-tailed 97.5% confidence interval (CI) > 0.67 for GMT ratio, and a 97.5% CI lower bound > − 10% for seroconversion. Primary safety endpoints were vaccine-related solicited adverse events (AEs) through Day 7 and vaccine-related unsolicited AEs and serious adverse events (SAEs) through Day 28. Follow-up occurred for 12 and 6 months for safety and immunogenicity evaluation, respectively. Between February 28 and August 30, 2023, 389 eligible participants were included in the safety population. Of 389 participants, 263 (67.6%) were female, median age of 60.1 years (IQR, 40.8–65.4) and most were White, 218 (56.0%). Among the 311 (77.8%), the GMT ratio (NDV-HXP-S/BNT162b2) of neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 (Wuhan-Hu-1) was 0.50 (95% CI: 0.40‒0.60), measured on Day 29. The difference in seroconversion was − 36.7% (-45.3% to -28.0%). Vaccine-related solicited AEs occurred in 132 (67.3%) in NDV-HXP-S and 149 (77.2%) in BNT162b2 ( P = 0.032) within 7 days post-vaccination, while vaccine-related unsolicited AE occurred in 46 (23.5%) in NDV-HXP-S vs. 51 (26.4%) in BNT162b2 ( P = 0.558) within 28 days. There were no vaccine-related SAEs within 28 days post-vaccination. Inactivated NDV-HXP-S at 10 μg did not meet the criteria for non-inferiority in comparison to BNT162b2 at 30 μg in SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan-Hu-1 seroconversion and neutralization as a fifth-dose booster. Both vaccines were generally well tolerated during the observed follow-up. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier : NCT05354024 (Registration date: 2022-04-27).

Maria Aparecida Alves Leite dos Santos Almeida

This was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled and non-inferiority Phase II clinical trial, to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of a fifth-dose booster of NDV-HXP-S 10 μg, an egg-derived, inactivated COVID-19 vectored-vaccine virus using the Newcastle disease virus (NDV) expressing stabilized prefusion S protein from the Wuhan-Hu-1 strain of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), versus BNT162b2 30 μg. Healthy participants aged 18–59 years ( n = 200) or ≥ 60 years ( n = 200) were randomized at a 1:1 ratio to receive a single intramuscular dose on Day 1. Primary immunogenicity endpoints (per-protocol) were the Day 29 geometric mean titer (GMT) ratio of the 50% neutralizing titer (NDV-HXP-S/BNT162b2) against SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan-Hu-1 and the difference in seroconversion proportions (≥ 4-fold rise if seropositive at baseline, or NT 50 > lower limit of quantification if seronegative). Non-inferiority margins were a point estimate ≥ 0.80 for GMT ratio, the lower bound of the one-tailed 97.5% confidence interval (CI) > 0.67 for GMT ratio, and a 97.5% CI lower bound > − 10% for seroconversion. Primary safety endpoints were vaccine-related solicited adverse events (AEs) through Day 7 and vaccine-related unsolicited AEs and serious adverse events (SAEs) through Day 28. Follow-up occurred for 12 and 6 months for safety and immunogenicity evaluation, respectively. Between February 28 and August 30, 2023, 389 eligible participants were included in the safety population. Of 389 participants, 263 (67.6%) were female, median age of 60.1 years (IQR, 40.8–65.4) and most were White, 218 (56.0%). Among the 311 (77.8%), the GMT ratio (NDV-HXP-S/BNT162b2) of neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 (Wuhan-Hu-1) was 0.50 (95% CI: 0.40‒0.60), measured on Day 29. The difference in seroconversion was − 36.7% (-45.3% to -28.0%). Vaccine-related solicited AEs occurred in 132 (67.3%) in NDV-HXP-S and 149 (77.2%) in BNT162b2 ( P = 0.032) within 7 days post-vaccination, while vaccine-related unsolicited AE occurred in 46 (23.5%) in NDV-HXP-S vs. 51 (26.4%) in BNT162b2 ( P = 0.558) within 28 days. There were no vaccine-related SAEs within 28 days post-vaccination. Inactivated NDV-HXP-S at 10 μg did not meet the criteria for non-inferiority in comparison to BNT162b2 at 30 μg in SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan-Hu-1 seroconversion and neutralization as a fifth-dose booster. Both vaccines were generally well tolerated during the observed follow-up. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier : NCT05354024 (Registration date: 2022-04-27).

title: Combining alum with a TLR7-nanoparticle adjuvant enhances vaccine-elicited humoral and cellular immunity.
abstract: The rational integration of complementary adjuvant mechanisms offers a promising strategy to overcome immunodominance while simultaneously enhancing vaccine-elicited humoral and cellular immunity. Here, we investigated how combining aluminum hydroxide (Alum) with a previously developed nanoparticle platform for intracellular delivery of a Toll-like receptor 7 agonist (TLR7-NP) reshapes early antigen-presenting cell responses and downstream adaptive immunity. Following immunization, the combination of Alum and TLR7-NP broadened antigen acquisition across B cells and multiple dendritic cell subsets, including conventional type 1 dendritic cells (cDC1s), conventional type 2 dendritic cells (cDC2s), and plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs), while promoting their activation in draining lymph nodes. These early responses were followed by enhanced plasmablast expansion, germinal center B cell responses, and T follicular helper cell differentiation. Notably, nanoparticle-mediated TLR7 signaling promoted germinal center responses against the conserved, immunosubdominant S2 subunit of SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, while combination with Alum further amplified the magnitude of this response. The combined formulation consequently accelerated the generation of S2-specific antibodies and produced the strongest early cross-reactive antibody responses against diverse coronavirus spike proteins. In addition, Alum and TLR7-NP synergistically enhanced IFN-γ and granzyme B-producing CD4 + and CD8 + T cell responses. Together, these findings demonstrate that combining Alum-mediated adjuvanticity with nanoparticle-mediated intracellular TLR7 signaling can reshape antigen-presenting cell engagement to enhance antibody breadth and cellular immunity, providing a design principle for combining complementary biomaterial-based adjuvants in next-generation vaccines.

title: Beyond Metastatic Lymphadenopathy in Breast Cancer: Approach to Axillary Masses.
abstract: The axilla is a pyramid-shaped space containing tissues of various origins including adipose, neural, vascular, cutaneous, myogenic, and lymphatic structures. Axillary masses are typically identified when patients present with palpable areas of concern or during imaging for breast cancer screening or staging. Breast imagers frequently encounter axillary masses while evaluating the axillary region at mammography and US. While reactive lymphadenopathy represents the most common cause of axillary lymph node enlargement, lymph node metastasis from breast cancer is a common cause of axillary masses requiring clinical evaluation. Recent immunization, particularly COVID-19 vaccination, is an important cause of unilateral axillary lymphadenopathy. Additional causes beyond metastatic lymphadenopathy must be considered in the differential diagnosis, including benign and malignant entities arising from accessory breast tissue, adipocytic, neurogenic, vascular, infectious, traumatic, and cutaneous origins. Understanding axillary anatomy is essential for developing a comprehensive differential diagnosis and determining appropriate management strategies. Systematic assessment of characteristic imaging and clinical findings, combined with thorough correlation with patient history and symptoms, enables accurate diagnosis. US serves as the primary imaging modality for mass assessment and biopsy guidance. Depending on the differential diagnosis, mammography, CT, and MRI provide supplementary information to better define mass origin and extent. Definitive diagnosis often requires histopathologic analysis. A systematic approach ensures accurate diagnosis and optimal management of axillary masses. © The Author(s), 2026. title: Trust as a hidden driver of epidemic-relevant behavior: Institution- and behavior-specific associations across 20 national survey waves.
abstract: Compartmental models of infectious disease transmission make assumptions about human behaviors. Specifically, they parameterize interactions across population groups, assumed to have distinct epidemiologically relevant behavioral patterns, primarily through contact matrices stratified by demographic variables such as age, gender, or socioeconomic status. Although such demographic characteristics are readily measurable, they may inadequately capture the social and psychological forces that govern protective behaviors. Drawing on 20 waves of a national survey conducted throughout the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, we show that institutional trust-particularly trust in public health agencies, physicians, and hospitals-is a dominant predictor of protective behavior adoption. For mask wearing during periods of strongest pandemic activity, institutional trust explains more behavioral difference across population groups than age, income, education, and partisan affiliation combined. In unadjusted analyses, the difference in protective behavior adoption between individuals with the highest and lowest trust in the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) was four- to six-fold larger than the corresponding differences by age, income, or education, and exceeded the difference between Democratic and Republican respondents. This association was institutionally specific (the relationship attenuates for trust in banks), and behaviorally specific (trust in the CDC is associated with protective behaviors but not visiting a doctor). The latter suggests that trust modifies voluntary compliance with public health recommendations rather than healthcare access or use. These findings identify institutional trust as a candidate stratifying variable for models of behavior-coupled transmission dynamics, and as a measurable target for public health surveillance.

title: Generation-time distortion is an emergent property of epidemic control
abstract: We find that a vast space of public health interventions necessarily reshape the intervals between successive infections, known as generation times, for directly-transmitted infectious diseases (e.g., COVID-19, Ebola virus, influenza). While some studies have connected specific interventions (e.g., contact-tracing, isolation) to shifted generation times, most epidemiological analyses assume these intervals are stationary. We reveal that this assumption is substantially more fragile than previously recognised. We develop a universal microscopic representation for all intervention mechanisms that reduce individual-level infectiousness and establish generation-time reshaping as a fundamental macroscopic feature of those interventions, emerging at the population level. By constraining the topology of our representation to reflect specific mechanisms, we explain and unify previous studies as well as predict generation-time phenomena yet to be observed. We further show that neglecting generation-time reshaping can under- or over-estimate intervention effectiveness and disease control- lability by 100%, under realistic parameter settings. A stringent intervention can even produce no estimated transmissibility difference. Generation-time distortion causes unavoidable and underrated biases that can severely limit model-driven public health policy and pandemic preparedness.

title: Intelligent service systems and value co-creation in hotel frontlines
abstract: Drawing on service-dominant logic, this study examines how mechanical- and feeling-intelligent service systems contribute to value co-creation through distinct customer-engagement pathways and how these effects change over time and following the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak. Using a large-scale dataset of hotel information and online reviews, we conduct text mining to measure key variables and regression analyses to examine the proposed relationships and their changes over time and following the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak. The results show that mechanical-intelligent service systems contribute to co-created value through functional engagement, whereas feeling-intelligent service systems contribute through emotional and social engagement. Additionally, value co-creation driven by both types of intelligent service systems strengthens over time, with a notable surge observed following the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak. This study advances understanding of how intelligent service systems participate in frontline value co-creation in hospitality and provides practical guidance for service firms seeking to deploy such systems strategically in service frontlines.

title: Multi-Pathogen Wastewater-Based Epidemiology Before, During, and After the Milano-Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic and Paralympic Games: Monitoring of the Alpine Tourist Sewersheds of the Province of Trento
abstract: Given worldwide advances in wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE), its implementation is also emerging in international sporting events. The WBE application to a major international sporting event held under winter and cold-climate conditions remains unexplored. The Milano-Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic and Paralympic Games, hosted in the Alpine region, provided a unique opportunity to explore the potential of wastewater surveillance during the winter period, when seasonal diseases also drive pathogen circulation. This paper presents the results of the WBE surveillance conducted in the Province of Trento, over six months (November 2025-April 2026) and covering the periods before, during, and after the Winter Olympic and Paralympic Games. A total of 96 wastewater samples were collected from six wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) serving the Fiemme and Fassa valleys, with a total census population of about 29,000 but reaching 143,000 population equivalents during tourist periods. The WBE monitoring involved quantitative analyses of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, RSV A/B, and Norovirus GI/GII, as well as screening for measles. Norovirus GI/GII and RSV A/B circulated as the number of event-related visitors increased, whereas SARS-CoV-2 and influenza viruses remained at background or seasonal levels. Clinical surveillance data in the Province of Trento effectively complemented this multi-pathogen WBE. In conclusion, this experience provided non-invasive, community-wide information and demonstrated the operational feasibility and usefulness of WBE as a multi-pathogen sentinel tool for situational awareness to complement public health surveillance.

source_records.title: Multi-Pathogen Wastewater-Based Epidemiology Before, During, and After the Milano-Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic and Paralympic Games: Monitoring of the Alpine Tourist Sewersheds of the Province of Trento
source_records.abstract: Given worldwide advances in wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE), its implementation is also emerging in international sporting events. The WBE application to a major international sporting event held under winter and cold-climate conditions remains unexplored. The Milano-Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic and Paralympic Games, hosted in the Alpine region, provided a unique opportunity to explore the potential of wastewater surveillance during the winter period, when seasonal diseases also drive pathogen circulation. This paper presents the results of the WBE surveillance conducted in the Province of Trento, over six months (November 2025-April 2026) and covering the periods before, during, and after the Winter Olympic and Paralympic Games. A total of 96 wastewater samples were collected from six wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) serving the Fiemme and Fassa valleys, with a total census population of about 29,000 but reaching 143,000 population equivalents during tourist periods. The WBE monitoring involved quantitative analyses of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, RSV A/B, and Norovirus GI/GII, as well as screening for measles. Norovirus GI/GII and RSV A/B circulated as the number of event-related visitors increased, whereas SARS-CoV-2 and influenza viruses remained at background or seasonal levels. Clinical surveillance data in the Province of Trento effectively complemented this multi-pathogen WBE. In conclusion, this experience provided non-invasive, community-wide information and demonstrated the operational feasibility and usefulness of WBE as a multi-pathogen sentinel tool for situational awareness to complement public health surveillance.

title: Lipoplex Nanoparticle-Based RNA Delivery to 3D Melanoma Spheroids.
abstract: Lipoplex nanoparticle-based vaccination technologies have shown tremendous efficiency for in vivo transfection during the COVID-19 pandemic and also hold promise for treating melanoma. While pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics need careful in vivo and clinical testing, other parameters of drug performance can be assessed with in vitro systems as well. Spheroids composed of more than one cell type can serve to assess drug penetration, cell-type specificity, and transfection efficiency at an early stage of drug development.

title: Beyond the Adolescent Window: HPV Vaccination in Adult Women
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination has traditionally targeted girls and adolescents before sexual debut, when its preventive potential is greatest. However, many women reach adulthood unvaccinated or incompletely vaccinated, a gap widened by the COVID-19 pandemic. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence on HPV vaccination in adult women and its implications for gynecological practice. Sexual debut, previous infection, or a positive HPV test does not preclude benefit, because few women have been exposed to all vaccine types; nevertheless, the vaccine is prophylactic and does not treat established infection or lesions. In women aged 27 to 45 years, trials show favorable immunogenicity, efficacy, and safety, and vaccination is recommended through shared clinical decision-making that considers prior exposure and the risk of new exposures. Evidence above 45 years of age remains scarce. After excisional treatment of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse, meta-analyses predominantly based on observational studies suggest lower recurrence rates following adjuvant vaccination, although this benefit has not been consistently confirmed by randomized controlled trials. We also discuss additional vaccination with the nonavalent vaccine after bivalent or quadrivalent series, single-dose schedules, people living with HIV, and cervical screening in vaccinated women, in whom HPV-based testing maintains better performance than cytology. Missed opportunities remain common, and the absence of a recommendation from a health care professional is among the main reasons adults remain unvaccinated. Reviewing vaccination history at every gynecological visit, combined with individualized counseling, may help close the gap between vaccinated young cohorts and unvaccinated adult women and support cervical cancer elimination goals.
