title: P-44: Fifteen years of sustained improvement in access and outcomes: a dedicated multidisciplinary clinic for high-risk youth with type 1 diabetes (2010–2025)
abstract: Adolescents and emerging adults with poorly controlled diabetes and adverse social determinants of health are at high risk for disengagement, elevated HbA1c, and recurrent emergency department (ED) visits and diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). In 2010, we established a Diabetes Multidisciplinary Comprehensive Care Clinic (DM CCC) to provide continuous, individualized care for high-risk patients. To evaluate long-term changes in access to care, glycemic control, and acute care utilization from program inception (2010) through 2025. The DM CCC is a team-based model embedded within pediatric endocrinology emphasizing flexible scheduling, individualized goal-setting, psychosocial support, and sustained engagement without premature discharge. Telehealth was integrated in 2020. Outcomes included clinic show rates, mean HbA1c, proportion with HbA1c ≥10%, ED visits, and DKA admissions, obtained via longitudinal EHR review. Show rates improved from 88% through 2025. Mean HbA1c decreased from 11.2% (2010) to 9.6% (2019), 9.0% (2022), and 8.5% (2025). The proportion of patients with HbA1c ≥10% declined by >45%. ED utilization decreased by approximately 35%, and DKA admissions declined by nearly 40% compared with baseline. During the COVID-19 pandemic, while division-wide DKA rates rose among newly diagnosed patients, rates within the established DM CCC cohort remained stable and subsequently declined further post-pandemic. No patients were discharged for non-adherence; all exits occurred through structured transition to adult care (mean age 19.6 years). Over 15 years, a relationship-centered multidisciplinary clinic for high-risk youth with diabetes produced sustained improvements in access, glycemic control, and acute care utilization, including during the COVID-19 era. This scalable model advances equity while delivering durable clinical impact.

title: P-409: Epidemiological profile and diagnostic presentation of type 1 diabetes mellitus in a tertiary center in Brazil
abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus(T1DM) is an endocrine disorder that impairs glucose metabolism. Diagnosis typically occurs during childhood, and may be established through laboratory abnormalities in asymptomatic patients, classic symptoms (polyuria, polydipsia, and weight loss) or diabetic ketoacidosis(DKA). To evaluate age at diagnosis and clinical presentation of T1DM, as well as the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in a pediatric population. This observational, retrospective, and descriptive study was conducted at a tertiary hospital in northeastern Brazil, with data collection from March 2025 to April 2026. Patients diagnosed with T1DM and followed between 2004 and 2026 were included. Data were obtained through medical record review. Variables analyzed included age at diagnosis, sex, and presence of DKA. Statistical analysis was performed using Epi InfoTM, with calculation of frequencies, means, and standard deviations(SD). Group comparisons were performed using the Mann–Whitney test, considering p 0.05). Patients presenting with DKA had a mean age of 7.32 years (SD±3.32), while those with classic symptoms had a mean age of 6.6 years (SD±3.6), with no significant difference (p>0.05). Among patients diagnosed up to 2019 (n=127), the mean age was 5.41 years (SD±3.19), whereas from 2020 onward (n=135) it was 7.32 years (SD±3.49), also without significant difference (p>0.05). However, after 2020, 63% of patients presented with DKA. Age at T1DM diagnosis did not differ by sex and was not significantly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. A high proportion of patients were diagnosed with DKA, a severe condition associated with increased morbidity and mortality, reinforcing the need for earlier recognition and diagnosis.

title: Electronic medical records for health system strengthening in Nepal: a community case study of phased implementation across public hospitals
abstract: Robust health information systems are foundational to universal health coverage, quality of care and health-system resilience, yet many public hospitals in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) still rely on paper-based records that fragment patient histories, duplicate diagnostics and limit routine data for management and policy. This community case study describes the phased implementation and observed system-level changes of open-source electronic medical records (EMRs) across public hospitals in Nepal and reflects on transferable lessons for comparable settings. From the early 2010s, Nepal adopted open-source EMR platforms principally Bahmni, built on OpenMRS as a license-free, locally adaptable alternative to proprietary systems. Adoption accelerated after the COVID-19 pandemic and was reinforced by Nepal's 2022 Joint External Evaluation and COVID-19 Intra-Action Review, both of which called for a transition from fragmented paper-based reporting towards integrated digital systems. With technical assistance from the World Health Organization (WHO) and financing from the Pandemic Fund, EMRs were deployed through a standardized six-phase model emphasizing readiness assessment, clinician engagement, local customization and sustained capacity-building; from 2024, legacy installations were upgraded to the FHIR-aligned OpenMRS 3 interface. By May 2026, 19 government hospitals across six of Nepal's seven provinces had transitioned to functional open-source EMRs, with longitudinal records accessible across departments, integrated laboratory and radiology results, standardized electronic reporting and expanded routine data for oversight. Optimizing the whole technical environment, particularly storage and network quality rather than processing power alone proved critical. Improvements in clinical continuity and efficiency were reported by users rather than formally measured. Nepal's experience suggests EMRs are best understood as organizational transformation rather than a purely technological upgrade.

title: Modeling and simulation methods used in the maritime industry: evolution, applications and future perspectives
abstract: Modeling and simulation (M&S) techniques have evolved from optional engineering tools to indispensable pillars of modern maritime practice. This article presents a comprehensive systematic review of the most important modeling and simulation methodologies applied to maritime industry processes, including workflows for ship design, shipyard fabrication and construction, port and terminal operations, vessel traffic management, maintenance scheduling, supply chain logistics, and risk management procedures. The study demonstrates that M&S techniques enable safer, more efficient, and more environmentally sustainable operations, validated by scientific standards. The COVID-19 pandemic served as a critical catalyst, consolidating the strategic value of M&S as a central component of maritime resilience and innovation. This research traces the evolution of M&S adoption from 2010 to 2025, identifying four dominant research directions: maritime simulators, computational fluid dynamics (CFD)/finite element analysis (FEA), digital twins, and artificial intelligence-based methods. The analysis reveals that while traditional approaches dominated the 2010-2020 period, emerging technologies—particularly digital twins and AI-based methods—have accelerated exponentially since 2020, reflecting the maritime industry's accelerated digitalization. Forward projections through 2035 indicate that AI-based methodologies will experience the highest growth rate at approximately 329%, followed by digital twins at 147%, underscoring the fundamental transformation of maritime research and practice. The integration of these advanced modeling approaches offers optimal equilibrium between physical precision and computational efficiency for addressing complex maritime challenges.

title: Pubertal timing is a critical dimension of adolescent brain vulnerability
abstract: Adolescence is a period of rapid brain development, during which biological maturational timing varies substantially between individuals. This variability may drive specific developmental vulnerabilities to adverse experiences with long-term consequences, warranting early identification of at-risk individuals. We utilized ultrasonic bone age measurements to track pubertal maturity, classifying participants by adolescent biological maturity relative to chronological age (accelerated, average, decelerated). Brain hierarchy was quantified as the irreversibility of brain signals in resting state electroencephalography, providing a brain-based method to detect vulnerability patterns. The COVID-19 pandemic presented a unique opportunity to also assess alterations in brain hierarchy following external disruption. We mapped maturity-defined trajectories and rates of hierarchical organization, and their post-pandemic deviation from expected development, capturing two distinct vulnerability forms. First, early maturing adolescents showed persistent reduction in brain hierarchy. Second, those undergoing their fastest phase of development – specifically, decelerated adolescents – showed the strongest disruption in brain hierarchy following the pandemic. These findings suggest that pubertal timing is a critical dimension of individual variation in adolescent brain development and vulnerability. They also emphasize the need for objective maturity measurements to tailor support to individual pubertal timelines, particularly given the secular trend toward earlier puberty and ongoing global ecological crises.

title: Epidemiology of acute respiratory infections in adult patients in Hospices Civils de Lyon, France, between October 2016 and April 2025
abstract: Background Multiple viruses can cause acute respiratory infections (ARI), impacting morbidity, mortality and hospital resources. The objective of this study was to describe viral circulation among patients with ARI, patients characteristics and severity outcomes. Methods A retrospective cohort was assembled using electronic health records from the Hospices Civils de Lyon, France. Adult patients ([≥]18 years) hospitalised or presenting to the emergency department from October 2016 to April 2025 with either an ICD-10 diagnostic code for ARI or a laboratory-confirmed viral detection were included. Administrative variables and laboratory results collected during the stay were extracted. Results 103,011 hospital visits involving 82,077 patients were included. The number of eligible stays increased substantially since the COVID-19 pandemic, along with year-round laboratory testing. Following disruption during the pandemic, winter peaks of ARI incidence, influenza and RSV detections re-emerged after 2022. Influenza, rhinovirus and SARS-CoV-2 positivity rates peaked in younger adults (<65 years), whereas RSV and hMPV positivity rates were highest in patients aged [≥]80 years. Patients aged [≥]65 years had longer hospitalisations (median 10 vs 8 days, p<0.001), twice in-hospital mortality rate (14% vs 7%, p<0.001), less frequent ICU admission (21% vs 33%, p<0.001) and use of respiratory support than younger adults. Influenza was the virus associated with the shortest length of stays, hMPV was associated with the longest in younger adults. Conclusions Real-world hospital data are valuable for surveillance of viral circulation, early identification of patients at risk of deterioration, and may be used to evaluate the impact of preventive intervention in community.
authors: Marta Cristina dos Santos Bispo Nunes

source_records.abstract: Background Multiple viruses can cause acute respiratory infections (ARI), impacting morbidity, mortality and hospital resources. title: Drug resistance and molecular epidemiology of pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae isolates in Southern China
abstract: ABSTRACT To investigate antimicrobial susceptibility and molecular typing of recent pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae strains, analyze the correlations between drug resistance, pneumonia severity, and strain types, and provide evidence for precise M. pneumoniae infection management. pneumoniae isolation and culture were applied to bronchoalveolar lavage fluid from 325 M. pneumoniae-infected children, with 23S rRNA resistance mutation detection. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing (eight antibiotics, microbroth dilution) was performed on 154 culture-positive strains, alongside multiple locus variable-number tandem repeat analysis (MLVA), whole-genome sequencing, and single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) genotyping. pneumoniae showed high macrolide resistance (99.35% for erythromycin and azithromycin), but high susceptibility to moxifloxacin/levofloxacin, with minocycline/doxycycline sensitivity at 98.71%. The 23S rRNA mutations occurred in 97.4% (150/154). MLVA type 4-5-7-2 dominated (135/154), with minor types totaling 15 cases. SNP typing clustered strains into four groups, mostly EC1 (138/154), with four genes showing cross-cluster mutations. pneumoniae strains exhibit high macrolide resistance but good minocycline/doxycycline susceptibility, with EC1-cluster dominance driving rapid spread. This supports individualized therapy and epidemic trend tracking for pediatric M. pneumoniae lung infections. IMPORTANCE This study sheds light on why many children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia do not respond well to common macrolide antibiotics—over 99% of strains in Southern China are resistant. It identifies effective alternative drugs and pinpoints the dominant spreading strain, helping doctors choose precise treatments. For public health, it provides key data to track outbreaks, guiding targeted surveillance and better management of pediatric respiratory infections post-COVID-19.

title: Antiviral activity of Rumex crispus extract and its bioactive constituent emodin against human coronavirus OC43
abstract: Coronaviruses are responsible for diseases ranging from mild respiratory symptoms to severe infections such as COVID-19. Despite the availability of vaccines and therapeutic agents, the emergence of new variants and drug-resistant strains highlights the need for additional antiviral strategies. In this study, Rumex crispus was investigated as a potential source of antiviral compounds. The ethanol (EtOH) extract of R. crispus roots was prepared and subsequently fractionated into n-hexane (n-hex), ethyl acetate (EA), and aqueous fractions. Among these, the n-hexane and EA fractions exhibited significant antiviral activity against human coronavirus OC43, as demonstrated by Western blot, qRT-PCR, and plaque assays. Chemical analysis of the extract by HPLC led to the identification of epicatechin, naphthalene derivatives, and anthraquinones. Notably, emodin, an anthraquinone, showed pronounced antiviral activity, and was found to be enriched in the active n-hexane and EA fractions. These findings suggest that emodin may contribute to the antiviral activity of R. crispus extract, although the potential involvement of other bioactive constituents cannot be excluded.

title: Automated Approaches to Extracting Arm-Level Numerical Results From Published Studies for Meta-Analysis
abstract: Systematic reviews depend on accurate extraction of outcome data from primary studies, yet this step remains largely manual and time-consuming. Automation tools exist for identifying and retrieving studies and for extracting non-numeric study characteristics, but few target the numerical arm-level results needed for meta-analysis. We developed and evaluated a hybrid approach for extracting arm-level results (number of events and number enrolled per arm) for binary outcomes from two-arm randomized controlled trials published as PDFs. Rule-based string processing in R locates and parses results tables and candidate sentences in the Results section; a large language model (ChatGPT, accessed through the OpenAI API) is then used only to structure the numerical information in the selected sentences. We evaluated the approach by replicating a Cochrane meta-analysis of favipiravir for COVID-19 (11 trials; all-cause mortality at 28 to 30 days). Table-based extraction was applied to five articles and in-line text extraction to six. The extracted data matched the published arm-level results for all studies except one, where the pipeline recovered a sample size (24) consistent with the trial's results table rather than its text (25). The replicated random-effects meta-analysis gave a summary risk ratio of 0.84 (95% CI 0.49–1.46), identical to the original review, with minor differences in study weights attributable to rounding. An independent test on infectious bovine keratoconjunctivitis vaccine trials showed partial transferability, with failures confined to scanned PDFs and complex table structures. The code and the list of extracted articles are publicly available on GitHub.

title: Observation of Nipah Virus Evolution Using the ATG Genomic Walks
abstract: In this paper, 32 complete genomic sequences of human-origin Nipah viruses registered in GenBank® from 1999 to 2025 are analyzed by tracking distributions of ATG triplets. The trajectories of these triplets are constructed, and their divergence parameter is calculated, revealing an increased value typical of highly mutated viruses that can form separate families with distinct properties. This conclusion aligns with the large deviation observed in the fractal dimension parameters of the distribution of inter-ATG-triplet distances in genomic sequences. The simulation results are compared with earlier data for SARS-CoV-2, MERS-CoV, dengue, and Ebola viruses.

title: ‘How Are We Going to Learn This Profession?’: A Multi-Stakeholder Qualitative Study of Educational Disruption Across Pandemic and Earthquake Crises
abstract: Background/Objectives: Crisis-related disruptions pose particular challenges for nursing and midwifery education because maintaining educational continuity also requires preserving experiential and clinical learning. The COVID-19 pandemic and the February 2023 earthquakes in Türkiye prompted changes in educational delivery. While the pandemic involved prolonged interruptions to face-to-face and clinical education, post-earthquake arrangements at the study institution primarily affected theoretical courses, with clinical and practical training continuing face-to-face. This study aimed to explore the experiences and perspectives of nursing and midwifery students, faculty members, and healthcare professionals regarding online and hybrid education implemented during the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2023 earthquakes in Türkiye, including its perceived implications for clinical learning and professional competence. Methods: This qualitative study employed a descriptive phenomenological design. Criterion purposive sampling was used to recruit 48 participants, including 20 senior nursing and midwifery students, 12 faculty members, and 16 nurses and midwives working with students in clinical settings. Data were collected through 11 face-to-face focus group interviews conducted between 15 and 26 May 2023. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using Colaizzi’s phenomenological analysis method. Two researchers independently analyzed the data, and credibility was further supported through external expert review and member checking. Results: Four interconnected themes emerged: (1) disrupted learning and unequal participation, (2) loss of experiential and clinical learning, (3) from educational disruption to professional competence concerns, and (4) reconsidering educational strategies during crises. Participants described technological and contextual barriers to educational participation across the two crises. Disruptions to laboratory and clinical learning, including reduced opportunities to develop and practice clinical skills, were primarily associated with the prolonged interruption of face-to-face education during the COVID-19 pandemic, whereas post-earthquake changes at the study institution mainly concerned theoretical course delivery. Students reported uncertainty about their clinical abilities and preparedness for professional practice, while faculty members and healthcare professionals described similar concerns from educational and clinical perspectives. Despite these challenges, participants recognized the value of online education for selected theoretical content and reported gains in digital skills. They emphasized preserving practice-based learning, strengthening technological and financial support, and involving relevant stakeholders in crisis-related educational decisions. Conclusions: Participants associated pandemic-related interruptions to experiential and clinical learning with concerns about professional preparedness, whereas their reflections on post-earthquake educational arrangements highlighted the importance of adapting theoretical course delivery to the circumstances of the crisis while maintaining face-to-face clinical training. The convergence of perspectives across students, faculty members, and healthcare professionals highlights the importance of protecting supervised experiential learning while maintaining educational continuity. Crisis preparedness in nursing and midwifery education should therefore incorporate adaptable educational models, contingency plans for clinical learning, appropriate assessment strategies, technological support, and collaboration among educational and clinical stakeholders.

title: A Structured Decision-Support Framework for Technology Adoption to Advance Airport Sustainability and Resilience
abstract: Airports face challenges in integrating sustainability and resilience into their long-term operational plans due to climate change, regulatory mandates, financial constraints, and disruptions such as the COVID-19 pandemic. While technology adoption plays a key role in addressing these issues, many airports lack structured strategies for evaluating, selecting, and implementing sustainability and resilience-focused innovations. Technology is often adopted reactively, driven by crises or regulatory compliance, rather than through proactive, strategic planning. This study introduces an empirically supported decision-support framework that combines established technology adoption models, sustainability and resilience assessment logic, and airport-specific implementation needs into a structured process for sustainable and resilient technology adoption. The framework synthesizes engineering-based maturity assessment, strategic planning, cross-disciplinary implementation, and Envision-based sustainability and resilience criteria, providing a tool that merges engineering judgment with organizational, regulatory, and environmental considerations. It equips airport decision-makers with a practical methodology for aligning technological innovation with operational performance, sustainability objectives, and long-term adaptability. The framework was empirically supported through expert input and statistical analyses of survey responses representing 27 commercial airports across the United States. An illustrative case study demonstrates an application of the framework by translating strategic sustainability and resilience goals into actionable implementation steps. This study contributes to the body of knowledge by presenting an evidence-based decision-support methodology that bridges the gap among strategic commitments and implementation, supports decarbonization, operational resilience, and infrastructure sustainability, while providing practical guidance for planners, sustainability leaders, and policymakers.

title: Epidemiology and burden of respiratory virus-associated acute respiratory infections: a multi-source integrated population-based surveillance study in Chongqing
abstract: Abstract Background Acute respiratory infections (ARIs), particularly severe acute respiratory infections (SARIs), impose a huge disease burden globally. Respiratory viruses are key etiological agents of ARIs. Population-based data on respiratory virus disease burden in China are limited, with most studies focusing on single pathogens and lacking population-level incidence and hospitalization estimates. Methods We integrated data from national hospital-based surveillance, local health system electronic medical records (EMRs), and census records in Chongqing from October 2023 to April 2025. We also conducted a community-based healthcare utilization survey and a pilot survey. We analyzed the seasonality of six respiratory viruses and used Joinpoint software to characterize age-specific epidemiological trends. Furthermore, we identified risk factors for severe acute respiratory infection (SARI). A modified multiplier model was employed to estimate population-based incidence and hospitalization rates of ARI associated with these viruses. Results We included 16,363 respiratory infection patients (12,669 outpatients, 3,694 inpatients). Most viruses resumed pre-COVID-19 seasonal patterns. The detection rate of influenza virus (IFV) peaked in adolescents and adults; respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human parainfluenza virus (HPIV) mainly affected infants and the elderly; human adenovirus (HAdv), human rhinovirus (HRV), and human metapneumovirus (HMPV) were most prevalent in preschoolers. RSV infection was significantly associated with a higher risk of SARI compared with other respiratory viruses (RSV vs. IFV: adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 95% confidence interval [CI]: 7.88, 5.4–11.51; RSV vs. HRV: 1.52, 1.13–2.04; RSV vs. HAdv: 3.21, 2.14–4.81; RSV vs. HMPV: 1.76, 1.24–2.50; RSV vs. HPIV: 1.63, 1.14–2.33). Incidence and hospitalization rates (per 100,000 person-years) of HRV (30,183; 2,153), HMPV (22,774; 514), RSV (22,181; 2,065), IFV (13,086; 807), HPIV (7,824; 556), and HAdv (6,991; 1,487) were highest in children under 5 years of age. Hospitalization rates rose again in those aged ≥ 60 years: HRV (170), RSV (80), IFV (70), HMPV (54), HAdv (27), HPIV (23). Conclusions Distinct age distributions and the high SARI risk of specific viruses such as RSV support targeted prevention. Integrating multi-source surveillance with sentinel surveys and standardizing the ARI case definition can yield population-level, real-world estimates of incidence and hospitalization rates for these viruses.

title: An Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Umbrella Review of Eating Disorder Meta-Analyses (2020–2025): Mapping Treatment Efficacy, Comorbidity, and Persistent Gaps in Sample Diversity
abstract: Background/Objectives: Eating disorders (EDs) are serious psychiatric illnesses that result in physical and mental-health impairments. A unifying summary of the broad collection of ED research findings is lacking. This umbrella review leveraged artificial intelligence (AI) to summarize ED-focused meta-analyses, to identify directions for future research and treatment. Methods: PubMed, PsycINFO, Web of Science, Embase, and ProQuest were searched for meta-analyses of human ED research published between 1 June 2020 and 31 May 2025 (inclusive). A large language model (LLM) conducted risk of bias assessment and data extraction for studies meeting all inclusion criteria. Neural topic modeling (BERTopic) identified the themes present across included meta-analyses, and an LLM summarized findings of articles in each category. Results: 220 meta-analyses were included. AI tools demonstrated good accuracy in quality appraisal, data extraction, and data synthesis (97%, 93%, and 96%, respectively). Most meta-analyses had at least one critical flaw (per AMSTAR 2 quality appraisal). Neural topic modeling identified 16 themes within the set of included articles: Neurocognition, Treatment Effectiveness, Intervention Efficacy, Biomarkers, Premorbid Conditions, Clinical Features, Epidemiology, Psychiatric Comorbidity, Behavioral Addictions, Long-Term Outcomes, Prevention, Psychological Factors, Treatment Gaps, COVID-19, Pharmacotherapy, and Avoidant Restrictive Food Intake Disorder. Article summaries collectively identified ED prevalence of 1.69% and associations of EDs with mortality and disability. Studies covered a range of illness mechanisms and treatments, though disproportionately included Western females. Conclusions: This review highlights the broad scope but limited generalizability of ED research, as well as the potential of AI to accelerate systematic review workflows.

Methods: PubMed, PsycINFO, Web of Science, Embase, and ProQuest were searched for meta-analyses of human ED research published between 1 June 2020 and 31 May 2025 (inclusive). A large language model (LLM) conducted risk of bias assessment and data extraction for studies meeting all inclusion criteria. Neural topic modeling (BERTopic) identified the themes present across included meta-analyses, and an LLM summarized findings of articles in each category. Results: 220 meta-analyses were included. AI tools demonstrated good accuracy in quality appraisal, data extraction, and data synthesis (97%, 93%, and 96%, respectively). Most meta-analyses had at least one critical flaw (per AMSTAR 2 quality appraisal). Neural topic modeling identified 16 themes within the set of included articles: Neurocognition, Treatment Effectiveness, Intervention Efficacy, Biomarkers, Premorbid Conditions, Clinical Features, Epidemiology, Psychiatric Comorbidity, Behavioral Addictions, Long-Term Outcomes, Prevention, Psychological Factors, Treatment Gaps, COVID-19, Pharmacotherapy, and Avoidant Restrictive Food Intake Disorder. Article summaries collectively identified ED prevalence of 1.69% and associations of EDs with mortality and disability. Studies covered a range of illness mechanisms and treatments, though disproportionately included Western females. Conclusions: This review highlights the broad scope but limited generalizability of ED research, as well as the potential of AI to accelerate systematic review workflows.

title: Finding the Missing Link: Public Health Advisories and Computable Decision Support for Frontline Health Care Personnel
abstract: Abstract Objective Timely recognition and response to emerging infectious diseases are critical, yet frontline health care personnel often struggle with access to crucial information. This study assessed Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Health Alert Network (HAN) advisories as potential computable data sources for clinical decision support (CDS) systems aimed at frontline health care personnel responding to emerging infectious diseases. Methods We analyzed 89 HAN advisories using a CDS prototype designed for emergency room triage nurses managing high-impact pathogens. Two reviewers systematically annotated advisories for key elements, with a third reviewer resolving discrepancies. Results Of 89 CDC HAN advisories, 70 addressed infectious pathogens, including 50 on 13 high-consequence organisms. Among these advisories, 47% included a start date, none had an end date, 53% mentioned symptoms, and 11% described isolation precautions, which varied significantly from 0% to 27%. Early COVID-19 advisories illustrated evolving guidance. Conclusions CDC HAN advisories are often incomplete, specifically lacking dynamic time-specific details and isolation precautions. Enhancing advisories with structured, computable data and a flexible CDS system will improve the timely dissemination of actionable information to frontline health care personnel. This will enable swift, informed decision-making and more optimized patient care.

title: Deciphering Viral Antigenic Relationships Through Antigenic Cartography: A Narrative Review
abstract: Background: Antigenic cartography is a computational approach that quantitatively visualizes antigenic relationships among viral strains using serological data, including hemagglutination inhibition and virus-neutralization assays. Since its introduction in the early 2000s, it has substantially advanced the study of viral antigenic evolution by transforming complex serological measurements into interpretable antigenic maps, thereby facilitating assessment of antigenic diversity, immune escape, cross-reactivity, and vaccine–virus relationships. Objective: This review examines the historical development, methodological principles, applications, limitations, and emerging directions of antigenic cartography across clinically relevant viruses, with particular emphasis on its relevance to viral surveillance, antigenic drift monitoring and vaccine-strain selection. Methods: The literature was synthesized comparatively across major applications of antigenic cartography, encompassing human seasonal influenza and other viruses, including dengue, lyssaviruses, foot-and-mouth disease virus, Enterovirus A71, norovirus, rotavirus, SARS-CoV-2, and HIV. Particular attention was given to real-world applications, methodological advances, sources of uncertainty, and integration with genomic, structural, evolutionary, and computational approaches. Findings: Influenza remains the most extensively studied viral pathogen, where antigenic cartography has supported recognition of epidemiologically relevant antigenic transitions and informed vaccine decisions. Examples include the emergence of A/Fujian/411/2002-like H3N2 viruses during 2004–2005 and assessment of A/California/07/2009 during 2010–2011. Applications to other viruses demonstrate broader utility for characterizing antigenic landscapes and evaluating cross-protective immunity and vaccine performance. However, map reliability is influenced by serological assay variability, serum-panel composition, measurement noise, incomplete and geographically biased datasets. Limited inter-operability among serological, genomic, and structural datasets further restricts reproducibility and cross-study comparability. Future Directions and Conclusions: The field is transitioning from retrospective visualization toward predictive and mechanistically informed antigenic surveillance. Integration of artificial intelligence, protein language models, evolutionary modelling, structural vaccinology, and real-time genomic–serological surveillance could enable earlier prediction of antigenic drift, identification of emerging vaccine mismatches, and prioritization of candidate vaccine strains. Future platforms should incorporate standardized and automated serological measurements, inter-laboratory calibration, harmonized data standards, geographically representative datasets, experimental validation, and interpretable continuously updated models. Such integration could establish antigenic cartography as a scalable predictive framework for vaccine design and for strengthening preparedness against emerging viral threats.

title: Virome analysis of bats in Hong Kong unveils diverse mammalian viruses
abstract: The emergence of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) and the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic highlights the importance of understanding viral diversity in wildlife, including bats, which are recognized reservoirs of many zoonotic viruses. Following the identification of bats as the origin of the SARS epidemic, surveillance in Hong Kong revealed diverse bat coronaviruses, yet comprehensive virome data remain limited. Here, we used next-generation sequencing (NGS) to analyse the viromes of nine bat species in Hong Kong. We identified coronaviruses from six subgenera (Decacovirus, Minunacovirus, Myotacovirus, Merbecovirus, Sarbecovirus, and Rhinacovirus) across seven bat species. Viruses from nine additional families were also detected, indicating broad viral diversity. Notably, bat coronavirus HKU4 was identified for the first time in Chinese horseshoe bats, expanding the known host range of this virus and warranting further investigation into its potential zoonotic significance. Coronaviridae, Picornaviridae, and Parvoviridae were the most abundant families, accounting for 65.0%, 17.0%, and 12.3% of mammalian viral reads, respectively. These viral families were also detected across seven bat species. Lesser bent-winged bats, Horsfield’s bats, and Rickett’s big-footed bats showed the greatest viral diversity, harbouring sequence reads from eight viral families. Using a reference database generated through an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted approach, we identified nearly one million additional sequence reads representing putative viral species from four mammalian virus supergroups, as well as over 5,000 reads belonging to two unclassified viral supergroups, which remain unclassified by International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses (ICTV). These findings provide comprehensive insights into the bat viromes of Hong Kong and demonstrate the value of integrating NGS with AI-assisted approach to enhance viral discovery and support future wildlife surveillance efforts.

title: Longitudinal trends in vaccination uptake and respiratory infection burden in systemic lupus erythematosus: a population-based cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES To evaluate longitudinal patterns of vaccination uptake and respiratory infection outcomes among patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) compared with controls and identify factors associated with vaccination uptake. METHODS Population-based cohort study using a healthcare organization database. Adult patients with SLE (diagnosed 2010-2023) were identified through a validated registry and matched 1:100 to controls by birth year, sex, and socioeconomic status. Vaccination uptake for influenza, pneumococcal, and COVID-19 vaccines, respiratory infections, hospitalizations, intensive care unit (ICU) admissions, and mortality were evaluated. Temporal trends and factors associated with vaccination uptake were assessed using multivariable models. RESULTS The study included 3,692 patients with SLE and 382,753 matched controls (median follow-ups 12.8 and 13.4 years, respectively). Vaccination uptake was higher among patients with SLE than controls (influenza: 77.6% vs. 56.4%; pneumococcal: 55.6% vs. 32.1%; COVID-19: 74.2% vs. 72.0%; all p < 0.01). Patients with SLE experienced higher rates of respiratory hospitalization (34.8% vs. 11.5%), pneumonia hospitalization (23.9% vs. 5.9%), ICU admission (12.8% vs. 2.7%), and all-cause mortality (21.0% vs. 8.5%) (all p < 0.001). Longitudinally, vaccination uptake and respiratory hospitalizations remained consistently higher among patients with SLE. Pneumonia hospitalization rates increased over time in controls but remained stable in SLE (interaction p = 0.020). Older age, more comorbidities, higher socioeconomic status, and exposure to glucocorticoids were independently associated with influenza and pneumococcal vaccination uptake rates in SLE. CONCLUSION Patients with SLE demonstrated substantially higher vaccine exposure than controls but experienced elevated respiratory infection rates and severe outcomes. These findings support efforts to optimize infection prevention strategies in SLE.

title: Wastewater pathogen composition in Atlanta, GA prior to and during the 2026 FIFA World Cup
abstract: Mass gatherings can have many impacts on public health, including facilitating the spread of infectious diseases. Alternative surveillance modalities, such as wastewater-based surveillance (WBS), can complement traditional clinical surveillance. We utilized WBS to examine the influence of the 2026 FIFA World Cup (FWC'26) on the range of infectious pathogens in Atlanta, GA surrounding matches held in the city. Samples (n = 102) were collected from three water reclamation facilities between April and July of 2026 (34 collection days) and tested using the BIOFIRE® WATCHFIRETM Respiratory (19 targets) and Gastrointestinal (22 targets) PCR Pathogen Panels. Primary data analysis included a temporal comparison of wastewater pathogen profiles before (April 1 to June 10; n = 60) and during (June 15 to July 15; n = 30) the FWC'26 across the three facilities using a modified Poisson model with Bonferroni correction. There were no statistically significant differences in target detection between the two periods. Samples collected after the FWC'26 (July 20 to 29; n = 12) were included in a sensitivity analysis which showed a statistically significant increase in SARS-CoV-2 (RR = 3.21, 95% CI = 1.40-7.39; p = 0.01, p-adjusted = 0.048) during and after the tournament compared to before. However, this coincided with regional and national increases in SARS-CoV-2 detection in wastewater, suggesting ongoing community burden. Wide confidence intervals, lack of quantitative data, and limited data collection after the matches limit our conclusions. This study demonstrates the use of qualitative, multiplexed PCR assays for WBS during a mass gathering sporting event.

title: P-463: Seasonal patterns and infectious triggers of pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis: a three-year study in a tertiary referral center
abstract: Abstract Introduction Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a severe acute complication of type 1 diabetes (T1D), frequently triggered by infections. Data on seasonal patterns and their relationship with new-onset versus previously diagnosed T1D in pediatric populations remain limited. Objectives To evaluate the impact of seasonality and infections on pediatric DKA, comparing new-onset T1D and previously diagnosed cases and to identify the most prevalent viral agents. Methods Retrospective observational study including pediatric patients admitted with DKA to a tertiary hospital in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, from June 2021 to June 2024. Patients with ICD-10 code E10.1 and DKA confirmed according to ISPAD 2022 criteria were included. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed. Qualitative variables were expressed as absolute and relative frequencies, and associations were assessed using Fisher’s exact test (p<0.05). Results A total of 208 hospitalizations were analyzed. Infection was the main precipitating factor (30.8%), predominantly upper respiratory tract infections (62.5%), followed by gastroenteritis (9.4%), and pneumonia and dengue (3.1% each). Most admissions (56.3%) occurred during autumn and winter, with peaks in March, April, and June. New-onset diabetes cases showed higher incidence in March, April, and August, suggesting a stronger association with seasonal infectious triggers. Previously diagnosed patients had a more evenly distributed pattern, with peaks in April, June, and November, likely reflecting behavioral factors such as treatment adherence. Although not statistically significant, infection was more frequent in new-onset cases (36.6% vs. Viral infections, particularly influenza and SARS-CoV-2, were frequently identified. Conclusions DKA shows a clear seasonal pattern, especially in new-onset T1D, likely driven by infections. In previously diagnosed patients, DKA appears more influenced by adherence and psychosocial factors, supporting targeted prevention strategies.

Most admissions (56.3%) occurred during autumn and winter, with peaks in March, April, and June. New-onset diabetes cases showed higher incidence in March, April, and August, suggesting a stronger association with seasonal infectious triggers. Previously diagnosed patients had a more evenly distributed pattern, with peaks in April, June, and November, likely reflecting behavioral factors such as treatment adherence. Although not statistically significant, infection was more frequent in new-onset cases (36.6% vs. Viral infections, particularly influenza and SARS-CoV-2, were frequently identified. DKA shows a clear seasonal pattern, especially in new-onset T1D, likely driven by infections. In previously diagnosed patients, DKA appears more influenced by adherence and psychosocial factors, supporting targeted prevention strategies.

title: ARE-Wochenbericht des RKI KW44
abstract: Die ARE-Aktivität liegt auf Bevölkerungsebene und im stationären Bereich auf einem niedrigen Niveau, im ambulanten Bereich weiterhin auf einem moderaten Niveau. Das ARE-Geschehen wird weiterhin hauptsächlich durch Rhino-/Enteroviren bestimmt. Die Aktivität von SARS-CoV-2 und Influenzaviren ist derzeit in allen Systemen noch niedrig, jedoch setzt sich der Anstieg der SARS-CoV-2- und Influenzavirus-Zirkulation in verschiedenen Systemen seit Saisonbeginn allmählich fort. Hinweise aus dem Abwassermonitoring zeigen, dass SARS-CoV-2 bereits flächendeckend bundesweit zirkuliert. Durch die Herbstferien können die Werte der Sentinelsurveillance stärker schwanken und sich durch Nachmeldungen nachträglich noch verändern. Die Aktivität akuter respiratorischer Erkrankungen (ARE) in der Bevölkerung ist in der 44. KW im Vergleich zur Vorwoche gesunken und befindet sich auf einem niedrigen Niveau. Im ambulanten Bereich ist die Zahl der Arztbesuche wegen ARE in der 44. KW im Vergleich zur Vorwoche leicht gestiegen und lag weiterhin auf einem moderaten Niveau. Im Nationalen Referenzzentrum (NRZ) für Influenzaviren wurden in der 44. KW 2026 in insgesamt 58 der 90 eingesandten Sentinelproben respiratorische Viren identifiziert, darunter hauptsächlich Rhino-/Enteroviren (43 %), gefolgt von Adenoviren und humanen saisonalen Coronaviren (hCoV) mit jeweils 9 %. Neben weiteren Viren des Erregerpanels wurden auch Influenza A-Viren (6 %) und SARS-CoV-2 (4 %) nachgewiesen. Respiratorische Synzytialviren (RSV) wurden in der 44. KW nicht nachgewiesen. Im stationären Bereich ist die Inzidenz schwerer akuter respiratorischer Infektionen (SARI) unter Berücksichtigung von erwarteten weiteren SARI-Diagnosen (Nowcasting) in der 44. KW 2026 stabil geblieben und lag auf einem niedrigen Niveau. Es erhielten 4 % der SARI-Patientinnen und -Patienten eine COVID-19- bzw. 3 % eine Influenza-Diagnose. In der virologischen SARI-Surveillance des NRZ für Influenzaviren wurden in der 44. KW 2026 hauptsächlich Rhino-/Enteroviren nachgewiesen. Die Zahl der an das RKI gemäß IfSG übermittelten Fälle mit Influenzavirusinfektion ist in der 44. Meldewoche (MW) 2026 im Vergleich zur 43. MW wieder leicht gestiegen und liegt auf einem ähnlichen Niveau wie letztes Jahr um diese Zeit. Die COVID-19-Fallzahlen sind im Vergleich zur Vorwoche ebenfalls angestiegen, es wurden bisher deutlich weniger Fälle im Vergleich zur Vorsaison übermittelt. Die Zahl der RSV-Infektionen blieb in der 44. MW weiterhin niedrig. Die rekombinante SARS-CoV-2-Variante XFG wurde in der 42. KW 2026 erneut am häufigsten unter den zirkulierenden SARS-CoV-2-Linien detektiert. Die im Abwasser gemessene SARS-CoV-2-Last ist weiterhin deutlich niedriger als im Vorjahr zu dieser Zeit, zeigt jedoch seit einigen Wochen einen ansteigenden Trend. Auch bei der Influenzavirus-last zeigt sich ein leichter Anstieg in den letzten Wochen. Die RSV-Last im Abwasser ist weiter niedrig.

title: Mapeo científico del gasto de bolsillo en salud: análisissobre la evolución e identificación de tendencias
abstract: Introduction: Health care services around the world in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic have prompted public policy makers to develop mechanisms to ensure that health spending is predominantly public, as out-of-pocket spending becomes impoverishing and catastrophic for families. Due to growing academic and professional interest in these issues, this research aims to conduct a literature review based on scientific mapping of out-of-pocket health spending. Objective: To analyze scientific developments in out-of-pocket health spending to determine trends in this area. Methodology: A search was conducted of scientific output recorded in WoS and Scopus over the last two decades. Subsequently, using bibliometric tools and network analysis, the current structure of knowledge on the subject was presented. Results: Four emerging research trends were identified: determinants of increased health spending, financial protection in health, impoverishing health spending, and catastrophic health spending. Conclusion: Out-of-pocket health expenditure has generated growing interest in the professional and scientific community due to its impact on medical care, especially for high-cost patients, on the financing of health systems, and on the reduction of economic inequalities.

title: Standardized Annotation of Quantitative Proteomics Datasets Using SDRF-Proteomics.
abstract: Proteomics datasets require detailed and standardized metadata annotation to ensure reproducibility, reusability, and alignment with FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles. This chapter presents a practical, hands-on workflow for annotating a label-free proteomics dataset using the Sample and Data Relationship Format for Proteomics (SDRF-Proteomics), a HUPO-PSI and EuBIC-MS standard that has been adopted by major proteomics data repositories. We demonstrate the process on a COVID-19 nasal-swab dataset (PXD020394), showing how to derive sample and assay metadata from the study files, encode them in SDRF with the lesSDRF web application, and validate the result. Although the worked example is label-free, the approach can be generalized to other quantification strategies.

title: Anticipated vs enacted telework: the roles of self-management and interpersonal trust in schedule flexibility and work-life balance
abstract: This study aims to examine whether telework evaluations and the relationships among key telework-related constructs differ between a low-experience, prospective context and a context of enacted telework. The study compares anticipated and enacted telework perceptions using two independent surveys of Romanian employees: a 2018 survey in which respondents evaluated telework as a hypothetical work arrangement (n = 1,180) and a 2020 survey in which respondents reported their actual telework experience during the COVID-19 pandemic (n = 1,142). The analysis combines mean comparisons with partial least squares structural equation modelling and multi-group analysis. Because the samples are independent, the design permits a contextual between-sample comparison but does not trace within-person change from anticipation to experience. Structural relationships differ across the two samples. In the 2018 anticipated-telework sample, self-management is positively associated with schedule flexibility, whereas in the 2020 enacted-telework sample this association is negative. Interpersonal trust is positively associated with schedule flexibility in both samples, with a larger estimated path coefficient in the 2020 sample. The association between schedule flexibility and work-life balance is also stronger in the 2020 sample. These results indicate between samples contextual differences rather than within-person change. The study relies on two independent cross-sectional samples rather than a longitudinal panel, so the findings should be interpreted as contextual differences rather than within-person change. The findings suggest that managers should consider both individual and relational dimensions when evaluating remote work arrangements. In particular, differences in the relationships among self-management, interpersonal trust, schedule flexibility and work–life balance indicate that employee expectations and contextual conditions require attention when remote work is introduced or redesigned. The study contributes by treating prospective and enacted telework as distinct evaluative contexts, a distinction relevant whenever employees assess remote-work arrangements before their specific organisational implementation.

title: Cardiovascular Features of Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children and Kawasaki Disease
abstract: Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) was a new condition with clinical features overlapping with Kawasaki disease (KD) observed during the COVID-19 pandemic. Differences emerged that supported distinguishing between the two conditions, including distinct cardiac presentations and sequelae. The study objective was to compare echocardiographic findings between MIS-C and KD utilizing prospectively collected longitudinal cohort data from a multicenter consortium and the Kawasaki Disease Research Center. Pre-COVID KD cases (2017-2019) and MIS-C cases (April 2020-March 2022) were analyzed for differences in coronary artery (CA) Z-score and left ventricular ejection fraction (EF) during admission and follow up. Relative risks (RRs) were calculated between disease category and cardiac presentation (diminished EF and aneurysm status). We analyzed 480 subjects (MIS-C n=262; KD n=218). KD subjects had a higher risk of CA aneurysm (RR= 1.86; 95% CI: 1.23, 2.79). Conversely, KD subjects had a lower risk of diminished EF (RR=0.09; 95% CI: 0.04, 0.18). Although most cardiovascular abnormalities resolved by follow-up, diminished EF persisted in 6 MIS-C patients (6%). None of the KD subjects had diminished EF at follow-up. CA Z-score ≥2.5 persisted in 3 MIS-C patients (10%) and 13 KD patients (25%). At follow-up, newly documented diminished EF was observed in 1 MIS-C subject, while a CA Z-score ≥2.5 was newly identified in 1 MIS-C subject and 2 KD subjects. MIS-C and KD demonstrate distinct cardiovascular phenotypes, with diminished EF more prominent in MIS-C and CA aneurysms more characteristic of KD. These findings support disease-specific approaches to cardiac monitoring and longitudinal follow-up.

title: Understanding suicide risk in higher education: Institutional context, modifiable behaviors, and implications for campus health promotion.
abstract: Objective: Individual-level suicide risk factors are well documented, yet contextual and behavioral influences remain less understood. Participants: Using survey data from 250,385 students across 373 U.S. universities collected from 2019 to 2022 by the American College Health Association. Methods: In this research, we hypothesized that institutional characteristics are associated with suicide risk and that physical and social activities mediate these relationships. Results: Institutional characteristics, including school location, geographic region, enrollment size, and having a religious affiliation, were significantly associated with suicide risks. Physical and social activities significantly mediated some of these relationships. The results highlight disparities in suicide risk across U.S. higher education institutions during the COVID-19 pandemic and suggest that institutional contexts and student behaviors jointly shape suicide risk. Physical and social activities may represent important modifiable pathways. Conclusions: This study supports a Healthy Campus framework that emphasizes context-responsive prevention strategies and opportunities for physical and social engagement.

title: Single-cell transcriptomics revealed immunological and molecular profiling of pangolin viruses at the viral interface.
abstract: Pangolins have been identified as potential intermediate hosts for various viruses, including coronaviruses related to SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV, yet the cellular mechanisms underlying their viral susceptibility remain poorly understood. Here, we establish the first comprehensive single-cell transcriptomic atlas for two pangolin species Manis pentadactyla and Manis javanica, generated through single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of 245 618 high-quality cells from 12 major tissues, combined with 123 bulk transcriptome datasets. This resource is integrated with cross-species data from Homo sapiens, Eptesicus fuscus, Sus scrofa, Mus musculus, and Panthera tigris. Our analysis reveals a myeloid-biased hematopoiesis in pangolin bone marrow, dominated by monocytes and T cells, which contrasts sharply with the lymphoid-skewed composition observed in H. We also identify species-specific features, including thyroid-specific expression of FKBP5 in M. pentadactyla, and MIF-signaling-mediated cellular interactions in intestinal lymph. Furthermore, key viral receptors ( AXL, NRP1, DPP4, ACE2, SCARB1, and UVRAG) are broadly expressed in immune cells (e.g., B cells, T cells, and macrophages), fibroblasts, and endothelial cells across tissues, as confirmed by single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses. Cross-species comparisons reveal fundamental differences in splenic immune architecture, hematopoietic lineage distribution, and viral receptor expression. Together, these findings based on single-cell transcriptomic profiling establish a molecular and cellular framework for understanding pangolins as potential mixing vessels for viruses and provide a foundation for the targeted surveillance of emerging zoonotic pathogens.

title: The placental transfer of nirmatrelvir using the ex vivo human placental perfusion model
abstract: AIMS: Nirmatrelvir is an effective therapeutic option for COVID-19 infection and is often administered after symptom onset in pregnant individuals, but few data are available on the associated fetal exposure. The placental perfusion model evaluates maternal-fetal drug transfer across the human placenta and thus can determine fetal drug exposure. The objective of our study was to quantify the amount of nirmatrelvir transfer across the human placenta using the ex vivo placental perfusion model. METHODS: In a dual closed-closed perfusion of a single human placenta lobule, nirmatrelvir was added to the maternal circulation at its clinical concentration (2.21 μg/mL) or at 10 times this level (22.1 μg/mL). For each placenta studied, there was a 1-h perfusion control period followed by a 3-h exposure period. Samples of the perfusate were collected throughout the experiment to measure nirmatrelvir concentrations and placental viability markers. RESULTS: Perfusions conducted with nirmatrelvir at 2.21 μg/mL (n = 4) and 22.1 μg/mL (n = 5) concentrations showed a fetal-maternal concentration ratio (F:M) of 0.34 and 0.42, respectively, at 180 min. F:M was adjusted for nonplacental physiological factors, including binding of albumin and α-1-acid glycoprotein, and ionization. The adjusted F:M ranged from 0.26 to 0.35 for placentas perfused with 2.21 μg/mL and from 0.33 to 0.47 for placentas perfused with 22.1 μg/mL of nirmatrelvir. CONCLUSIONS: Nirmatrelvir readily crosses the term human placenta in a concentration-dependent manner. These transfer kinetics provide a foundation for future physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling, supporting the development of personalized nirmatrelvir dosing strategies in pregnancy.

title: Host-Directed Antiviral Discovery: Integrating Computational Strategies and Mechanistic Virology
abstract: Herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) remains a globally prevalent pathogen capable of establishing lifelong latency and recurrent infection, while current antiviral therapies are limited by incomplete viral clearance and the emergence of drug resistance. This thesis demonstrates the translational potential of a host-targeted antiviral approach by identifying a host factor distinguished by consistent upregulation across diverse viral transcriptomic datasets. A computational pipeline integrating molecular docking and predictive modeling was used to prioritize high-affinity inhibitors targeting this factor, followed by experimental validation of a lead compound for antiviral efficacy across in vitro, in vivo, and behavioral models of HSV-1, with relevance extending across additional viral families. Integrative transcriptomic analyses across multiple families of DNA and RNA viruses identified glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta (GSK3β), a serine/threonine kinase, as a consistently upregulated host factor, implicating it as a central regulator of virus–host interactions. Following identification of this kinase, computational methods were used to prioritize candidate inhibitors through structure-based analysis. Building on earlier work with HerpDock, a platform for structure-based targeting of viral proteins, HostDock was extended for application to host cell proteins with integrated QSAR-guided screening, molecular docking, and ADME evaluation. This enabled identification and ranking of GSK3β-targeting compounds, with alsterpaullone (ALP) emerging as the lead compound based on predicted binding affinity and pharmacological suitability. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that pharmacological inhibition of GSK3β with ALP alters STAT-mediated inflammatory gene expression and host receptor dynamics, defining its role in shaping cellular conditions permissive for viral infection. Inhibition of GSK3β suppressed viral infection across multiple stages of the HSV-1 life cycle, including binding, entry, and replication, and retained inhibitory effects on viral replication in acyclovir-resistant HSV-1 strains, while reducing inflammatory signaling. Parallel inhibition of viral entry and replication was observed in RNA viruses (SARS-CoV-2, Chikungunya [CHIKV], and Zika virus [ZIKV]). These effects were supported in vivo, where ALP administration reduced disease severity and improved functional outcomes in murine models of HSV-1 infection, with comparable effects observed in HSV-2. These findings position GSK3β as a conserved host regulator of viral infection and demonstrate that targeting host pathways can modulate viral pathogenesis across multiple stages of infection. This work establishes an integrated framework for host-directed antiviral discovery and provides a validated foundation for advancing this area of research.

title: THE IMPACT OF THE HYBRID LEARNING APPROACH ON MATHEMATICS PERFORMANCE IN ELEMENTARY AND MIDDLE SCHOOL
abstract: Hybrid learning, also known as blended learning, combines face-to-face classroom instruction with online learning activities in which students exercise some control over time, place, path, or pace. Over the past two decades, and especially after the disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, hybrid arrangements have become widespread in elementary and middle schools across the United States. This article examines the impact of the hybrid learning approach on mathematics performance among students in grades K–8. Methodologically, it is a qualitative, integrative literature review that synthesizes meta-analyses, randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental studies, and national assessment data published mainly between 2006 and 2023. The findings indicate that well-designed hybrid models, particularly those that integrate adaptive software, intelligent tutoring systems, and immediate feedback with active teacher mediation, tend to produce small to moderate positive effects on mathematics achievement when compared with traditional instruction alone. However, the evidence also shows that hybrid schooling adopted as an emergency response during the pandemic was associated with substantial declines in mathematics performance, particularly among low-income students and younger learners. The effectiveness of hybrid learning therefore depends less on the modality itself than on the quality of instructional design, teacher preparation, implementation fidelity, students’ self-regulation skills, and equitable access to devices and connectivity. The article concludes that hybrid learning can be a powerful tool for improving mathematics outcomes in the elementary and middle grades, provided that schools treat it as a deliberate pedagogical model rather than as a simple substitute for in-person teaching.

title: Early antenatal care initiation and associated factors in Hohoe Municipality, Ghana: A five-year multi-facility repeated cross-sectional record review study
abstract: Background Early initiation of antenatal care (ANC) is a critical strategy for improving maternal and neonatal health outcomes, as it enables timely detection and management of pregnancy-related risks. However, women in low- and middle-income countries initiate ANC late. This study estimated the proportion of women initiating ANC within the first trimester in three health facilities in the Hohoe Municipality, Ghana, over a five-year period (2020-2024). It also assessed trends across years and examined factors associated with early ANC initiation. Methods We conducted a multi-facility repeated cross-sectional record review of ANC records from three health facilities in Hohoe Municipality from January 2020 to December 2024. Of 7,660 records identified, 1,381 were excluded because the first ANC contact had occurred at another facility, leaving 6,279 for analysis. Background characteristics were summarised using frequencies and percentages, and the proportion of women initiating ANC within the first trimester was calculated overall and for each year. Multivariable binary logistic regression was used to examine the factors associated with early ANC initiation; age-by-parity interaction terms tested, and facility-by-predictor interaction models were fitted to assess effect heterogeneity. Results were presented as odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results Early ANC initiation increased slightly from 45.3% in 2020 to 46.4% in 2023 before declining to 44.3% in 2024, with an overall proportion of 45.1% across the study period. Patterns differed by facility between the COVID-19 (2020–2021) and post-COVID-19 (2022–2024) periods. Early initiation declined at Gbi-Wegbe Health Center (54.3% to 46.0%; p = 0.008) but increased at Adabraka Health Center (31.5% to 42.0%; p < 0.001) and at the Volta Regional Hospital (45.4% to 47.6%; p = 0.002). The odds of early ANC initiation was higher among women aged 31–40 years (aOR = 1.15; 95% CI: 1.01–1.31) than those aged 14-30, and among women with high-end of the acceptable range blood pressure (aOR = 1.44; 95% CI: 1.26–1.65), and those with above acceptable/Grade 1 hypertension (aOR = 1.95; 95% CI: 1.34–2.83) relative to those with acceptable hypertension status. Odds were lower with increasing parity, and lower at Adabraka Health Center and Volta Regional Hospital than at Gbi-Wedbe Health Center. The interaction analysis between maternal age and parity showed that multiparous women aged 31–40 had lower odds of early ANC initiation (OR = 0.61; 95% CI: 0.41–0.91), and lower among grand multiparous women of the same age (OR = 0.29; 95% CI: 0.11–0.77). In the facility-stratified analyses, grand multiparity was the only factor associated with early ANC initiation, which was consistent across all three facilities. Conclusion Fewer than half of women initiated ANC early in the Hohoe Municipality, with less variations across the study period and divergent trajectories between facilities. Early initiation was more likely among women aged 31–40 years and those with raised blood pressure, and less likely with increasing parity, with age and parity interacting. Facility-specific interventions prioritising women with high parity and reproductive education and needed to increase ANC initiation, whiles improving access to health facilities.

title: Disease-specific C-reactive protein heterogeneity across common infections is associated with a shared systemic inflammatory laboratory profile
abstract: C-reactive protein (CRP) is widely used to characterize systemic inflammation in infectious diseases, yet its absolute concentration may be influenced by infection type, anatomic extent, host characteristics, disease severity, and treatment exposure. We examined whether CRP distributions and the laboratory profile accompanying CRP elevation show reproducible cross-disease directions when evaluated within a harmonized analytical framework. This study was a baseline cross-sectional analysis nested within a single-center retrospective multicohort study of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP), influenza, active tuberculosis, sepsis, acute pyelonephritis (APN), diagnosis-record-defined candidiasis, and diagnosis-record-defined acute COVID-19. The first eligible hospitalization per patient within each disease was retained. Baseline laboratory values were the first reported results from 6 h before to 48 h after admission or the disease index time. Cross-disease CRP differences were quantified using nonparametric tests and effect sizes; disease-specific associations were assessed using Spearman correlations with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction, bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, and CRP-quartile analyses. CRP-by-disease interaction models evaluated whether CRP-associated laboratory slopes differed across diseases. Age- and sex-adjusted cross-disease models and a narrower -6 h to +24 h sensitivity analysis were also performed. The analysis included 2,717 disease-specific hospital records from 2,714 unique patients. CRP distributions differed across diseases (Kruskal-Wallis chi-square=245.64, P<0.001; epsilon-squared=0.088). Median CRP was highest in sepsis (92.3 mg/L), intermediate and overlapping in CAP (38.0), influenza (33.9), APN (29.7), and MPP (25.2), and lower in active tuberculosis (8.6), candidiasis (11.1), and COVID-19 (14.1). Across all eight cohorts, CRP correlated positively with NLR and neutrophil count and inversely with albumin; lymphocyte count was inversely associated in seven cohorts. However, CRP-by-disease interactions were significant for NLR (P = 0.020), neutrophils (P = 0.037), and albumin (P = 0.008), but not clearly for lymphocytes (P = 0.059), indicating shared directions with disease-dependent association strength rather than identical slopes. Cross-disease heterogeneity persisted after age and sex adjustment and in the narrower -6 h to +24 h window (n=2,003; P<0.001). Common infectious-disease cohorts show marked heterogeneity in absolute CRP concentration while higher CRP is accompanied by recurrent directional changes in routine inflammatory laboratory measures. These cross-sectional findings support disease-context-aware interpretation of CRP as a measure of systemic inflammatory burden. Diagnostic accuracy and prognostic performance were not directly evaluated, and the observed overlap should not be interpreted as establishing a universal etiologic, severity, or prognostic CRP threshold.

title: Wenn der beste Freund zubeißt When the best friend bites
abstract: Abstract Due to their small size and inapt behavior children are often victims of bite wounds. This can lead to severe injuries which require adequate medical care to prevent lasting damage and to enhance the healing process. Dog bites, in particular, can have severe consequences. A retrospective study was conducted to compare the incidence and characteristics of bite wounds before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. The results showed significantly more children were bitten during the pandemic. Furthermore, the number of bite wounds was significantly increased during the pandemic. The head/neck region was the most frequently injured region of the body. To prevent bite wounds in children, they as well as their parents need to be educated on how to deal with domestic animals and be supported in the implementation of the recommended guidelines.

title: Factors Associated with Patient Contact Management and Self-Reported Infection Risk Exposure Status Among Healthcare Workers: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study in Palu City, Indonesia
abstract: Introduction: Effective disaster management at national and global levels remains a major challenge in preparing for future pandemic risks. Experiences from major outbreaks such as Ebola, SARS, and COVID-19 highlight the need to strengthen emergency response systems in healthcare facilities. Patient contact management is an important component of infection-risk mitigation in healthcare settings because it aims to interrupt the transmission of infectious microorganisms. This study aimed to analyze factors associated with patient contact management and self-reported infection-exposure risk status among healthcare workers during the COVID-19 pandemic in Palu City, Indonesia. Methods: This quantitative retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted from April 2024 to July 2025 at 14 community health centers and one regional hospital in Palu City, Indonesia. Using proportional stratified random sampling, 131 participants were selected from a population of 198 healthcare workers. Data were analyzed using the chi-square test and Cramer's V. Results: Health-worker protection measures (p 0.05). Self-reported interactions lasting 3–5 minutes were the most frequent during patient care; however, contact duration was not significantly associated with either patient contact management or infection-exposure risk. Clinical skills were significantly associated with self-reported infection-exposure risk (p < 0.001; Cramer's V = 0.361). Conclusion: Patient contact management among healthcare workers was associated with individual and institutional factors, including knowledge, institutional/facility policy, health-worker protection, triage management, and infection zoning. Self-reported infection-exposure risk was significantly associated with healthcare workers' clinical skills.

This study aimed to analyze factors associated with patient contact management and self-reported infection-exposure risk status among healthcare workers during the COVID-19 pandemic in Palu City, Indonesia. Methods: This quantitative retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted from April 2024 to July 2025 at 14 community health centers and one regional hospital in Palu City, Indonesia. Using proportional stratified random sampling, 131 participants were selected from a population of 198 healthcare workers. Data were analyzed using the chi-square test and Cramer's V. Results: Health-worker protection measures (p 0.05). Self-reported interactions lasting 3–5 minutes were the most frequent during patient care; however, contact duration was not significantly associated with either patient contact management or infection-exposure risk. Clinical skills were significantly associated with self-reported infection-exposure risk (p < 0.001; Cramer's V = 0.361). Conclusion: Patient contact management among healthcare workers was associated with individual and institutional factors, including knowledge, institutional/facility policy, health-worker protection, triage management, and infection zoning. Self-reported infection-exposure risk was significantly associated with healthcare workers' clinical skills.

title: Development of Heterocyclic Small Molecule Antiviral Entry Inhibitors
abstract: There is an urgent need to develop novel antiviral therapeutics to address the growing threat posed by viruses. Small-molecule inhibitors of viral entry are attractive antiviral agents because they block the virus at its earliest step, preventing the virus from entering host cells and causing downstream damage. Some of the viruses of greatest concern for human health, such as human immunodeficiency virus, respiratory syncytial virus, influenza virus, Ebola virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, and Lassa virus, encode Class 1 fusion proteins which mediate membrane fusion and viral entry. In this dissertation, we highlight recent advances in the discovery and development of small-molecule entry inhibitors reported over the past five years that target viruses encoding Class 1 fusion proteins. Additionally, we report thieno[3,2-b]pyrroles as novel Group 2 influenza A virus entry inhibitors. Lastly, we report the further optimization of the raloxifene‐inspired benzothiophenes scaffold as novel pan-filovirus entry inhibitors.

title: P-263: Vaccination coverage assessment among children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1D) at a reference center
abstract: T1D is increasing among children and adolescents and is associated with a higher risk of infections. Immunization is an essential strategy for health protection. To assess vaccination coverage among pediatric patients with T1D followed in an outpatient clinic of a tertiary hospital and identify factors associated with incomplete immunization schedules. Cross-sectional study of patients aged 0-18 years with T1D at a reference center in Brazil, evaluating clinical, epidemiological, and laboratory data, family income, and vaccination status in accordance with the National Immunization Program (PNI) and the Reference Centers for Special Immunobiologicals (CRIE) recommendations. A total of 55 patients were analyzed, 52% female; mean age 11.3 years. They had an average of 5 medical visits per year. Regarding socioeconomic status, 52% of mothers had completed high school, and 41% of families had incomes between 1 and 3 times the minimum wage. Overall, 61.8% had up-to-date vaccinations. Of those with delayed vaccination, 42.8% were delayed only because they had not received the COVID-19 vaccine. Group comparison showed no significant differences in age (p=0.465) or number of visits (p=0.101); however, the delayed group had a higher rate of missed appointments (p=0.036). No significant association was found related to family income (p=0.737) or maternal education (p=0.228). Only 7.3% were aware of T1D-specific vaccines, and just 3.6% had received them at CRIE. Low vaccination rates were seen among patients with T1D. Delays in vaccination are mainly due to COVID-19 vaccines and are linked to more missed appointments. Awareness and use of specialized vaccines were very limited. These results emphasize the importance of developing strategies to increase vaccination coverage in this group.

title: Bovine-associated viruses at the human–animal interface: Zoonotic risks, spillover dynamics, and one health implications
abstract: Cattle serve as critical ecological reservoirs and amplifying hosts for numerous zoonotic viruses, thereby playing a central role in their maintenance, evolution, and interspecies transmission. Here, we briefly evaluate six viral pathogens of significant public health relevance linked to cattle, namely cowpox virus, bovine coronavirus, influenza A virus (H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b), bovine rotavirus, bovine leukemia virus, and SARS-CoV-2. This review focuses on advances in viral characterization, host tropism, and the mechanisms that may facilitate spillover through routes such as direct contact, environmental exposure, and foodborne transmission. It further highlights the bidirectional nature of pathogen exchange at the human-animal interface, where cattle may act as a source of viral variants with potential public health implications, though the risk varies considerably among the viruses discussed. Moreover, we discuss the imperative for integrated surveillance and One Health interventions to mitigate these transmission risks, highlighting cattle as valuable sentinel species within global health security frameworks.
