title: Transmission-route–specific trends in communicable diseases in Taiwan: an interrupted time-series analysis
abstract: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic substantially altered patterns of communicable disease (CD) transmission through implementation of non-pharmaceutical interventions and changes in healthcare utilization. However, long-term trends remain insufficiently characterized. We conducted an ecological time-series study using national surveillance data of notifiable CD in Taiwan from January 2017 to December 2023. Diseases were categorized into transmission-route groups, and temporal trends were assessed using segmented interrupted time-series models with autoregressive integrated moving average error structures to estimate phase-specific level and slope changes. A total of 240556 cases were reported, with more than 96% locally acquired. Overall incidence declined during the pandemic phase (2020–2022) and increased in 2023, exceeding pre-pandemic levels. This increase was largely influenced by dengue-related vector-borne disease activity. Substantial heterogeneity was observed across transmission pathways: airborne and droplet diseases declined markedly with partial recovery, sexually transmitted and blood-borne diseases increased consistently, and vector-borne diseases showed an outbreak-driven increase in 2023. Interrupted time-series analysis identified significant negative level changes at the onset of the pandemic and positive slope changes in the post-pandemic phase. These findings suggest transmission-route–specific temporal patterns during pandemic and post-pandemic phases and underscore the need for adaptive surveillance and prevention strategies in the post-pandemic era.

title: Human metapneumovirus-associated ARI hospitalisation rates in comparison to respiratory syncytial virus and influenza in eastern China, 2020-2024: a time-series analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVES We estimated human metapneumovirus (hMPV)-associated acute respiratory infection (ARI) hospitalisations in eastern China, and provided a direct comparison with RSV and influenza during 2020-2024. METHODS Leveraging a large regional medical database, we analysed weekly ARI hospitalisations and viral test-positives (hMPV, RSV and influenza) by age group and region, using negative binomial regression models with natural cubic splines, time-offsets for viral activity, excluding COVID-19 patients and adjusting for COVID-19 waves. RESULTS hMPV, RSV, and influenza were associated with 100,792 (5.35%), 266,826 (14.17%), and 409,599 (21.76%) ARI hospitalisations, respectively. RSV hospitalisations rebounded first in 2021/2022, followed by hMPV in 2022/2023, while influenza hospitalisations increased annually during the study period; meanwhile, hMPV- and influenza-associated hospitalisations shifted towards those aged 5-19 years, while RSV-associated hospitalisations shifted towards those aged ≥5 years. hMPV rates were highest among infants aged 0-5 months and 6-11 months (6.19 and 8.15 per 1,000 per year on average, respectively), followed by ages 12-23 months (18.54). RSV and influenza rates were highest in age groups within <1 year and 1-4 years, respectively. CONCLUSIONS Infants aged <1 year are the primary group for preventing severe hMPV infections, with a substantial additional burden observed in children aged 1-4 years. These findings support hMPV vaccine development and virus-specific intervention strategies.

title: Data-Driven Near-Optimal Regional Epidemic Surveillance
abstract: In the early stages of an epidemic outbreak, when the incidence data is limited, policy makers actively try to establish the scale and scope of the outbreak. Two of the most pertinent questions they seek to answer are i) has the outbreak started in a particular region (e.g. a country) and ii) how many sub-regions (e.g. a state or a county) have been affected thus far? We study these problems as a data-driven knowledge extraction task, i.e., given mobility and epidemiological data, we aim to extract actionable knowledge about which regions should receive additional surveillance resources so that an outbreak is detected early and its spatial footprint is accurately characterized. To this end, we formulate two discrete-lattice optimization objectives for epidemic surveillance, 1) maximizing the probability of detecting at least one infected sub-region and 2) maximizing the expected number of infected sub-regions detected. Both objectives turn out to be NP-hard. However, we prove that they are both submodular, which paves the way for efficient epidemic surveillance from limited data. We use this structure to derive curvature bounds for the objective. We also relate the bound with the parameters of the metapopulation disease dynamics. We propose a scalable algorithm, Lattice-Adapted Modified Greedy (LAMGreedy), that uses the curvature, and marginal-gain machinery to establish constant factor approximation guarantee. Extensive experiments on real-world mobility networks for COVID-19 and Influenza across three U.S. states show that LAMGreedy consistently outperforms natural and the state-of-the-art baselines under multiple cost models. The empirical results validate the prevalence and curvature estimates, and demonstrate that the proposed tools extract high-quality surveillance knowledge from mobility and epidemic data under realistic budget constraints.

title: Trends in mortality with both lung cancer and diabetes mellitus listed on the death certificate in the United States, 1999–2023
abstract: Lung cancer and diabetes mellitus are both common, yet national trends in deaths with both recorded have not been described. We analyzed CDC WONDER multiple cause-of-death data for 1999–2023, identifying deaths in adults aged 25 years or older with lung cancer and diabetes mellitus (ICD-10 C34, E10–E14) both listed on the certificate. We calculated age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 overall and by sex, race and Hispanic origin, region and (1999–2020) urbanization, estimated annual percent change (APC) with Joinpoint regression, compared groups with rate ratios and, for 2020–2023, excluded certificates also listing COVID-19. There were 174,422 deaths. The AAMR rose from 2.871 in 1999 to 3.425 in 2007, fell to 2.731 in 2018 (2007–2018 APC − 2.46%; 95% CI − 3.05 to − 1.88), rose to 3.262 in 2021 (2018–2021 APC 7.22%; 95% CI − 0.26 to 15.26; not significant) and was 2.990 in 2023. Excluding certificates also listing COVID-19 removed about 31% of the 2019–2021 increase. The male-to-female ratio fell from 2.22 to 1.74. In 2023 the Black-to-White ratio was 1.28 (95% CI 1.20 to 1.37) and the South-to-Northeast ratio 1.64 (95% CI 1.53 to 1.75). By point estimate, the South has had the highest regional rate since 2017. Non-metropolitan rates exceeded metropolitan rates in every year to 2020 (ratio 1.55 in 2020). Mortality with both conditions recorded differed persistently by sex, race, region and urbanization. These descriptive data cannot establish why rates changed or estimate risk among people with diabetes. Part of the 2019–2021 increase remains unexplained.

title: An Interferon-Braked Monocyte State and Compartment-Specific Myeloid Programming Across Severe Respiratory Infections
abstract: Severe COVID-19 is accompanied by marked remodeling of airway myeloid compartments, yet how infiltrating monocytes are routed toward inflammatory versus pro-fibrotic fates, and why resident alveolar macrophages fail to recover, remains incompletely understood. We re-analyzed BALF single-cell data (GSE145926; 3 healthy, 3 mild/moderate, 6 severe; 27,807 cells), re-clustering myeloid cells (n = 19,485) into 37 fine states (13 families) with functional module scoring, diffusion pseudotime, PAGA, a curated ligand–receptor screen, and per-donor decomposition; validation used the independent fatal-COVID-19 BALF cohort GSE157344 and the healthy-BALF cohort GSE151928 as a specificity control, a human endotoxin bone-marrow comparator (GSE212092), two sepsis blood cohorts (GSE175453; GSE167363, paired 0 h/6 h), three cross-pathogen blood cohorts (influenza A GSE243629, infant RSV GSE283746, bacterial ARDS GSE157789), and cross-disease comparison with IPF lung (GSE128033). Healthy BALF comprised resident alveolar macrophages, depleted in severe disease and replaced by interferon-activated, CXCL8-high, and SPP1+ populations. A CD14+SPP1−FCN1+ population co-expressing interferon-stimulated genes and IL1RN—an interferon-braked state distinct from LPS-type trained immunity—was enriched in severe disease, driven predominantly by one patient. PAGA delineated an FCN1+→intermediate→SPP1+ continuum; severe-enriched circuits included MIF–CD74 and an autocrine CXCL8–CXCR2 loop. The interferon-braked signature and SPP1+ compartments were reproduced in an independent fatal-COVID-19 BALF cohort and were at baseline in a healthy-BALF reference cohort (0.343 ± 0.091); LPS-challenged marrow showed the reciprocal pattern (TLR4-high, interferon-silent); and IPF lung shared SPP1/TREM2 induction with resident-AM collapse (SPP1 p = 0.0005). In sepsis blood, monocytes retained the interferon-braked signature with the LPS/TLR4 module near baseline; the signature was likewise elevated in bacterial ARDS, influenza A, and infant RSV monocytes, extending the compartment model beyond COVID-19. The data support a two-signal model: interferon restrains recruited monocytes at entry, while TLR4/HIF-1α- and SPP1-associated programs act downstream. The brake state is a measurable, stage-specific marker; MIF–CD74, CXCL8–CXCR2, and SPP1–CD44 are candidate nodes for stage-specific intervention. These mechanistic interpretations are grounded in the data and are proposed as testable hypotheses.

title: Pandemic-Driven Shifts in RSV Diversity, Evolution, and Global Spread
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic dramatically disrupted the seasonal circulation of RSV, with subsequent heterogeneous global resurgence. We aimed to characterize how pandemic-era disruptions restructured global RSV transmission dynamics, evolutionary patterns, and drivers of reemergence. We show that RSV-A and RSV-B genetic diversity underwent profound pandemic-associated suppression followed by heterogeneous resurgence. The post-pandemic period was characterized by pronounced changes in diversity, with the emergence of novel RSV-A genotypes (A.D.3 and A.D.5.2) and the expansion of the RSV-B, B.D.E.1 genotype. The recovery of RSV-B deviated strongly from neutral expectations and positive selection was detected at 20 sites in the G glycoprotein, F fusion protein, and M2-2 regulatory protein. Phylogeographic reconstruction revealed a sharp decline in international viral spread during the pandemic, followed by increasing persistence. Europe consistently served as the predominant global source, followed by Western Pacific and North America. Air-travel volume was the strongest predictor of dissemination (log coefficient >0.68 for both subtypes). Post-pandemic RSV resurgence represented fundamental epidemiological restructuring shaped by a population bottleneck, positive selection and major impact of air-travel. These findings underscore the need for robust genomic surveillance to track the global circulation of lineages, and to monitor effectiveness of pharmaceutical interventions given the emergence of new genotypes. We show that RSV-A and RSV-B genetic diversity underwent profound pandemic-associated suppression followed by heterogeneous resurgence. The post-pandemic period was characterized by pronounced changes in diversity, with the emergence of novel RSV-A genotypes (A.D.3 and A.D.5.2) and the expansion of the RSV-B, B.D.E.1 genotype. The recovery of RSV-B deviated strongly from neutral expectations and positive selection was detected at 20 sites in the G glycoprotein, F fusion protein, and M2-2 regulatory protein. Phylogeographic reconstruction revealed a sharp decline in international viral spread during the pandemic, followed by increasing persistence. Europe consistently served as the predominant global source, followed by Western Pacific and North America. Air-travel volume was the strongest predictor of dissemination (log coefficient >0.68 for both subtypes). Post-pandemic RSV resurgence represented fundamental epidemiological restructuring shaped by a population bottleneck, positive selection and major impact of air-travel. These findings underscore the need for robust genomic surveillance to track the global circulation of lineages, and to monitor effectiveness of pharmaceutical interventions given the emergence of new genotypes. title: An Industrial Psychological Approach: Impact of Remote Work on Employee Motivation
abstract: Over the last few years, remote work has gained grounds—it has shifted from being a temporary necessity during the COVID-19 pandemic to becoming a permanent feature of the contemporary workplace. The paper seeks to contribute to the literature of remote work by analysing its repercussions on employee motivation, which is one of the key drivers in employee relations. It examines how an altered work environment would influence intrinsic and extrinsic motivations, the latter focusing more specifically on job satisfaction, engagement, and resultant productivity attained. Based on the replication of existing scholarly literature and empirical research and the results of an online survey data collection instrument among remote workers in varying industries, the paper informs the comprehensive understanding of the nuanced relationship between remote work and employee motivation.

title: A Review of Cristiano B. Moura's (Ed.) (2024) A Sociopolitical Turn in Science Education: Towards Post-Pandemic Worlds
abstract: This book review examines Cristiano B. Moura’s (2024) A Sociopolitical Turn in Science Education: Towards Post-Pandemic Worlds. This edited book is about how science education can imagine a more just future for the planet by interrogating hegemonic science norms. With the COVID-19 pandemic as a lens for understanding science and society, the different authors in this book articulate new perspectives for addressing social and ecological injustices while advocating for a sociopolitical movement in science education. Although the primary audience for Moura’s book is science education researchers, this book review also draws attention to chapters sharing practical examples of a sociopolitical approach for possible K–12 classroom adaptations. In this review, an overview of each book section is provided while highlighting chapters of interest. Strengths and critiques of the text are also discussed. Overall, this book, which brings together diverse perspectives from global contexts, provides a valuable and timely contribution to science education research. It is a powerful call to action for science educators to engage with the sociopolitical movement in their scholarship and teaching practices. Keywords: science education, sociopolitical turn, socioscientific issues, social justice, ecological justice

title: All-cause and cause-specific mortality in people with rare autoimmune rheumatic diseases in England using whole population data.
abstract: OBJECTIVES People with rare autoimmune rheumatic diseases (RAIRD) experience morbidity and premature mortality due to disease activity and immunosuppression. We conducted a nationwide, whole-population retrospective cohort study using linked routinely collected healthcare data in England. METHODS All individuals in England with a RAIRD diagnosis recorded in hospital admissions data and alive in 2013 were included. Linked demographic and death certificate data were used to calculate crude and age-sex-standardised mortality rates for all causes and leading causes of death from 2013 to 2020. Rates were compared with Office for National Statistics data for the general population of England. RESULTS There were 53,237 deaths among people with RAIRD. The cohort was 69.9% female, median age rose from 61.5 to 62.5 years during the study. All-cause mortality declined between 2013 and 2019 but rose in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. The age-sex-standardised mortality rate ratio versus the general population decreased from 2.6 (95% CI 2.6-2.7) in 2013 to 2.3 (2.2-2.3) in 2020. Mortality was particularly elevated for infection (rate ratio 4.10, 3.81-4.39), cardiovascular disease (2.50, 2.45-2.55), COVID-19 (2.74, 2.59-2.89) and respiratory disease (2.90, 2.82-2.98). Highest all-cause mortality occurred in systemic sclerosis, polymyositis/dermatomyositis, microscopic polyangiitis and unspecified arteritis. Deaths from opportunistic infections were rare. CONCLUSIONS Mortality in RAIRD remains more than twice that of the general population despite modest improvement over time. Infection, respiratory disease and COVID-19 remain major contributors, highlighting the need for targeted infection prevention and cardiovascular risk management.

title: Trade Exposure and Consumer Behavior During Recessions: The Case of the European Union Wine Industry
abstract: This paper examines how the financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic affected wine consumption across European Union (EU) member states, focusing on countries’ trade positions. Using a balanced panel of 28 EU countries from 2000 to 2022, we apply a panel difference-in-differences framework and a complementary event-study analysis to estimate the effects of these shocks. Because year fixed effects absorb shocks common to all countries, the design identifies differences between export-oriented and other countries, not EU-wide effects of the crises. Export-oriented EU countries show a larger, significant decline in measured wine consumption after the financial crisis, at the end of the post-crisis period. The comparison of the impact of COVID-19 is inconclusive because parallel trends are not supported. The estimates are conditional associations and may reflect how consumption is measured and characteristics shared by wine exporting countries. Findings highlight the importance of structural market characteristics for consumer behavior and suggest that global integration may condition the resilience of EU wine markets.

title: Navigating Malaria in a Border Zone: A Qualitative Study of Behavioural Determinants, Structural Barriers and Elimination Challenges in Tak Province, Thailand.
abstract: BACKGROUND Malaria elimination in the Greater Mekong Subregion (GMS) is still struggling with barriers in border regions, where population mobility, occupational exposure, and health system fragility continue to drive ongoing malaria transmission. Tak Province is a typical example of such challenges along the Thailand-Myanmar border. Qualitative evidence of the lived experience of frontline health actors is crucial for the design of contextually placed elimination strategies. METHODS This qualitative descriptive study was conducted in Khane Chue Subdistrict, Mae Ramat District, Tak Province, a malaria-endemic area bordering Myanmar. A total of 17 informants participated: 13 village health volunteers, two health workers and two non-governmental organization staffs. Semi-structured instruments were developed to suit each group of participants and used to guide the in-depth interviews. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to analyse data, applying both deductive and inductive coding. RESULTS Five factors related to malaria prevention behaviours were identified: cross-border mobility and migration; occupational exposure of agricultural and forest workers; a knowledge-behaviour gap related to malaria risk normalization and availability of free treatment; lifestyle routines that coincide with peak vector biting hours; socioeconomic and environmental vulnerability. Five programmatic bottlenecks were also prominent: funding cuts after USAID's exit, human resource shortages and low rates of compensation for community health workers (CHWs), fear-based avoidance of health care services by undocumented migrants, poor uptake of long-lasting insecticidal nets and compounding external shocks such as Myanmar's political instability and COVID-19 pandemic. CONCLUSION Malaria control in this border area is influenced by the interaction of many behavioural, environmental, and health system determinants on multiple levels. To achieve elimination will need migrant-inclusive health policies, occupation-specific vector control, active surveillance for a prolonged period, cross-border programmatic coordination and stable financing. Findings provide specific recommendations for health planners in similar border contexts in Southeast Asia.

title: Single-Cell Multi-Omics Reveals Dynamic Chromatin Remodeling of Adaptive Immunity During Prime-Boost Vaccination
abstract: Vaccination induces durable adaptive immunity, yet how transcriptional and chromatin programs are dynamically established and reorganized across successive vaccine doses remains poorly understood. Here, we performed paired single-nucleus RNA sequencing and chromatin accessibility profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells collected from four individuals at ten time points spanning primary and booster immunization with the inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine BBIBP-CorV. More differentially expressed genes and accessible regions were detected after primary than booster vaccination. Notably, independent public Hi-C data provided structural context for candidate DAR-gene associations. In B cells, AP-1 motif accessibility decreased dynamically after primary vaccination, followed by increased plasma cell differentiation and secretory programs. In T cells, signature scores decreased on day 1 after primary vaccination and were accompanied by remodeling of transcription factor-associated chromatin accessibility. These intracellular changes were accompanied by temporal reorganization of T and B cell communication and the emergence of distinct multicellular modules associated with primary and booster responses. Together, our findings describe temporal changes in gene expression and chromatin accessibility across circulating T and B cells following primary and booster vaccination in this cohort.

title: Extracellular galectin-3 preferentially through CD44 and PD-1 binds activated T cells and marks memory-phenotype T cell subsets
abstract: Background Galectin-3 (Gal-3) is a multifunctional β-galactoside-binding lectin implicated in immune regulation, yet its association with T cell phenotypes under physiological and inflammatory conditions remains incompletely defined. Methods We investigated Gal-3 expression and binding on murine and human T cells across developmental stages, tissues, sex, genetic background, circadian time, and inflammatory disease settings. Results In mice, Gal-3-associated CD4 + and CD8 + T cells were dynamically regulated by age, anatomical location, strain, sex, and circadian rhythm. Gal-3 + T cells displayed increased activation markers, enhanced TCR-associated signaling molecules, elevated cytolytic mediators, increased proliferation, and greater apoptosis. Gal-3 + T cells were enriched within central and effector memory compartments and expressed higher levels of co-inhibitory receptors, including PD-1, with ImageStream analysis confirming Gal-3 co-expressed with PD-1. Recombinant Gal-3 preferentially bound activated, but not resting T cells, and associated with CD44 and CD3, suggesting activation-dependent acquisition of extracellular Gal-3. Re-analysis of human thymocyte and Long COVID single-cell RNA-seq datasets further supported an association between LGALS3 expression and activated/exhausted T cell states. Finally, intracellular staining indicated that T cells are unlikely to be a major source of Gal-3. Conclusion Our findings identify Gal-3 as a context-dependent marker and potential regulator of activated, antigen-experienced T cells, which promotes T cell apoptosis.

title: Recent increases in new HIV diagnoses among cisgender women in King, Los Angeles and San Francisco Counties, 2015-2024
abstract: Syphilis cases among cisgender (cis) women have been rising in jurisdictions across the United States, raising concerns about potential increases in HIV. Using public health data, we summarized trends in HIV diagnoses among cis women in three west coast jurisdictions. We analyzed data from the National HIV Surveillance System and local partner services databases for King County, Washington; Los Angeles (LA) County, California; and San Francisco (SF) County, California from 2015-2024. Individuals were included if sex was “female”, current gender was “woman”, and HIV diagnosis was classified as new. From 2015-2020, all three jurisdictions reported decreases in HIV rates among cis women. Rates began increasing in 2021, and in 2024, were 38%, 14% and 63% higher for King, LA and SF counties, respectively, compared to 2019 (pre-COVID). There were significant and persistent racial/ethnic disparities, which varied by county. Across three urban jurisdictions, HIV diagnoses among cis women increased from 2022-2024, with over a quarter of women newly diagnosed in 2024 reporting being unhoused at diagnosis. While 2024 HIV rates were similar to pre-COVID-19, the recent increases are concerning as they follow years of declining rates of new HIV diagnoses. Improved access to stigma-free HIV screening, prevention and treatment for cis women are important to reverse this trend.

title: Emissions of quaternary ammonium compounds and pharmaceuticals from wastewater treatment plants under different operational conditions.
abstract: The use of both quaternary ammonium compounds (QACs)-biocides increasingly consumed after the outbreak of covid-19-and pharmaceuticals causes concerns about adverse effects on aquatic organisms and links to antimicrobial resistance. Though they largely enter wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), there exists a gap in knowledge of the effects of solids retention time (SRT) and hydraulic retention time (HRT) on their removal in the activated sludge process. We monitored 14 QACs, another disinfectant, and 13 pharmaceuticals in treated effluents of 14 activated sludge WWTPs with wide ranges of SRT (5-48 days) and HRT (7-70 h), within an administrative district over a year. The total mean concentrations of all compounds ranged from 2.4 to 15 μg/L among the WWTP effluents, to which 14 labile compounds (11 QACs and 3 drugs) contributed 6% to 76%. Their contributions were higher in WWTPs with shorter SRTs and HRTs. Relative standard deviations (RSDs) of effluent concentrations of labile compounds were mostly >50% among seasons and >100% among the WWTPs, largely exceeding those in raw sewage. The higher the WWTP removal rate of a compound was, the larger the effluent RSD was among the WWTPs and seasons. Per-capita mass outflows of most compounds other than persistent drugs were negatively correlated with SRTs or HRTs among the WWTPs, indicating that they were key factors affecting their removal and emission. Interpretation of these associations should consider the limited number of WWTPs and the availability of operational data. Our findings will be useful in managing QACs and pharmaceuticals.

title: Predictors of falls among robust community-dwelling older adults: a prospective cohort study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Falls and their consequent injuries represent a threat to active aging, independence, and well-being, with critical impacts on older adults, families, and society. OBJECTIVE To investigate predictors of falls among robust community-dwelling older adults. METHODS This was a prospective cohort study in which the primary outcome was the incidence of falls during a one-year follow-up. Older adults (≥ 65 years) classified as robust according to the Clinical-Functional Vulnerability Index-20 (IVCF-20) and living in the community were included. Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected, and participants were assessed using the Timed Up and Go Test (TUG), Activities-specific Balance Confidence Scale (ABC), Falls Behavioral Scale for the Elderly (FaB-Brazil), Montreal Cognitive Assessment Basic (MoCA-B), handgrip strength test, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). The log-rank test and multivariate Cox regression model were used for statistical analysis. RESULTS A total of 94 robust older adults were included, most of whom were women (74.5%) with a mean age of 71.2 ± 4.7 years. The incidence of falls was 28.7%. In the multivariate model, a previous history of COVID-19 infection (HR = 4.30; 95% CI: 1.55-12.61; p = 0.006) and higher clinical-functional vulnerability (HR = 1.30; 95% CI: 1.02-1.70; p = 0.043) were significantly associated with the incidence of falls. CONCLUSION Even among robust older adults, the incidence of falls was substantial. These findings reinforce the importance of screening for clinical-functional vulnerability and maintaining post-COVID-19 monitoring strategies to prevent falls in this population.

title: Green Radiative Cooling and Antimicrobial Materials Based on Polylactic Acid Oligomer Hexagonal Microspheres
abstract: Thermal management relying on passive radiative cooling materials can result in remarkable energy savings and greenhouse gas emissions reductions compared with traditional air conditioner-based cooling. However, few of these materials are degradable; thus, their disposal may generate a new environmental problem. At the same time, the COVID-19 pandemic and other infectious diseases have raised requirements for hygienic and antimicrobial performance. In this work, we use a facile solvent evaporation method to prepare a novel hierarchically porous polylactic acid oligomer (PLAO) coating that exhibits a radiative cooling effect, broad-spectrum antimicrobial properties, and degradability (with a degradation rate of 99.5% after 28 days). title: De-risking from China: how US firms reconfigure sourcing through decoupling, diversification and friendshoring across geopolitical disruptions
abstract: We examine whether US firms use three location strategies—decoupling, diversification, and friendshoring—to de-risk their sourcing portfolios. We investigate how the use of these strategies varies across bilateral (2018 US–China trade war), systemic (COVID-19 pandemic) and alliance-based (Russia–Ukraine war) shocks. We also test whether firms operating in high-tech industries de-risk more aggressively. Using Panjiva US seaborne import records, we build firm-year measures of the three strategies for 1,565 US firms over 2011–2024. We then estimate fixed-effects models that interact firm's pre-disruption China exposure with the three disruption periods and a high-tech indicator. Highly China-exposed firms decouple during all three disruptions, with decoupling switching on sharply at the trade war. Diversification activates specifically at the COVID-19 pandemic. Friendshoring peaks during the COVID-19 pandemic and reverses once the war begins. Sourcing portfolios appear more diversified and politically aligned, but these gains vanish once the China sourcing share is excluded, revealing them as mechanical by-products of decoupling. High-tech firms generally do not de-risk more than their peers. We move the study of de-risking from perception-based case evidence to large-scale observed sourcing behavior. We conceptualize decoupling, diversification, and friendshoring as three sourcing location strategies and match each to its most salient disruption type, laying the groundwork for a contingency theory of strategy–shock fit. We further show that portfolio-wide indices of diversification and political alignment may overstate genuine de-risking because they incorporate the effects of decoupling. Moreover, policymakers' ambitions to de-risk high-tech industries and promote friendshoring have generated only a limited corporate response.

title: Discovering molecular modulators with nanoswitch screening
abstract: Molecules that modulate protein-protein interactions, including through ternary complex formation, have been established as key therapeutics. Yet they can be challenging to discover, as standard screening approaches often lack throughput or fail to directly assay multibody interactions. We addressed this by combining DNA nanoswitch-based selection of nucleotide-encoded libraries with next-generation sequencing to create FIND (Functional Interaction-based Nanoswitch Discovery), which enables ultrahigh-throughput discovery of compounds that induce or increase protein-protein interactions. We demonstrate FIND by discovering nanobodies that stabilize the interaction between angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 and the receptor-binding domain of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 and by discovering agonists of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma from a DNA-barcoded small-molecule library. By enabling rapid discovery of molecular modulators, FIND could lead to new therapeutics across many conditions.

title: Application of CRISPR Based Diagnostics for Rapid and Specific Detection of Emerging Pathogens
abstract: The emergence and reappearance of infectious pathogens have prompted the need for developing diagnostic technologies that are quick, accurate, and reliable. Conventional technologies for pathogen detection such as polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR) provide accurate pathogen detection, but they may require sophisticated equipment, labor and time. This paper explores the application of CRISPR-based diagnostic tools as a quick, selective and efficient method for pathogen detection. This paper applies secondary research in examining the scientific literature on CRISPR-based diagnostics, particularly, Cas12 and Cas13, and their applications in infectious disease diagnosis. One gets attracted to the SHERLOCK and DETECTR systems which make use of programmable recognition of nucleic acids and collateral cleavage to generate detectable signals. These results indicate the utility of the CRISPR diagnostics for detecting viral and bacterial pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2, dengue, Newcastle disease viruses and antimicrobial resistant bacteria. Moreover, the ability to integrate into isothermal amplification methods, such as the recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA), is useful in increasing efficiency of the diagnostic tests as well as their portability. There are, however, a number of challenges related to sensitivity, sample processing, stability of the reagents, standardization and validation. The authors note that CRISPR diagnostics provide an important complement to traditional molecular diagnostics.

title: Oil prices versus global Islamic indices: evidence from S&P sectoral stock indices
abstract: This study aims to examine the time-varying dynamic dependencies between crude oil returns and global Islamic S&P sectoral stock indices, specifically focusing on the sectors most affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. The analysis spans from 2008 to 2022, using continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and wavelet coherence analysis to capture multi-scale co-movements across short, medium and long-term horizons. Results reveal that the relationship between crude oil prices and global sectoral stock index returns is scale-dependent and time-varying. Strong correlations are observed in most sectors, particularly energy and industrials, whereas the real estate sector exhibits a unique decoupling behavior. Notably, crude oil plays a crucial role in mitigating sectoral portfolio performance with the real estate sector exhibiting the lowest risk when exposed to crude oil fluctuations. Unlike previous studies that focus on aggregate Islamic market indices, this paper provides a granular analysis of sector-specific vulnerabilities. It contributes to the literature by identifying the distinct “safe-haven” potential of Islamic real estate during energy shocks and offering tailored portfolio diversification strategies for investors during periods of extreme market disruption like the COVID-19 pandemic.
journal: Journal of Islamic Accounting and Business Research

title: Application of Machine Learning and Deep Learning in diagnosis Covid19
abstract: Predicting the progression of COVID-19 in hospitalised patients was an important challenge during the pandemic, particularly when healthcare resources were limited. This study investigates the use of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models to predict three clinical outcomes: death, admission to the intensive care unit (ICU), and clinical status (improvement or worsening). The study uses two patient datasets: an Algerian cohort of 80 patients from the Internal Medicine Department of the University Hospital Centre of Constantine, collected between July and August 2020, and a French cohort of 99 patients collected between March and May 2020. Five ML classifiers were evaluated: logistic regression (LR), k-nearest neighbours (KNN), classification and regression trees (CART), Naive Bayes (NB), and support vector machines (SVM). Their performance was examined in combination with three feature-selection methods: analysis of variance (ANOVA), mutual information (MI), and recursive feature elimination (RFE). The results were also compared with multilayer perceptron (MLP) models using one to five hidden layers. Model evaluation included 30 repetitions of five-fold cross-validation on the training data, followed by evaluation on a separate hold-out test set. The results showed that selecting 20 features generally provided better cross-validated accuracy than selecting 30 features or using the full feature set. The best-performing classifier-feature-selection combination varied across the six dataset-outcome tasks. LR combined with RFE was selected for three tasks, LR combined with ANOVA for one task, and CART combined with ANOVA for two tasks. The selected ML models achieved test-set accuracies ranging from 0.47 to 0.95 and higher accuracy than the average MLP results in five of the six tasks. These findings suggest that ML methods can be useful for exploring clinical outcomes in hospitalised COVID-19 patients. However, the small sample sizes and limitations of the available data mean that the results should be interpreted with caution. Further evaluation using larger and independent patient datasets is needed before these models can be considered for clinical use.

title: P-370: Epidemiological profile of pediatric patients with diabetic ketoacidosis admitted to a reference hospital in western São Paulo, Brazil
abstract: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a life-threatening complication of type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), characterized by hyperglycemia, ketosis and metabolic acidosis. Its incidence and clinical profile in public referral centers in Brazil remain poorly documented. To assess DKA incidence trends over 10 years and describe the clinical and epidemiological profile of pediatric patients admitted to a tertiary public referral hospital in western São Paulo. Retrospective descriptive study analyzing electronic medical records of patients aged 0–17 years admitted between January 2013 and December 2023 with ICD-10 codes E14 or E101 at Hospital Regional de Presidente Prudente. Data collected included age, sex, municipality of origin, length of stay, laboratory findings, and clinical complications. Ethics committee approval was obtained. Of 278 patients screened, 247 met inclusion criteria. DKA was confirmed in 180 patients (73%). Female patients predominated (58%). Mean age at admission was 12.1 years; mean hospital stay was 8 days. A total of 751 hospitalizations were recorded, averaging 4.17 admissions per patient. Hypovolemic shock occurred in 3 patients (1.6% of DKA cases); 6 patients (2.4%) required orotracheal intubation; vasoactive drugs were used in 2 cases (1.1%). Only 38% of patients resided in the hospital’s home city. DKA admissions peaked in 2016 (n=110) and showed a declining trend thereafter. DKA predominantly affected female adolescents, consistent with literature. Severe complications were uncommon. A declining trend in admissions was observed after 2016, contrasting with studies reporting increased DKA rates during the COVID-19 pandemic. This regional epidemiological profile supports the need for early DM diagnosis strategies in public health systems.

title: Modeling public opinion emotional structure in emergencies through cross-conditional analysis of the SMP2020-EWECT Weibo benchmark
abstract: In emergencies, social media is one of the main platforms on which people share how they feel, and those expressions carry information that matters for situational awareness and risk communication. This study models public opinion through fine-grained emotion classification on a public benchmark, the SMP2020-EWECT Weibo dataset, which is labeled with six emotions: happy, angry, sad, fear, surprise and neutral. In the emergency subset the happy label rarely marks private cheerfulness. It marks encouragement, mutual support and praise directed at medical staff and at the affected city, a crisis-specific reading of the label that the token-level analysis in Sect. 6 confirms, and for that reason this class is referred to throughout as the positive, solidarity-oriented class. The benchmark contains two subsets that share the same label scheme and the same platform. The usual subset reflects ordinary online discussion, while the virus subset was collected during the COVID-19 outbreak and represents the emergency condition. Comparing the two subsets is the main analytical device of the study, because it shows how the emotional structure of public expression differs between an emergency and an ordinary period. A bidirectional gated recurrent unit encoder followed by an additive attention layer is trained separately on each subset and is compared with strong linear baselines built on term frequency features, with a variant of the same encoder in which attention is replaced by mean pooling, and with a Transformer encoder of matched scale that shares every other component of the pipeline. Emoji tokens and hashtag topic words are kept during preprocessing because they carry sentiment on microblogs, and a class-weighted loss counters the strong imbalance of the rare emotions. All neural results are reported as the mean and standard deviation over five random seeds. The attention model reaches an accuracy of 0.679 ± 0.005 on the general subset and 0.685 ± 0.011 on the emergency subset. The linear baselines are higher, at 0.716 and 0.734; an exact McNemar test shows that this advantage is statistically significant on both subsets, and a Transformer encoder trained under the same protocol does not close the gap. The attention layer therefore contributes interpretability rather than accuracy, and a token deletion test quantifies that contribution: deleting the three tokens that receive the highest attention in a post costs 16.8 accuracy points on the emergency subset and 15.2 points on the general subset, against 6.9 and 3.4 points for deleting three tokens at random. The emotional structure itself differs sharply between the two conditions, with the positive, solidarity-oriented class covering 51.4% of the emergency subset, or 48.7% once repeated posts are removed from the training split, while anger covers 30.0% of the general subset, a contrast that is directly informative for monitoring. Because the benchmark records neither who wrote a post nor which posts were removed, the study cannot separate spontaneous solidarity from expression shaped by state-led mobilization or platform moderation, and the solidarity-oriented share is interpreted as the composition of visible posts. The result is a transparent and reproducible account of how the structure of visible public emotion shifts during an emergency.

title: Growing through crisis: Qualitative nursing perspectives of posttraumatic growth after the pandemic.
abstract: BackgroundNurses working through the COVID-19 pandemic experienced moral, ethical, and psychological trauma. Posttraumatic Growth (PTG) is an increasingly recognized recovery phenomena following highly traumatic circumstances. Few qualitative studies explore PTG in nurses during the pandemic.Research aimThis study investigated (1) the context and nature of trauma experienced by nurses during the COVID-19 pandemic, (2) nurses' responses to these traumatic experiences, and (3) whether the core dimensions of posttraumatic growth were present or absent, including how these dimensions manifested in nurses' experiences.Research design and methodsUsing a qualitative descriptive design, one-on-one interviews were conducted with participants using an open-ended interview guide informed by the PTG conceptual model.Participants and research context17 clinical nurses from two campuses within a single academic medical center network in New York City were interviewed.Ethical ConsiderationsThis study was conducted with ethical approval (IRB protocol #23-04025921) from the Weill Cornell Medicine IRB, and informed verbal consent was obtained prior to each interview.FindingsFollowing inductive analysis, three emergent themes were identified: (1) Trauma Experienced; (2) Post Trauma Period; and (3) Enduring Adaptations Following Trauma. Following deductive analysis, four of the five PTG model dimensions were endorsed by participants: Appreciation for Life; New Possibilities; Relating to Others; Personal Strength. No participants identified spiritual growth as an outcome of their experience working through the pandemic.ConclusionsNurses that worked through the pandemic experienced high psychological, moral and ethical stress. Despite the highly challenging and traumatic circumstances, nurses demonstrated remarkable capacity for growth through an evolved appreciation for life and professional purpose. Two primary protective factors emerged including the clinical family and active interdisciplinary engagement.

Few qualitative studies explore PTG in nurses during the pandemic.Research aimThis study investigated (1) the context and nature of trauma experienced by nurses during the COVID-19 pandemic, (2) nurses' responses to these traumatic experiences, and (3) whether the core dimensions of posttraumatic growth were present or absent, including how these dimensions manifested in nurses' experiences.Research design and methodsUsing a qualitative descriptive design, one-on-one interviews were conducted with participants using an open-ended interview guide informed by the PTG conceptual model.Participants and research context17 clinical nurses from two campuses within a single academic medical center network in New York City were interviewed.Ethical ConsiderationsThis study was conducted with ethical approval (IRB protocol #23-04025921) from the Weill Cornell Medicine IRB, and informed verbal consent was obtained prior to each interview.FindingsFollowing inductive analysis, three emergent themes were identified: (1) Trauma Experienced; (2) Post Trauma Period; and (3) Enduring Adaptations Following Trauma. Following deductive analysis, four of the five PTG model dimensions were endorsed by participants: Appreciation for Life; New Possibilities; Relating to Others; Personal Strength. No participants identified spiritual growth as an outcome of their experience working through the pandemic.ConclusionsNurses that worked through the pandemic experienced high psychological, moral and ethical stress. Despite the highly challenging and traumatic circumstances, nurses demonstrated remarkable capacity for growth through an evolved appreciation for life and professional purpose. Two primary protective factors emerged including the clinical family and active interdisciplinary engagement.

title: Evaluation of targets for normalization of viral pathogen concentrations in building dust.
abstract: Building dust is potentially an important public health tool for monitoring human pathogens because it contains genetic material from pathogens. However, building dust is heterogeneous and presents technical challenges for environmental pathogen surveillance. To effectively use pathogen measurements in building dust for environmental surveillance, normalization procedures that account for human contribution to dust may be necessary and could help account for variability in occupancy and temporal resolution. Our analysis investigates potential indicators of human emission that could be used to normalize data on concentration of pathogens in dust. Ninety-nine vacuum dust samples were collected from 33 buildings and concentrations were measured for three emission indicators (i.e., human cytochrome B gene, Carjivirus communis (previously crAssphage), and pepper mild mottle virus) and two respiratory pathogens (i.e. SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus). All of these were detected in ≥91% of the samples, with the exception of influenza A virus (73%). Most pairings of indicators (nine of 10) showed a weak to moderate positive correlation with one another (Kendall's τ ≤ 0.28). Correlations between occupancy and emission indicators and respiratory pathogens were weak (Kendall's τ 0.1). Among all potential markers, MT-CYB was most promising, with detection in 96% of the samples, higher concentration than others, and stronger correlation with other potential measures of occupancy.

title: Depressive Symptoms Among Frontline Healthcare Workers in a Public Hospital in Ciudad Juárez, Mexico: A Post-Pandemic Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with substantial psychological burden among healthcare workers worldwide. Reported prevalences of depressive symptoms range from 21.7% to 64.7%. Nurses and physicians working on the front lines were particularly vulnerable to these psychological changes. This study aimed to describe the severity of depressive symptoms and explore their association with the sociodemographic and occupational characteristics of healthcare workers in a public hospital in Ciudad Juárez, Mexico. Materials and Methods: A cross-sectional observational study was conducted at a public hospital of the Mexican Social Security Institute in Ciudad Juarez Mexico. The sample consisted of 296 healthcare workers providing front-line care to patients with COVID-19. A questionnaire collected sociodemographic and occupational variables, including age, sex, marital status, pre-existing health conditions, job title, academic level, and access to personal protective equipment (PPE). The Beck Depression Inventory II (BDI II) was utilized to evaluate depressive symptoms. Bivariate analysis was performed using the chi-square test (X2) with the severity of depressive symptoms. Bivariate analyses were performed using a chi-square test (X2), calculating odds ratios (ORs) and confidence intervals (CIs). Binary logistic regression analysis was conducted to explore the independent predictors of depressive symptoms severity. Results: The overall prevalence of depressive symptoms was 38.5%. The presence of depression was significantly associated with pre-existing medical conditions (p < 0.00001), anxiety (p < 0.00001), female sex (p < 0.006), and having self-isolated to protect one’s family (p < 0.01). Additionally, being a specialist physician was significantly associated with the risk of severe depressive symptoms (p < 0.04). Regarding moderate depressive symptoms, significant associations were found with rarely having access to the cafeteria during the workday (p < 0.004), occasionally having access to PPE (p < 0.005), and not having personal protective equipment at all (p < 0.04). Conclusions: A high prevalence of depressive symptoms was observed among front-line healthcare workers, showing significant statistical associations with female sex, specific medical backgrounds, self-isolation practices, and occupational pathways.

title: Nanozyme-Catalyzed Lateral Flow Assay for the Simultaneous Detection of RNA and Protein Biomarkers
abstract: Molecular diagnostics have advanced rapidly over the past decade, driven by the demand for accessible and scalable testing solutions. However, current assays often focus on single biomolecule types, limiting their ability to capture the multifactorial nature of disease. Integrating distinct molecular readouts─such as transcriptomic and proteomic biomarkers─could provide richer diagnostic information and improve clinical decision-making. Here, we present MOSAIC (Multiplexed Orthogonal Sensing Assay Integrated with CRISPRZyme), a unified lateral flow assay that enables simultaneous detection of RNA and protein biomarkers using a shared nanozyme-catalyzed readout. The assay combines CRISPR/Cas13a-mediated RNA detection and antibody-based protein detection, with assay components optimized through antibody conjugation tuning, blocking agent optimization, and probe loading calibration to achieve balanced and cross-talk-free performance. Using cardiovascular disease as a model, the platform successfully detects NTproBNP and LIPCAR long noncoding RNA simultaneously from the same sample. The assay was further optimized for spiked human plasma, incorporating tailored pretreatment and recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) to maintain RNA stability and performance in complex biofluids. Extending its versatility, the same assay design was adapted to detect SARS-CoV-2 biomarkers, the spike (S) protein and ORF1ab gene, in pooled human saliva. To enable standardized interpretation of multiplexed readouts, we additionally developed a machine-learning-assisted computational workflow that automates strip localization, signal extraction, and calibration curve construction. Together, these results demonstrate a modular, paper-based diagnostic platform that unites transcriptomic and proteomic analyses within one assay architecture, offering a practical step toward accessible and multiplexed molecular diagnostics across diverse disease contexts.

title: Fragile rights: rights consciousness in hospitals in times of crisis
abstract: This paper examines rights consciousness (RC) in hospitals during emergencies, drawing on interviews with bereaved relatives and healthcare workers from isolated COVID-19 wards in Israel. It reveals that neither group framed visitation as a formal legal entitlement but rather as a privilege, gift, or luxury. While visitation is a routine and expected practice in ordinary times, the crisis exposed its fragility, transforming it into a discretionary allowance whose availability depended on institutional priorities and frontline discretion. Family responses ranged from compliance to selective resistance, with rights awareness often emerging retrospectively and collectively. The analysis advances few theoretical insights. First, it conceptualizes visitation as a “fragile right” robust in everyday practice yet weakly anchored in law and easily erased in crisis. Second, it shows how “de facto rights” can re-emerge from within institutions through professional ethics, norms, and informal organizational diffusion. Third, it demonstrates that RC is relational and spatial, suppressed inside hospitals by clinical hierarchies, yet reconstructed outside them through collective comparison and shared experience. These dynamics suggest that strengthening such fragile rights may depend not only on legal reform but on bottom-up participation of patient/family in hospital policymaking during crisis, which can cultivate rights awareness from within care itself.

title: A hidden Markov model for disease trend analysis with joinpoints
abstract: The joinpoint model assumes piece-wise linear curves joined at multiple unknown joinpoints where the slope changes and has been widely used for disease surveillance. There are 2 analytical challenges that cannot be addressed with standard joinpoint methods. First, computation becomes infeasible as the number of potential joinpoints become large. Second, assessing the uncertainty that a joinpoint occurs at a particular time or window of time. We propose a hidden Markov model (HMM) that provides a computationally feasible approach to deal with these challenges. We show that it is natural to formulate the joinpoint model by modelling successive differences in observations as an HMM with the Markov chain being specified as a birth-process where each state change reflects the occurrence of a subsequent joinpoint. An extension of the forward–backward algorithm, developed for maximum-likelihood estimation of HMMs, easily accommodates long disease sequences with a large number of joinpoints. Further, we show how functions of the posterior distribution of state occupancy can be used to access joinpoint uncertainty. We show simulations with various settings and an application study of COVID-19 incidence data.
journal: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series A (Statistics in Society)

title: Process evaluation of a migrant-inclusive risk communication and community engagement intervention: lessons from the Health Handbook for Vietnamese Workers in Japan
abstract: Migrant workers in Japan face persistent barriers in accessing timely and culturally appropriate health information owing to language constraints, complex administrative systems, and fragmented risk communication channels. These challenges have been exacerbated during the COVID-19 pandemic, highlighting the need for migrant-inclusive risk communication and community engagement (RCCE). In response, the Government of Vietnam, the International Organization for Migration (IOM), and Japanese partners collaboratively developed the Health Handbook for Vietnamese Workers in Japan as a transnational RCCE intervention. This study evaluates a process the development, dissemination, monitoring, and iterative adaptation of the Handbook. Multiple data sources were triangulated, including mixed-methods situation analyses, technical working group documentation, Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT) assessment, digital analytics, and qualitative stakeholder feedback. Qualitative data were analysed using an inductive thematic approach. Themes generated from the data were subsequently interpreted in relation to RCCE principles and the social determinants of health framework to identify mechanisms relevant to the implementation of a migrant-inclusive RCCE. The evaluation identified three interrelated mechanisms that appeared to support migrant-inclusive RCCE: (1) addressing structural vulnerabilities; (2) deploying multichannel communication strategies tailored to migrants; and (3) engaging migrant communities and stakeholders. The Handbook was designed to provide practical health information, particularly on occupational health, healthcare navigation, and rights-related topics. Digital analytics showed an increased reach following collaboration with community-based platforms, while the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT) assessment indicated high understandability (81.3%) but moderate actionability (66.7%), indicating a need for iterative revisions. The intervention provided a platform for multi-sectoral collaboration and supported the continuity of health messaging across the migration cycle. This study illustrates that migrant-inclusive RCCE, when implemented through participatory, multi-sectoral, and transnational approaches, may support more equitable access to health information and contribute to health system resilience. Integrating such approaches within national preparedness frameworks may strengthen effective emergency responses and help address the structural determinants that shape migrant health by influencing exposure to health risks, access to reliable information and essential services, and the ability to seek timely and appropriate care.

title: [Strain, teamwork, and appreciation: General practitioners' perspectives on the situation of medical assistants during the pandemic - Results of a qualitative study].
abstract: BACKGROUND The COVID-19 pandemic posed major challenges for the healthcare system. While the situation faced by physicians and nurses has been extensively studied, the working conditions of medical assistants (MA) in primary care have received comparatively little attention in research to date. This article presents preliminary findings from the PIPER project (Pandemic Management in General Practice - Experience and Reflection) and examines how general practitioners (GPs) perceived the workload of MAs and what strategies were (jointly) developed to alleviate it. METHOD Between February and July 2021, 23 guided qualitative interviews were conducted with GPs. The data were analyzed using qualitative content analysis according to Kuckartz, with the assistance of MAXQDA. RESULT The pandemic led to high levels of physical and mental stress and intentions to resign among MAs, which was recognized by the GPs. To boost the MAs' resilience, joint solutions were developed. GPs primarily relied on collegiality and appreciation to reduce stress, but some also offered flexible work arrangements (e.g., working from home) and financial compensation. CONCLUSION Early interventions to identify signs of burnout, along with psychosocial support, appear to be crucial for strengthening the resilience of MAs and ensuring the ability of family practice teams to continue working during times of crisis.
journal: Zeitschrift fur Evidenz, Fortbildung und Qualitat im Gesundheitswesen

title: The biochemical composition of coronavirus Nucleocapsid proteins drives the bicistronic properties of their sub-genomic mRNAs
abstract: The nucleocapsid (N) gene of coronaviruses (CoVs) encodes a structural RNA-binding protein required for viral assembly. In SARS- and MERS-CoV viruses, reading frame 2 of N contains an overlapping open reading frame (ORF) encoding an innate immune antagonist accessory protein. However, the extent of this dual coding capacity across the CoV family, and the genetic features driving overlapping ORF formation, remain unexamined. Here, we developed an in-silico tool (ORFan) to screen structural gene sub-genomic mRNA sequences from 152 species of coronavirus for the presence of overlapping accessory gene candidates. We found that frame 2 of the N gene in Alpha-, Beta- and Delta-CoVs frequently contains a potential accessory ORF (AcORF), conserved at the subgenus level, unlike the spike, envelope and membrane genes. We also show that CoV nucleotide biases in conjunction with codon biases integral to N protein function drive the relatively high abundances of start codons in frame two and stop codons in frame three, explaining the tendency towards frame 2 AcORFs. We further suggest that viral nucleotide biases and the codon composition required for RNA-binding function facilitate overlapping ORF formation in other virus families

title: Transformación digital y su incidencia en el crecimiento económico de las medianas empresas del sector comercial en Machala, durante el período 2020-2025
abstract: This research aimed to analyze, based on the perceptions of business representatives, how digital transformation is related to the economic growth of medium-sized companies in the commercial sector of Machala during the 2020–2025 period. A qualitative approach with a descriptive and interpretive scope was employed, and semi-structured interviews were conducted with representatives of fourteen companies from the sector under study. The inquiry addressed the tools implemented, the organizational areas perceived as most transformed, the main barriers to their adoption, and the economic benefits identified by the participants. The testimonies indicated that the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the adoption of ERP and CRM systems, e-commerce, social media, electronic invoicing, and inventory control platforms. According to the interviewees, these tools were associated with perceived improvements in sales, logistics, administration, and customer service, mainly due to error reduction, time optimization, operational control, and the expansion of commercial channels. Most participants estimated that the contribution of digitalization accounted for between 30% and 40% of revenue growth. It is concluded that the participants perceived a favorable relationship between digital transformation, productivity, competitiveness, and business sustainability; however, they identified barriers related to costs, resistance to change, and the shortage of digital skills.

title: Sentidos da experiência universitária de ingressantes em Psicologia na pandemia
abstract: A pandemia do SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) produziu uma série de efeitos sociais que indicaram a necessidade de reformulação do cotidiano durante o período pandêmico (2020 – 2021), com implicações para os processos subjetivos. Não obstante, as instituições de ensino superior também precisaram se adaptar e passaram a adotar ferramentas de ensino remoto, inclusive para cursos presenciais, interferindo na relação dos estudantes com o contexto universitário. Esta pesquisa buscou apreender e analisar os sentidos da experiência universitária, decorrentes da pandemia da COVID-19, para discentes ingressantes em 2020 no curso de graduação em psicologia de uma instituição pública do interior do estado de São Paulo. O sentido, atributo de singularidade à atividade do sujeito, se estrutura pela dialética entre condições objetivas e subjetivas mediante processos cognitivos e afetivos em constante transformação. Para a produção dos dados de pesquisa, utilizou-se a entrevista semiestruturada com quatro estudantes, realizadas no início de 2022, em consonância com o retorno das atividades presenciais, tendo como aporte teórico a Psicologia Histórico-Cultural, em conformidade com a metodologia dos Núcleos de Significação. title: Diagnóstico de hemoparásitos, enteroparásitos y virus de importancia zoonótica en poblaciones urbanas de Columba livia en Colombia
abstract: Tras la pandemia de COVID-19, la vigilancia epidemiológica de patógenos con potencial zoonótico ha adquirido mayor relevancia. Columba livia, especie introducida ampliamente distribuida en ambientes urbanos de Colombia, alberga diversos agentes infecciosos. Sin embargo, su papel en la circulación del virus del Nilo Occidental (VNO) y la influenza aviar (VIA) sigue siendo poco conocido. El objetivo de este estudio fue evaluar la presencia de enteroparásitos, hemoparásitos y de ambos virus en poblaciones ferales de Bogotá, Arauca y Aguazul. Se analizaron muestras fecales, sanguíneas, orofaríngeas y cloacales de 48 individuos mediante microscopía y RT-qPCR. Se detectó Haemoproteus columbae como el hemoparásito más frecuente y enteroparásitos de los géneros Eimeria, Blastocystis, entre otros, en Arauca y Bogotá. No se obtuvo evidencia de infección activa por VIA ni por VNO. La confirmación de los resultados mediante RT-qPCR con SYBR Green permitió descartar como falsos positivos las muestras inicialmente reactivas para VNO por TaqMan. Estos hallazgos resaltan la importancia de confirmar los resultados moleculares con valores de Ct cercanos al límite de detección y respaldan la vigilancia epidemiológica de especies sinantrópicas como herramienta para el monitoreo de patógenos de importancia en salud pública.

title: On conducting diary-based social contact surveys to inform transmission models of close-contact infections: a systematic review and expert-informed questionnaire
abstract: Background: Diary-based social contact surveys are widely used to parameterise transmission models of close-contact infections. However, variation in study design, contact definitions, and questionnaire content limits comparability across studies. These challenges became particularly evident during the COVID-19 pandemic, when rapid and repeated data collection was urgently needed, often without harmonised instruments. To address these challenges, we aimed to develop an expert-informed questionnaire and update the recommendations on conducting diary-based social contact studies previously proposed by Hoang et al. Methods and findings: We conducted a systematic review of diary-based social contact surveys published between 31 January 2018 and 25 September 2025 using PubMed and the Web of Science Core Collection, extracting information on study design, survey methodology, contact definitions, and survey items from available questionnaires. Methodological quality and reporting were assessed using an adapted AXIS tool, with results summarised for each criterion. In total, we identified 129 studies across 62 countries, with most studies conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic (59.7% in 2021-2022). Retrospective reporting (86.0%) and non-probability sampling (77.5%) were largely adopted and became increasingly common during the pandemic, while non-paper-based data collection rose sharply from 2021 onwards. Across 36 retrievable questionnaires from general-population surveys, we identified 54 survey items. An online assessment involving 26 experts informed the classification of these items according to their perceived importance, resulting in an expert-informed questionnaire comprising 22 core items. Based on our findings, we updated previous recommendations on sampling, survey methods, contact definitions, behavioural change, essential contact information, and data governance. Conclusions: This study provides an expert-informed questionnaire and updated recommendations to support harmonised social contact data collection, improve comparability across studies, and strengthen preparedness for future public health emergencies.

title: The Effect Of ROA, EPS, And PBV On Stock Prices In The Financial Sector Listed On The Indonesia Stock Exchange 2021–2025
abstract: The financial sector capital market has experienced considerable dynamics and fluctuations in the post-COVID-19 period that have not always moved in line with companies’ financial fundamentals. An empirical anomaly occurred in 2023, when improvements in financial ratios were followed by a weakening of the sectoral stock price index. Objective This study examines the effects of Return On Assets (ROA), Earning Per Share (EPS), and Price to Book Value (PBV) on stock prices of financial sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2021–2025. Method: A quantitative explanatory approach was employed. Using purposive sampling, 13 companies were selected, resulting in 65 observations. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression. Results: ROA has no significant effect on stock prices (Sig. 0.053 > 0.05), while EPS and PBV have positive and significant effects (Sig. Simultaneously, ROA, EPS, and PBV significantly affect stock prices, with a coefficient of determination of 52.2%. Conclusion EPS and PBV are stronger determinants of investor decisions than ROA. The findings confirm the applicability of signaling theory in the Indonesian capital market.

title: Manejo odontológico de pacientes con enfermedades transmisibles: revisión sistemática
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre el manejo odontológico de pacientes con enfermedades transmisibles. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones, estudios transversales y retrospectivos. Resultados: la exposición ocupacional a la sangre, sobre todo por objetos punzocortantes, fue el principal riesgo para el personal. La vacunación contra la hepatitis B y la profilaxis posexposición fueron las medidas más eficaces frente a las infecciones sanguíneas. Frente al SARS-CoV-2 se recomendaron el triaje, el control de aerosoles y el equipo de protección. Conclusión: el manejo se basa en precauciones estándar aplicadas a todos los pacientes, que permiten una atención segura y sin discriminación.

title: Neural Score-Driven Volatility and Risk Forecasting
abstract: We develop a score-driven volatility model in which no particular parametric innovation distribution needs to be specified. The proposed method relies on a lightweight neural network to represent the negative score of the innovation density. By integrating and normalizing the learned score and imposing location-scale identification, we recover a flexible innovation density that can accommodate asymmetry, including negative skewness commonly observed in financial returns. Two estimation procedures are considered. A two-step procedure estimates the neural score by score matching and subsequently fits the volatility recursion with the identified density held fixed. A one-step procedure jointly refines the neural and volatility parameters under the conditional likelihood. We illustrate the practical relevance of the proposed method using eight international equity indices, with a separate evaluation of the high-volatility first half of 2020. The results show that the neural score-driven models are competitive with Gaussian and Student-$t$ GAS benchmarks that require a prespecified parametric innovation distribution, with particularly strong performance during the COVID-19 period.

title: How do we build a transfusion safety program during challenging times?
abstract: BACKGROUND The SARS-CoV-2 pandemic led to systemic shortages in the blood supply that highlighted the importance of blood stewardship and optimal blood utilization. We built a transfusion safety program in late 2020, the impact of which was immediately apparent. STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS We describe how we justified and obtained funding and resources to build a transfusion safety program at our institution, how we hired and trained two Transfusion Safety Officers (one registered nurse and one medical laboratory scientist), and highlight three early successful projects: (1) decreasing rejected samples, (2) decreasing blood wastage, and 3. improving processes around ordering Massive Transfusion Protocols (MTPs). RESULTS Through gap analysis and developing metrics with a goal of providing "early wins," our Transfusion Safety team decreased rejected specimens and blood wastage by approximately 30% each and instituted best practices around MTPs including notification of discontinuation of the protocol to >95%. DISCUSSION We successfully started a Transfusion Safety Program during a national blood shortage, which immediately impacted our hospital's blood supply through successful projects including blood stewardship. We highlight our program to serve as a practical resource for institutions seeking guidance on how to initiate and sustain a similar program at their institution.

title: Inferring viral variants and fitness advantages from longitudinal wastewater sequencing data
abstract: During the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, wastewater-based epidemiology emerged as an effective tool for monitoring infection dynamics. However, wastewater represents a pooled sample of incomplete viral genomic fragments originating from multiple individuals in the catchment area of a wastewater treatment plant, preventing the assembly of complete viral genomes. Existing computational pipelines are therefore limited in detecting new variants that are absent from clinical sequencing data. We developed FitNMF, an integrated viral dynamics and non-negative matrix factorization model that leverages the temporal structure of wastewater sequencing data and the underlying variant competition to jointly infer mutational signatures, relative abundances, and fitness advantages of circulating variants directly from wastewater next-generation sequencing data. Using simulated data as well as wastewater time-series data collected between 2021 and 2024 across six Swiss wastewater treatment plants, we demonstrate FitNMF's ability to identify and quantify emerging variants de novo, offering a powerful tool for real-time variant surveillance in settings with limited clinical sequencing.

title: A scalable invariant causal discovery framework reveals direct genetic and clinical determinants of complex human traits
abstract: Identifying genetic and clinical factors that exert direct causal effects on complex traits is central to precision medicine, yet remains a major challenge. Association-based methods cannot distinguish cause from consequence, and existing causal frameworks are limited by stringent assumptions or computational intractability in high-dimensional settings. Invariant causal prediction (ICP) offers a principled alternative but has seen minimal application in genetic epidemiology due to exponential complexity. Here, we introduce the Invariant Generalized Covariance Measure (I-GCM), a scalable framework that integrates ICP principles with machine learning to identify direct causal variables. I-GCM combines PC-simple screening with a generalized covariance measure (GCM) computed via gradient-boosted trees to test invariance across environments, capturing both linear and nonlinear dependencies. In simulations (up to 3,000 variables, 50,000 samples), I-GCM achieved PPV of approximately 0.84-1.00 and specificity >=0.99, outperforming PC-simple by 0.21-0.29 in precision with comparable sensitivity. Applying I-GCM to the UK Biobank, we identified direct causal genes and clinical risk factors for COVID-19 susceptibility and severity and for HDL and triglyceride levels, with many findings supported by existing literature and pathway enrichment. Notably, JAK1 was identified as a direct causal gene for severe COVID-19, consistent with clinical use of the JAK1-targeting therapy baricitinib. To our knowledge, this is among the first applications of invariance-based causal discovery to genetic epidemiology at a biobank scale. By bridging statistical causality and translational medicine, I-GCM offers a scalable, interpretable, and high-precision framework for mechanistic discovery and therapeutic target prioritization.

title: Identifying the viral and epidemiological factors behind the apparent global extinction of influenza B/Yamagata
abstract: Until 2020, two lineages of the influenza B virus had co-circulated globally. Measures to control the COVID-19 pandemic led to a near-absence of influenza infections. While B/Victoria reemerged in late 2021, there have been no reports of B/Yamagata since the pandemic. To investigate which epidemiological and immunological factors were primarily responsible for the extinction of B/Yamagata, we developed a global model for the two influenza B lineages. To mimic the transmission impacts of the pandemic, we implemented a transient reduction in contacts and identified parameter values that recapitulated viral coexistence dynamic before the pandemic and the qualitative post-pandemic outcomes of B/Victoria (reemergence in late 2021) and B/Yamagata (extinction). Our results suggest that, rather than immunological or evolutionary mechanisms, the extinction of B/Yamagata was mainly driven by its lower basic reproduction number making the virus particularly vulnerable during the early phase of the pandemic. Stochastic simulations of our best-fitting model suggest that B/Victoria was also close to extinction during this period. We investigate the model to assess the feasibility of B/Victoria eradication through vaccination and the potential for a sustained re-emergence of B/Yamagata in the 2026-27 flu season, thus highlighting important considerations for biosafety.
